items.desc:
The Challenge: Complex Scientific Data & Representation Learning 
 We’re building foundation models for scientific signals, starting with the brain (EEG, fMRI, ultrasound) and aim to extend the same approaches to other complex domains where data is scarce and difficult to collect.
 We finished as silver medalists at the NeurIPS 2025 EEG challenge and have had recent papers accepted to CVPR and submitted to ICML. This feels like we’re just beginning to find our footing. For every problem we solve, we seem to stumble upon three more fundamental questions we can’t answer yet. We’re still trying to figure out the basics of how these signals behave, and we find that uncertainty is much more motivating than the ‘solved’ parts.
 What the Work Looks Like 
 This role is about architecture-level thinking:
 Understanding Failures 
 Why do standard methods fail on irregular, noisy, or scarce data? How can we adapt?
 Pre-Training Strategy 
 Develop methods tailored to physical signals (small samples, irregular structures).
 Multimodal Alignment 
 Bridge gaps between signals and find the right inductive biases for physical systems.
 End-to-End Ownership 
 If the core is scientific exploration (experimental and evaluation design), note that as a member of a small team, you’ll own experiments from hypothesis to deployment and contribute to engineering (pipelines, infrastructure).

RequirementsEducation: PhD (preferred) in Machine Learning, Deep Learning, or a closely related quantitative field.Technical Expertise: Strong proficiency in PyTorch and experience running large models on GPU infrastructureData Experience: Hands-on experience handling challenging/complex data, including irregular time series, scientific signals, and geometric or physical structures.The “Data-First” Mindset: A practical approach to research where you prioritise analysing raw signals and data quality over just monitoring loss curves.Navigating Ambiguity: Ability to thrive in an environment with open-ended problems and the communication skills to make complex research approachable for non-scientific teams.Fluent English (the team speaks English in the day-to-day)Bonus SkillsSpecialised Deep Learning: Experience with multimodal alignment or large-scale pre-training and foundation models.Advanced Domains: Specific knowledge in geometric deep learning or physical signal processing.Academic Track Record: A history of publications in top-tier venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, or equivalent conferences.Unconventional Backgrounds: Experience working with “exotic” signals or unique data systems that demonstrate deep thinking and adaptability.Beyond Technical Skills:While technical excellence is critical, we place equal importance on how we work together. We believe the best teams are built on:Integrity & RespectWe are striving for honesty, kindness, and fairness. We value people who treat others with dignity and foster an environment where everyone feels heard.Open Communication & HumilityGreat ideas come from collaboration. We look for teammates who listen actively, communicate clearly, and approach challenges with self-awareness and humility.Psychological Safety & CamaraderieWe strive to create a space where people feel safe to take risks, ask questions, and grow.

items.desc: Le descriptif de l’offre ci-dessous est en Anglais Niveau de diplôme exigé : Bac + 5 ou équivalent Fonction : Ingénieur scientifique contractuel Contexte et atouts du poste The position is in the ARAMIS project-team (Inria, CNRS, Inserm, Sorbonne Université), at the Paris Brain Institute (ICM) on the Pitié-Salpêtrière hospital campus. ARAMIS develops computational and statistical methods for multimodal patient data in brain disorders. The engineer will be supervised by Reuben Dorent (Inria research scientist), whose work focuses on multimodal representation learning and statistical inference from incomplete medical data. Mission confiée Assignments : With the help of Reuben Dorent, the recruited person will be taken to: Build a reproducible pipeline that extracts and stores representations from several foundation models per modality (histology, spatial transcriptomics, MRI) on public multimodal datasets; Set up an evaluation protocol for alignment from few pairs, using datasets in which the true correspondences are known but only a few hundred of them are revealed during training; Extend the team's two-modality alignment method [1] to a first setting with three modalities, and compare it with existing baselines; Support a PhD student of the team working on histology-spatial transcriptomics integration, by providing shared tools for data preprocessing, feature extraction and evaluation. For a better knowledge of the proposed research subject : [1] J. Kordes, R. Dorent. Representation Alignment from a Few Paired Data via Distilled Optimal Transport. arXiv:2610.12781, 2026. [2] S. Ruyter, R. Dorent et al. Program-space Diffusion for Morphology-to-Transcriptomics Prediction. COMPAYL workshop, MICCAI 2026. [3] J. Ostermaier, S. Ruyter, R. Dorent et al. Disentangled shared representations improve morpho-transcriptomic integration. COMPAYL workshop, MICCAI 2026. Collaboration : The recruited person will be working closely with a PhD student of the ARAMIS team. Responsibilities : Write data loaders and preprocessing for public datasets such as HEST-1k (paired histology and spatial transcriptomics), TCGA (MRI, histology and clinical data), Ivy GAP and the Allen Human Brain Atlas. Extract embeddings from several pretrained foundation models per modality (e.g. pathology, single-cell / spatial transcriptomics and 3D MRI models) and organise them in a common, documented format. Implement the evaluation protocol: train/test splits that reveal only a few hundred pairs, retrieval and matching metrics, and robustness to the choice of paired samples. Implement and run baselines and the extension of the team's alignment method to three modalities; analyse the results. Package the code (tests, documentation, example notebooks) so that it can be reused by the PhD students of the team and released as open-source software. Take part in team meetings, present results and contribute to the writing of technical reports and, where results allow, scientific publications. Principales activités Analyse and implement related work. Design novel innovative solutions. Write progress reports and papers. Communicate advancement to the team. items.desc: AI4I — Italian Institute of Artificial Intelligence, Turin, Italy Scientific Lead Prof. Michele Magno Location Turin, Italy Positions 2 Working language English Start date As soon as possible. Compensation Approximately €33,000 gross per year (±15%), depending on experience, qualifications, and performance. The Edge AI & Intelligent Sensing (EIS) Laboratory at the Italian Institute of Artificial Intelligence (AI4I) is seeking two Research Engineers / Research Fellows to work at the intersection of Edge AI and emerging sensing technologies . The EIS Lab is scientifically led by Prof. Michele Magno , Professor at ETH Zurich and internationally recognized researcher in Edge AI, intelligent sensing systems, ultra-low-power embedded computing, and autonomous systems. The laboratory develops intelligent systems that bring AI directly to the edge, where AI meets the physical world, enabling real-time, reliable, and energy-efficient intelligence on resource-constrained devices and in real-world environments . We are looking for researchers and engineers who are excited about working across the boundaries of machine learning, embedded systems, sensing, and hardware/software co-design , and who want to translate research ideas into working experimental systems. Research spans application domains including robotics and autonomous systems, wearables, automotive, industrial systems, and biosignal sensing and processing , with a strong focus on real-world deployment and technologies with clear industrial relevance . The role Research Engineers / Research Fellows will work closely with Prof. Magno and the EIS research team to design, implement, and experimentally validate new approaches for intelligent sensing and Edge AI. Responsibilities May Include Develop and evaluate machine learning and deep learning methods for edge and embedded applications. Work with embedded platforms, edge accelerators, MCUs, NPUs, FPGAs, or other specialized computing hardware. Integrate AI algorithms with novel intelligent sensing technologies, including event-based cameras, depth cameras, radars, and other emerging sensing modalities. Develop and experimentally evaluate prototypes toward high-TRL solutions, with a strong focus on real-world deployment and industrial relevance, across applications such as robotics, wearables, automotive, and industrial systems. Contribute to scientific publications, research prototypes, open-source software, and collaborations with academic and industrial partners. Who We Are Looking For We are looking for candidates with a strong technical and experimental profile who are motivated by the challenge of bringing intelligence to real-world sensing and embedded systems. Required MSc degree in Electronic Engineering, or a closely related field. Strong programming skills in Python, C/C++, or similar languages. Practical experience with machine learning or deep learning frameworks, particularly PyTorch or equivalent. Strong interest in Edge AI, embedded intelligence, intelligent sensing, computer vision, or related areas. Hands-on experimental attitude and the ability to build, test, debug, and evaluate real systems. Strong written and spoken English. Candidates may have 1–3 years of relevant research or industrial R&D experience , or may be excellent recent MSc graduates with a strong experimental profile. For recent graduates, evidence of research or technical ability may include a high-quality MSc thesis, research or industrial internship, period abroad, publications, open-source contributions, or significant technical projects. Nice to have Experience in one or more of the following areas is highly valued: Embedded systems and Edge AI deployment, including experience with MCUs, NPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, or other edge AI accelerators Model optimization and efficient inference, including techniques such as quantization, pruning, and deployment on resource-constrained platforms. Computer vision and intelligent sensing, including multimodal perception, sensor fusion, event-based cameras, depth cameras, radars, or other emerging sensing technologies. Electronics prototyping and debugging, including PCB design and familiarity with laboratory instrumentation such as oscilloscopes and logic analyzers. Experience with application domains such as robotics and autonomous systems, wearables, automotive, or biosignal sensing. A demonstrated research or engineering track record, through publications, research projects, open-source contributions, a technical portfolio, or relevant industrial R&D experience. Candidates are not expected to cover every area . We value technical depth, experimental ability, curiosity, and the potential to develop into an independent researcher more than a perfect match to a checklist of technologies. What We Offer An ambitious interdisciplinary research environment. Work at the intersection of AI, embedded systems, sensing, and autonomous systems, with substantial intellectual and technical ownership. …

items.desc: Your Mission As Research Scientist / Engineer — Large-scale Training , you will develop the architectures and training methods that make UMA’s robotic foundation models more capable and more efficient to train . You will investigate how model design, optimization, and hardware-aware implementation work together to deliver better humanoid robot performance within a given compute budget. Your primary focus will be pretraining , with work extending into mid-training and post-training . You will explore efficient multimodal architectures, faster training recipes, and compute-efficient scaling strategies, using controlled experiments to determine which improvements translate into stronger capabilities on real robots. We already have a working training stack and a strong team behind it. Working closely with AI researchers and Training Infrastructure engineers, you will take ideas from architectural changes and kernel-level prototypes through training experiments to larger-scale validation. Your findings will shape what we train, how we train it, and how we allocate compute . Key responsibilities: Research efficient model architectures for robotic foundation models, including attention mechanisms, multimodal fusion, visual and action tokenization, sequence compression, and dense versus sparse or mixture-of-experts designs. Optimize training recipes and convergence through choices of optimizers, learning-rate schedules, initialization, normalization, batch sizes, and numerical precision. Measure improvements in time and compute required to reach a target capability. Co-design architectures and compute kernels: identify expensive operations, explore hardware-friendly alternatives, and prototype fused or custom kernels using tools such as Triton or CUDA where useful. Investigate efficient attention and sequence processing, reducing the cost of learning from video, temporal context, and action sequences while preserving useful information. Develop scaling laws and compute-allocation studies to understand how performance changes with model size, training data, and compute. Use smaller experiments to guide larger runs, and validate where those predictions hold. Research training acceleration techniques, such as progressive increases in resolution or context length, selective freezing, parameter sharing, and lower-precision computation, evaluating their effects on stability and final performance. Run controlled ablations and performance benchmarks that distinguish faster execution from better learning efficiency, tracking wall-clock time, compute, memory, convergence, and downstream capability. Diagnose training dynamics and numerical instabilities, including gradient behavior, sensitivity to precision, loss spikes, and changes that emerge as models or batch sizes scale. Evaluate how pretraining improvements transfer through mid-training and post-training to real-robot success, generalization, robustness, and adaptation efficiency. Work with Training Infrastructure engineers to integrate validated methods into scalable, reproducible training systems, and with Data researchers to study interactions between model capacity, data mixtures, and training duration. What You Bring To The Table Previous experience in training large-scale frontier foundation models such as LLMs, Video Generation Or Vision Encoders Strong experience in deep learning research, efficient model training, foundation models, or ML systems, demonstrated through research projects, publications, deployed systems, or open-source work. Strong Python and PyTorch, with hands-on experience implementing architectures and running substantial training experiments. A deep understanding of model architectures, optimization, and training dynamics, and the ability to explain why a change affects convergence, stability, or computational cost. Experience improving training efficiency, whether through architecture design, optimization methods, numerical precision, or hardware-aware implementation. The ability to reason about compute, memory bandwidth, tensor shapes, and GPU execution, and connect profiling results to research decisions. Strong experimental judgment: meaningful baselines, fair compute comparisons, reproducible results, and careful interpretation of scaling trends. Interest in connecting efficient training research to multimodal learning and real-world robot capabilities. Thrive in a hands-on, fast-paced startup: autonomous, rigorous, collaborative, and comfortable moving between research and implementation. Bonus: Triton, CUDA, fused kernels, efficient attention, or compiler-based optimization. Bonus: scaling laws, compute-optimal training, mixture-of-experts models, or large-scale multimodal pretraining. Bonus: distributed training, low-precision training, vision-language-action models, or robot learning. Bonus: open-source contributions, reproducible research implementations, or technical writing. We value deep expertise in one or more of these areas , …

items.desc: Irfu is recruiting an engineer specialized in data processing and artificial intelligence (AI) / deep learning as part of the development of a foundation model dedicated to particle physics to address the scientific and technological challenges of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC). Scheduled to begin operation around 2029, the HL-LHC will increase the integrated luminosity of the current LHC by a factor of ten, producing unprecedented volumes of data (on the order of several exabytes over its lifetime). This major evolution makes the development of new AI and algorithmic approaches essential, particularly for event reconstruction and physics analysis. Scientific objectives include Higgs boson physics, searches for physics beyond the Standard Model, heavy-flavour physics and QCD phenomenology. Within this context, Irfu is developing a foundation model trained on large volumes of simulated and/or real data from the ATLAS, CMS and LHCb experiments to enable efficient transfer learning (fine-tuning) for a wide range of downstream physics tasks. This approach is directly inspired by the success of large language models (LLMs) and vision foundation models. You will join a multidisciplinary team composed of particle physicists, scientific computing engineers and machine learning researchers. Main responsibilities: Design, train and evaluate AI model architectures adapted to particle physics data. Develop self-supervised learning strategies using simulated and real LHC datasets. Develop data processing pipelines, experiment tracking tools and physics performance benchmarks. Contribute to scientific and technical documentation, publications and presentations at international conferences. Profil du candidat LET’S TALK ABOUT YOU ! PhD in computational physics, signal processing/AI or a related field. Good knowledge of particle physics and/or nuclear physics. Strong background in large-scale data processing and machine learning/deep learning (neural networks, transformers, etc.). Proficiency with Python AI/ML frameworks (PyTorch) and the scientific Python ecosystem (NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn, etc.). Experience with collaborative software development tools such as Git and CI/CD. Experience working in high-performance computing environments (HPC, GPU clusters, SLURM). Additional assets: Knowledge of HEP data formats and tools such as ROOT and HDF5. Experience with particle-physics-specific architectures (ParticleNet, PELICAN, Particle Transformer, JetGPT, OmniJet, etc.). Experience publishing scientific papers or contributing to HEP-ML open-source software. Personal skills: Ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams and proactively propose new ideas. Pragmatic, rigorous and able to tackle complex problems under multiple constraints. Curious, adaptable, autonomous and possessing excellent interpersonal skills. Excellent written and spoken communication skills in both French and English, including technical English. You enjoy working in a multidisciplinary team and know how to be proactive. You are pragmatic and know how to take initiative. Your analytical skills, rigour and ability to take a step back allow you to calmly tackle complex problems under multiple constraints (deadlines to meet, major technical challenges). You are curious, adaptable and autonomous, and have good interpersonal skills. You have excellent written and oral communication skills in both French and English and are proficient in technical English (comprehension and written and oral expression). LET’S TALK ABOUT US! Joining the CEA means joining a public research organization whose mission is to provide the French government, industry and local authorities with the means to address the major challenges of our time: the energy transition, climate change, tomorrow's energy systems, the medicine of the future, digital technologies and defense. items.desc: Here at Humanoid, we believe in a future where robots amplify human potential. That’s why we’ve set out on a mission to build the world’s most capable, commercially-scalable, and safe humanoid robots. We’re bringing that mission to life with HMND‑01 - our rapidly developed humanoid platform being deployed in real industrial environments - and we’re growing the team to take it even further. Our Mission At Humanoid we strive to create the world's leading, commercially scalable, safe, and advanced humanoid robots that seamlessly integrate into daily life and amplify human capacity. About The Role As a Research Engineer on the World Models team, you will build action-conditioned generative models that predict how the world evolves around our robots — future video, proprioception, contacts, and outcomes — from past observations and actions. World models serve four purposes in our stack: a pretrained, physics-aware prior for our VLA policies; an engine for rare data collection, cross-platform transfer, and sim-to-real transfer; a testbed for policy evaluation and testing before hardware; and a future-prediction rollout engine that surfaces what our policies intend to do, for safety and planning. This is a hands-on individual contributor role: you will design architectures, run large training jobs, and validate your models against real fleet data from industrial deployments. What You'll Do Design and train multimodal world models — video, state, action, and language — using diffusion-based and transformer architectures. Build action-conditioned video prediction and dynamics models that stay physically consistent over long horizons, including contact-rich manipulation, and serve as pretrained priors for VLA policies. Develop learned-simulator evaluation: score candidate policies offline, predict real-world success rates before deployment, and roll out policy futures to expose intended behaviour for safety review and planning. Generate synthetic rollouts and counterfactual experience — including rare events, cross-platform transfer, and sim-to-real transfer — to augment policy training, and measure their effect on downstream task performance. Establish fidelity metrics and calibration protocols that quantify where the world model can be trusted and where it diverges from reality. Build data pipelines that turn fleet telemetry, teleoperation logs, and internet-scale video into training corpora for world models. Run scaling and ablation studies on architecture, data mixture, and context length; communicate findings crisply. Collaborate with pretraining, RL, and manipulation teams to integrate world models into policy training and evaluation loops. What We're Looking For A track record of training large generative models — video, world, or multimodal — with shipped models or published artifacts to show for it. Deep hands-on experience with modern generative architectures: diffusion models, autoregressive transformers, latent-variable models, or video prediction. Experience with large-scale distributed training: streaming datasets, checkpointing and state management, debugging numerics and training instabilities. Strong Python + PyTorch/JAX; you can profile kernels, optimize data loaders, and write maintainable research code. Empirical rigor: you design careful evaluations, run honest baselines, and document experiments clearly. Excitement about grounding generative models in physical reality rather than pixels alone. Nice to have Experience with world models for robotics or autonomous driving (e.g., action-conditioned video models, learned simulators, model-based RL). Familiarity with robotics simulators (Isaac Sim, MuJoCo) and sim-to-real considerations. Experience using world models for policy evaluation or synthetic data generation at scale. Publications at top-tier deep learning conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CoRL, CVPR) or equivalent open-source contributions. Experience optimizing generative models for fast inference. What We Offer Competitive equity: stock options with meaningful upside as we scale. 30+ paid days off, including 23 days of annual leave, all UK bank holidays, and additional company closure days (including Christmas–New Year shutdown). Private healthcare, including virtual and in-person care. Pension scheme with 8% total contribution (5% employee, 3% employer) on full earnings. Free daily breakfast, catered lunch, and snacks in-office. Work at the frontier - collaborate daily with world-class engineers, researchers, and product experts building the next generation of AI and humanoid robotics. Real ownership - direct access to founding leadership, meaningful input on product direction, and the ability to drive key initiatives from day one.

items.desc: The University of Kassel is a modern and growing University with round about 21.000 students. The university’s wide range of expertise covers subjects in the natural, applied, cultural and social sciences. In the Department of Electrical Engineering/Computer Science, Intelligent Embedded Systems Group (Prof. Dr Bernhard Sick), the following vacancy is available from 1st January 2027. Research Associate (m/f/d), EG 14 TV-H, fixed-term, full-time (currently 40 hours per week) Application deadline: 20.11.2026 Date of hire: 01.01.2027 vacancy number: 39545 The post is initially limited until 31 December 2028 as part of the ‘DyNaMo’ project, in accordance with its duration (academic qualification position pursuant to § 2 WissZeitVG). An extension of the employment is planned. The opportunity to obtain a habilitation degree is given. The Intelligent Embedded Systems (IES) group conducts research in the area of fundamentals and applications of methods in data analysis, machine learning (e.g. deep learning, active learning) and artificial intelligence. In the focus of basic research are, for example, self-learning and self-organizing systems, methods of collaborative and active learning, methods of transfer learning, and techniques for real-time analysis of time series. Applied research focuses on the fields of energy systems, automotive (autonomous driving) and experimental physics/materials. The IES group currently employs around 20 researchers in the above areas. Your tasks: Methods for perceiving cyclists’ behaviour by using machine learning techniques (in particular deep learning approaches) based on data from vehicle sensors (e.g. camera and LiDAR data). Cross-labelling approaches for the highly automated annotation of cyclists’ behaviour data, i.e. transferring ‘labels’ from, for example, camera data to LiDAR data. Methods for integrating information from models trained on different data modalities and evaluating the resulting information gain. Planning and conducting measurement campaigns in the form of laboratory experiments as well as field experiments. Research within the DyNaMo project. Contributing to the group’s general tasks. Requirements: A PhD and a completed university degree in Computer Science or a closely related field Excellent knowledge in perception and computer vision. Very good fundamental knowledge in machine learning and data analysis. A successful academic career with high-impact publications in the relevant fields. Experience in external fundraising (e.g. LOEWE, BMFTR, DFG). Experience in programming, particularly in Python, but also in other programming languages. Good knowledge of AI tools, e.g. PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, Pandas, OpenCV and NumPy. A structured approach to work that enables you to lead a team. A keen interest in the challenges posed by machine learning applications in the field of automated driving. An independent and goal-oriented approach to work, and a passion for scientific research. Very good written and spoken German and English (at least B2 level in each). A driving licence valid in Germany for passenger cars. The following conditions are advantageous Experience in organisation and coordination (e.g. project management, team leadership). Experience in supervising PhD students, e.g. when they write publications. As a member of staff in the Intelligent Embedded Systems group: You will lead a small but highly motivated team, you will have the opportunity to attend conferences, summer schools, and various professional development programmes (e.g. the opportunity to obtain a habilitation degree), you will have access to your own, very large Slurm-based compute cluster (CPU and GPU), you will have access to your own, state-of-the-art test vehicle (a car equipped with a camera, LiDAR and radar), you will be able to develop new methods for use in practical applications. In case of any questions ask Prof. Dr. B. Sick, bsick(at)uni-kassel.de. We are looking for a world-class AI researcher to join the FMAI4Air project, a high-stakes mission to revolutionise how we predict air pollution, evaluating its impacts on people’s health and protecting millions of lives. items.desc: The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research. We have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee. Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to make a real difference. The role Do you want to build the first-ever Foundation Model for air quality? We are looking for a world-class AI researcher to join the FMAI4Air project, a high-stakes mission to revolutionise how we predict air pollution, evaluating its impacts on people’s health and protecting millions of lives. Role This isn't just another incremental AI project; we are pioneering a Physics-Informed Multimodal High-Resolution Foundation Model. You will be at the intersection of deep learning and atmospheric sciences, working within the prestigious and word-leading ecosystem of Surrey's PAI, CVSSP and GCARE, under the leadership of Assoc Prof Erick Sperandio. Your role will be: Architect the Future of AI for Environmental Sciences: Design and pre-train a novel, task-agnostic, multimodal, high-resolution and physics-informed Foundation Model (FM) for air quality prediction that fuses heterogeneous data, from satellite imagery and surface sensors to meteorological grids and emissions inventories, and evaluates the impacts of air pollution on people’s health. Bridge AI and Atmospheric Physics: Move beyond the "black box" by embedding physical constraints (such as advection-diffusion equations) directly into the model architecture to ensure scientific consistency, interpretability and trustworthiness. Push the Resolution Limit: Implement state-of-the-art super-resolution and downscaling techniques to translate coarse global data into street-level, actionable insights. Solve Real-World Grand Challenges: Fine-tune the pretrained FM for critical downstream applications, including early-warning systems for wildfires and simulating urban air-quality mitigation scenarios to inform government policy through a web-based application for FMAI4Air proof-of-concept. Leverage High-Performance Computing: Pretrain and fine-tune the models on world-leading HPC infrastructure, including Surrey’s AI@Surrey and the national Isambard-AI HPC. Collaborate Nationally and Globally: You will work alongside a powerhouse consortium including Imperial College London, the University of Manchester, and NTNU (Norway), as well as with consortium partners from academia including IAG-USP (Brazil), NC Climate Office at NCSU (USA), Chiba University (Japan), from industry including NVIDIA and WSP Global, and from government such as Guildford Borough Council. About You Expertise in designing and training large-scale Deep Learning architectures (e.g., Transformers, Mamba, or similar spatiotemporal models). Proven experience in multimodal data fusion (handling a mix of time-series, imagery, and tabular data). Strong proficiency in PyTorch and Tensorflow, and experience deploying models on HPC clusters and on the edge for fast and efficient inference. Expertise in developing and deploying Web applications that will be used to operationalise FMAI4Air models for policy and decision making. A solid mathematical foundation in calculus and linear algebra, with the ability to implement physics-informed constraints into neural networks’ loss functions. A track record of publishing high-quality research in top-tier AI or environmental science conferences/journals. Commitment to deliver high-quality research and innovation outcomes, including publishing papers in top-tier venues, and support research, dissemination, communication and management activities. How To Apply To apply please submit your CV and a cover letter via our website. For an informal conversation about the role please contact Erick Sperandio via erick.sperandio@surrey.ac.uk

items.desc: Your Mission As AI Infra / Engineer — Large-scale Training , you will build the systems that make UMA’s humanoid robot learning fast, scalable, and reliable . You will turn experimental training code into robust execution pipelines that scale across thousands of GPUs and support rapid iteration. You will work directly with AI researchers, shaping the software used to train our robotic foundation models across pretraining, mid-training, and post-training on large-scale multimodal data . You will own the engineering challenges of distributed execution: choosing parallelism strategies, optimizing memory and communication, accelerating critical operations, and keeping long-running jobs reliable.. We already have a working training stack and a strong team behind it. You will build on that foundation, with room to rethink components where needed. Working closely with AI researchers, you will scale pretraining across GPUs and nodes , optimize compute, memory, and communication , and make long-running training jobs reliable. The goal is to reduce training time and increase experiment throughput , enabling larger models and faster research iteration within our compute budget. Debugging here goes beyond keeping jobs running. You will understand enough of the learning process to recognize when a numerical issue or distributed implementation bug appears in a loss curve, and work with researchers to resolve it. The systems you build will also support mid-training and post-training as our models evolve. Key responsibilities: Build distributed pretraining systems across multiple GPUs and nodes, selecting appropriate strategies such as DDP, FSDP, and tensor, pipeline, or expert parallelism as workloads require. Develop RL and post-training execution infrastructure, including distributed rollouts, actor–learner coordination, policy synchronization, replay buffers, and efficient batching. Maximize MFU and eliminate bottlenecks: Profile the complete training loop—data loading, decoding, CPU-GPU memory transfers, and compute kernels—eliminating bottlenecks to keep MFU high and ensure accelerators operate at peak efficiency. Integrate and benchmark accelerated kernels and execution techniques, such as FlashAttention, fused operations, mixed precision, and compilation; develop custom optimizations where they provide clear value. Build efficient training-time data movement and buffering, including out-of-core storage, caching, prefetching, and asynchronous transfers, in partnership with the Data Infrastructure team. Turn research prototypes into maintainable training systems, with reusable components that support evolving architectures and experimental workflows. Diagnose distributed and numerical failures, including deadlocks, memory leaks, gradient anomalies, precision issues, and inconsistencies between single-device and distributed runs. Deep numerical debugging and run determinism: Diagnose complex issues across the stack—from distributed deadlocks and memory leaks to training instabilities and gradient anomalies—while enforcing numerical determinism so that training runs, evaluations, and experiments are strictly reproducible. Build reliable checkpointing and fault-tolerant resumption, preserving model, optimizer, and relevant execution state so interrupted jobs can recover correctly. Strengthen observability and reproducibility through configuration tracking, profiling, run diagnostics, and deterministic execution where practical. What You Bring To The Table Solid experience building ML training infrastructure, distributed systems, or high-performance ML software. Strong Python and PyTorch, with hands-on knowledge of distributed training tools such as DDP, FSDP, or Megatron. Experience with multiprocessing, asynchronous execution, and GPU memory management, and an understanding of how communication and synchronization affect scaling. Practical knowledge of losses, optimizers, gradients, and numerical precision, sufficient to debug training behavior alongside researchers. Experience profiling accelerator workloads with tools such as PyTorch Profiler or Nsight Systems, and translating findings into measurable improvements. A pragmatic engineering mindset: you can turn experimental code into reliable, scalable systems while keeping research iteration fast. Clear communication and a collaborative approach to working with researchers whose requirements evolve quickly. Bonus: RL infrastructure, distributed rollouts, replay buffers, or actor–learner architectures. Bonus: C++, CUDA, Triton, custom kernels, or compiler-based optimization. Bonus: Slurm or Kubernetes, GPU networking such as InfiniBand/RoCE, or storage caching. Bonus: contributions to open-source training tools or technical writing. For Bachelor’s and Master’s candidates, research experience is required but can take other forms, e.g. thesis work, open-source contributions, or projects Hands-on experience with modern deep learning architectures, such as transformers, sequence models, representation learning, self-supervised learning, and/or generative models Solid understanding of the theoretical foundations of deep learning, optimization, statistical learning, and neural network training dynamics Strong programming skills in Python and hands-on experience with at least one modern deep learning framework, such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow Strong communication skills with the ability to explain technical ideas clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences You may submit one application per role each year. Though you may apply to multiple roles, please note that each application will be evaluated based on the specific criteria established for that particular role. If you have already applied for this position during the current recruitment season and were not selected, you may reapply when the next recruitment season begins in 2027. Foundation Models on Structured Data, like SAP-RPT-1, have ushered in the GenAI era for business relevant scenarios – scenarios that have so far been addressed with classical, often tree-based methods. Now, we are taking the next step. Contribute to thought leadership in an entirely new field of Foundation and World Models on Structured Data. Work closely with the team developing the relational pre-trained transformer (SAP-RPT-1) to exchange information and ensure that internal initiatives and project deliverables are aligned with community best practices. Collaborate with established academic partners and supervise PhD students during summer internships or as part of academic collaborations. items.desc: Your Mission As Research Scientist / Engineer — Data , you will develop the methods that efficiently turn diverse data into better humanoid robot policies at UMA. You will investigate which data improves robot learning , how to make it useful, and when to introduce it during training. You will work with on-robot teleoperation, simulation, and off-robot data —including egocentric human recordings and UMI-style demonstrations—across pretraining, mid-training, and post-training . Your research will help answer central questions: what should we collect next? How can human demonstrations transfer to robots? Which data mixtures, representations, and supervision signals produce the greatest gains in real-world performance? We already have a working data and training stack and a strong team behind it. Working closely with our AI, Robotics, and Data Infrastructure teams, you will take ideas from dataset design and research prototypes through controlled training experiments to validation on humanoid robots . Your findings will directly shape our data collection and acquisition strategy , helping us improve robot capabilities while making the best and most efficient use of collection effort and compute. Key responsibilities: Develop methods to make off-robot data useful for robot learning, including action inference, retargeting, and alignment across viewpoints and embodiments, drawing on camera and hand pose estimation or object tracking where useful. Research data composition across training stages: broad pretraining, mid-training, and post-training using demonstrations, simulation, and deployment experience. Design data curation tools and selection methods for filtering, segmentation, annotation, quality scoring, and identifying informative examples. Study source mixtures, sampling strategies, curricula, supervision signals, re-annotation and data ingestion strategies, and implement these ideas in training experiments. Run controlled ablations and scaling studies to isolate the effects of data quantity, quality, diversity, and source under realistic compute budgets. Measure impact on real-robot success, generalization, robustness, and adaptation efficiency, including how much additional robot data is needed to learn new tasks. Shape collection and acquisition priorities based on evidence: which tasks, environments, embodiments, data types, failures, and recoveries are worth capturing, and at what cost. Work with data engineers to turn validated research methods into reproducible processing and training workflows. What You Bring To The Table Strong experience in data-centric research, robot learning, computer vision, or multimodal learning, demonstrated through research projects, deployed systems, publications, or open-source work. Strong Python and PyTorch, with hands-on experience implementing research ideas and training or fine-tuning models. A solid understanding of machine learning and experimental design: meaningful baselines, controlled comparisons, reproducibility, and evaluation beyond training loss. Experience investigating how data quality, coverage, mixtures, and distribution shifts affect downstream model behavior. Experience with multimodal or sequential data, such as video, motion, sensor streams, or action trajectories. The ability to connect research findings to practical decisions about data collection, training, and robot evaluation. Experience in working with large-scale multimodal data. Thrive in a hands-on, fast-paced startup: autonomous, rigorous, collaborative, and curious about robotics and learning. Bonus: egocentric data, robot teleoperation, UMI-style demonstrations, simulation, or autonomous-vehicle datasets. Bonus: 3D geometry, pose estimation, retargeting, cross-embodiment learning, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, or sim-to-real transfer. Bonus: active data selection, public datasets, open-source contributions, or technical writing. Bonus: Optimizing data ingestion pipelines during training. UMA is an inclusive workplace that values exceptional researchers and builders over perfect resumes . If you enjoy discovering what makes data useful and turning those findings into better robot capabilities, we strongly encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box.

items.desc: Develop the Next Generation of AI for Computational Life Sciences At JIJ, we develop advanced computational technologies for solving complex scientific and industrial problems. Our R&D spans machine learning, mathematical optimisation, network science, quantum and quantum-inspired computing, with a strong emphasis on translating fundamental research into practical scientific impact. We are expanding our interdisciplinary life-sciences research team to develop advanced computational approaches for challenging problems in microbiology, bioinformatics, genetics, microbiome science, and biological network modelling . Example problems include understanding how microbial communities change over time, how microorganisms interact, how biological perturbations propagate through these communities, and which mechanisms determine recovery or loss of resilience. This is not a role focused simply on applying standard machine-learning pipelines to biological datasets. It is particularly suited to researchers interested in developing new computational methodology and translating research ideas into reproducible scientific technology. The Opportunity We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer with expertise spanning computational biology and machine learning to develop next-generation models of longitudinal microbiome systems. You will work with high-dimensional biological datasets including microbial abundance, genomic and functional information, environmental or intervention metadata, and potentially metabolomic and other multi-omics measurements. A central research direction will be representing biological systems as dynamic graphs , where microorganisms, genes, metabolites, pathways, or host factors form interacting networks whose topology and state evolve over time. You will investigate state-of-the-art approaches including: Graph machine learning : GNNs, message passing, graph attention, graph transformers, and heterogeneous or knowledge-graph models. Temporal and dynamic modelling : evolving interaction networks and continuous-time or state-space approaches. Biologically informed learning : combining pathway, phylogenetic, metabolic, and genomic priors with data-driven models. Representation and multi-omics learning : self-supervised methods, foundation-model representations, and multimodal integration. Causal, interpretable, and uncertainty-aware modelling for perturbation analysis, biological discovery, and robust prediction. Where scientifically justified, you may also investigate quantum or quantum-inspired approaches (e.g. quantum machine learning, quantum kernels, tensor networks, Ising/QUBO formulations). These are complementary research directions rather than mandatory components of every project. What You'll Do Computational Biology & Biological Representation Develop computational models for microbiome dynamics, perturbation, recovery, resilience, and broader biological network problems. Build biologically meaningful graph and multi-omics representations that integrate microbial, genomic, metabolic, pathway, phylogenetic, and host information. Formulate biologically meaningful questions and translate them into rigorous computational experiments. Graph, Temporal & Interpretable Learning Design and evaluate GNN, graph-transformer, temporal, causal, and interpretable learning methods. Address microbiome-specific challenges such as compositionality, sparsity, batch effects, confounding, and irregular sampling. Establish strong classical and statistical baselines and distinguish statistical associations from biologically plausible mechanisms. Research to Impact Translate state-of-the-art research into reproducible experiments, research software, technical reports, and peer-reviewed publications. Collaborate across computational and experimental teams and with academic, scientific, and industry partners. Develop reusable methods and technologies rather than one-off analyses wherever possible. Qualifications We are looking for engineers and researchers who can move comfortably between biology, mathematics, and machine learning . You may be an excellent fit if you have: A PhD, or a research-intensive MSc with significant experience, in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Microbiology, Genetics, Genomics, Systems Biology, or a closely related discipline. A strong background in statistics and machine learning, with the ability to design, train, validate, and rigorously benchmark predictive models for complex scientific datasets. Practical experience developing models in Python using PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, or an equivalent framework. Experience with graph machine learning or biological network modelling (GNNs, graph attention or transformers, heterogeneous graphs, knowledge graphs, or temporal graph models). Strong working knowledge of microbiology, microbial ecosystems, genetics, molecular biology, or bioinformatics, enabling effective communication with biological …

items.desc: Le descriptif de l’offre ci-dessous est en Anglais Type de contrat : CDD Niveau de diplôme exigé : Bac + 5 ou équivalent Fonction : Chercheur contractuel A propos du centre ou de la direction fonctionnelle The Inria center at the University of Rennes is one of eight Inria centers and has more than thirty research teams. The Inria center is a major and recognized player in the field of digital sciences. It is at the heart of a rich ecosystem of R&D and innovation, including highly innovative SMEs, large industrial groups, competitiveness clusters, research and higher education institutions, centers of excellence, and technological research institutes. Contexte et atouts du poste Context and Background As artificial intelligence expands across edge devices, data centers, and embedded systems, the demand for computational power has grown dramatically. Deep neural networks require billions of arithmetic operations and move vast amounts of data, which drives up both energy consumption and hardware complexity. Specialized accelerators like GPUs and TPUs have delivered significant improvements over general-purpose processors, yet the increasing scale of AI models continues to push power and thermal limits. This becomes particularly challenging for edge and battery-powered devices, where energy efficiency determines not just performance but practical viability and long-term sustainability. Approximate computing offers a compelling approach to these energy constraints by trading some computational precision for improvements in power efficiency, performance, and chip area. The fundamental insight is that many AI applications, such as image recognition, speech processing, and recommendation systems, can tolerate a degree of error. Neural networks are particularly resilient, maintaining acceptable accuracy even when operations use reduced precision, simplified circuits, or probabilistic components. Leveraging this tolerance allows designers to reduce switching activity, memory bandwidth, and overall hardware complexity. For AI hardware accelerators, approximate computing can be implemented across multiple design layers: algorithmic techniques like model pruning and quantization, architectural approaches such as approximate memory hierarchies, and circuit-level methods including approximate multipliers and adders. Together, these strategies can substantially reduce both dynamic and static power while keeping application performance within acceptable error margins. As AI deployment scales from resource-constrained edge devices to large data centers, approximate computing has become an essential research direction for achieving sustainable and energy-efficient acceleration. Mission confiée The primary objective of this job is to investigate and advance the design of energy-efficient AI accelerators by dynamically applying approximate computing techniques and to advance hardware-software co-design methodologies. The research will build upon recent advancements in efficient domain-specific architectures for AI. The goal is to develop novel approaches that balance performance, energy efficiency, and accuracy, while addressing the unique challenges of implementing approximate computing in real-world AI systems. Principales activités This research explores the principles and practical implications of approximate computing as a pathway toward more energy-efficient AI hardware accelerators. It examines how different forms of approximation affect computational efficiency, prediction accuracy, and overall system-level performance. Rather than treating these techniques in isolation, the study considers their combined impact across the computing stack , with particular attention to how accuracy-efficiency trade-offs can be characterized and controlled. A central theme of the work is the integration of hardware and software perspectives through a co-design approach. By closely aligning algorithmic characteristics with architectural features, the research aims to uncover strategies for embedding approximation mechanisms directly into accelerator designs. Emphasis is placed on adaptive and context-aware approximation techniques that can dynamically balance energy savings and output quality, ensuring that efficiency gains do not compromise application-level requirements. To ground these ideas in practice, the research involves modeling, simulation, and experimental prototyping using representative AI workloads, including deep learning inference and computer vision applications. Through systematic evaluation and validation , the study aims to assess the feasibility, robustness, and scalability of proposed approaches, contributing insights into the design of next-generation energy-efficient AI systems. items.desc: The Role The video understanding pipeline—from multi-object tracking and re-identification to action recognition—is yours to own and scale. The technical challenge lies in balancing high-throughput, low-latency GPU inference with cutting-edge detection accuracy across massive streams of sports footage. You will establish rigorous benchmark suites and decide which vision foundation models make it into production. About the Product The platform ingests live and recorded sports video to automatically extract real-time metadata, temporal key moments, player statistics, and scene-boundary events. Operating across multiple sports leagues, it relies on frame-accurate video parsing to power downstream broadcast automation, search, and analytics tooling. Technology Stack: The core ML pipeline is built in Python using PyTorch for model training and fine-tuning. Production GPU inference is optimized for cost and latency using TensorRT and ONNX Runtime within Dockerized, queue-driven microservices. FFmpeg handles large-scale video decoding, while Azure (Service Bus, Blob Storage) underpins the asynchronous messaging infrastructure. What You’ll Be Doing Own and improve the vision services Own the video understanding pipeline, including object detection, multi-object tracking, player re-identification, jersey-number recognition and on-screen text recognition (OCR). Own event and action recognition, including temporal localisation of key moments, shot and scene-boundary detection, replay detection and camera-view classification. Optimise GPU inference for throughput and cost through batching, precision tuning and compilation. Monitor production quality and latency, and investigate failures and regressions. Evaluate and test new models Build and maintain labelled sports benchmarks, split by sport, league and content type. Define and track key metrics, including mAP, F1, precision, recall, IoU, latency and GPU cost. Run systematic bake-offs comparing new detection, tracking, segmentation, re-identification and video foundation models. Reproduce published results on our data. Write decision memos with clear recommendations, trade-offs and licensing considerations. Own the regression suite and shadow or A/B testing pipelines, ensuring every model or configuration change is validated before deployment. Track new papers, model releases and leaderboards, and identify which developments warrant further evaluation. What We Expect Must have 3–5+ years of experience shipping production ML systems, including 2+ years in computer vision, ideally working with video. Strong Python and PyTorch skills, including hands-on experience profiling and optimising GPU inference using TensorRT and ONNX Runtime. Hands-on experience in at least two of the following areas: object detection and segmentation (YOLO, DETR-family, SAM), OCR and scene-text recognition, or video action recognition and temporal localisation. Experience building test sets, calculating evaluation metrics such as mAP, F1 and temporal IoU, and running rigorous model comparisons. Ability to critically evaluate new research papers and model cards, and reproduce published results. Production deployment experience with Docker, queue-driven services and cloud GPU infrastructure. Experience with video processing at scale, including FFmpeg, video decoding pipelines and frame sampling. Strong written communication skills, with the ability to document technical trade-offs and make clear recommendations. Nice to have Experience with Azure (Service Bus, Blob Storage) and message-driven architectures. Experience with vision-language models and multimodal understanding across video, audio and text. Experience fine-tuning or adapting vision models to specific domains, particularly sports video. Experience with self-supervised learning or synthetic data generation to reduce labelling costs. Familiarity with annotation tools such as CVAT and Label Studio, and experience working with labelling teams. Experience with shadow deployments and A/B testing. Familiarity with commercial model licensing. Why This Role Is Worth Your Time Direct, unconstrained ownership of the full ML lifecycle—from paper replication and benchmark creation to live GPU optimization. Production impact at scale, where your model optimization directly lowers real-world infrastructure costs and improves latency on high-volume video data. High-rigor, evidence-driven engineering environment that prioritizes A/B testing, shadow paths, and statistical validation over hype. Category Machine Learning · Сomputer Vision Type Location hybrid · Poland · Warsaw

items.desc: Here at Humanoid, we believe in a future where robots amplify human potential. That’s why we’ve set out on a mission to build the world’s most capable, commercially-scalable, and safe humanoid robots. We’re bringing that mission to life with HMND‑01 - our rapidly developed humanoid platform being deployed in real industrial environments - and we’re growing the team to take it even further. About The Role We're hiring a strong Robotics Learning Engineer to join our Manipulation team based in London. In this role, you will work on teaching our robots to manipulate the world around them. This is a role at the intersection of applied deep learning and robotics, and to be set up for success you need both experience of working with real robot hardware (e.g. identifying issues in control or teleop), and applied deep learning (you don’t have to be an expert on cutting edge neural network techniques, but you should be perfectly capable of curating data, fine-tuning a policy on that data and hypothesising potential mitigations when something doesn’t work). What You’ll Do Post-train manipulation policies via behaviour cloning and RL; own the full loop from data to deployment. Come up with data preprocessing strategies to improve the quality of collected data. Work with the simulation team to set up RL training using digital twin, and then iterate on reward and simulation quality to ensure successful transfer to the real world. Partner with the data collection organization to drive data collection activities for a specific capability: specify what good data looks like, ensure diversity and coverage, and iterate on instructions. Expand observation and action spaces with new components required to support novel capabilities, and work with the Teleoperations team to expose these components to robot operators. Partner with Teleoperations and Controls teams to improve motion smoothness and teleoperation experience. Interface with hardware design team to ensure that manipulation team findings regarding the current generation of hardware are reflected in future designs. What We're Looking For 3+ years working on robots (industry or research) with shipped artifacts to show for it. A good understanding of modern teleoperation and low-level control stack. Experience with neural network post-training. Familiarity with deep learning infrastructure: streaming datasets, checkpointing & state management, distributed training, PyTorch or JAX. Ability to profile & debug numerics and write maintainable research code. Good familiarity with modern software engineering practices. Ability to document experiments clearly and communicate trade‑offs crisply. Nice To Have Experience training VLA models for manipulation (autoregressive, diffusion or flow-matching based). Familiarity with OpenVLA, Physical Intelligence (π) models, or similar open VLA frameworks. Experience applying RL to robotics problems. Publications at top-tier robotics or deep learning conferences or equivalent open‑source contributions. What We Offer Competitive equity: stock options with meaningful upside as we scale. 30+ paid days off, including 23 days of annual leave, all UK bank holidays, and additional company closure days (including Christmas–New Year shutdown). Private healthcare, including virtual and in-person care. Pension scheme with 8% total contribution (5% employee, 3% employer) on full earnings. Free daily breakfast, catered lunch, and snacks in-office. Work at the frontier - collaborate daily with world-class engineers, researchers, and product experts building the next generation of AI and humanoid robotics. Real ownership - direct access to founding leadership, meaningful input on product direction, and the ability to drive key initiatives from day one.

items.desc:
RIVR, an Amazon company, is building Physical AI by deploying autonomous robots for real-world doorstep delivery. Operating daily in diverse urban environments, RIVR's robots continuously learn from and navigate the millions of scenarios encountered during deliveries. By owning the full stack from software.
Our fleet of delivery robots operates globally today, generating vast amounts of robotic real-world data. By utilizing state-of-the-art Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, large-scale generalist models (like Transformers), generative AI, and similar methods, we can leverage this pool of data to significantly enhance its autonomy, navigation, and manipulation skills. In this role, you will develop multi-modal models that enable robots to autonomously generate actions from demonstrations, real-time sensor data, and natural language commands. We are seeking an expert in VLA models, imitation learning, and generative AI techniques with a deep knowledge of supervised, and self-supervised learning algorithms. If you are passionate about pushing the boundaries of AI we invite you to join us in shaping the future of intelligent robotics. 
Key job responsibilities
Develop and implement Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, generalist robot transformers, and imitation learning algorithms (e.g., diffusion policies) to enable robots to autonomously execute complex tasks.
Design, test, and refine your algorithms to meet the demands of complex real-world autonomy and navigation tasks, with a focus on spatial reasoning and generalization.
Streamline the data collection and training workflow to efficiently expand model capabilities with new tasks and data sources.
Collaborate with the reinforcement learning team to innovate methods that leverage both simulated and real-world data.
Optimize and distill networks for real-time deployment on the edge (e.g. Nvidia Jetson Thor).
Build, lead and mentor an exceptional team of software engineers.
Provide expert guidance to product managers and executives for strategic decision-making.
Create and maintain documentation, guidelines, and best practices to streamline knowledge sharing.
About the team
Our team is focused on applying scientific research to solve meaningful customer problems at Amazon scale. We bring together scientists and engineers who are passionate about translating ideas from the latest academic literature into production systems that make a real difference. We value collaboration, intellectual curiosity, and a commitment to rigorous, reproducible science. As we continue to grow, you will have the opportunity to shape new solutions, contribute to published research, and develop your career alongside some of the most talented minds in the industry.
- Master’s degree or higher in a relevant field such as Engineering, Robotics, or Machine Learning.
- At least three years of industry or research experience, with PhD experience applicable.
- Strong deep learning fundamentals including supervised learning, self-supervised learning, Transformer-based architectures, policy optimization algorithms, imitation learning, and generative AI techniques (including Diffusion Models).
- Proven experience in developing Vision-Language-Action models or large-scale generalist robot models (e.g., RT-2, Octo).
- Strong background in robotics including autonomy, navigation.
- Experience with deploying artificial neural networks on hardware platforms.
- Ability to prototype algorithms and train deep neural networks in Python (Pytorch)
- PhD degree in Robotics, Engineering, Computer Science, Machine Learning or a similar discipline, or an equivalent amount of research experience.
- Publications at top-tier conferences.
- Experience in managing a software team.
- Ability to write production-level code in modern C++

The UCL Cancer Institute is a world-leading centre for cancer research, bringing together more than 400 scientists and clinicians who work collaboratively to understand cancer and translate discoveries into improved diagnostics, treatments and patient outcomes. Professor Attard’s research group utilises bioinformatic analysis, computational modelling, and digital histopathology to interrogate treatment resistance in prostate cancer, and he leads several of the world leading trials in prostate cancer, including STAMPEDE, that have changed clinical practice multiple times. Dr. Chakraborty’s research group TRAIL is a computational lab that develops state of the art explainable and trustable AI/ML methods applied to grand challenges in personalised healthcare and precision biomedicine, particularly multimodal computational cancer problems. UCL Medical Physics & Biomedical Engineering is a world-leading multidisciplinary department that develops innovative technologies spanning medical imaging, biomedical engineering, healthcare technologies, artificial intelligence and computational medicine. Cancer is a complex, multi-scale disease involving interacting processes across the molecular, cellular, tissue and organ levels. At the same time, advances in genomics, molecular profiling, pathology, imaging and clinical data collection have generated unprecedented volumes of multimodal cancer data. A major challenge is to integrate these diverse data sources into coherent computational frameworks that can generate biological insights, support clinical decision-making and accelerate therapeutic discovery. We are seeking a highly motivated and talented Data Scientist (Grade 7) in AI for computational cancer to join an ambitious and multidisciplinary research programme focused on constructing and validating transparent, interpretable, and biologically grounded models directly from multimodal cancer datasets. About the role The successful candidate will lead the research, generation, and exploration of novel multi-modal AI models, intended to deepen our understanding the underlying relationships between different forms of computational cancer data - including digital histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and genomics - generated from tissue samples collected as part of prostate cancer clinical trials. The researcher will contribute to fundamental advances in our understanding of cancer biology while supporting the development of innovative approaches for patient stratification, therapeutic target discovery, treatment optimisation and precision oncology. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to publish in leading journals, present their work at major international conferences and contribute to the development of transformative AI technologies with significant scientific and clinical impact. This is an exceptional opportunity for an ambitious AI researcher to develop and apply cutting-edge AI technologies to challenging real-world problems in biomedicine. For more details about the Attard Group, please visit: Treatment Resistance | Faculty of Medical Sciences This post is funded for 1 year in the first instance, with potential of extension subject to availability of funds. You will possess excellent programming skills, particularly in Python and modern machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow, and have experience in areas such as computer vision, natural language processing or multimodal AI. You will be an analytical and innovative researcher with excellent problem-solving skills and, ideally, experience applying AI to healthcare or computational cancer research. items.desc: « Rejoignez le CEA pour donner du sens à votre activité, mener ou soutenir des projets de R&D nationaux et internationaux, cultiver et faire vivre votre esprit de curiosité. » EN SYNTHESE, QU’EST-CE QUE NOUS VOUS PROPOSONS ? Nous cherchons un(e) Ingénieur(e)-chercheur(se) en IA embarquée pour le CND et le SHM pour le laboratoire « Instrumentation Intelligente, Distribuée et Embarquée » (LIIDE). Ce poste de cadre en CDI est basé sur le site du CEA Paris-Saclay, Essonne (91). Ce poste est à pourvoir dès que possible. QU’ATTENDONS-NOUS DE VOUS ? En tant qu’ingénieur-chercheur en IA embarquée, vous renforcez une équipe multidisciplinaire spécialisée en intelligence artificielle et en micro-électronique dont la mission est de développer une plateforme mixte, matérielle et logicielle, pour concevoir les fonctionnalités de l’instrumentation du futur pour le Contrôle non destructif (CND) et la surveillance des structures et des systèmes (SHM – Structural Health Monitoring). Vous aurez pour missions de : Développer des algorithmes d’IA et de Machine Learning pour l’analyse de données issues de systèmes de CND et de SHM : signaux temporels/fréquentiels, images et données multimodales ; Adapter et optimiser les modèles pour leur déploiement sur des architectures embarquées contraintes développées au CEA (Orchestra, Aidge, etc.) ; Implémenter et évaluer les solutions sur différentes cibles matérielles : microcontrôleurs, processeurs embarqués, GPU/NPU ou FPGA ; Contribuer à l’intégration et à la validation expérimentale des solutions développées sur des démonstrateurs en collaboration avec l’équipe de micro-électronique et les contributeurs des projets utilisant ces outils ; Participer au montage et à la réalisation de projets de R&D collaboratifs ou industriels ; Contribuer au suivi technique et au reporting des projets, en lien avec le chef de laboratoire ; Valoriser les travaux de R&D par des publications, communications scientifiques et dépôts de brevets. Profil du candidat Ingénieur.e /docteur.e en méthodes IA / sciences des données / technologies de l’information, vous disposez de compétences solides dans plusieurs des domaines suivants : Machine Learning et Deep Learning ; Mathématiques appliquées, méthodes statistiques ; Traitement du signal embarqué ; Architectures de réseaux de neurones : CNN, RNN, LSTM, Transformers ; IA embarquée / Edge AI et optimisation de modèles pour des architectures à ressources contraintes (compression, etc.); Programmation Python/C++ et maîtrise de frameworks de Deep Learning tels que PyTorch ou TensorFlow. Des connaissances en microélectronique, architectures matérielles et systèmes embarqués constitueraient un plus. VOUS AVEZ ENCORE UN DOUTE ? Les à-côtés de votre mission principale peuvent vous intéresser : Un écosystème de recherche à la pointe, unique en son genre et dédié à des thématiques à fort enjeu sociétal, qui donne du sens à votre mission Des formations pour renforcer vos compétences, en acquérir de nouvelles et booster votre mission Un équilibre vie privée / vie professionnelle reconnu par nos collaborateurs La possibilité de télétravailler pour équilibrer les temps de transport et contribuer à votre qualité de vie Un CE riche en avantages et en activités sociales, culturelles et sportives Un lieu de travail au cœur d’un plateau dynamique, entouré d’écoles et d’entreprises de la tech Un restaurant d’entreprise subventionné à proximité Un plan d’épargne entreprise avec abondement employeur Des frais de transports en commun couverts à 75% Cela vous tente ? Postulez, ce poste est fait pour vous ! Conformément aux engagements pris par le CEA en faveur de l'intégration des personnes en situation de handicap, cet emploi est ouvert à toutes et à tous Localisation du poste Site Saclay Localisation du poste France, Ile-de-France, Essonne (91) Ville Saclay Demandeur Disponibilité du poste 01/10/2026

items.desc: About the company: KIEFER is building Greece's integrated AI ecosystem. From renewable energy infrastructure and AI systems to robotics and enterprise applications, we connect the technologies that power Europe's intelligent future. Founded in 2014, KIEFER has delivered 600MW+ of energy projects and is now developing sovereign AI infrastructure, enterprise AI products and physical AI systems for Greece and Southeast Europe. About The Role We are looking for an ML Engineer to improve the agent and long-context LLM capabilities behind Kiefer Tech’s AI products. You will work hands-on across post-training, data, evaluation, agent design, and inference, with the goal of making multi-step tasks more reliable in production. What You Will Do Run post-training experiments using supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, reinforcement learning, or other suitable methods. Improve how agents plan, use tools, manage execution, and recover from errors. Build benchmarks, verifiers, and diagnostic tools to measure agent performance and identify failures. Generate and curate training data, including agent trajectories and difficult cases from target workflows. Evaluate and improve long-context behavior, memory and retrieval interactions, and reliability over multi-step tasks. Work with ML, Product, and Engineering to improve inference and bring successful experiments into production with clear regression checks. What You Will Need 3+ years of relevant ML or research engineering experience, with clear technical ownership and measurable results. Hands-on LLM post-training experience in at least one area: supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, reinforcement learning, or a comparable method. Experience building agent systems involving tool use, multi-step execution, and error recovery. Strong skills in model and agent evaluation, failure analysis, and the creation or curation of training data. Strong Python, hands-on experience with PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, or a similar framework, and solid software engineering skills. Experience improving or deploying model-backed systems, with an understanding of LLM inference performance and cost. Nice to have Reward modeling or verifier-based training. Long-context training, memory systems, retrieval, or context compression. Distributed training or high-performance LLM serving. Experience delivering agents for complex enterprise, coding, or research workflows. What Is There For You Compensation: Competitive package aligned with talent benchmarks. Impact: Hands-on work shaping AI capabilities for Kiefer Tech’s products and real-world applications. AI-native environment: Real challenges across model development, evaluation, and production AI systems. Culture: Engineering-first, high autonomy, low bureaucracy, and space to shape meaningful AI products.

We like being around each other because the best conversations here rarely happen in meetings. We are not your typical team. It’s not just the 10 countries we’re from, the languages we speak or our non-traditional backgrounds. We’re solving hard problems with people we respect - we make the most of our time together, we make it special. We are not another “polished” SF startup . We value velocity over speed, raw talent over brands, and genuine human connection above all else. We value being successful, not looking successful. What You’ll Own & Build Model human differences . Turn motivation, goals, personality, identity, experience and technical fluency into psychologically grounded, computationally useful models that guide agents and generalise across users. Infer users’ internal states. Use clickstreams, navigation paths and dwell time to model intent, confusion, patience, confidence and engagement, linking these states to each agent’s persona. Shape behaviour in live interfaces. Model how traits, goals, experience and changing states such as frustration or uncertainty influence agents’ attention, choices and actions during computer use. Measure human fidelity. Compare agent behaviour with human data, build benchmarks and quantify uncertainty to identify where simulations succeed or fail across user types. Understand how users interpret interfaces. Study attention, expectations and mental models: what users notice first, what they overlook, and where interfaces conflict with their expectations. Experiment with synthetic populations. Test how different users respond to interface and flow changes, analysing trajectories for patterns, failure modes and edge cases before launch. Are comfortable interpreting data, collaborating with engineers, and working in a fast-moving environment.
