It brings together expertise across microbiology, immunology, clinical sciences, data science and artificial intelligence.The Department offers a highly interdisciplinary and collaborative environment, with strong links to clinical partners and access to outstanding research infrastructure and cross faculty initiatives.About usThis is an exciting project Supported by the BBSRC. Antibiotic resistance (ABR) is one of the biggest public health challenges of our time. In 2019, 1.27 million deaths were attributed to antibiotic resistant bacteria. The gut microbiome is composed of harmless symbionts, commensal bacteria, and opportunistic pathogens, all of which play crucial roles in human and animal health and disease. In physiological conditions the gut microbiome is stable, but when perturbative events occur (e.g., dietary changes, infections, stress, antibiotic administration) the population of microbiota changes, influencing health and protection against further colonisation. These changes may involve new resistant bacteria becoming permanent residents or transferring resistance to the commensals). The core concepts underlying our project are: to gaining a better understanding of how the gut microbiome changes as consequence of infection, co-infection, or treatment (including the development of resistant traits) is a fundamental starting point towards understanding the mechanisms of inception and spread of endemic diseases and antimicrobial resistance.The research associate will be responsible for developing, implementing and applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning and data-mining methods to address complex research questions. They will lead the analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous datasets, including sequencing, sensor, biological and medical data, and ensure robust, reproducible computational workflows.The postholder will be responsible for developing and applying AI methods across the following areas, demonstrated through scientific publications or other academic/industrial achievements:Generative AI (text and numerical data; excluding image, audio, video generation)Agentic AI, orchestration, and adaptive systems (continuous feedback, dynamic reasoning, self-optimisation)AI methods for mining, classifying, and forecasting from heterogeneous data sourcesSpatial-temporal statistics/modelling from heterogeneous data (Bayesian hierarchical models, autoregressive models, random fields)Sequence/time-series modelling and language models, particularly transformer architecturesExplainable AI methodsCausal AI methodsMachine learningThis is a full-time post 35 Hours a week, and you will be offered a fixed term contract until 31st August 2028. You will shape and lead an ambitious research portfolio spanning compliant data pipelines, model pre-training, reinforcement learning and post-training, advanced distillation, agentic systems and efficient deployment. items.desc: Et si votre prochain défi s’écrivait chez Parrot ? Du Bluetooth dans l’automobile aux drones grand public, jusqu’aux drones professionnels : depuis 1994, nous avons fait de l’innovation notre culture . Année après année, nous transformons notre savoir-faire technologique en solutions toujours plus intelligentes, performantes et ambitieuses . Trois décennies d’innovations nous ont permis de construire une expertise unique et de nous imposer sur des marchés en constante évolution. Et cette dynamique se traduit aussi dans nos chiffres : le Groupe a réalisé près de 80 M€ de chiffre d’affaires en 2025, dont 87 % à l’international . À Paris, 180 ingénieur·e·s R&D imaginent et développent les prochaines générations de drones. De la conception aux essais, les équipes interviennent sur l’ensemble de la chaîne technologique dans un environnement international et multiculturel propice à l’autonomie et à la prise d’initiative . Des projets qui évoluent vite, des cycles courts et des défis technologiques qui se renouvellent en permanence. Votre terrain de jeu : apprendre à un drone à voir, à comprendre son environnement et à s’y repérer en temps réel. Au sein de l’équipe Computer Vision – Deep Learning, votre cœur de métier sera de concevoir et développer les réseaux de neurones qui répondent à un problème de perception concret (détection, segmentation, tracking, estimation de profondeur…), puis de les intégrer, les tester et les fiabiliser jusqu’à ce qu’ils tournent à bord de nos drones. Données, formulation du problème et contrainte embarquée se pensent d’un bloc : exploiter nos données de façon créative en mettant les foundation models les plus récents au service de nos datasets , choisir le paradigme d’apprentissage adapté, et concevoir une architecture taillée pour le NPU embarqué. Vous travaillerez aux côtés d’ingénieur·e·s spécialisé·e·s dans la conception et l’intégration de réseaux de neurones embarqués , en lien étroit avec les autres métiers du drone. Vous développerez votre expertise sur trois fronts : avant tout le deep learning , de la conception des architectures à leur entraînement ; la computer vision , important pour concevoir les réseaux et tout ce qui les entoure ; et l’intégration embarquée (C++, optimisation, tests, debug). Pour progresser sur ces trois fronts, vous pourrez compter sur la veille active de l’équipe, qui suit de près l’état de l’art en deep learning pour le transformer en solutions réalistes sur des cibles contraintes. Vous aimez autant lire un article de recherche récent que traquer un bug sur cible ? La robotique et l'IA embarquée vous passionnent, et la rigueur comme la persévérance qu'exigent l'intégration et les tests ne vous font pas peur ? Ce poste est fait pour vous. VOS MISSIONS : Concevoir : poser le problème de perception, choisir le paradigme d’apprentissage adapté et définir l’architecture du réseau en intégrant d’emblée les contraintes du NPU embarqué, en vous appuyant sur l’état de l’art. Valoriser les données : imaginer des solutions créatives pour exploiter nos données dans les apprentissages, notamment à base de foundation models (auto-annotation, pseudo-labels, curation et constitution de datasets ciblés). Entraîner et itérer : piloter les apprentissages sous PyTorch avec des stratégies d’entraînement en plusieurs étapes, et faire évoluer conjointement données, formulation et architecture, notamment pour la rendre quantization-friendly, jusqu’à la solution la plus performante sur cible. Embarquer : compresser et optimiser le réseau et le code pour la cible (quantification, profiling de latence sur NPU), implémenter la librairie C++ et l’intégrer au firmware, en lien étroit avec les autres métiers du drone. Valider : construire les outils de test et de validation de la fonction embarquée et des briques de computer vision qui entourent le réseau, et mener des benchmarks précision/latence rigoureux et reproductibles, représentatifs de l’usage opérationnel. Voler : éprouver vos algorithmes en conditions réelles, lors de tests avec nos drones. VOTRE PROFIL : Vous êtes diplômé·e d'une école d'ingénieur avec spécialisation en computer vision et deep learning ou disposez d'une expérience équivalente. Vous justifiez de plus de 3 ans d'expérience en industrie . Vous maîtrisez la conception et l'entrainement de réseaux de neurones pour la perception, en Python / PyTorch et avez une forte connaissance de l'état de l'art . Des connaissances en compression de modèles, déploiement sur NPU, en foundation models et modèles multimodaux en C++, outils de test et de débug embarqué et en MLOps seraient un plus. Vous êtes passionné de robotique et IA embarquée , vous êtes curieux et faite de la veille sur l'état de l'art. Vous êtes reconnu·e pour votre rigueur et persévérance, votre prise d'initiative et votre esprit d'équipe. Vous êtes à l'aise en français et anglais pour des échanges réguliers écrits et oraux. items.desc: Fusionality is building the measurement, simulation, and control stack for the fusion energy reactors of the future. Spun out of EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center and backed by top investors, our technology enables reliable operation, real-time monitoring, and analysis of high-temperature plasmas in fusion devices. We are founded by world-class experts at the intersection of fusion physics, advanced control, and AI (ex-Google DeepMind, EPFL). We are assembling a founding engineering team in Lausanne to build our core technology platform. We are looking for a Data / Machine Learning Engineer to join our team. This job is for you if you like turning large, messy, heterogeneous experimental data into clean, labelled, trustworthy datasets. You have done this with scientific or industrial sensor data. Familiarity with fusion is a plus but not a strict requirement. Responsibilities Build, maintain and run pipelines that bring experimental fusion data into high quality, consistent, documented, versioned datasets. Develop ML-assisted labelling and event detection (e.g. disruptions, MHD activity, diagnostic faults), using weak supervision, active learning and anomaly detection. Own data quality and provisioning: provenance, calibration metadata, automated validation. Manage and facilitate access for the rest of the team. Work with physicists validating the datasets & labels. Work with our computational scientists and control engineers, who build models and controllers on these datasets, and with customers to understand and integrate their data. Requirements Hands-on experience building data pipelines for large scientific or industrial time-series data formats (e.g. HDF5, Parquet, Zarr). Proficiency in designing, querying and optimizing SQL and noSQL database systems and familiarity with Time Series databases such as TimescaleDB, InfluxDB. Experience in applying ML techniques to time series in Python (PyTorch or JAX): sequence models, anomaly and event detection, semi- or weakly-supervised labelling. Solid software engineering habits: testing, reproducibility, data versioning are second nature to you. Evidence of independent work at the highest level: a PhD thesis and/or published code that is used by others, or an industry project you owned. You should be comfortable designing data architectures independently from day 1. The following are an advantage but not strictly required: Human-in-the-loop labelling tools and workflows. Pipeline Orchestration (e.g. Dagster, Airflow, Prefect) and data versioning (e.g. DVC, lakeFS). Data from large physics experiments: fusion, accelerators, astronomy, or exposure to fusion data systems (MDSplus, IMAS). What we offer Play a key role at a dynamic, fast-growing startup, shaping the technical solutions and products from the ground up. Build cutting edge technology to monitor and control plasmas in real fusion devices, working side-by-side with leading plasma and control experts. Great working conditions, located in Lausanne, Switzerland, a city and country known for its high quality of life. Competitive salary and equity compensation, matched to level of seniority, and benefits including immigration assistance.

items.desc: Et si votre prochain défi s’écrivait chez Parrot ? Du Bluetooth dans l’automobile aux drones grand public, jusqu’aux drones professionnels : depuis 1994, nous avons fait de l’innovation notre culture . Année après année, nous transformons notre savoir-faire technologique en solutions toujours plus intelligentes, performantes et ambitieuses . Trois décennies d’innovations nous ont permis de construire une expertise unique et de nous imposer sur des marchés en constante évolution. Et cette dynamique se traduit aussi dans nos chiffres : le Groupe a réalisé près de 80 M€ de chiffre d’affaires en 2025, dont 87 % à l’international . À Paris, 180 ingénieur·e·s R&D imaginent et développent les prochaines générations de drones. De la conception aux essais, les équipes interviennent sur l’ensemble de la chaîne technologique dans un environnement international et multiculturel propice à l’autonomie et à la prise d’initiative . Des projets qui évoluent vite, des cycles courts et des défis technologiques qui se renouvellent en permanence. Votre terrain de jeu : apprendre à un drone à voir, à comprendre son environnement et à s’y repérer en temps réel. Au sein de l’équipe Computer Vision – Deep Learning, votre cœur de métier sera de concevoir et développer les réseaux de neurones qui répondent à un problème de perception concret (détection, segmentation, tracking, estimation de profondeur…), puis de les intégrer, les tester et les fiabiliser jusqu’à ce qu’ils tournent à bord de nos drones. Données, formulation du problème et contrainte embarquée se pensent d’un bloc : exploiter nos données de façon créative en mettant les foundation models les plus récents au service de nos datasets , choisir le paradigme d’apprentissage adapté, et concevoir une architecture taillée pour le NPU embarqué. Vous travaillerez aux côtés d’ingénieur·e·s spécialisé·e·s dans la conception et l’intégration de réseaux de neurones embarqués , en lien étroit avec les autres métiers du drone. Vous développerez votre expertise sur trois fronts : avant tout le deep learning , de la conception des architectures à leur entraînement ; la computer vision , important pour concevoir les réseaux et tout ce qui les entoure ; et l’intégration embarquée (C++, optimisation, tests, debug). Pour progresser sur ces trois fronts, vous pourrez compter sur la veille active de l’équipe, qui suit de près l’état de l’art en deep learning pour le transformer en solutions réalistes sur des cibles contraintes. Vous aimez autant lire un article de recherche récent que traquer un bug sur cible ? La robotique et l'IA embarquée vous passionnent, et la rigueur comme la persévérance qu'exigent l'intégration et les tests ne vous font pas peur ? Ce poste est fait pour vous. VOS MISSIONS : Concevoir : poser le problème de perception, choisir le paradigme d’apprentissage adapté et définir l’architecture du réseau en intégrant d’emblée les contraintes du NPU embarqué, en vous appuyant sur l’état de l’art. Valoriser les données : imaginer des solutions créatives pour exploiter nos données dans les apprentissages, notamment à base de foundation models (auto-annotation, pseudo-labels, curation et constitution de datasets ciblés). Entraîner et itérer : piloter les apprentissages sous PyTorch avec des stratégies d’entraînement en plusieurs étapes, et faire évoluer conjointement données, formulation et architecture, notamment pour la rendre quantization-friendly, jusqu’à la solution la plus performante sur cible. Embarquer : compresser et optimiser le réseau et le code pour la cible (quantification, profiling de latence sur NPU), implémenter la librairie C++ et l’intégrer au firmware, en lien étroit avec les autres métiers du drone. Valider : construire les outils de test et de validation de la fonction embarquée et des briques de computer vision qui entourent le réseau, et mener des benchmarks précision/latence rigoureux et reproductibles, représentatifs de l’usage opérationnel. Voler : éprouver vos algorithmes en conditions réelles, lors de tests avec nos drones. VOTRE PROFIL : Vous êtes diplômé·e d'une école d'ingénieur avec spécialisation en computer vision et deep learning ou disposez d'une expérience équivalente. Vous justifiez de plus de 3 ans d'expérience en industrie . Vous maîtrisez la conception et l'entrainement de réseaux de neurones pour la perception, en Python / PyTorch et avez une forte connaissance de l'état de l'art . Des connaissances en compression de modèles, déploiement sur NPU, en foundation models et modèles multimodaux en C++, outils de test et de débug embarqué et en MLOps seraient un plus. Vous êtes passionné de robotique et IA embarquée , vous êtes curieux et faite de la veille sur l'état de l'art. Vous êtes reconnu·e pour votre rigueur et persévérance, votre prise d'initiative et votre esprit d'équipe. Vous êtes à l'aise en français et anglais pour des échanges réguliers écrits et oraux. You embed with a small number of accounts, work in their environment, and own whatever stands between them and production on Fireworks: the model, the serving path, the integration, the performance. You scope the work before signature and deliver what you scoped. Depth over breadth: few accounts, owned end to end. What we value most is first principles thinking: reasoning about unfamiliar problems from the ground up rather than from playbooks. You will be evaluated on this directly in the interview process, and strength here can outweigh gaps elsewhere in your background. Four Spikes Software engineering. You ship production systems and are comfortable dropped into an unfamiliar codebase or a customer environment with a deadline. Backend and systems depth, strong Python plus at least one systems language, and fluency with AI-assisted and agentic engineering as a core part of how you build. Machine learning. You take open models and make them better on a customer's task: SFT, LoRA and other parameter-efficient methods, reinforcement learning (RLHF, RLVR), distillation. Just as important, you design evaluations that reflect the real task and let them drive training decisions, and you know when fine-tuning is not the answer. Infrastructure and performance. You know your GPUs: memory bandwidth, kernels, parallelism, what utilization numbers actually mean. Serving and inference optimization: quantization, speculative decoding, batching, KV cache behavior, latency vs throughput tradeoffs, multi-GPU and multi-node serving, capacity planning. You can take a deployment that works and make it fast and economical, and reason about where the bottleneck is before touching a profiler. Customer engagement. You want to be in the room. The point of this role is creating specialized intelligence for each customer: the best model for their task, their data, their constraints. That takes real interest in the customer's problem, not just the technical one. Exceptional here looks like founder energy with customers; the floor is genuine appetite to embed, explain, and own outcomes with them. Key Responsibilities Own Engagements: Take customer deployments from scoping through production, as the single accountable technical owner. Embed: Work directly inside customer teams; understand their domain, data, and constraints well enough to make decisions they trust. Train and Tune: Run fine-tuning and post-training work where the engagement needs it, from data to evaluation to a model serving in production. Optimize: Drive serving performance and cost on Fireworks: model choice, deployment shape, and inference optimization. Scope Honestly: Assess what is achievable before we commit, and inherit what you scope. Product Signal: Feed what customers need back to product and engineering, with enough precision to be actionable. Minimum Qualifications Spikes in two or all three areas. For the ML spike: formal training (PhD, PhD in progress, or a strong MSc) and experience post-training LLMs specifically. For the infrastructure spike: experience with GPU infrastructure, distributed serving, or inference engines. Founder or founding engineer experience. Experience in a startup or fast-paced environment. Why Fireworks? Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving. Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally. Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results. Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation. Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators.

items.desc: Fusionality is building the measurement, simulation, and control stack for the fusion energy reactors of the future. Spun out of EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center and backed by top investors, our technology enables reliable operation, real-time monitoring, and analysis of high-temperature plasmas in fusion devices. We are founded by world-class experts at the intersection of fusion physics, advanced control, and AI (ex-Google DeepMind, EPFL). We are assembling a founding engineering team in Lausanne to build our core technology platform. We are looking for a Data / Machine Learning Engineer to join our team. This job is for you if you like turning large, messy, heterogeneous experimental data into clean, labelled, trustworthy datasets. You have done this with scientific or industrial sensor data. Familiarity with fusion is a plus but not a strict requirement. Responsibilities Build, maintain and run pipelines that bring experimental fusion data into high quality, consistent, documented, versioned datasets. Develop ML-assisted labelling and event detection (e.g. disruptions, MHD activity, diagnostic faults), using weak supervision, active learning and anomaly detection. Own data quality and provisioning: provenance, calibration metadata, automated validation. Manage and facilitate access for the rest of the team. Work with physicists validating the datasets & labels. Work with our computational scientists and control engineers, who build models and controllers on these datasets, and with customers to understand and integrate their data. Requirements Hands-on experience building data pipelines for large scientific or industrial time-series data formats (e.g. HDF5, Parquet, Zarr). Proficiency in designing, querying and optimizing SQL and noSQL database systems and familiarity with Time Series databases such as TimescaleDB, InfluxDB. Experience in applying ML techniques to time series in Python (PyTorch or JAX): sequence models, anomaly and event detection, semi- or weakly-supervised labelling. Solid software engineering habits: testing, reproducibility, data versioning are second nature to you. Evidence of independent work at the highest level: a PhD thesis and/or published code that is used by others, or an industry project you owned. You should be comfortable designing data architectures independently from day 1. The following are an advantage but not strictly required: Human-in-the-loop labelling tools and workflows. Pipeline Orchestration (e.g. Dagster, Airflow, Prefect) and data versioning (e.g. DVC, lakeFS). Data from large physics experiments: fusion, accelerators, astronomy, or exposure to fusion data systems (MDSplus, IMAS). What we offer Play a key role at a dynamic, fast-growing startup, shaping the technical solutions and products from the ground up. Build cutting edge technology to monitor and control plasmas in real fusion devices, working side-by-side with leading plasma and control experts. Great working conditions, located in Lausanne, Switzerland, a city and country known for its high quality of life. Competitive salary and equity compensation, matched to level of seniority, and benefits including immigration assistance.

items.desc: Over Terramira Terramira is een nieuwe kracht in Earth Intelligence, ontstaan uit de gecombineerde expertise van NEO, eLEAF en 52impact. Wij zetten satelliet- en sensordata om in bruikbare informatie voor uitdagingen als klimaatverandering, waterschaarste, biodiversiteit en infrastructuur. Onze klanten – van agro-ondernemingen en waterautoriteiten tot internationale organisaties en overheden – hebben behoefte aan inzichten die betere beslissingen mogelijk maken. Dat is precies wat wij leveren. Bij Terramira geloven we dat impact begint met helder zien. We maken impact zichtbaar. En we brengen deze binnen bereik. Wij zijn een groeiende organisatie met korte lijnen, een open cultuur en een oprechte drive om werk te doen dat ertoe doet. Over de functie Als AI Data Scientist ontwikkel je AI-modellen die geospatiale data omzetten in bruikbare intelligence. Je werkt met satelliet- en luchtbeelden, tijdreeksen en sensordata om veranderingen in water, natuur, landbouw en infrastructuur zichtbaar en meetbaar te maken. Je combineert diepgaande kennis van machine learning met gevoel voor de geospatiale en ruimtelijke context van onze data — en zorgt dat de uitkomsten betrouwbaar zijn, waar en wanneer ze ook worden toegepast. Wat ga je doen? Je traint en evalueert machine-learning- en deep-learning-modellen, en past computer vision toe op satelliet- en luchtbeelden om veranderingen in water, natuur, landbouw en infrastructuur zichtbaar te maken. Daarnaast ontwikkel je time-series- en spatiotemporele modellen en werk je met Earth Observation foundation models, die je waar nodig fine-tuned voor onze specifieke toepassingen. Concreet houdt dat onder andere in dat je: Veranderingen detecteert in water, natuur, landbouw of infrastructuur; Natuurlijke-taalvragen vertaalt naar concrete ruimtelijke en temporele analyses; Modelresultaten valideert over verschillende locaties, seizoenen en databronnen, zodat klanten kunnen vertrouwen op wat we opleveren. Wat zoeken we? Je hebt ruime ervaring met machine learning, deep learning en computer vision, en weet je weg met time-series- en spatiotemporele modellering. Je hebt eerder gewerkt met foundation models, model training, fine-tuning en model-evaluatie, en je hebt affiniteit met uncertainty estimation en explainable AI, zodat je resultaten niet alleen accuraat maar ook uitlegbaar zijn. Daarnaast breng je mee: Kennis van remote sensing, GIS, raster- en vectordata, satellietbeelden, SAR, multispectrale data en/of LiDAR; Begrip van coördinatensystemen en spatial statistics; Goede Python-vaardigheden en ervaring met databases zoals PostgreSQL; Ervaring met reproduceerbare analyses, feature engineering, data preparation, experiment tracking en model pipelines. From renewable energy infrastructure and AI systems to robotics and enterprise applications, we connect the technologies that power Europe's intelligent future. Founded in 2014, KIEFER has delivered 600MW+ of energy projects and is now developing sovereign AI infrastructure, enterprise AI products and physical AI systems for Greece and Southeast Europe. About The Role We are looking for an ML Engineer to develop capabilities that work on physical robots. You will take ideas from model and data experiments through robotics integration and evaluation on real hardware. Our fleet includes Unitree Go2, G1, H1, and B2 robots using NVIDIA Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor compute. Current areas of focus include navigation, learned policies, vision-language-action models, and robotics data. What You Will Do Develop, train, adapt, and evaluate models for navigation, perception, planning, and robot behavior. Apply suitable methods such as imitation learning, reinforcement learning, or vision-language-action approaches. Build data collection and evaluation pipelines using real-world and simulated robotics data. Integrate models with robotics software, sensors, actuators, and control systems. Test on physical robots, measuring task success, sim-to-real performance, on-device latency, and failure modes. Work with ML, Engineering, robotics specialists, and Product to improve reliability and move prototypes toward repeatable deployment. What You Will Need 3+ years of relevant ML or robotics engineering experience, or equivalent impact taking research into real-world systems. Hands-on experience developing and evaluating ML-enabled systems on physical robots. Strong Python and production software engineering skills, including experience with ROS or a comparable robotics framework. A strong ML background in robot learning, perception, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, multimodal models, or a related area. Experience with robotics data, simulation, experiment design, and evaluation on real hardware. Practical understanding of sensors, actuators, control loops, latency, and hardware debugging. Nice to have Vision-language-action models, multimodal foundation models, or generative world models. Experience with humanoids, mobile or dexterous manipulation, or other complex robotic platforms. Sim-to-real transfer, teleoperation, human demonstration data, or large-scale robotics data collection. C++, low-level control, tactile or force sensing, or real-time systems. What Is There For You Compensation: Competitive package aligned with talent benchmarks. Impact: Hands-on work shaping AI capabilities for Kiefer Tech’s products and real-world applications. AI-native environment: Real challenges across model development, evaluation, and production AI systems. Culture: Engineering-first, high autonomy, low bureaucracy, and space to shape meaningful AI products.

items.desc: Rejoignez les activités Advanced Computing d’ANEO ANEO est un cabinet de conseil tech-first qui accompagne depuis plus de vingt ans des entreprises du CAC 40, des ETI et des start-up dans leurs transformations technologiques et organisationnelles. Notre singularité : intervenir à la croisée du calcul scientifique, du software, du HPC, du cloud, de l’IA et des systèmes distribués. Cette annonce ne correspond pas à un poste unique. Elle constitue une porte d’entrée vers les activités Advanced Computing d’ANEO, pour des profils techniques aux parcours et aux niveaux d’expérience variés. Nos équipes conçoivent, modernisent et industrialisent des plateformes et des applications de calcul complexes. Nous intervenons de la compréhension du besoin jusqu’au passage à l’échelle : architecture, optimisation, migration vers le cloud, mise en production et exploitation de workloads critiques. Cette expertise se prolonge avec ArmoniK, notre orchestrateur open source de calcul distribué, conçu pour exécuter des workloads intensifs dans des environnements on-premise, cloud et hybrides. Quelques projets représentatifs Plateformes IA hybrides et multi-GPU : Concevoir et industrialiser une plateforme capable de gérer l’entraînement distribué de modèles sur plusieurs GPU, avec des enjeux de performance, de scalabilité, de robustesse et de mise en production. Migration et bursting HPC vers le cloud : Faire évoluer une plateforme de calcul afin d’absorber des pics de charge dans le cloud, tout en maîtrisant les coûts, la résilience et l’exploitation des workloads. Optimisation de codes scientifiques : Améliorer les performances de codes de calcul sur CPU et GPU dans des environnements massivement parallèles, en travaillant sur le profilage, la parallélisation et l’utilisation des accélérateurs. Calcul distribué et ArmoniK : Contribuer au développement d’ArmoniK et à l’orchestration de workloads intensifs entre environnements on-premise, cloud public, cloud souverain et multi-cloud. Ces projets illustrent la diversité des sujets traités chez ANEO : développement scientifique, architecture, infrastructure, cloud, systèmes distribués, plateformes IA et passage à l’échelle. Selon les missions, vous pourrez travailler avec des chercheurs, des développeurs, des équipes data science, des experts infrastructure et cloud, des métiers et des décideurs. Si vous souhaitez en savoir plus, c’est ici . Les profils que nous souhaitons rencontrer Nous sommes ouverts à des parcours variés : jeunes docteurs et post-doctorants souhaitant appliquer leur expertise à des problématiques industrielles ; ingénieurs et développeurs scientifiques ; spécialistes du HPC, du GPU, du cloud ou des infrastructures de calcul ; experts des plateformes IA et des systèmes distribués ; architectes et leaders techniques capables de porter des choix structurants. Vous n’avez pas besoin de maîtriser l’ensemble de ces domaines. Nous recherchons avant tout une expertise ou un potentiel technique réel, de la curiosité et l’envie de comprendre des systèmes complexes dans leur globalité. Votre périmètre, votre niveau d’autonomie et vos responsabilités seront définis en fonction de votre expérience, de vos aspirations et des opportunités identifiées. Ce qui fera la différence Au-delà de votre expertise technique, nous recherchons des personnes capables de comprendre avant de proposer, d’expliquer clairement leurs choix et de construire avec les équipes et les clients. Une expérience du conseil est un plus, pas un prérequis. Un anglais professionnel est attendu. La maîtrise parfaite du français n’est pas indispensable à votre arrivée, dès lors que la communication est fluide. Informations pratiques Contrat : CDI Localisation : Boulogne-Billancourt Organisation du travail : hybride Prise de poste : à partir de 2027 Les candidatures sont étudiées tout au long de l’année. Certaines opportunités correspondent à des besoins immédiats ; d’autres peuvent se construire en fonction de votre expertise, de votre projet professionnel et de votre disponibilité. Vous terminez une thèse, un post-doctorat ou un projet structurant ? Nous pouvons commencer à échanger dès maintenant. Parcours de recrutement Le parcours est adapté à votre niveau d’expérience et au type de contribution envisagé. Il comprend généralement : un premier échange avec l’équipe recrutement ; une rencontre technique avec un membre de la communauté Advanced Computing ; un échange de projection sur votre parcours et votre place chez ANEO. Chez ANEO, chacun et chacune a sa place. Nous recrutons dans le respect de l’égalité des chances.

items.desc: Het handmatig invullen van pensioenformulieren is niet alleen foutgevoelig, maar ook inefficiënt. In deze opdracht ga je een mobiele app ontwikkelen die gegevens uit documenten automatisch scant en invoert met behulp van multimodale AI. Je werkt een Proof of Concept uit waarin je de functionaliteit van de app en de bescherming van persoonsgegevens demonstreert. Hierbij leg je de nadruk op het ontwikkelen van een gebruiksvriendelijke en privacy vriendelijke oplossing. Deze afstudeeropdracht maakt onderdeel uit van het project ‘Van GRIJSpensioen naar GROENpensioen’. Met dit project geven we de pensioenwereld een digitale boost door het optimaliseren van digitale infrastructuren en processen. Zo maken we pensioenfondsen efficiënter en duurzamer, met beter datamanagement, sterke privacybescherming en gepersonaliseerde dienstverlening. Het handmatig overnemen van gegevens uit identiteitsdocumenten, werkgeversverklaringen en financiële overzichten naar pensioenformulieren is niet alleen monotoon en saai, maar ook foutgevoelig en inefficiënt. Fouten kunnen leiden tot onjuiste pensioenopbouw en -uitkeringen, met mogelijk aanzienlijke financiële gevolgen voor de betrokkenen. Daarnaast is het essentieel om de privacy van pensioengegevens te waarborgen, aangezien deze gevoelige financiële en persoonlijke informatie bevatten die beschermd moet worden tegen ongeautoriseerde toegang en datalekken. De opdracht Ontwikkel een mobiele applicatie die gebruikmaakt van multimodale AI om het invullen van pensioenformulieren te automatiseren. Dit doe je door documenten te scannen met de camera van een smartphone en de relevante informatie automatisch in het formulier te plaatsen. De applicatie moet zowel gebruiksvriendelijk als privacy vriendelijk zijn, met een sterke focus op de beveiliging van persoonsgegevens. Jouw taak is om een Proof of Concept te ontwikkelen dat niet alleen de functionaliteit demonstreert, maar ook hoe de applicatie de privacy van de gebruiker waarborgt. Over Info Support Info Support is specialist in maatwerksoftware, data/AI solutions, beheer en trainingen en actief in de sectoren Finance, Industry, Agriculture, Food & Retail, Mobility & Public en Healthcare. Wij bieden solide en innovatieve oplossingen voor complexe en bedrijfkritische softwarevraagstukken. Onze hoofdkantoren zijn gevestigd in Veenendaal (NL) en Mechelen (BE). Op dit moment zijn er circa 500 medewerkers bij Info Support in dienst. De werkwijze van Info Support kenmerkt zich door een aantal kernwaarden: soliditeit, integriteit, vakmanschap en passie. Deze kernwaarden zijn verweven in ons werk en de manier waarop we met elkaar omgaan. Om te zorgen dat alle medewerkers altijd op de hoogte kunnen zijn van de nieuwste ontwikkelingen beschikt Info Support over een inhouse IT Academy waar graag wordt voldaan aan de honger naar meer of andere kennis en vaardigheden. Om deze opdracht te kunnen doen is B2-taalvaardigheid in het Nederlands vereist.

Strong communication skills and the ability to explain quantitative results clearly to both technical and business stakeholders. The ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative trading environment. Additional Assets The following would be considered an advantage: Previous exposure to energy, commodities or financial markets. Understanding of European power markets, power generation or energy supply mechanisms. Experience working with trading signals, forecasting models or optimization problems. You will bridge systems operations and academic inquiry: keep the infrastructure performant and reliable through daily operations while contributing to research on cloud architectures, virtualization, AI-driven operations (AIOps) and software execution environments. You will use operational challenges to inform research, and hands-on experiments and prototypes to evaluate new system concepts. The role calls for practical engineering, debugging and active systems management alongside scientific curiosity—not theory alone.
 What You Will Do 
• Operate and evolve the OpenStack cloud and compute environment used by Ericsson and academic researchers.
• Troubleshoot complex distributed systems, investigate root causes, and help ensure reliable services.
• Design, prototype and evaluate system concepts, software execution environments, performance and reliability.
• Contribute to and drive research studies in compute systems, cloud architectures, virtualization and AIOps, including collaboration on scientific publications.
• Automate repetitive tasks, improve workflows and scale infrastructure; work across operations, engineering and research to turn practical challenges into real-world solutions.
 The Skills You Bring 
• A research-oriented degree, such as a Ph.D., or equivalent experience in a research-intensive role.
• Demonstrated research contribution in compute, cloud virtualization or software systems, for example through publications, patents, technical reports or working prototypes.
• Hands-on Linux administration and systems engineering experience, with a solid understanding of cloud technologies, Kubernetes, data-center operations and networking fundamentals.
• Experience with containers (Docker or Podman) and orchestration with Kubernetes.
• Ability to research, instrument and maintain compute environments with AI capabilities supporting workflows, monitoring and intelligent observability.
• A hands-on “doer” mindset; analytical and scientific curiosity; strong troubleshooting and root-cause analysis; and a drive to automate and improve workflows.
• Strong collaboration skills across operational, engineering and research teams.
• It is an advantage to bring or develop skills in Ansible, Terraform or Helm; advanced OpenStack operations; HPC or accelerators (GPUs, DPUs or FPGAs); and research collaboration or patenting processes.

items.title: Researcher Sorting Technologies & AI for Circular Plastics
items.card: responsibilities Design, execute and optimize experiments using NIR-HSI, RGB imaging, 3D sensing and automated sorting systems. Develop and validate machine learning, chemometric and data analytics models for material classification and process optimization. Analyze complex datasets and translate findings into practical solutions for industry. Develop and improve data acquisition, processing and visualization tools.
items.desc: We are looking for a driven and innovative researcher with expertise in plastics recycling and sorting technologies, combined with strong capabilities in AI, machine learning, optical sensing and data-driven process optimization. NTCP is a dynamic, forward‑thinking applied research organisation leading the way in circular plastics. From our bold and colourful facility in Heerenveen, the Netherlands, we run unique industrial-scale setups that support independent R&D across the full plastics lifecycle – from product characteristics and post‑consumer collection to sorting, washing, mechanical and chemical recycling, and finally new product creation. We hold a strong position in the plastics recycling landscape, backed by a broad network of partners spanning waste management, FMCG brands, universities, NGOs, technology providers, polymer and chemical producers, water‑treatment specialists, and government bodies. Our strength lies in our rare combination of sensor‑equipped industrial‑scale sorting and washing lines, pilot setups for decontamination, pyrolysis and extrusion, a dedicated laboratory, and - most importantly - a team of around 25 experts. We are looking for a driven and innovative researcher with expertise in plastics recycling and sorting technologies, combined with strong capabilities in AI, machine learning, optical sensing and data-driven process optimization. Researcher Sorting Technologies & AI for Circular Plastics Key responsibilities Design, execute and optimize experiments using NIR-HSI, RGB imaging, 3D sensing and automated sorting systems. Develop and validate machine learning, chemometric and data analytics models for material classification and process optimization. Analyze complex datasets and translate findings into practical solutions for industry. Develop and improve data acquisition, processing and visualization tools. Execute and lead R&D projects in sorting technologies, optical sensors and AI-driven material identification. Present results to customers, partners and scientific audiences. Identify new research opportunities and contribute to proposals and innovation projects. What you bring BSc or MSc degree in Engineering, Materials Science, Experimental Physics, or a related field, with at least 2-3 years of relevant industrial R&D experience. Hands-on experience with optical sensing technologies (NIR-HSI, RGB vision and/or 3D imaging systems), and/or machine learning, chemometric and computer vision applications (e.g. YOLO, PLS-DA). Strong proficiency in Python programming and data analytics, with the ability to develop data-driven insights and solutions for industrial applications. Experience with software development, data platforms, sensor data processing and visualization tools is a plus. Ability to understand industrial challenges and translate them into research questions, project plans and innovative solutions. Strong passion for and affinity with plastics recycling and circular economy. Excellent communication skills in English (written and spoken); knowledge of Dutch is an advantage but not required. Eligibility to work in the Netherlands. What we offer We offer the opportunity to work in a creative and innovative environment where your work makes a real impact on the circular use of resources. You will work on innovative national and international R&D projects together with leading industrial and academic partners. Depending on project objectives, you will have opportunities to publish results and present your work at conferences, workshops and industry events. NTCP is committed to fostering an inclusive working environment where everyone has equal opportunities to grow, develop, and be themselves. Benefits Salary aligned with the responsibilities of the role and the candidate’s level of expertise A one-year contract, with outlook on a permanent position 25 leave days plus national holidays with a possibility to purchase 5 additional days Commuter allowance. Interested? Please apply by sending your CV and motivation letter (in English) to Martine Brandsma (Director at NTCP): mbrandsma@ntcp.nl and Marjon Claes ( mclaes@ntcp.nl ). For further information, feel free to contact Martine directly.

items.desc: Phasecraft is the quantum algorithms company. We are building the mathematical foundations for quantum computing applications that solve real-world problems. Founded in 2019 by Toby Cubitt, Ashley Montanaro and John Morton, we are based in London and Bristol in the UK and opened an office in Washington DC in 2024, led by Steve Flammia. In 2025 we completed a $34m Series B funding round co-led by Plural, existing investor Playground Global, and Novo Holdings’ Quantum Fund in its first direct quantum software investment. Phasecraft’s unprecedented access to today’s best quantum computers – through partnerships with Google, IBM, Quantinuum and QuEra – provides us with unique opportunities to develop foundational IP, inform the development of next-generation quantum hardware, and accelerate commercialization of high-value breakthroughs. We are looking to hire a Quantum Algorithms Scientist to join our team, in a role focusing on implementing and executing experiments on cutting-edge quantum computing hardware. The ideal candidate will have experience in implementing quantum algorithms on real quantum hardware, in addition to exposure to the theory of quantum algorithms for gate-model quantum computers or related topics in quantum computing theory, quantum information theory, or related areas of quantum theory. Their work will contribute to Phasecraft’s goal of developing quantum algorithms for near-term quantum computers and may encompass topics such as algorithm optimization and design, quantum error-correction, resource analysis, error mitigation, and hardware benchmarking. The role will involve both theoretical research and practical implementation, leveraging access to quantum hardware platforms. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge quantum research while applying quantum algorithms on real devices, helping to push the boundaries of what is possible with near-term quantum computing. Requirements Job Description Develop and implement quantum algorithms on state-of-the-art quantum hardware platforms, optimizing performance and resource usage. Undertake both theoretical and applied research on near-term quantum computing algorithms, applications, and enabling technologies. Contribute to research on error mitigation, circuit optimization, and benchmarking techniques for quantum hardware. Help to author publications, presentations, patent applications, and similar research outputs. Work collaboratively in a small international team made up of full-time staff and affiliated PhD students. Contribute to the broader growth and success of Phasecraft through research, development, and technical leadership. Essential Criteria Expertise in quantum algorithms and quantum information theory with a strong foundation in quantum computing. PhD (or soon to receive one) in quantum information, quantum computation, computer science, physics, or a closely related field. Extensive experience in implementing quantum algorithms on quantum hardware. Strong understanding of quantum circuit design, compilation, and optimization techniques. Ability to work independently on research projects while contributing to a collaborative team environment. Strong publication track record in relevant disciplines. Proficiency in quantum programming languages such as Qiskit, Cirq, PennyLane, or similar. Flexibility to work across different aspects of quantum software, algorithms, and underpinning theory. Desirable Criteria Experience in developing and/or benchmarking error mitigation techniques for quantum algorithms. Knowledge of classical simulation methods for quantum circuits and hybrid quantum-classical approaches. Strong software development skills, including experience with Python, C++, or other programming languages used in quantum computing. Experience working with industrial quantum hardware providers or in industry-academic collaborations. Enthusiasm for learning, research, and translating theoretical quantum computing advances into practical applications. Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present complex concepts to diverse audiences. The closing date for applications is 8 November 2026.

items.desc: Imagine working with cutting-edge machine learning models, crunching high frequency data sets and sparring with exceptional and fun colleagues, all while taking part in scaling our business even further. Does this sound highly appealing to you? Then you might be our new Machine Learning Researcher at Alipes. At Alipes, we have been the market leader in automating the financial markets since we started back in 2008, shaping a fully automatic natural language processing system for reading and interpreting financial news. To accomplish our mission of being the best at what we do, we understand the importance of elevating our predictive modeling standards to the highest levels. Your work will involve leading the efforts in creating a world class modeling workflow, enabling the team to seamlessly turn massive data sets of financial information into mathematical models that accurately predict movements in the financial markets. In doing so, you will get a chance to tackle a variety of software infrastructure challenges, such as: Development and optimization of calibration and benchmarking frameworks Building out and implementing best practices for data preparation and dataset generation pipelines Prototyping and releasing novel predictive architectures, especially with respect to time-series models. You will get instant validation of your work and experience short feedback cycles, where going from inception to deployment can be a matter of hours. There will be no red tape to cut and no sales people to consult. About the team All of this will happen in an informal atmosphere where technical discussions are valued, and you are encouraged to take ownership of, and pride in, your work. You will impact the direction of the team, prioritize your work and choose the tools that get the job done. We are a tight-knit modeling team with fourteen passionate quantitative researchers covering 6 nationalities – eleven PhD’s and three MSc’s with expertise in statistical analysis, mathematical modeling and machine learning. We enjoy collaboration and are always willing to lend a helping hand. We are working alongside two other teams of software developers and traders that implement and conceive the mathematical models together with us. What makes this constellation work great is that all of the individual team members write code and understand that a seemingly trivial change can actually require a lot of work, and vice versa. About you Fluency within mathematics and statistics. Experience working with the full Machine Learning stack from data generation through model calibration and real-life validation and monitoring. Programming experience with Python, in particular data-wrangling and numerical programming. Proficiency with computer science fundamentals. A scientific and inquisitive mind. Nice to have Experience working with ‘out-of-core’ datasets. Experience working with tools like PyTorch, Tensorflow, XGBoost and/or Catboost. Programming experience with languages like C# and C/C++. PhD or MSc degree in engineering, physics, computer science, mathematics or economics. What we can offer you Competitive benefits, including pension, health insurance, and 30 days of vacation. A modern, harbour front office in Copenhagen (Nordhavn) with a flexible hybrid work model. A flat hierarchy with high levels of trust, autonomy, and freedom to make decisions. A valued role with unique responsibilities and plenty of room for creativity. Fast feedback and recognition of your contributions in a high-growth company. Strong team spirit - successes are celebrated with company events and trips. Practicalities To apply, please send us your CV and, in lieu of providing a cover letter, concisely answer the questions on the application. If your profile looks like a good match, we will get in touch to coordinate an online technical test as a first step in the interview process. Should you have questions about the role that you would like clarified before applying, you're welcome to send an email to quant_jobs@alipescapital.com. Please note that applications should not be sent to the email address but rather via the job link.

This position is hired in Zipf, Austia in hybrid work (min. 3 days per week in office). 
 Job Description 
 AI Data Engineer (f/m/d) 
 As AI Data Engineer in GE HealthCare's Advanced Imaging Solutions business, you will develop reusable tools, operate shared data infrastructure, and evaluate platforms for ultrasound teams worldwide.
 GE HealthCare develops medical technology, pharmaceutical diagnostics, and digital solutions that help clinicians make informed decisions and improve patient outcomes. With more than a century of healthcare experience, we pursue a world where healthcare has no limits and embrace respect, transparency, integrity, and diversity.
 Job Description 
 Working with local teams and infrastructure owners, you will turn requirements into tested solutions and help teams adopt and operate common tools.
 In this role you will:
 Work with AI technical leaders to translate cross-team requirements, reference architectures, and priorities into working solutions and operational procedures.
 Design and run reproducible experiments, proofs of concept, and benchmarks on third-party and internal data management and AI development platforms using representative ultrasound team workflows.
 Assess functional fit, interoperability, performance, scalability, usability, integration effort, and operating cost against agreed requirements. Document methods, results, limitations, and recommendations to inform platform selection.
 Collaborate with individual teams to extend internally developed tools for use across the ultrasound organization. Refactor team-specific assumptions into configurable modules and standardize interfaces to increase reuse.
 Develop and maintain shared libraries, services, and connectors, with automated tests, versioned packages, and deployment workflows that make adoption and maintenance easier for other teams.
 Build and operate data ingestion, transformation, and validation pipelines supporting data curation, annotation, dataset preparation, and AI development.
 Carry out day-to-day operation of agreed shared tools and environments, including configuration, updates, job monitoring, troubleshooting, and performance tuning, in coordination with platform owners.
 Support teams with platform onboarding, tool integration, and data or workflow migrations, and provide practical feedback on gaps in shared infrastructure.
 Implement data quality checks, logging, and traceability, and automate approved data access, de-identification, and retention workflows with guidance from the responsible specialists.
 Investigate pipeline and platform failures, reproduce issues, and work with internal platform teams or external vendors to resolve root causes and prevent recurrence.
 Create user guides, integration examples, and operational runbooks; provide training and technical support so teams can adopt, operate, and contribute to shared tools.
 Qualifications

 Master's degree in computer science, data engineering, software engineering, information systems, AI, or a related technical field.
 Hands-on experience developing and operating data pipelines, shared software tools, or AI development infrastructure.
 Practical knowledge of cloud environments, containers, Linux, and data workflow orchestration.
 Strong programming skills in Python and SQL, with experience designing APIs, integrating services, and working with structured and unstructured data.
 Experience with Git, automated testing, code review, continuous integration and delivery, and maintainable software packaging.
 Ability to design controlled technical experiments, benchmark platforms, and communicate results and trade-offs clearly.
 Understanding of AI data workflows, including curation, annotation, dataset versioning, and training and validation data preparation.
 Awareness of security, privacy, and traceability requirements when handling healthcare data.
 Fluent English and the ability to collaborate with globally distributed engineering, data science, and infrastructure teams.

 PhD in computer science, data engineering, software engineering, information systems, AI, or a related technical field
 Experience with medical imaging or ultrasound data and healthcare data formats.

 Familiarity with data catalogs, annotation tools, experiment tracking, model registries, and AI development platforms.

items.desc:
Join our Team
 About the opportunity 
Join Ericsson Research and help shape the future of connectivity. AI is central to Ericsson’s 6G vision, enabling intelligent, sustainable, and secure networks for people and industries in the 2030s and beyond. Our work combines machine learning, advanced reasoning, and real network systems, with access to live network data and opportunities to influence global standards and technologies used worldwide. 
This early-career role suits a recent master’s graduate or someone with a few years of experience in AI/ML. You’ll take on meaningful research from day one, collaborate with global, cross-disciplinary teams, and learn from experienced mentors. A telecom degree or prior radio expertise isn’t required: you can build domain knowledge through hands-on work with radio specialists. We value diverse perspectives and offer an inclusive environment, flexible ways of working, wellbeing support, benefits, and growth opportunities. You don’t need to meet every preferred qualification; curiosity and motivation matter. 
 What you will do 
• Research, design, and evaluate AI/ML concepts for future radio access networks and AI-native systems, including autonomous, large-scale telecom networks. 
• Develop algorithms, models, and simulation frameworks. Explore AI applications in radio access networks. 
• Use modern AI-assisted development tools to prototype and iterate quickly. 
• Collaborate with experts in radio systems, networking, and hardware, connecting research ideas with practical needs such as performance, scalability, robustness, automation and energy efficiency. 
• Turn research into prototypes, publications, patents, and contributions to future standards. Share findings, build your research profile, and keep learning with support from senior researchers. 
 Skills you bring 
• An MSc in AI, data science, computer science, engineering physics, robotics, or a closely related field is preferred. Candidates with an MSc and strong AI research experience are also encouraged to apply. 
• A strong foundation in modern AI, such as deep, reinforcement, or distributed learning; generative AI; probabilistic modelling; stochastic optimization; or graph-based methods. 
• Python programming skills and familiarity with ML frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow. 
• Some experience designing, training, or validating ML-driven systems through studies, internships, or personal projects. Familiarity with simulation-based evaluation is valuable. 
• Interest in AI coding assistants and openness to new tools. Experience with Docker or Kubernetes is a plus. 
• Interest in telecommunications, networking, or signal processing. Telecom expertise can be learned on the job. 
• A curious, self-directed approach: you generate and test ideas, learn independently, ask questions, seek expert input, and work through uncertainty. You bring analytical problem-solving, ownership, and collaborative skills, and can communicate clearly, including explaining AI concepts to non-specialists.

items.desc: Fusionality is building the measurement, simulation, and control stack for the fusion energy reactors of the future. Spun out of EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center and backed by top investors, our technology enables reliable operation, real-time monitoring, and analysis of high-temperature plasmas in fusion devices. We are founded by world-class experts at the intersection of fusion physics, advanced control, and AI (ex-Google DeepMind, EPFL). We are assembling a founding engineering team in Lausanne to build our core technology platform. We are looking for a Computational Scientist specialized in Scientific Machine Learning (SciML) to join our team. This job is for you if you know how to write numerical solvers that are fast, correct and differentiable end to end, and want to see them run against real plasma data and inside real control systems. We are looking for a PhD-level or senior computational researcher for this role. Responsibilities Design, implement and validate differentiable solvers in JAX for plasma physics problems such as free-boundary equilibrium, transport and state estimation. Make them robust and fast enough for production use via advanced numerical techniques for differential equation time stepping, as well as optimization of GPU/TPU performance. Using automatic differentiation for model calibration against experimental data, parameter estimation and controller design and optimization, working with our data and control engineers. Code ownership: quality, testing, verification against reference solutions, packaging and documentation. Requirements Substantial code written in a differentiable framework. Our stack is in JAX, Julia or PyTorch experts are very welcome if they’re happy to switch. Strong background in numerical methods for ODEs and PDEs: discretisation, stiff and implicit solvers, nonlinear and sparse linear solvers. Demonstrated ability to operate at the frontier of SciML, Universal Differential Equations, Neural ODEs, and other emerging hybrid data-driven/mechanistic paradigms. Evidence of independent work at the highest level: a PhD or thesis, published code that is used by others, or an industry project you owned. Experience in the following fields an advantage but not strictly required: The JAX ecosystem: Diffrax, Equinox, Optax, Lineax. Plasma, fluid, electromagnetic, or other multiphysics simulation. Having led the design of a scientific codebase used by others. What we offer Play a key role at a dynamic, fast-growing startup, shaping the technical solutions and products from the ground up. Build cutting-edge technology to monitor and control plasmas in real fusion devices, working side-by-side with leading plasma and control experts. Great working conditions, located in Lausanne, Switzerland, a city and country known for its high quality of life. Competitive salary and equity compensation and benefits including immigration assistance.

items.desc: Your Impact at LILA We're building a talent-dense, high-agency AI safety team at Lila that will engage all core teams within the organization (science, model training, lab integration, etc.), to identify and mitigate risks from scientific superintelligence while retaining the core scientific discovery capabilities of the stack. The initial focus of this team will be to build and implement a bespoke safety strategy for Lila, tailored to its specific goals and deployment strategies. This will involve technical safety strategy development, broader ecosystem engagement, safety-focused evaluations, safety systems to mitigate risks, and a research agenda that explores longer-term needs such as oversight of superintelligent scientific systems. As scientific AI systems become more capable and autonomous, their safety assessment and safeguards must develop alongside them. At Lila Sciences, you will help build the research methods and tools that make this possible, so that more and more decision-enablers can be automated safely. This will move us closer to the vision of a safety and security apparatus that is robust to a fully autonomous scientific engine. Your initial focus will be misuse: developing flexible and automated red-teaming approaches that test safety-relevant scientific capabilities and the robustness of safeguards. You will also contribute to safety automation beyond red teaming, helping the team evaluate, monitor and respond to risks across increasingly autonomous scientific workflows. You will own reusable research methods and assessment tools, working with mitigation engineers who implement protective mechanisms. We welcome Research Scientists and Research Engineers; responsibilities can span or evolve between the two profiles. What You'll Be Building Develop and run capability evaluations of scientific models, agents and tool-mediated workflows (including simulated lab environments), working with domain experts to make tests scientifically meaningful. Create methods or systems that explore diverse failure modes, adapt tests as evidence emerges and support systematic investigation beyond fixed benchmarks. Build reproducible experiments and evaluation tools that capture relevant behavior, outcomes and the evidence needed to interpret findings. Measure the quality and coverage of automated assessments, including failure cases in the evaluators themselves. Develop broader safety automation, across threat model management, evidence triage, regression testing, monitoring workflows or tools that help researchers assess and respond to risks. Collaborate with risk researchers and mitigation engineers to translate findings into improved assessments and safeguards, and verify whether those changes work. What You'll Need to Succeed Strong empirical judgment, practical programming ability and experience working with modern AI systems. The ability to investigate ambiguous failures, design informative comparisons and communicate limitations clearly. An interest in scientific misuse risks and the ability to collaborate productively with domain specialists. For the Research Scientist profile: evidence of selecting valuable research questions, developing or adapting methods, and designing experiments that yield defensible conclusions. You should be able to prototype and test your ideas. For the Research Engineer profile: evidence of building reliable research software, evaluation infrastructure or agent systems that enable reproducible experiments and efficient iteration. You should be able to contribute to experimental design and interpretation. Bonus Points For Automated red teaming, adversarial testing or evaluation-method research. Scientific AI, tool-using agents, laboratory automation or other complex environments. Experience with safety monitoring, model-based evaluators or scalable experimental infrastructure. About LILA Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves. LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. Learn more at www.lila.ai. Guided by our core values of truth, trust, curiosity, grit, and velocity, we move with startup speed while tackling problems of historic importance. If this sounds like an environment you'd love to work in, even if you don't meet every qualification listed above, we encourage you to apply. We're All In Lila Sciences is committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. …

items.desc: Project Tricorder — Clinical Infrastructure for Field Operations We're looking for a hands-on engineer to build two foundations of the Tricorder product: the evaluation harness and training data pipeline behind our AI models, and a clinical knowledge base grounded in tactical combat care, SNOMED CT and ICD-10. About Project Tricorder - https://www.tricorder-systems.com/ Most healthcare technology assumes a hospital: reliable power, connectivity and a clinician at a desk. Care increasingly happens somewhere else - in the field, in transit, in remote and contested environments, and in the critical minutes before a patient reaches a ward. Tricorder builds the deployable clinical infrastructure for that world: a rugged, self-contained hardware and software platform that lets clinical teams capture, monitor and act on patient data anywhere, even when the network or the grid can't be relied on. It is a dual-use venture serving defence medical and civilian pre-hospital care. Our prototype product is already in user testing. Edge AI sits at the core: multimodal language models that turn video, sensor data and clinical notes into patient records, drive predictions and inform data-driven learnings across deployments. To trust those models in the field, we need rigorous data and evaluation - that's where you come in. What you'll do You'll own two workstreams, working day to day with the founder and the FF build team. 1. Data pipeline and evaluation harness Build the data foundations that tell us whether our models are good enough for clinical use. Data labelling: design labelling schemas and guidelines, set up tooling, and run labelling with clinical input, including quality checks and inter-annotator agreement. Data processing: build reproducible pipelines to ingest, clean, de-identify and transform multimodal data (video, sensor streams, text). Video data organisation: structure, version and catalogue video datasets so clips, annotations and metadata stay searchable and traceable. Training dataset preparation: assemble balanced, well-documented train, validation and test splits, with clear lineage from raw data to model input. Eval harness: build an automated harness that benchmarks vision-language and NLP models against clinically meaningful metrics, tracks regressions and supports build-vs-buy model decisions. 2. Clinical knowledge base Build the structured clinical knowledge base that turns unstructured input into coded, interoperable records. Database design: design the schema and stand up the data store for clinical concepts and their relationships. Clinical terminologies: ingest and map TC3, SNOMED CT, ICD-10 and related NHS standards, including cross-mappings between them. Natural language processing: extract entities and relationships from clinical text and link them to coded concepts. Document handling: parse and structure clinical documents (PDFs, notes, forms) into the database. Clinical knowledge: work with clinicians to make sure the database reflects real-world clinical reasoning and pre-hospital workflows. By the end of the first 3 months, we'd expect a working eval harness in use for model decisions, a labelled and versioned core dataset, and a first version of the knowledge base linked to the product. What we're looking for We don't expect one person to be expert in everything below. Strong candidates will be deep in one workstream and credible in the other. Must-haves Strong Python and data engineering skills, with a track record of shipping production data or ML pipelines, not just research notebooks. Hands-on experience building ML evaluation frameworks, benchmarks or test harnesses, ideally for vision, video or language models. Experience running data labelling and training-data preparation, including annotation tooling and quality control. Working knowledge of databases and data modelling. Practical NLP experience: entity extraction, entity linking or document parsing. Comfort handling sensitive data under data protection and clinical safety constraints. Pragmatism and speed: you can work with ambiguity, make good build-vs-buy calls and ship in weeks, not quarters. Nice to have Experience with SNOMED CT, ICD-10, dm+d or other NHS clinical terminologies and coding. A background in health-tech, clinical informatics or another regulated domain such as defence. Experience with video data at scale (frame sampling, temporal annotation, multimodal datasets). Familiarity with FHIR or HL7 interoperability standards. Experience working with LLMs and VLMs, including edge or on-device deployment. Early-stage startup experience, especially as a founding or early engineer. Probably not the right fit if You need detailed specs and a large team around you to be effective. You prefer pure research over building tools people use every day. items.desc: Job number ENG04085 Faculties Faculty of Engineering Departments Department of Computing Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus South Kensington Campus - On site only Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 22 Nov 2026 About the role We are looking for a motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate (PDRA/PostDoc) to join the Safety&Alignment lab at Imperial College London, led by Dr. Oana-Maria Camburu in a fully funded research role. The position is fully funded in the context of Dr. Oana-Maria Camburu’s grant on the project Detecting Unverbalized Dangerous Capabilities in Frontier Models . The project focuses on the detection of frontier model’s dangerous capabilities that are not verbalized in their Chain-of-Thoughts (CoTs). Externalized reasoning oversight is a safety paradigm focusing on monitoring the CoTs of large language models (LLMs). As frontier models learn that they are monitored, they can become incentivized to hide their dangerous capabilities from their CoTs. Moreover, as these models become increasingly capable, their obfuscation capabilities also increase, allowing them to bypass monitors. This project investigates ways to detect and defend against such emerging scenarios. The post is based in the Department of Computing at Imperial College London at the South Kensington Campus. The Department of Computing is a leading department of Computer Science in the UK and worldwide and has consistently been awarded the highest research rating. In the previous REF assessment, the Department was ranked third (1st in the Research Intensity table published by The Times Higher) and was rated as "Excellent" in the previous national assessment of teaching quality. What you would be doing We strive in publishing in top-tier conferences and journals. Some of the areas you will work on are: Designing and developing novel algorithms for detecting and defending against unverbalized dangerous capabilities in frontier models. Conducting independent and collaborative research within the group. Publishing results in top-tier conferences and journals (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, AIJ, TACL, etc). Contributing to research projects involving frontier models. Contributing to the life and development of the Safety & Alignment lab, such weekly meetings, presentations, etc. Mentoring PhD and MSc students. What we are looking for Candidates should have, or expect shortly to obtain, a PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics or a closely related discipline, or equivalent research/industrial experience. You will have practical experience within a research environment and publications in relevant and refereed journals/conferences, such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, TACL, AIJ, etc as well as experience in a broad range of techniques including model checking, monitoring, and CoT. Research experience in frontier models and in coding with deep learning libraries such as Pytorch is also essential. Please see job description for a full list of requirements. What we can offer you The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity. items.desc: RaySearch is looking for a machine learning engineer with strong experience in medical image analysis to join our ML Imaging team in Stockholm. You will develop deep learning algorithms for medical image analysis in RayStation, our radiotherapy treatment planning system, helping clinical teams deliver effective cancer treatments. RayStation is used at more than 1,000 cancer clinics in more than 50 countries. About The Role You will develop machine learning models for use in clinical practice, working on medical image segmentation, synthetic CT generation, image registration, and other medical imaging applications. Working closely with internal clinical specialists and external partner clinics, you will translate clinical needs into methods and models and evaluate their performance. You will also collaborate with regulatory and quality experts to ensure that algorithms are developed, validated, and documented in accordance with applicable medical device requirements. You will Develop and evaluate deep learning algorithms for medical imaging using Python and PyTorch. Prepare and curate clinical imaging datasets, configure and run model training, and maintain reproducible training workflows. Review relevant research and assess the suitability of methods for clinical applications. Design experiments and evaluate model performance using appropriate quantitative measures and clinical acceptance criteria. Collaborate with clinical experts and external clinics on development and validation. Contribute to the testing and documentation required for medical device software. Your profile You have strong experience in medical image analysis. You enjoy investigating problems, testing ideas, and turning promising methods into machine learning models. You take ownership of your work, can plan and carry out development independently, and know when to involve colleagues. You value collaboration, careful evaluation, and clear documentation, and are motivated by improving cancer care. Requirements A PhD or master’s degree in computer science, machine learning, engineering, mathematics, physics, or a related field. At least four years of relevant experience in machine learning or medical image analysis, gained through research or industry, including doctoral research. Extensive experience developing and evaluating deep learning models for medical image analysis. A strong understanding of deep learning, computer vision, statistics, and applied mathematics. Strong programming skills in Python and hands-on experience with PyTorch. Familiarity with software engineering practices, including version control, testing, and code reviews. Excellent spoken and written communication skills in English. Meriting Experience with 3D medical imaging, particularly CT, MR, or CBCT. Experience with one or more of medical image segmentation, image registration, or image synthesis. Experience developing and validating medical device software or other regulated software.
