items.desc: *** FOR APPLICATION please apply by emailing CV and cover letter to info@spliceor.com *** Research Scientist — RNA Therapeutics Spliceor · Babraham Research Campus, Cambridge Full time, Permanent · On site · Start: January 2027 · Closing date: November 15 th About Spliceor Spliceor is a University of Cambridge spin-out, backed by venture funding. We are building a next-generation programmable RNA technology to treat cancer and inflammatory conditions in new ways. One of the biggest challenges in building programmable RNA technologies is control. A treatment delivered to the chosen destination, can also end up in non-target tissues and cells. We build that control into the medicine itself, so it only acts inside the cells it is meant to treat, avoiding off-target effects, and enabling multi-dosing. We are a small team, where everyone inputs into experimental design, execution and interpretation. Being a start-up, we have the agility to make decisions quickly, keeping the gap between having an idea and testing it to a minimum. The role We are looking for a scientist to join the laboratory and take ownership of experimental work on our core RNA constructs. This is primarily a hands-on laboratory-based role. You will design and build vectors, run experiments in mammalian cells, and generate data that moves the programme forward. You will work closely with the rest of the team, and you will be encouraged to contribute your ideas, not just conduct experiments. What you will do Design and build gene expression constructs and RNA vectors. Run mammalian cell culture and transfection experiments. Analyse and interpret data and present it to the team. Build assays from the ground up, troubleshooting them along the way. Keep clear, reproducible records of what you did and what you found. Contribute to grant reports, patent filings and publications. The impact you can have In a startup of this size, one piece of data can change the direction of the science. This is a great opportunity to have real impact in a growing company, with personal visibility, and take on a stimulating, varied role. What we are looking for Ideally you will bring: A doctorate in RNA biology, gene expression, molecular biology, synthetic biology, or a closely related subject. Strong hands-on experience of mammalian cell culture and of the molecular biology behind gene expression studies. Skill in designing gene expression vectors, and experience of advanced molecular cloning (for example Gibson assembly or Golden Gate). A proven ability to design, run, troubleshoot and interpret your own experiments, and to keep clear records of them. Clear communication, and a genuinely collaborative way of working. Also useful, though not essential: A deep understanding of RNA biology: how RNA is processed, how stable it is, how it is translated, and how all of that is regulated. Experience of in vitro transcription of RNA. Experience of qPCR, Western blotting, and plate-based assays such as ELISA and luminescence readouts. A publication record, or an industry track record, in RNA biology or a related field. Experience of flow cytometry workflows and/or quantitative cell imaging methods. What we offer Salary and pension, with level dependent on experience A cross-functional team: you will work directly with people who have run businesses in pharma and biotech, and with people who have spent careers doing the science in industry. A supportive working environment, where you will be given all appropriate training and guidance to thrive in the role. Broad learning. You will see the commercial side of a company and understand how decisions are made as well as having the opportunity to expand your laboratory skills and experience You will be eligible to participate in our employee share option scheme Where you will work Our laboratory and offices are in the Live Labs institute space on the Babraham Research Campus, just south of Cambridge. The campus is one of the largest clusters of early-stage life science companies in the United Kingdom, with shared scientific facilities, a regular seminar programme, and a substantial research community on site. There is free parking, a regular bus service from Cambridge city centre and the railway station, and cafés and a gym on site. How to apply Send a CV and a covering letter to info@spliceor.com We read applications as they arrive, and we will close the advert once we have found the right person. Early applications are encouraged. We aim to have sent invites for interview to prospective candidates by Wednesday 4 th November. We are a small company and we are unfortunately not able to reply and give application feedback to everyone. If you have not heard from us by mid November, please assume we have not taken your application forward on this occasion. We are sorry to do it that way, and we are grateful for the time it takes to apply. Spliceor is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from every background, …

items.desc: AI/ML Engineer – Applied Research & Systems Design The Opportunity We're looking for an experienced AI/ML Engineer to help design and build a shared AI/ML platform supporting multiple engineering and research teams. This is a hands-on engineering role with a strong applied research component. You'll tackle complex technical problems, design targeted experiments and evaluate different systems and architectures to determine the most effective solutions. The focus isn't on developing new AI models, but on designing or selecting the systems and infrastructure that enable machine learning at scale. What You'll Do Translate ambiguous technical challenges into clearly defined problems, hypotheses and targeted experiments. Evaluate different systems, technologies and architectural approaches through prototyping, benchmarking and experimentation. Design scalable, reliable infrastructure supporting both traditional ML and emerging AI workloads. Work closely with engineering and research teams to understand requirements and identify shared platform needs. Turn experimental findings into technical designs and hands-on engineering projects. Assess architectural trade-offs across performance, scalability, reliability and efficiency. What We're Looking For Strong software engineering background, particularly Python and systems design. Solid understanding of traditional machine learning, including algorithms, model training, validation and evaluation. Experience designing distributed systems, ML infrastructure or large-scale data processing platforms. A scientific approach to problem-solving, with experience designing experiments, testing hypotheses and making evidence-based technical decisions. Ability to move from technical discovery and experimentation through to architecture and implementation. Strong communication skills and experience collaborating with technical stakeholders. Particularly Relevant Experience Building shared ML platforms or research infrastructure. ML experimentation, benchmarking and evaluation frameworks. Distributed computing, high-performance systems or large-scale ML workloads. Experience combining traditional ML and modern AI technologies. The ideal candidate is a strong AI/ML engineer or software engineer with deep ML knowledge, excellent systems design skills and a scientific mindset. Someone who enjoys figuring out which approach works best, why it works and how to turn that understanding into a scalable engineering solution. If interested in learning more, apply or contact James@atlanticsearch.com directly with your CV to arrange a call. Thanks, James

items.desc: Do you love turning demanding optical setups into robust hardware that others can rely on? Are you at home in the lab with lasers and optics, and comfortable working across electronics, control software, mechanics, and automation? Would you like to help build a deep-tech startup—not only by developing technology, but by turning it into products for real customers? The Institute of Physics (IoP) is looking for a hands-on Research Engineer to work with the Ultracold Strontium Gases group and its spin-off OpticsFoundry B.V. Working at the UvA Join Us! OpticsFoundry is developing technology for the robotic manufacture of compact, stable optical circuits for quantum technology and other demanding applications. Our optical circuit boards are already used in the AQuRA optical lattice clock; the next challenge is to broaden the platform to lasers, optical cavities, frequency references, and other active systems. Working at the boundary between the University of Amsterdam and OpticsFoundry, and in collaboration with the Nonlinear Nanophotonics group at the University of Twente, you will help turn advanced laboratory optics into repeatable, manufacturable products. This is an opportunity to join at an early stage, shape both the technology and the way we build it, and—if there is a strong mutual fit—progressively move from UvA into a core engineering role at OpticsFoundry over the course of the project. A good salary Your salary will be determined on the basis of your experience and seniority, in accordance with the Labour agreement. Your grading and therefore the amounts mentioned are based on full employment of 38 hours per week. 232 vacation hours We also offer parental leave, partner leave and social engagement leave. Through the Employment Conditions Menu Card, there are opportunities for even more vacation hours. Financial arrangements On top of your salary, you receive holiday allowance (8%) and a year-end bonus (8.3%). You build up a good pension with ABP. And in addition, we offer many other allowances and schemes. Career development and room for growth The UvA encourages you to continue to professionalise through training courses and open UvA lectures. Family matters Relocating to the Netherlands with your family? Find out about daycare, schooling, health insurance or employment options and support for your partner or spouse. Including the IDCN-network which provides support for your spouse through various training sessions, social activities, and networking events. All About This Vacancy This is what you will do You will take ownership of challenging engineering problems from first idea to tested hardware. In a small, fast-moving team, you will design experiments, build prototypes, measure performance, find failure modes, and iterate until a system is robust enough for production and customer use. Your work will include: designing and building compact optical circuits that incorporate gain media, piezo and motorized actuators, optical cavities, spectroscopy cells, photonic integrated circuits, and related components; developing robotic methods to place, align, bond, and integrate optical components reproducibly; building and benchmarking complete systems, such as laser sources and laser-frequency locks; designing or integrating the electronics, instrumentation, and control software needed to operate and test those systems; translating prototypes into scalable production processes, fixtures, test procedures, and clear technical documentation; and working directly with researchers and early customers to understand requirements and deliver practical, reliable hardware. The role offers substantial freedom and responsibility. You will be encouraged to propose solutions, make design decisions, and develop new technical capabilities—not simply execute a predefined research plan. What We Ask Of You We are looking for a curious, pragmatic engineer who enjoys difficult technical puzzles and wants to help grow a young deep-tech company. You do not need to match every item below. We would particularly like to hear from you if you bring: a Master's degree, PhD, or equivalent professional experience in applied physics, optical engineering, electrical engineering, mechatronics, or a related field; hands-on experience building and troubleshooting optical systems, ideally involving lasers, precision alignment, interferometry, spectroscopy, cavities, or photonic systems; enough experience with electronics, instrumentation, and control software to work effectively across discipline boundaries; an experimental mindset: you turn open-ended problems into testable ideas, learn quickly from data, and keep going when the first design does not work; the initiative to own projects, communicate clearly in English, and collaborate closely in a small team. Experience with automation, optomechanical design, PCB design, embedded systems, Python or LabVIEW, precision assembly, or design for manufacture is welcome, but not required. This …

items.desc: Junior AI/ML Engineer - Applied Computer Vision The Role We’re looking for a motivated Junior AI/ML Engineer to join a growing engineering team working on advanced computer vision and machine learning technologies. You’ll work with CNNs, Vision Transformers and emerging deep learning architectures, contributing to projects from early experimentation through to production deployment. You’ll learn from experienced engineers and researchers, developing your technical skills while taking on increasing responsibility. This is a hands-on engineering role where you’ll write code, run experiments, evaluate models and help turn cutting-edge research into reliable software for demanding applications. What You’ll Do Develop and test computer vision algorithms using CNNs, Vision Transformers and other deep learning architectures. Run experiments and evaluate model performance, including training strategies, loss functions and evaluation metrics. Help translate research into robust, production-ready software. Contribute to scalable model training, evaluation and inference pipelines. Support model optimisation for accuracy, speed and deployment across edge and cloud platforms. Explore emerging AI architectures and contribute to the development of new machine learning solutions. Work alongside experienced engineers, researchers and technical leadership on customer projects. Take part in technical discussions and develop your understanding of software engineering best practice. Essential Skills and Experience Strong foundations in machine learning and deep learning, gained through a degree, personal projects, internships or professional experience. Hands-on experience with PyTorch. TensorFlow experience is also welcome. Good understanding of CNNs and Vision Transformers, with an interest in current computer vision research. Strong Python programming skills. Familiarity with software engineering practices, including version control, testing and code reviews. Comfortable working in Linux and/or Windows environments. Good analytical and problem-solving skills. Clear communication skills and a willingness to learn, ask questions and collaborate with others. Desirable Skills Experience with object detection, tracking, image segmentation or pose estimation. Exposure to aerial, satellite or intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) imagery. Interest in edge deployment, real-time AI or GPU optimisation. Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes, Kubeflow or other MLOps tools. Experience with synthetic data or simulation platforms, such as Unreal Engine or NVIDIA Omniverse. Experience working alongside researchers. An interest in defence, government or national security applications. Education An MSc or PhD in Computer Vision, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Robotics or a related discipline would be beneficial. Equivalent practical experience and demonstrable project work are equally welcome. Security Requirements Candidates must be eligible to obtain UK security clearance. The ability to achieve Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required, with Security Check (SC) clearance or higher desirable. What’s on Offer? The opportunity to work on advanced AI and computer vision technologies. Mentoring and technical development from experienced engineers and researchers. Exposure to both research-led development and production engineering. The chance to contribute to systems used in demanding operational environments. Opportunities to develop your skills, take on greater responsibility and progress your career within a highly technical team.

items.desc: Imagine working on Denmark's most critical systems, turning unique customer data into real value through applied machine learning. As our new Data Scientist, you will play a key role in analysing customer data and training models within our established product. Ready to make an impact? The job You will be responsible for generating value from customer data within our established product, which underpins national security and critical infrastructure domains. Our customers are classified and cannot be disclosed, so your work will take place in secure environments, often in collaboration with Product teams, security teams and onsite at customer locations. As this is a newly established position, you will have the opportunity to help shape this role as it grows. In short, you can look forward to: Analysing and preparing customer data for use in our established product Training, evaluating and refining machine learning models on customer data Integrating models and data-driven features that generate measurable value Exploring customer data to identify new opportunities for value creation Collaborating with security teams to ensure compliance with national classifications and profiles Joining the team You will join an organisation where you will be associated with multiple teams, part of our NSI business unit. We develop and maintain military-grade solutions that support a nation's most critical systems. The organisation is highly collaborative, organised around Products that make a difference. If you are located in Aarhus, we are open to discussing a hybrid arrangement, but you should expect regular presence in Copenhagen (6–8 days per month). Your Qualifications We are looking for a data scientist with hands-on experience applying machine learning to real-world data in production settings, who can work confidently in high-stakes, security-classified environments. Relevant technical education, Bachelor's or Master's, in Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics or equivalent experience Documented experience with applied machine learning on real-world data Some hands-on experience with data science and machine learning in production settings Strong knowledge of Python, machine learning frameworks (scikit-learn, PyTorch or TensorFlow), SQL and data processing tools Fluent Danish and English skills A strong security mindset and ability to work in high-stakes environments Alongside this, we value: A collaborative and proactive work style Comfortable working independently and navigating ambiguity, particularly as this is a newly established role Detail-oriented with strong problem-solving abilities Comfortable working onsite at customer environments when needed Expect travel activity to our HQ in Aarhus and to customer sites, primarily in Copenhagen. items.desc: Italy Commitment & contract: collaboration contract, 13 months, Fellow position Location: Center for Sustainable Future Technologies, Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia, Torino, Italy Step into a world of endless possibilities, together let’s leave something for the future! At IIT, we are committed to advancing human-centered Science and Technology to address the most urgent societal challenges of our era. We foster excellence in both fundamental and applied research, spanning fields such as neuroscience and cognition, humanoid technologies and robotics, artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, and material sciences, offering a truly interdisciplinary scientific experience. Our approach integrates cutting-edge tools and technology, empowering researchers to push the limits of knowledge and innovation. With us, your curiosity will know no bounds. We are dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering diversity in all its forms, creating an inclusive environment. We value the unique experiences, knowledge, backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives of our people. By embracing diversity, we believe science can achieve its fullest potential. THE ROLE You will be working in a multicultural and multi-disciplinary group, where junior and senior scientists collaborate, each with their expertise, to carry out a scientific activity with a shared research goal. The Center for Sustainable Future Technologies (CSFT) is an interdisciplinary research center committed to addressing sustainability challenges through innovative solutions for the energy transition, circular economy, and valorization of renewable resources. The Center develops advanced materials, processes, and systems aimed at reducing environmental impact and promoting the conversion of waste streams and carbon-based feedstocks into valuable products. The Advanced Materials for Sustainable Future Technologies Research unit is coordinated by Prof. Candido Fabrizio Pirri. The research focuses on a combination of advanced materials science with microbial biotechnology, focusing on the development of innovative bioprocesses based on photosynthetic and gas-fermenting microorganisms for the sustainable production of chemicals, fuels, and other value-added products. This includes research activities carried out within the European project GoodByO (Multi-commodities microbial-driven Biorefinery based on food-processing industry wastes, biogenic CO₂ and bioprocess wastewaters). In particular, the development and optimization of microbial gas fermentation processes for the conversion of biogenic CO₂ and renewable hydrogen into bio-based chemicals, contributing to the advancement of sustainable biorefinery technologies. Within the research team, your main responsibilities will be: Maintain and cultivate anaerobic microbial strains, prepare culture media and inocula, and perform routine laboratory activities required for the operation of gas fermentation experiments. Operate and monitor anaerobic bioreactors and gas fermentation systems. Perform analytical characterization of fermentation products, with particular focus on bio-hexanol production. Analyze process performance and microbial growth data. Contribute to process optimization and scale-up activities. Contribute to the preparation of technical reports, scientific publications and project deliverables. ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS Master's degree in Biotechnology, Industrial Biotechnology, Microbiology, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Biochemistry or related disciplines. Hands-on experience in microbial cultivation and lab-scale bioprocesses. Hands-on experience with gaseous flows control systems. Basic knowledge of molecular biology technologies. Basic knowledge of fermentation technologies and anaerobic microbiology. Good command of spoken and written English. ADDITIONAL SKILLS Knowledge of analytical techniques such as HPLC, GC and spectrophotometry Ability to work in a challenging and international environment Capacity to work autonomously and collaboratively in a highly interdisciplinary environment Possess Analytical Reasoning skills and a growth mindset COMPENSATION PACKAGE A yearly gross salary of 21.000 euro Private health care coverage depending on your role and contract Candidates from abroad or Italian citizens who have carried scientific research activity permanently abroad and meet specific requirements, may be entitled to a deduction from taxable income of up to 90% from 6 to 13 years. This open position is financed by Circular Bio-based Europe Joint Undertaking (CBE JU) wihin the GoodByO – Multi-commodities microbial-driven BiOrefinery based on food-processing industry wastes, biogenic CO₂ and bioprocess wastewaters project (Grant Agreement No. 101156486 ). Please submit your application using the online form and including a detailed CV, cover letter and 2 reference letters Application’s deadline: 04/11/2026. Reporting directly to Professor Ana Namburete, the successful candidate will work within a multidisciplinary team of deep learning researchers, research software engineers, and neonatologists, and will collaborate with Dr Frances O’Brien (Consultant Neonatologist, Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust). The post-holder will contribute to research at the intersection of 3D computer vision, neural rendering, and medical image analysis. This includes physics-informed rendering models that account for view-dependent acoustic appearance, and working with multi-fontanelle data acquired by clinical colleagues. This post is based at the Department of Computer Science. About Us The University of Oxford is a stimulating work environment, which enjoys an international reputation as a world-class centre of excellence. Our research plays a key role in tackling many global challenges, from reducing our carbon emissions to developing vaccines during a pandemic. The Department of Computer Science at Oxford is renowned for pioneering research and teaching across diverse fields, consistently ranking among the best in the world. Our commitment to innovation drives us to tackle complex technological and societal challenges. What We Offer As an employer, we genuinely care about our employees’ wellbeing, reflected in the range of benefits that we offer including: Excellent contributory pension scheme 38 days annual leave (including public holidays) – pro rata for part time jobs Family leave schemes Cycle loan scheme and discounted public transport The successful candidate will be based onsite in the Department of Computer Science buildings in central Oxford. However, remote working from within the UK and flexible working arrangements can be considered. Diversity Committed to equality and valuing diversity. Application Process You will be required to upload a supporting statement and an up-to-date CV as part of your online application. Your supporting statement must clearly demonstrate how you meet each of the essential selection criteria listed in the job description. Applications that do not include a supporting statement or CV, or fail to address the criteria in sufficient detail, will not be considered. While we recognise the value of AI tools in assisting with application preparation, submissions that are clearly AI-generated without personalisation or insight will be rejected. It's crucial that your application reflects your own experiences and understanding of the role. The closing date for applications is midday on 23 November 2026 . Interviews are expected to be held in early December.

items.desc: Four-year Researcher position on Greenland marine ecosystems The Department of Ecoscience, Aarhus University, invites applications for a four-year scientist position on the biodiversity and coastal ecosystem status and trends along Greenland’s coast with a special focus on the use of eDNA for monitoring of marine macroalgae. The position is linked to multiple international projects, including the Greenland Ecosystem Monitoring Programme with an overarching theme of studying the impacts of climate change on coastal ecosystems in Greenland. The position requires active participation in developing and attracting funding for new projects including a special focus on developing and implementing eDNA tools for the ecological research and monitoring. This is a four–year position available from 15 February 2027. Job description The position focuses on the ecology of coastal marine ecosystems in Greenland and their responses to climate change, particularly warming and the ongoing loss of the cryosphere. You are expected to participate in annual field campaigns in Greenland and contribute to the analysis and interpretation of monitoring and experimental data from coastal Greenland ecosystems. A particular focus will be on developing and applying environmental DNA (eDNA) methods for characterising and quantifying marine biodiversity, with an emphasis on marine macroalgae. This includes establishing high-quality biodiversity baselines and improving our capacity to detect changes in species distributions and the arrival of new species. Your profile Applicants must hold a PhD in biology or a closely related field. Documented experience with Arctic marine vegetation and ecosystem ecology is considered an advantage, together with expertise in eDNA-based approaches, including metabarcoding, quantitative PCR-based methods such as digital PCR (dPCR), bioinformatics and biostatistics. Experience with marine fieldwork, DNA barcoding, experimental design and morphological species identification is also an advantage. The successful candidate is expected to have experience in developing research ideas and in contributing to research proposals and grant applications. A scientific diving certification is considered an advantage. Fluency in spoken and written English is required. In addition, the candidate should enjoy working collaboratively in an interdisciplinary and international research environment and be motivated to contribute actively to fieldwork, research development and scientific publication. Who we are The Department of Ecoscience (https://ecos.au.dk/en/) is organised under the Faculty of Technical Sciences. The department’s research areas cover most aspects of biology and ecology, spanning all biological levels from genetics, physiological processes, individuals, populations and species to entire ecosystems. Strategic and applied research account for a large part of the research activities at the Department of Ecoscience. Geographically, the department works from the tropics to the poles, but with greater focus on Danish conditions. The department has an obligation towards the Ministry of Environment and Food of Denmark and the authorities in Greenland as national advisors on environmental issues. The department’s research, consultancy and teaching are linked to strong and active research groups. What we offer The successful candidate is offered: Access to a well-developed research infrastructure Office space and shared equipment a research climate inviting lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research a working environment with teamwork, close working relations, network activities among young scientists and social activities a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance Place of work and area of employment The place of work is the main University campus in Aarhus, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C. Contact information For further information, please contact Mikael Sejr (mse@ecos.au.dk) or Dorte Krause-Jensen (dkj@ecos.au.dk). This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. Visant à approfondir les connaissances en IA tout en gardant l'être humain au centre de ses préoccupations, la Région Ile-de-France ambitionne de jouer un rôle majeur dans ce secteur d'avenir, par son excellence scientifique et son écosystème incomparable et souhaite de faire de ce dernier un acteur incontournable de la construction d'une Intelligence Artificielle (IA) frugale, fiable, efficace , amenée à cohabiter avec l'être humain et à l'assister dans ses décisions. A cet effet, DIM AI4IDF lance périodiquement des appels à projets de recherche doctorale. Cette thèse s'inscrit dans cet cadre et établit un partenariat entre les clusters Hi!Paris et PRAIRIE, très précisément entre Telecom ParisTech et Inria Centre de Paris. L’ objectif de cette thèse est de mener des recherches commune sur la persistance dans les modèles génératifs de monde pour la robotique et de développer des algorithmes capables d'intégrer les concepts physiques lors de la génération d'images en particulier. Le projet développera des méthodes pour imposer la persistance dans les modèles génératifs du monde, avec des contributions incluant une définition formelle de la persistance, des méthodes d’apprentissage à l’échelle de la trajectoire, et une validation empirique en prédiction et contrôle robotiques. Des déplacements réguliers sont prévus pour ce poste , notamment à des fins de dissémination, de formation scientifique et de participation à des réunions de projet et de collaboration . Le français est fortement recommandé. Compétences relationnelles : être ouvert à des environnements de recherche multiculturels et inclusif et adhérer au bon-vivre social et professionnel établi dans les laboratoires d'accueil. Respecter les règles professionnelles et de conduite ainsi que l'éthique de la recherche est nécessaire. Compétences additionnelles appréciées : maîtriser les outils, langages et bibliothèques de développement pour le développement en vision par odinateur et IA. La combinaison essentielle est Python, PyTorch, Git, (Linux est un plus) , complétée par des compétences en calcul GPU, en traitement de données à grande échelle, et une solide culture mathématique. items.desc: Build the science that shapes the future of human health. Application closing date: 11.11.2026 Join a place where ambitious science thrives Human Technopole (Milan) is a rapidly expanding life science institute where international researchers and cutting-edge technologies converge to accelerate biomedical discovery. Our mission is to transform bold scientific ideas into advances that improve human health. Within this mission, the Casale Group in the Health Data Science Centre develops AI methods that transform population-scale human data into mechanistic models of disease. Our research integrates large-scale human genetics with molecular and clinical data to generate testable hypotheses that accelerate biological discovery and therapeutic innovation. We are recruiting an ambitious AI Scientist to build the reusable AI foundations and agentic scientific systems that power the group’s research across human genetics, multimodal biology, and disease. Your mission As AI Scientist, you will develop next-generation AI systems at the interface of ambitious biological research and frontier artificial intelligence, using population-scale genetics and multimodal biomedical data to uncover mechanisms of human disease. You will turn methods and models emerging from this research into robust, reusable AI capabilities—including foundation models, multimodal representation learning, agentic workflows, evaluation frameworks, and scalable research software—that can accelerate discovery across multiple projects. A longer-term goal is to develop AI systems that increasingly act as scientific collaborators: connecting evidence across biological scales, proposing testable hypotheses, identifying informative analyses, and working alongside researchers to accelerate iterative cycles of biological discovery. Your work will combine methodological innovation, biological discovery, and scientific software development at the intersection of artificial intelligence, computational biology, and human genetics. You will have substantial scientific and technical ownership, with the opportunity to help shape the group’s technical AI architecture while leading and contributing to high-impact scientific publications, open-source software, and reusable research capabilities. As part of Human Technopole’s interdisciplinary AI ecosystem, you will engage closely with the European AI community, including through collaborations with Helmholtz Munich and connections to the ELLIS network. Your work will benefit from interactions with computational, biological, and clinical groups across the institute, alongside opportunities for international collaboration, research exchanges, interdisciplinary training, and engagement with industry. You will also draw on the group’s established network across leading academic institutions and industry partners in Europe and North America, helping you build collaborations, broaden your expertise, and accelerate the impact of your research. Grow Your Skills You will enhance your scientific and professional skills by: Developing next-generation AI methods through ambitious biological research. Building foundation models, multimodal representation learning approaches, and agentic AI systems for scientific discovery. Turning scientific advances into robust, benchmarked, and reusable AI capabilities that accelerate discovery across multiple research projects. Building scalable research software and AI workflows for large and heterogeneous scientific datasets. Shaping the future of AI for science through high-impact publications, open-source software, international collaborations, and entrepreneurial initiatives. Human Technopole supports career development through training, mentoring and dedicated learning opportunities. Essential What you'll bring PhD in Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Computational Biology, or a related quantitative discipline, or expected completion within the next six months. At least 4 years of relevant research experience by the start of the position, including doctoral research. Strong track record of scientific output in AI, machine learning, computational biology, or biomedicine, demonstrating independent methodological or technical contributions through publications, open-source software, models, or comparable research outputs. Excellent programming and software engineering skills in Python, with experience building scalable and maintainable research software, model-training workflows, or AI systems. Strong expertise in modern machine learning and AI, with demonstrated ability to design, develop, and critically evaluate advanced methods for challenging research problems. Experience with modern software engineering and computational research practices, including version control, testing, documentation, reproducibility, and large-scale GPU or HPC environments. With more than 20 million new cancer cases diagnosed globally each year , there is an urgent need for more effective and personalized treatment strategies to improve patient survival while reducing the costs associated with ineffective therapies. By advancing the ability to predict patients' responses to treatments , Rosetta Omics empowers physicians with deeper molecular insights to guide therapeutic decisions and deliver the most effective care to each patient as early as possible. The company's mission is to accelerate the transition toward a future where precision medicine becomes the standard of care for cancer patients worldwide . Ensure data quality, traceability, documentation, and reproducibility across computational workflows. 4. Our AI-powered Demand Side Platform (DSP) connects the world's most ambitious marketers with their ideal audiences across the open internet, delivering results that actually move the needle. Since 2006, we've been the industry's trailblazer, launching the first AI-powered measurement platform for publishers and the first AI-driven DSP. Our AI doesn't just optimize—it delivers the measurable outcomes that matter most to our clients, giving them the competitive edge they need in a crowded marketplace. Ready to join the team that's defining the future of digital advertising? The Modeling team is responsible for Machine Learning (ML) systems at Quantcast. We build and maintain high-frequency ML infrastructure that prices millions of advertising opportunities per second in a real-time auction environment to maximise advertiser outcomes. In less than 100 milliseconds, our models predict age, gender, viewability, fraud, advertiser relevance and many more characteristics of internet users. Using NLP, clustering and LLMs we build topics in multiple languages to help our advertisers target customers interested in their products. Collaborate with senior scientists and engineers to iterate on ML models and learn industry best practices for high-quality ML products and large-scale systems. Write clean, efficient, and maintainable code using industry best practices. Participate in code reviews and provide constructive feedback to team members. Identify performance bottlenecks and optimise system components for enhanced scalability. Keep up to date with developments in machine learning outside the company. Notre cabinet rassemble 2800 collaborateurs présents sur 4 continents, figure parmi les leaders indépendants du conseil en Europe, et constitue le 1er cabinet de conseil indépendant en France. Pour satisfaire nos clients, nous développons 18 terrains d’excellence, à la fois sectoriels, fonctionnels, et technologiques. items.desc: About Us We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity. Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next. The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve. Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost. Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor. In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence. We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you. About The Role Choosing between algorithmic strategies for multi-step LLM work is a measurement problem, and most teams solve it badly: comparisons run case by case, by whoever needs them that week, on whatever task is closest to hand. That doesn't scale, and it doesn't hold up to outside scrutiny - from a customer, or from a reviewer. Callosum needs one benchmarking system: reproducible, contamination-controlled, and trusted enough to be the evidence that decides which approach ships. This role owns that system. You will build a harness that measures task success, quality, and robustness across motifs, agent topologies, and decomposition strategies, grounded in execution - real commits, real traces, sandboxed grading - rather than self-reported or model-graded scores. The results become the proof points we show customers, the evidence behind the benchmarks we co-publish, and the basis on which an approach ships or doesn't. This is a research hire that builds. We expect the rigour of a strong evaluation paper applied to a production system, and the engineering ability to design, build, and curate it yourself rather than hand it off. What You'll Build Design and build a unified system for evaluating agentic and algorithmic solutions - task success, quality, and robustness across motifs, agent topologies, and decomposition strategies, on workloads that match what customers actually run. Cost per resolved task is an outcome you track, not the object of the exercise. Mine real commits and traces, run sandboxed execution grading, and build task suites that reflect real agentic work: code search, code edit and repair, repository summarisation, tool use. Self-reported or model-graded success isn't enough on its own. Enforce controls against contamination, overfitting to benchmarks, and metric gaming, and keep baselines stable over time - any result should be re-runnable to the same number, by us or by a reviewer Compare algorithmic and agentic approaches honestly, not models or chips - a motif that adds steps, latency, or cost has to earn it in resolved-task quality, and the system says clearly when it doesn't Lead external benchmark co-publications, held to a standard that survives peer and customer review Feed results directly into which approach ships, into the proof points behind customer engagements, and review quality claims across the company before they go out What You'll Bring PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field, or an equivalent research track record Authorship or co-authorship of a benchmark or evaluation paper at a recognised venue - NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks, ICML, ICLR, ACL - ideally …

About The Role Callosum believes that orders of magnitude improvements in AI systems will come through application-aware orchestration across heterogeneous models and hardware. Our team is developing the science that makes that possible: a principled, evidence-based method for building agentic systems automatically at unprecedented scale. The team tackles these problems on two fronts. We build the tools to analyse and evaluate agentic systems rigorously enough to say where and why they go wrong, and we use what we learn to design better ones. We are not simply building a better harness; the best harness will change with every new model, task and generation of silicon. We are building the layer beneath it, so that design decisions follow from evidence rather than taste. This role owns the first of those fronts. Agentic evaluation today is not up to the job: benchmarks saturate, scores move for reasons unrelated to capability, results fail to reproduce across runs, and a single number tells you nothing about which step went wrong. Every design decision the rest of the team makes rests on the quality of that instrument. You will build measures whose construct we can defend, whose variance we understand, and which localise a failure rather than merely scoring it. The mandate is broad, and most of the questions inside it are still unanswered. You will have wide latitude to choose problems, and your results will shape what the company builds in the future. What You'll Build Design benchmarks and evaluation suites for agentic behaviour – multi-turn, long-horizon, tool-using, operating in non-stationary environments – including the properties that are hard to score, such as reliability and recovery from error Build the methodology as well as the harness: statistical power, variance across runs, contamination and construct validity Be the independent voice on the quality of our own results. Red-team our evaluations, design the sanity checks that catch a flattering number before it reaches a decision. Turn raw traces into structured evidence. En étroite collaboration avec nos chercheurs en laboratoire, nous développons, exploitons et améliorons en permanence des plateformes omiques à haut débit et haute précision. Dans le cadre de programmes multidisciplinaires de découverte de médicaments, nous collaborons avec des experts issus d’un large éventail de disciplines scientifiques au sein d’une organisation mondiale comptant plus de 5 000 collaborateurs à travers le monde. Notre travail couvre la gestion et le contrôle qualité des données omiques, le développement de méthodes et de logiciels, l’analyse avancée des données, ainsi que l’interprétation biologique des résultats. Notre mission consiste à générer des connaissances exploitables qui permettent de prendre de meilleures décisions et d’accélérer le développement de médicaments qui font la différence. Afin de renforcer notre groupe d’oncologie computationnelle, nous recherchons un(e) candidat(e) très motivé(e) Bioinformaticien - biologie computationnelle CDI à temps plein Vos Principales Responsabilités Accompagner les chercheurs en oncologie au sein d’équipes de projet interdisciplinaires en apportant votre expertise en oncologie, en bioinformatique et en analyse de données. Contribuer à des projets de découverte de médicaments grâce à l’analyse de divers ensembles de données omiques générés en interne ou provenant de sources publiques. Vos Qualifications Idéales Doctorat en bioinformatique, biologie computationnelle, oncologie ou dans un domaine connexe, avec au moins 2 ans d’expérience postdoctorale ou en entreprise, de préférence dans la découverte de médicaments. Solide compréhension de la biologie moléculaire, de la génomique, de la génétique et des voies biologiques pertinentes en oncologie Maîtrise approfondie des méthodes et outils bioinformatiques Expérience dans la découverte de médicaments et l’analyse de données liées à l’oncologie, notamment des ensembles de données omiques, des données de criblage cellulaire et des bases de données oncologiques. La maîtrise du langage de programmation R est requise. Une expérience de travail dans des environnements basés sur Linux est attendue. Solides compétences organisationnelles, avec la capacité de gérer plusieurs priorités et de respecter les délais. Excellentes compétences en communication et en relations interpersonnelles, avec la capacité de travailler à la fois de manière autonome et en collaboration au sein d’équipes interdisciplinaires dans un environnement dynamique. Une équipe diversifiée et internationale dans un environnement collaboratif qui encourage la créativité, l’innovation et le travail d’équipe. Des avantages sociaux compétitifs, notamment des avantages en capital, des horaires de travail flexibles, des congés payés et une prime annuelle liée à la performance. In close collaboration with our laboratory scientists, we develop, operate, and continuously enhance high-throughput, high-precision omics platforms. As part of multidisciplinary drug discovery programs, we collaborate with experts from a wide range of scientific disciplines across a global organization of more than 5,000 employees worldwide. Our work spans omics data management and quality control, method and software development, advanced data analysis, and the biological interpretation of results. Our mission is to generate actionable insights that enable better decisions and accelerate the development of medicines that matter. Whether it's a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe. About This Role Join our Partner Algorithms team and help build the intelligence behind Just Eat's marketplace, powering personalised experiences for tens of millions of customers across 14 countries. This is your opportunity to deliver end-to-end machine learning solutions that directly impact customer engagement and order growth. We're building JET's recommendation systems, generating personalised carousels of restaurants to help people find their order right on the home page of the app. We're looking for someone who can live our behaviours of lead, deliver and care while bringing technical excellence and innovation. This role sits at the intersection of cutting-edge AI as we integrate, train and develop ML and generative models into a live production environment. Help us compute data at scale for millions of users to help people find the food they want. We need someone who can challenge assumptions, translate ambiguous business problems into elegant technical solutions, and ship production-quality ML systems that make a measurable difference to our customers and partners. These are some of the key components to the position: Work within a team on the development and deployment of ML/AI solutions including embedding models, fine-tuned LLMs, and ranking systems that drive engagement and orders while raising the bar for technical excellence. Apply generative AI and LLM techniques to personalisation challenges at scale, generating recommendations for millions of customers Own your results by designing, running and interpreting A/B experiments with statistical rigour, measuring real impact on business metrics and holding yourself accountable. Collaborate with ML engineers to productionise models, implementing MLOps best practices and maintaining monitored pipelines that deliver consistent value. Break down silos by translating complex business questions into clear modelling approaches and communicating results effectively to product and commercial stakeholders. Be determined to take end-to-end ownership of well-scoped workstreams, independently framing problems, choosing approaches, running experiments and presenting findings. Move fast by writing production-quality Python code and efficient SQL for data pipelines and analyses that can scale across our marketplace. Aim higher by staying current with advances in search, retrieval, recommendations and LLM applications, bringing fresh ideas to drive the vision forward. What will you bring to the team? Strong experimentation skills with ability to design and interpret A/B tests, reason about statistical significance, and understand the gap between offline and online performance. Production-grade Python coding abilities that go beyond notebooks, writing clean, testable code suitable for engineering workflows and collaboration with technical teams. Proficient SQL skills across complex data warehouses, including partitioning, window functions, and large-table joins, with focus on query efficiency and data quality. Self-starter attitude comfortable with autonomy and ambiguity, thriving in fast-paced environments where you can build rapidly, test rigorously and roll out successes at scale. The position is offered until 31/05/2028 in the
items.desc: Magnesium alloys offer exceptional lightweighting potential for aerospace and space applications, but their wider use in extreme environments is limited by challenges including microstructural instability, temperature fluctuations and irradiation-induced damage. At the same time, oxide inclusions formed during casting and manufacturing are conventionally regarded as detrimental to structural performance. This project seeks to turn these"liabilities into assets" by exploiting solid-state, friction-based manufacturing to create finely dispersed oxide nanoparticles in magnesium alloys, enabling the development of oxide-dispersion-strengthened (ODS) magnesium alloys with enhanced thermal stability, high-temperature performance and radiation resistance. You will work within the research group led by Dr Dikai Guan at the University of Southampton on an NSF-EPSRC research project. The project brings together the University of Southampton, Baylor University, UK National Ion Beam Centre, integrating alloy processing, friction-based manufacturing, multiscale characterisation, modelling and extreme-environment testing. The position is offered until 31/05/2028 in the first instance, with the possibility of extension for up to 1 further year. The Research Fellow will be a major contributor to the experimental research activities at the University of Southampton, including: Feedstock alloy development and characterisation Multiscale microstructure characterisation Cryogenic and thermal-cycling testing Radiation-resistance testing You will have a good track record in carrying out independent and original scientific research, and publication of research papers. You should have the ability to work and communicate efficiently with other members of the team (supervisors, students and postdocs), and collaborators outside the University. Regular reports of research progress are required, and research plans should be adjusted accordingly. Critical analysis of experimental results and problem solving skills are essential to this role. You will also be required to write research papers for publication in high impact research journals and attend/present at relevant conferences. There will be an opportunity to supervisor PhD and Master students as a secondary supervisor. You should hold a PhD (or near completion)/ relevant experience in materials science or a relevant discipline. Research experience in physical metallurgy, metallic materials and advanced microstructure characterisation is particularly relevant to this position. Experience with SEM/EDS and EBSD, together with TEM/STEM or related high-resolution characterisation techniques, is highly desirable. Experience in oxide-dispersion-strengthened materials, metal casting, friction-based processing, cryogenic testing, thermal cycling, ion irradiation, or other advanced characterisation methods would be advantageous. Equality, diversity and inclusion are central to the ethos in the School of Engineering. We give full consideration to applicants who wish to work flexibly including part-time and due consideration will be given to applicants who have taken a career break. The University has onsite childcare facilities and we foster a good work-life balance. We also offer a mentorship programme and the school runs a women-oriented network event on a bi-weekly basis. The University of Southampton is in the top 1% of world universities and the top 10 of the UK’s research-intensive universities. We are committed to sustainability and being a globally responsible university, with the principles of sustainability embedded into all aspects of our individual and collective work, in our business planning, policy-making, and professional activities. For further information please contact Dr Dikai Guan dikai.guan@soton.ac.uk

items.desc: About Us We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity. Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next. The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve. Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost. Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor. In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence. We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you. About The Role Callosum believes that the next generation of AI systems will be co-optimised across models, software, and hardware. As we operate across increasingly heterogeneous workloads and accelerators, the number of possible system configurations grows combinatorially. Manually exploring that space does not scale – we need systems that can search it themselves. This role owns Callosum’s program evolution and optimisation loop: an LLM-guided search system that iteratively generates, evaluates, and improves programs against verifiable objectives. We already use this approach across kernels, inference runtimes, scheduling and scaling policies, KV caching strategies, and more. You will develop the loop both as a reusable internal optimisation system and as a research object in its own right, improving how it searches, measuring what makes it effective, and pushing its capabilities on increasingly difficult optimisation and reasoning problems. items.desc: We're assembling a group of senior software and ML engineers to work on one of the hardest open problems in AI today: how well can frontier models reason about LLM inference systems, GPU-level performance optimization, and model-serving architecture? You'll help design evaluation scenarios, write reference solutions, and grade model outputs on real systems-engineering problems - the same class of problems you likely work on day-to-day. This is a research-and-evaluation role, not a traditional engineering job - you won't be shipping production code for us, you'll be defining what "correct" and "excellent" look like for AI models tackling the problems you already know deeply. Responsibilities What You'll Do Design realistic technical scenarios and problem sets in LLM inference optimization, GPU kernel design, and systems performance engineering Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field Strong, hands-on background in one or more of: GPU inference optimization, custom CUDA kernel development, model-serving systems (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang), quantization, or optimizer design Experience at a recognized technology or AI company, in a role with real systems-engineering ownership Strong written communication - you'll be authoring technical explanations and feedback, not just code Preferred Qualifications Direct experience with SGLang, Mamba/Mamba2 architectures, or IBM Granite-family models Open-source contributions to inference/serving frameworks (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, etc.) Experience with distributed inference (tensor/expert parallelism, continuous batching, KV-cache optimization) Why apply Remote, contract, part-time Flexible - work on your own schedule

Proven ability to execute, analyse, and optimise HPC benchmarks and performance validation tests across compute, storage, and networking infrastructure. Solid knowledge of parallel computing technologies, including MPI, OpenMP, CUDA, NCCL, and GPU-accelerated applications. Experience benchmarking and tuning scientific, engineering, AI, and data analytics workloads on large-scale HPC platforms. Strong understanding of NVIDIA GPU technologies and architectures, including H100, H200, B200, and GB200/GB300. Hands-on experience with high-performance networking technologies such as InfiniBand and RoCEv2. Expertise with industry-standard benchmark suites including HPL, HPL-MxP, HPCG, IO500, MLPerf, STREAM, FIO, IOR, and NCCL tests. Knowledge of Top500, Green500, customer acceptance testing methodologies, and HPC performance benchmarking best practices. Experience working with HPC storage solutions such as Lustre, GPFS (IBM Storage Scale), BeeGFS, VAST, WEKA, or similar parallel file systems. Strong Linux skills across RHEL, Rocky Linux, and Ubuntu, combined with shell scripting for automation, benchmark execution, and performance analysis. Ability to identify performance bottlenecks, deliver optimisation recommendations, and create customer-facing benchmark reports, technical documentation, and performance studies. Excellent communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work directly with customers, architects, and engineering teams; experience with AI infrastructure benchmarking, LLMs, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Kubernetes, OpenShift, cloud HPC (Azure/AWS/GCP), Python automation, GPU profiling tools, and enterprise AI acceptance testing is highly desirable. items.title: Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter/Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin (m/w/d) Else Kröner Fresenius-Zentrum
items.card: Ihre Aufgaben Identifikation, Auswahl und Aufbereitung geeigneter histologischer Bilddatensätze für die Entwicklung und Validierung von KI-Modellen Entwicklung, Implementierung und Optimierung von Deep-Learning-Modellen für histologische Bilddaten mit PyTorch Konzeption und Implementierung effizienter Daten- und Trainingspipelines, einschließlich Datenladen, Vorverarbeitung und Training Optimierung und Portierung
items.desc: Bewerbungsfrist: 25.10.2026 Befristung: 24 Monate Arbeitszeit: Voll- und Teilzeit Stellenanzeigen ID: 2139 Das Universitätsklinikum Carl Gustav Carus und die Medizinische Fakultät bilden gemeinsam die Dresdner Hochschulmedizin. Sie ist zur Exzellenz in der Hochleistungsmedizin, der medizinischen Forschung und Lehre sowie der Gesundheitsdienstleistung für Patient*innen der gesamten Region verpflichtet. Gemeinsam für die Spitzenmedizin von morgen – werden Sie Teil der Hochschulmedizin Dresden. Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter/ Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin (m/w/d) am Else Kröner Fresenius Zentrum für Digitale Gesundheit Die Stelle ist zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt in Voll- oder Teilzeitbeschäftigung für 24 Monate befristet zu besetzen, mit der Option auf Verlängerung und längerfristige Zusammenarbeit. Die Vergütung erfolgt nach den Eingruppierungsvorschriften des Tarifvertrages für den öffentlichen Dienst (TV-L) und ist bei Vorliegen der persönlichen Voraussetzungen in die Entgeltgruppe E13 möglich. Die Stelle ist im Rahmen des Forschungsprojekts “MedSecureAI – Zertifizierbare Chip-Plattform für sichere KI-Akzelerator-Integration in der bildbasierten medizinischen Detektion” zu besetzen. Das Projekt ist Teil des Zukunftsclusters SEMECO und verbindet Forschung aus medizinischer KI, digitaler Pathologie, Edge Computing und vertrauenswürdigen Hardwareplattformen. Ziel des Projekts ist die Entwicklung und Validierung einer modularen, sicheren und ressourceneffizienten Plattform für KI-gestützte medizinische Bildanalyse. Im medizinischen Anwendungsszenario werden KI-Modelle für die digitale Pathologie entwickelt, zunächst auf leistungsfähiger GPU-Infrastruktur trainiert und anschließend für die lokale Ausführung am Mikroskop auf ressourcenbeschränkter Edge-Hardware optimiert. Ein Demonstrator soll die direkte, erklärbare Analyse histologischer Bilddaten am Mikroskop ermöglichen. Die Position wird in einem interdisziplinären und internationalen Forschungsumfeld in der Forschungsgruppe von Marco Gustav, PhD am Else Kröner Fresenius Zentrum für Digitale Gesundheit der TU Dresden angesiedelt sein und eng mit akademischen Einrichtungen und Praxispartnern zusammenarbeiten. Die Gruppe entwickelt praxisnahe KI-Lösungen für konkrete Herausforderungen aus der klinischen Versorgung. Ein besonderer Schwerpunkt liegt auf effizienten, lokal einsetzbaren KI-Verfahren für die Pathologie und deren klinisch relevanter Anwendung. Ihre Aufgaben Identifikation, Auswahl und Aufbereitung geeigneter histologischer Bilddatensätze für die Entwicklung und Validierung von KI-Modellen Entwicklung, Implementierung und Optimierung von Deep-Learning-Modellen für histologische Bilddaten mit PyTorch Konzeption und Implementierung effizienter Daten- und Trainingspipelines, einschließlich Datenladen, Vorverarbeitung und Training Optimierung und Portierung der entwickelten Modelle auf die Zielhardware, insbesondere hinsichtlich Rechen- und Speichereffizienz sowie Inferenzgeschwindigkeit unter Berücksichtigung von Edge-AI-Ansätzen, in Zusammenarbeit mit den technischen Projektpartnern Entwicklung und Validierung eines Demonstrators zur lokalen KI-gestützten Analyse histologischer Bilddaten am Mikroskop Wissenschaftliche Auswertung, Dokumentation und Publikation der Forschungsergebnisse in Fachzeitschriften sowie Präsentation auf wissenschaftlichen Konferenzen Ihr Profil Abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium in Informatik, Künstlicher Intelligenz, Ingenieurwissenschaften, Data Science oder einem verwandten Fachgebiet Fundierte Programmierkenntnisse in Python und PyTorch sowie sehr gute Kenntnisse im Bereich Deep Learning Erfahrung in der KI-gestützten Analyse histologischer Bilddaten Erfahrung in der Optimierung von KI-Modellen unter Hardware- und Ressourcenbeschränkungen, z. items.card: The role You lead our research on AI agents that reason over confidential data across organisations without leaking it. You define what “no leakage” means, how to measure it and how to prove it. You also design the secure link between a private deployment on a customer’s own servers and our public cloud platform, which a distributed-systems engineer in the team builds. Why this role An open problem where formal
items.desc: Make AI privacy provable: define, measure and prove what AI agents can leak when they reason over confidential data. About Serinyx Serinyx builds AI for high-stakes decisions on confidential data. On our decision-intelligence platform, AI agents break a hard question down, research it with checked citations and debate the findings under human review. The result is a verified, cited and signed report. Our second product gives universities and research institutes an always-current, AI-built view of their research. We were founded in Saarbrücken in 2026 and are now building our engineering team. The role You lead our research on AI agents that reason over confidential data across organisations without leaking it. You define what “no leakage” means, how to measure it and how to prove it. You also design the secure link between a private deployment on a customer’s own servers and our public cloud platform, which a distributed-systems engineer in the team builds. Why this role An open problem where formal methods, cryptography and LLMs meet. Your theory goes straight into a working system, built by an engineer in the team. You lead the research agenda and write up the results for a peer-reviewed venue. What you will do in your first year Define, formally, a measurable bound on what a debate between AI agents can leak, and build and validate an estimator for it. Design the link between the private and public sides: the protocol agents use to exchange arguments across it, and the proof that protected data cannot cross it directly. Design, with our CTO, how the checks that protect confidential data can be proven to an outside auditor. Set the measurement method, run the main leakage measurements and write up the results for a peer-reviewed venue. What you bring A PhD (or a submitted thesis) in computer science, security, cryptography or a related field. Formal methods or information-flow control: non-interference, security type systems, protocol verification. Statistics for estimation: confidence bounds, variance reduction. Publications at strong security, formal-methods or machine-learning venues. Enough Python to build and run your own experiments. Nice to have Zero-knowledge proofs; multi-agent LLM systems; Tamarin, ProVerif, TLA+, Lean or Coq. How we work One team, one backlog. Everyone builds from day one and works directly with our CTO, Dr Raja Naeem Akram. Owners, not ticket-takers. Each engineer owns parts of the codebase and leads the AI coding agents working in them: writing their work orders, reviewing every pull request and deciding what merges. A typical week. Much of your time goes into specifying and reviewing work done by AI coding agents; the hardest parts you write yourself. AI agents take the routine platform work. Infrastructure, deployment and monitoring are done by AI agents under engineering review, so your time goes into design and the hard problems. You still own what you build once it is live. Quality is part of the job. You write the tests for your own work and keep CI green. Done means tests pass, security scans are clean, docs are updated and container images are signed. Two-week cycles. Planning on day one, a demo on day ten and a short written retro. English first. English is our working language; German is welcome but not required. What we offer Real ownership. An early role in a small team: you shape the product, the code and how we work, not a ticket queue. A modern stack. Python, FastAPI, Temporal, Kubernetes, React with TypeScript, and the best AI models for each task. Saarbrücken, hybrid. We are based in one of Europe’s leading centres for computer science, and we work hybrid. 30 days of holidays per year. International applicants welcome. If you come from outside the EU, we support you through the work-permit process, usually the EU Blue Card. How to apply Send your CV and one link that shows your work (code, a paper or a project you built) to contact@serinyx.com with the job title in the subject line. English or German is fine. The process has three steps: a call with our CTO, a technical interview on a problem typical of the role, with your usual AI tools, and a conversation with the founders. Equal opportunity We welcome applications from everyone, whatever their ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual identity. You don’t need to include a photo or your date of birth. Job Type: Full-time Pay: 63.600,00€ - 71.200,00€ per year Work Location: Hybrid remote in 66111 Saarbrücken

items.desc: Our Future Health is building the UK’s largest health research programme. To grow and improve it, we need to understand what works, what doesn’t and why. Our Experimentation & Insights team helps colleagues answer those questions through surveys, experiments, pilots and analysis. We’re looking for a Research Scientist for our Health Questionnaires squad, with strong experience in psychometrics and questionnaire research. You’ll help validate and improve screening and health research questionnaires, working closely with a questionnaire scientist developing new measures. We’re interested in more than whether a questionnaire meets standard measures of reliability and validity. We want someone who looks closely at the evidence: how people respond, where patterns emerge, which questions may be working differently for different groups, and what the data suggests should happen next. You’ll bring curiosity and sound research judgement to questionnaire testing, with the ability to choose the right methods and explain what the findings mean in practice. The role You’ll take research projects from initial question through to insight and recommendations. This includes shaping research plans and protocols, selecting appropriate methods and samples, programming and quality assuring surveys, analysing results and communicating findings to stakeholders. Questionnaire validation and psychometrics will be an important part of your work. You’ll also contribute to wider experimentation and test-and-learn activity, helping teams understand outcomes, refine success measures and decide what to do next. The role suits someone with substantial research training and a strong applied track record. You may have a PhD or MSc with significant relevant industry experience, particularly in pharmaceuticals, clinical trials, health research or a related field. We welcome candidates whose expertise has developed in academic or commercial settings. You will: Design and deliver research projects that support organisational, scientific, participant and researcher objectives. Lead the scientific validation of screening, filtering and health research questionnaires, including assessment of reliability and validity. Look beyond validation statistics to investigate response patterns, data quality, potential sources of bias and what the findings reveal about how a measure performs. Work with a questionnaire scientist to test and improve novel questionnaires. Develop research plans and protocols that address clear questions and information needs. Select appropriate methods, outcomes, samples and participant recruitment approaches for each piece of work. Design and oversee surveys, experiments, pilots and other studies, managing delivery, quality and timelines. Programme and quality assure surveys using Qualtrics and analyse and wrangle data using R or Python. Apply appropriate statistical methods, such as descriptive analysis, regression, chi-square, ANOVA and comparisons across experimental conditions. Help teams define research questions, outcomes and success measures before work begins. Secure appropriate ethical, data protection, security and other approvals, consulting relevant internal and external groups when needed. Document research from planning through to delivery, ensuring methods and decisions are clear and transparent. Present results and recommendations in a concise, accessible and actionable way for technical and non-technical audiences. Manage several research and experimentation projects at once, working independently while keeping stakeholders informed. Collaborate with squads and teams to shape ideas into research questions, test initiatives and help colleagues decide what to do next. Requirements Significant research training, such as a PhD or equivalent in a relevant subject with a strong research component. We’ll also consider an MSc or comparable qualification alongside substantial relevant experience. Proven experience in psychometrics and questionnaire validation. Experience applying research and experimentation in a questionnaire or survey setting, with evidence of analytical thinking beyond standard validation. The curiosity to investigate response patterns and data, identify interesting findings and consider what they mean for the measure and the people completing it. A broad understanding of questionnaire validity and reliability, research methods, sampling and participant selection. Experience designing surveys and experiments and knowing which methodology is appropriate for different questions. A sound working knowledge of statistics, including comparisons across conditions, descriptive and predictive analysis, regression, chi-square, sampling and sources of bias. Experience using survey tools such as Qualtrics. Experience using R or Python for data wrangling and analysis.
