Are you excited by the challenge of combining data, simulation, and policy to tackle the world’s biggest health problems? The Centre for Health Economics & Policy Innovation (CHEPI) at Imperial Business School is seeking a Research Associate / Research Fellow in Computational Health Policy Modelling to play a central role in developing Health-GPS — our state-of-the-art microsimulation model for non-communicable disease (NCD) policy analysis. Appointment will be made at Research Associate or Research Fellow level, depending on experience. Why This Role Matters Chronic diseases such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease remain leading causes of illness and premature death worldwide. Yet, the tools available to evaluate and design effective prevention policies are still evolving. Health-GPS provides a framework to explore how changes in diet, physical activity, and related risk factors affect long-term population health and economic outcomes. Health-GPS represents the gradual accumulation and interaction of individual-level risk factors — such as BMI, diet, and income — offering insights into the potential impact of different policy interventions over time. You will help develop and apply this model across major international projects including: GOLDFINCH – estimating the effects of fiscal policies on ultra-processed food consumption. JA Prevent NCD – a European Joint Action on integrated strategies for NCD prevention. JACARDI – a European initiative to reduce cardiovascular and diabetes risk. Working with economists, epidemiologists, and data scientists, you’ll push the boundaries of policy simulation and shape real-world decision-making. This is a hands-on computational role. Alongside using Health-GPS for policy analysis, you will write, test and review code in its C++ codebase, working within the team’s collaborative development workflow (version control, pull requests and code review). C++ experience is highly desirable, but we also welcome strong programmers in other relevant languages who are willing to work in C++. What you would be doing Contribute to the architecture, development, optimisation, and maintenance of Health-GPS, writing and reviewing code in its C++ codebase and ensuring its continued scientific and policy relevance. Work with colleagues to plan and deliver modelling work across multiple projects, producing high-quality outputs on time. Help integrate new methodologies, including AI and machine-learning approaches, into simulation design. Conduct quantitative analyses to estimate the health and economic impact of proposed policies. Identify and manage relevant datasets in collaboration with internal and external partners. Communicate findings through academic papers, policy briefs, and stakeholder workshops. Contribute to funding proposals and the expansion of CHEPI’s modelling activities. Strong programming skills in at least one language (e.g. Python, R, or C++), and experience contributing to a shared codebase using version control (e.g. git). Experience working with large or longitudinal datasets. The ability to translate complex model outputs into actionable policy insights. Curiosity, independence, and enthusiasm for multidisciplinary collaboration. Experience with C++ is highly desirable. Experience applying AI or ML methods to health or policy modelling is also desirable. Candidates for appointment as Research Fellow should also demonstrate a strong publication record, experience contributing to funding proposals, and the ability to design and lead original research. The successful candidate will contribute to the preclinical evaluation of novel therapeutic agents in animal models of cerebral ischemia, with particular emphasis on the middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model. items.desc: At OneSpan, we specialize in digital identity and anti-fraud solutions that create exceptional and secure experiences. We are looking for the first ML research hire on the team. Your job will be to turn our telemetry into new detection and prevention capabilities: from understanding the problem alongside the Security team, to ideating, prototyping, and validating models and algorithms on real data. We are not looking for someone who applies recipes. We are looking for someone who enjoys tackling an open problem with an adversary that adapts, and who can move comfortably between the paper and the working prototype. Here Is a Little Taste Of Your Challenge Work side by side with the Security team to understand current and emerging attack techniques against mobile apps, and translate them into well-framed data problems. Explore and analyze our telemetry (datalake on ClickHouse and S3) to uncover signals, patterns, and anomalies with detection value. Design, prototype, and evaluate attack detection and prevention models: anomaly detection, classification with scarce labels, behavioral models, event time-series analysis. Define how success is measured: detection metrics, acceptable false-positive rates, and evaluation methodology when complete ground truth doesn't exist. Take validated prototypes toward production in collaboration with the engineering team, and lay the foundations (features, datasets, labeling processes) for the team's ML capability to grow. Stay current with research in ML applied to security (anomaly detection, adversarial ML, fraud) and bring actionable ideas. Who are you? Proven experience (5+ years, or PhD plus applied experience) researching and developing ML models on real-world problems, ideally in security, fraud, anti-bot, anti-malware, or similar adversarial domains. Strong command of anomaly detection and unsupervised / semi-supervised learning: labeled data is scarce in this domain, and that shapes the entire approach. Experience with large-scale telemetry or event data: logs, time series, user or device behavior data. Full autonomy with raw data: solid Python (pandas/polars, scikit-learn, PyTorch or similar), advanced SQL, and comfort working directly against a datalake without prepared datasets. Product mindset: the ability to go from a research idea to an evaluable prototype in weeks, not months, and to communicate results to non-technical stakeholders. Genuine curiosity about cybersecurity and the drive to learn the domain in depth alongside the team's experts. Nice to have Prior experience in mobile security, EDR, banking anti-fraud, or intrusion detection systems. Knowledge of adversarial machine learning (model evasion, robustness). Experience with AWS S3, ClickHouse or other high-volume analytical databases. Publications, open-source contributions, or talks in applied ML or security. Experience deploying models to production (basic MLOps). Practically Speaking, What's In It For You The chance to define the company's ML strategy from scratch, with direct product impact and full visibility. A technically fascinating problem: a real adversary that evolves, massive untapped data, and freedom to research. Daily collaboration with a Security team with deep domain expertise. Optimized onboarding – for your optimal start and customized induction. Technical ownership – take responsibility for key components and shape how we build our platform. Enthusiastic team – waiting to help you succeed and collaborate with experienced engineers. Beautiful office spaces – in the heart of Barcelona, 200m from Sants Estació with regular team/community events (breakfast, lunch…). Good transport connections – easy to reach by public transport. Flexible working hours & Hybrid working!

items.desc: À propos de nous L’IRT Jules Verne est le centre de recherche industriel et collaboratif au service du manufacturing, qui œuvre pour renforcer la compétitivité des usines en France. L’équipe de Recherche Technologique « Monitoring, Inspection & Contrôle procédés » (ERT MIC) est composée d’une quinzaine de collaborateurs, docteurs(es), ingénieurs(es) et techniciens(nnes), en charge de développer des solutions d’inspection innovantes et de les déployer en production et en maintenance dans l’industrie aéronautique, navale, l’énergie et le transport. Son objectif est de réduire les coûts d’inspection. Pour cela, l’équipe MIC développe des technologies innovantes en surveillance des procédés (PHM), contrôles non destructifs (CND) et contrôle santé intégré (SHM). Enfin, l’ERT MIC propose autour de ces trois activités les outils numériques indispensables à l’analyse automatique en temps réel des données collectées pour réduire le facteur humain, rétroagir sur les procédés, faciliter le travail des opérateurs… et assurer la continuité numérique de l’ensemble des opérations d’inspection. Les projets menés dans l’équipe sont de natures variées : des projets collaboratifs multi partenaires industriels de l’IRT JV, de la prestation de recherche et des projets européens. Mission L'équipe MIC recherche un(e) Ingénieur(e) R&D Data Scientist, pour un CDD de 12 mois , dans le cadre du développement de nos activités autour de l'exploitation et de l'analyse des données par Intelligence Artificielle (IA) des données CND, SHM et PHM. Fort(e) d’une expérience en R&D industrielle , vous savez anticiper les risques techniques, prendre du recul et adapter vos développements aux contraintes du terrain. Was wir suchen Wir suchen eine neugierige, unternehmerisch denkende Person, die KI nicht nur verfolgt, sondern selbst ausprobiert. Du bist nah an den aktuellen Entwicklungen, entdeckst neue Modelle, Tools und Ansätze früh und prüfst praktisch, was davon mehr ist als Hype. Aus deinen Tests leitest du konkrete Ideen ab, wie wir unsere Technologie besser machen können. Du arbeitest eigenständig, bewegst dich gern zwischen Experiment und produktiver Umsetzung und möchtest technische Entscheidungen und die Entwicklung unseres Produkts aktiv mitgestalten. Deine Aufgaben Du passt KI-Modelle an unsere Anforderungen an, zum Beispiel durch Fine-Tuning. Du entwickelst Harnesses, um Modelle und neue Ansätze systematisch zu testen und zu bewerten. Du arbeitest mit AWS und bringst KI-Anwendungen in Richtung produktiver Nutzung. Du verfolgst laufend neue Entwicklungen in KI und Software – von neuen Modellen und Tools bis zu Techniken, über die sich die AI-Community austauscht. Du testest vielversprechende Ansätze selbst, baust sie in unsere Umgebung ein, und bewertest, was davon für unser Produkt wirklich nützlich ist. Du teilst deine Einschätzung mit dem Team: Was ist Hype, was könnte relevant werden und was sollten wir als Nächstes ausprobieren? Du gestaltest unsere Architektur und technische Richtung mit und hilfst uns, eine marktführende Technologie aufzubauen. Das bringst du mit Berufserfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung. Erfahrung mit KI-Modellen und idealerweise mit deren Anpassung oder Fine-Tuning. Erfahrung darin, Software zu entwickeln und technische Lösungen eigenständig umzusetzen. Erfahrung mit AWS oder vergleichbaren Cloud-Umgebungen. Du bist neugierig auf neue KI-Technologien und hältst dich selbstständig auf dem Laufenden, zum Beispiel über Online-Communities und Plattformen wie X. Du probierst neue Ansätze gerne praktisch aus und kannst einschätzen und erklären, was davon für unser Produkt relevant sein könnte. Du arbeitest selbstständig und kannst deine technischen Entscheidungen begründen. Deutschkenntnisse sind hilfreich, aber keine Voraussetzung. Erfahrung mit Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, PEFT/LoRA, Model Evaluation oder Model Serving ist hilfreich. Was wir bieten Eine Vollzeitrolle mit viel Gestaltungsspielraum und direktem Einfluss auf Produkt und technische Entscheidungen. Die Möglichkeit, neue Technologien praktisch zu erproben und mit uns weiterzuentwickeln. items.desc: About this opportunity This role is being recruited by Calyptus on behalf of one of our clients. Calyptus is a specialist recruitment partner helping startups and high-growth technology companies hire across engineering, product and design. What to expect We’ll review your application and, if your experience is a strong match, one of our team will be in touch We’ll support you throughout the interview process and keep you updated at each stage If this particular role isn’t the right fit, we may consider you for other relevant opportunities with our clients ______________________________________________________ A new open-source model is released and you are compelled to reach inside and understand how it actually works. You instinctively try to push it beyond what most people say is already impressive. You observe model behavior and don’t think, “What’s a better prompt?”, but “How do I improve its fundamentals?” Our Senior Machine Learning Engineer will operate deep within the model stack, working directly with weights, activations, and architectures to build the systems that make AI governance deterministic. Your work powers the Policy Engine, the core technology that gives enterprises real-time, auditable control over model behavior in production. Your mandate is ostensibly simple but difficult in execution: determine how a model can be improved for a specific purpose and build the systems that operationalize that within our platform. As opposed to simply using models, you will probe the mechanics of their cognition. What You Will Do Take ideas from mechanistic interpretability and related work and turn them into code that runs in production, making research into reality. Work directly with model internals to improve behavior and performance across commercial and open-source models. Leverage techniques like activation patching, control vectors, and feature extraction to achieve targeted, repeatable improvements in model output. Build the evaluation and deployment loops needed to ship changes reliably into enterprise environments. Design and optimize the feature-level intervention systems that enable deterministic policy enforcement at inference time. Who You Are Strong understanding of Transformer architectures, PyTorch internals, and the mathematical foundations of deep learning. Have trained, fine-tuned, or optimized models beyond superficial augmentation. Can read a paper, decide what matters, and implement it. Notice when something is not working and take ownership of fixing it. Motivated by the challenge of making large language models reliable and controllable enough for the highest-stakes enterprise applications. Our Stack Languages: Python, Rust, and Node/TypeScript, with React on the frontend Data: Postgresql, vector, and graph databases Infra: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, across several cloud providers and customer VPCs ML: Self hosted models on multiple GPU providers and frontier APIs ______________________________________________________ Genuine opportunities Every role advertised by Calyptus is a live position we’re actively recruiting for. Some clients prefer to remain confidential during the early stages of the hiring process. When that’s the case, certain company details may be shared later in the process. Why work with Calyptus? Access opportunities with ambitious startups and high-growth technology companies Direct support from experienced specialist recruiters Honest feedback and clear communication throughout the hiring process Long-term career support, not just a single job application We look forward to hearing from you.

items.desc: About The Role About ElevenLabs ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. How we work High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. What we offer Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy. Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. About the role We are looking for a Research Engineer to join the research team at ElevenLabs, focused on large-scale web crawling for our frontier AI models. The quality of our models is bounded by the quality and scale of the data behind them, and you will own the crawling systems that source world-class data from the open web. You will thrive in this role if you enjoy: Building and operating large-scale, distributed web crawlers that discover, fetch, and extract data across billions of pages reliably and efficiently. Solving hard crawling problems such as content extraction from messy HTML, deduplication at web scale, freshness and recrawl strategies, and politeness and rate-limit handling. Designing targeted crawling pipelines that find high-value data sources, including audio, video, and multilingual content, and turn them into clean training-ready datasets. Creating tooling and infrastructure that lets researchers request, monitor, and explore newly crawled web data quickly and reliably. Requirements We do not require any formal certifications or degrees. Instead, we are seeking enthusiastic engineers who can showcase solving impressively hard problems with artifacts such as past projects, designs, or GitHub contributions. Ideally, you bring: Hands-on experience building and scaling web crawlers or scraping systems, ideally in support of machine learning training data. Strong engineering skills in distributed systems at scale (e.g., Kubernetes, queue-based architectures, or custom pipelines processing billions of documents). The capacity to autonomously evaluate the quality, coverage, and compliance of crawled data, and to build the tooling to measure it. Location This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, San Francisco, and Warsaw. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses. items.desc: ¡Hola! Somos OGA Nos ilusiona que estés considerando esta oportunidad de empleo. Esto lo conseguimos gracias al talento de nuestro equipo, que incluye a matemáticos/as, estadísticos/as o desarrolladores/as de software, entre otros, y a la confianza de grandes clientes. Además, mantenemos una estrecha colaboración con la Universidad a través de nuestro Consejo Asesor Tecnológico, Grupo CÁTEDRA, compuesto por 14 catedráticos de renombre nacional e internacional, especializados en Investigación Operativa y ciencia de datos, y con el que reforzamos nuestra propuesta y valor científico. Colaboración e innovación Trabajar con equipos de Ingeniería de Datos, Investigación Operativa e Ingeniería de Software. Traducir necesidades de negocio en problemas de modelado y evaluación. Personalize results using Bayesian hierarchies and time-series methods to learn individual baselines and detect meaningful changes. Requirements Already based in Berlin (non-negotiable) Eager to work in an early-stage, science-driven, female health startup Comfortable with ambiguity, self-directed, and proactive Benefits Hybrid work environment with office space in Berlin A competitive salary for 1 year with the possibility of extension pHera is closing the gender health gap! Most existing vaginal pH test strips are analog, low-resolution, visually subjective, and poorly suited for women’s health applications. Doctors need fast, reliable tools to help with complicated diagnoses. Women deserve clarity, not guesswork when managing their vaginal health from home. A high-resolution pH test can catch imbalances early, making it easier to monitor issues like bacterial vaginosis, recurring vaginal infections, sexually transmitted infections, ovulation, PCOS, and menopause. By building pHera, you would be building a tool that would advance women's health .

items.desc: About this opportunity This role is being recruited by Calyptus on behalf of one of our clients. Calyptus is a specialist recruitment partner helping startups and high-growth technology companies hire across engineering, product and design. What to expect We’ll review your application and, if your experience is a strong match, one of our team will be in touch We’ll support you throughout the interview process and keep you updated at each stage If this particular role isn’t the right fit, we may consider you for other relevant opportunities with our clients ______________________________________________________ The role The core of this job is taking raw sensor data from extrusion lines and building the algorithm that decides what the line should do differently. It has to be right often enough, and explain itself well enough, that an experienced operator will act on it. In time it will drive setpoints directly, so it also has to know when it does not know. Getting the recommendation right is only half the job. The other half is understanding how and when a recommendation can safely become an actual setpoint change on the machine, and building the supervisory control layer that makes that happen without fighting the line's existing controls or its operators. You will also be responsible for version one of the product around that algorithm: the data platform, the models, the deployment and the application operators use. This is a senior, hands-on role with ownership of the technical stack. You will make the architectural calls, write the code, spend time on customer sites and help hire the engineers who follow. What you will do The decision-making algorithm Design and build the core algorithm that turns live sensor data into decisions: which setpoints to change, by how much and when. Frame the problem properly. Decide whether it is best treated as prediction plus optimisation, model predictive control, Bayesian optimisation, contextual bandits, offline reinforcement learning or a combination, and justify the choice with evidence. Build process models that link settings and operating conditions to quality, scrap, throughput and energy, and that respect the dynamics of the process, including time delays, dead time and variation in raw material. Learn from historical data in which settings were rarely varied deliberately. Deal with confounding, operator interventions and changes of regime, and design safe experiments on live lines to fill the gaps. Quantify uncertainty and build in the ability to make no recommendation when conditions fall outside what the model has seen. Evaluate decisions properly: offline policy evaluation before anything goes live, and controlled trials against real production outcomes afterwards. Sensor data and features Build the pipeline from raw sensor data to model-ready features, covering synchronisation, resampling, lag alignment, filtering, missing data and faulty sensors. Develop soft sensors for quality measures that are only taken occasionally or offline. Link process data to production context such as product, recipe, material batch and shift. Detect anomalies, sensor faults and model drift, and retrain as lines, materials and products change. From recommendation to setpoint change Work out, for each adjustable variable, when a recommendation can safely be applied, taking account of process state, operating envelope, rate of change, interaction with other variables and the time the process needs to settle. Design the supervisory layer that sits above the line's existing PLC control loops, adjusting their setpoints while those loops continue to regulate the process, and make sure it never works against them. Define the conditions under which the system must hold or hand control back to the operator, such as start-up, product changeovers, alarms, sensor faults or unfamiliar material, and make handover between manual and automatic operation smooth. Monitor the effect of every change and reverse it automatically if the process does not respond as expected. Design the staged route from advisory to closed-loop operation, with clear, measurable criteria for when a line, or an individual variable, is ready for the next stage. Specify how setpoints are written back to the PLC (range checks, rate limits, reversibility and fallback to the last known good state), working with our integration partner and the customer's engineers. Machine safety functions stay in the PLC's safety layer and are never overridden by our software. Present recommendations with the reasoning behind them, in a form operators can check quickly and trust. The Centre for Health Economics & Policy Innovation (CHEPI) at Imperial Business School is seeking a Research Associate /
items.desc: Job number: BUS00904 Salary or Salary range: £50,733 - £67,351 per annum Posting End Date: 22 Nov 2026 About the role Build the Next Generation of Health Policy Simulation Models Do you want your research to influence how governments design policies to prevent chronic disease? Are you excited by the challenge of combining data, simulation, and policy to tackle the world’s biggest health problems? The Centre for Health Economics & Policy Innovation (CHEPI) at Imperial Business School is seeking a Research Associate / Research Fellow in Computational Health Policy Modelling to play a central role in developing Health-GPS — our state-of-the-art microsimulation model for non-communicable disease (NCD) policy analysis. Appointment will be made at Research Associate or Research Fellow level, depending on experience. Why This Role Matters Chronic diseases such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease remain leading causes of illness and premature death worldwide. Yet, the tools available to evaluate and design effective prevention policies are still evolving. Health-GPS provides a framework to explore how changes in diet, physical activity, and related risk factors affect long-term population health and economic outcomes. Health-GPS represents the gradual accumulation and interaction of individual-level risk factors — such as BMI, diet, and income — offering insights into the potential impact of different policy interventions over time. You will help develop and apply this model across major international projects including: GOLDFINCH – estimating the effects of fiscal policies on ultra-processed food consumption. JA Prevent NCD – a European Joint Action on integrated strategies for NCD prevention. JACARDI – a European initiative to reduce cardiovascular and diabetes risk. Working with economists, epidemiologists, and data scientists, you’ll push the boundaries of policy simulation and shape real-world decision-making. This is a hands-on computational role. Alongside using Health-GPS for policy analysis, you will write, test and review code in its C++ codebase, working within the team’s collaborative development workflow (version control, pull requests and code review). C++ experience is highly desirable, but we also welcome strong programmers in other relevant languages who are willing to work in C++. What you would be doing Contribute to the architecture, development, optimisation, and maintenance of Health-GPS, writing and reviewing code in its C++ codebase and ensuring its continued scientific and policy relevance. Work with colleagues to plan and deliver modelling work across multiple projects, producing high-quality outputs on time. Help integrate new methodologies, including AI and machine-learning approaches, into simulation design. Conduct quantitative analyses to estimate the health and economic impact of proposed policies. Identify and manage relevant datasets in collaboration with internal and external partners. Communicate findings through academic papers, policy briefs, and stakeholder workshops. Contribute to funding proposals and the expansion of CHEPI’s modelling activities. What we are looking for We’re seeking a creative and technically strong individual with: A PhD (or equivalent, or near completion) in health economics, epidemiology, computer science, or a related field. Experience building or using microsimulation models or other quantitative policy tools. Strong programming skills in at least one language (e.g. Python, R, or C++), and experience contributing to a shared codebase using version control (e.g. git). Experience working with large or longitudinal datasets. The ability to translate complex model outputs into actionable policy insights. Curiosity, independence, and enthusiasm for multidisciplinary collaboration. Experience with C++ is highly desirable. Experience applying AI or ML methods to health or policy modelling is also desirable. Candidates for appointment as Research Fellow should also demonstrate a strong publication record, experience contributing to funding proposals, and the ability to design and lead original research. What we can offer you The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to use science for humanity. Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression. Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes). Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing . Further information Interested? items.desc: We are seeking a motivated and collaborative individual to join our team as a Research Associate within the Department of Chemistry, School of Natural Sciences. This exciting research project aims to produce ultra-thin polymer-based membranes and fluidic chips with polymers of intrinsic porosity (PIMs), to study molecular and ionic permeation for ionic gating, ionic memory applications, and molecular separations. You will be expected to publish academic papers and contribute towards advanced new concepts. You will be responsible for: Conduct original research and collaborate within the group and internationally as per the project needs Develop research objectives and proposals for own or joint research, with the assistance of a mentor if required. Conduct individual and collaborative research projects. Write up research work for publication. Training students and others in skills appropriate to the project. We welcome candidates who bring diverse perspectives, experiences, and approaches to their work. About You We encourage applications from individuals with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. You should demonstrate: Essential Criteria A PhD (or be about to obtain) in electrochemistry, polymer science or membranes with experimental work in chemistry, materials science or chemical engineering. Experience of working with electrochemical measurements, electrical source meters, precision electrical meters, patch-clamp amplifiers, neuromorphic measurements. Significant experience of nanofabrication, measurement and characterization of ultrathin membranes, 2D materials van der Waals heterostructures. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Desirable Criteria Expertise in electrochemistry. Experience of working in nanofluidics/membrane technologies. Experience in clean room micro/nanofabrication and working with 2D materials devices. Experience of sequencing measurements with biomolecules. We value transferable skills and real-world experience as much as formal qualifications. items.desc: Your job Do you want to contribute to the innovations shaping the future of sustainable horticulture and agriculture? As a Research Software Engineer, you will develop applications, data solutions, and software building blocks that support our research and innovation projects. You could be working on autonomous greenhouse control, ranging from climate management to robotics for crop scouting or crop maintenance. You will also help improve the standardization, accessibility, and reuse of data from greenhouses and field experiments, enabling stronger insights across projects. Working closely with researchers and industry partners, you will help transform ideas into practical digital solutions while ensuring they remain reliable, scalable, and reusable. Your duties and responsibilities as a research software engineer include: develop software tools and applications for research, experimentation, and decision support both for colleagues and growers; build and maintain data infrastructures, databases, and integrations between control systems and sensors; develop dashboards and analytics solutions that turn research data into actionable insights for colleagues and our customers; collaborate with researchers and project partners to translate scientific and operational needs into software solutions; enable the long-term reuse, scalability, and quality of software and data solutions across multiple projects. Your team You will be part of the Greenhouse Automation and Robotics team, a multidisciplinary group that combines expertise in AI, sensor technology, and robotics. The team develops innovative solutions for both greenhouse horticulture and open-field agriculture. You will work in an environment where collaboration, knowledge sharing, and innovation are at the core, with plenty of opportunities to take initiative and turn new ideas into reality. This provides an inspiring and supportive workplace with a strong connection between technology and real-world agricultural applications. Your primary workplace will be Wageningen, where you will be based for most of your work. Depending on project needs, you may also spend time at other locations, such as Bleiswijk or field sites where experiments and trials are conducted. Your qualities We are looking for a versatile Research Software Engineer who enjoys working at the intersection of software development, data engineering, and applied research. You are able to understand the needs of researchers and project partners and translate them into practical, robust, and user-friendly software solutions. You enjoy working in multidisciplinary teams and are comfortable switching between project-specific developments and more generic software components that can be reused across multiple projects. You Also Possess a bachelor's or master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or a related field; several years of experience in software development, data engineering, or a similar role; strong programming skills in Python; experience with C++ and/or C# is an advantage; experience with databases, data pipelines, and modern data engineering practices; familiarity with tools such as Airflow or TimescaleDB is a plus; experience with robotics software, ROS 2, machine learning, or related technologies is an advantage. In our international working environment there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about language level (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-1-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-global-scale) B2. We offer Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/conditions-of-employment). A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include: working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance; sabbatical leave, study leave, and partially paid parental leave; there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee; a fixed year-end bonus of 8,3%; excellent pension scheme. In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will of course receive a good salary. We offer, depending on your experience, a competitive gross salary of between € 3,554.- and € 5,698.- for a full-time working week of 36 hours, in accordance with the CLA Wageningen Research (scale 10). Additionally, for this role a contract for 32 to 36 hours can be discussed. We initially offer a one-year contract, with the possibility of renewal subject to satisfactory performance and depending on the organisation’s financial situation. We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help. Coming from abroad WUR welcomes applications from international …

items.desc: Research Fellow – SHIFTIN Project | UCL University College London (UCL) – The Bartlett School of Sustainable Construction Location: London, UK (Hybrid) Salary: £43,981–£54,019 per annum Contract: Full-time, fixed-term (12 months, potential extension subject to funding) Closing date: 9 November 2026 Job reference: B04-07915 About the Role We are seeking an ambitious and highly motivated Research Fellow to join our growing research team at University College London and contribute to SHIFTIN, a Horizon Europe-funded project advancing circular reconstruction, sustainable materials and resilient transport infrastructure. The position offers an exciting opportunity to develop innovative approaches to infrastructure reconstruction, including transforming war-damaged construction materials into low-carbon infrastructure solutions and supporting real-world demonstrations in Ukraine. The successful candidate will collaborate with leading European research institutions, industry partners and infrastructure stakeholders. Key Responsibilities Research circular construction materials and recycled aggregates from war-damaged infrastructure. Develop and assess sustainable modular structural components. Apply complex systems modelling, infrastructure network analysis and multi-hazard stress testing. Integrate Digital Twins, AI and geospatial methods into infrastructure resilience assessment. Evaluate whole-life sustainability, circularity, structural performance and environmental impacts. Support demonstrations and validation activities in Ukraine. Contribute to scientific publications, European project deliverables, policy recommendations and stakeholder engagement. Essential Qualifications and Experience Applicants should demonstrate: A PhD in Civil, Structural, Materials or Transport Infrastructure Engineering, or a closely related discipline. Experience in experimental or computational research relevant to sustainable construction, infrastructure systems or materials. Strong analytical skills, including computational modelling, data analysis or related methods. Knowledge of infrastructure resilience, circularity, sustainability and whole-life performance. Evidence of high-quality research outputs and effective scientific communication. Experience contributing to collaborative research projects, including European research programmes. Expertise in Digital Twins, AI, geospatial analysis, infrastructure networks, climate resilience or circular materials is particularly welcome. Salary and Benefits UCL offers a salary of £43,981–£54,019 , together with: 41 days of holiday, including bank holidays and university closure days. Defined benefit pension scheme. Hybrid working arrangements. Additional annual leave purchase scheme. Cycle-to-work scheme and season ticket loans. Relocation and immigration loan schemes, subject to eligibility. items.desc: The University of Southampton is inviting applications for a postdoctoral position (Research Fellow) in numerical relativity. The successful candidate will undertake research as part of the recently awarded STFC grant Simulating realistic neutron-star mergers. Southampton's School of Mathematical Sciences is home to a large research group in gravitational physics, currently comprising 7 staff members and a number of postdocs and PhD students. Research in the group includes black-hole and neutron-star physics, gravitational-wave source modelling and data analysis, numerical relativity and gravitational self-force modelling. Members of the group are actively involved with the LIGO Scientific Collaboration, the Einstein Telescope Collaboration and the LISA Consortium. The successful applicant will contribute to work aimed at carrying out numerical simulations of neutron star mergers with realistic physics, with particular focus of resistive magnetohydrodynamics. The ideal candidate will have a track record in numerical relativity and ideally some understanding of neutron star modelling, gravitational-wave astronomy and data analysis. Applicants will have, or be about to obtain, a relevant PhD degree in physics or mathematics. This is a fixed term post until 30th September 2027. A complete application should include (i) a CV, including a list of publications, and (ii) a statement of research interests (no more than 1 page). Informal enquiries may be made to Prof. Ian Hawke at I.Hawke@soton.ac.uk. Lenovo’s continued investment in world-changing innovation is building a more equitable, trustworthy, and smarter future for everyone, everywhere. This transformation together with Lenovo’s world-changing innovation is building a more inclusive, trustworthy, and smarter future for everyone, everywhere. To find out more visit www.lenovo.com, and read about the latest news via our StoryHub. Lenovo is a global leader in AI infrastructure, high-performance computing, and data centre technologies, helping customers build and scale next-generation accelerated computing environments. As part of the Lenovo Infrastructure Deployment Services (LIDS) team, you will support the validation, benchmarking, and optimisation of large-scale HPC and AI solutions for some of Lenovo's most strategic global customers. In this role, you will execute performance testing, analyse benchmark results, and provide optimisation recommendations across cutting-edge HPC and AI environments, working closely with customers, architects, consultants, and engineering teams. Design and execute benchmarking and performance test plans across compute, storage, networking, GPUs, and AI workloads, then analyze and present results. Profile applications, identify performance bottlenecks, and provide practical optimization recommendations for HPC, AI, and GPU-accelerated environments. Work with industry-standard HPC benchmarks, AI training and inference workloads, MPI-based applications, storage testing tools, and large-scale cluster validation processes. Partner closely with customers, solution architects, technical consultants, delivery teams, and technology partners to support successful solution deployment and operational readiness. Contribute to the development of benchmarking methodologies, best practices, technical documentation, training materials, and knowledge-sharing initiatives that strengthen Lenovo’s global HPC and AI capabilities. What You Will Bring Strong experience with High Performance Computing (HPC) environments, including cluster architectures, Linux administration, job scheduling, and distributed computing. Proven ability to execute, analyse, and optimise HPC benchmarks and performance validation tests across compute, storage, and networking infrastructure. Solid knowledge of parallel computing technologies, including MPI, OpenMP, CUDA, NCCL, and GPU-accelerated applications. Experience benchmarking and tuning scientific, engineering, AI, and data analytics workloads on large-scale HPC platforms. Strong understanding of NVIDIA GPU technologies and architectures, including H100, H200, B200, and GB200/GB300. Hands-on experience with high-performance networking technologies such as InfiniBand and RoCEv2. Expertise with industry-standard benchmark suites including HPL, HPL-MxP, HPCG, IO500, MLPerf, STREAM, FIO, IOR, and NCCL tests. Knowledge of Top500, Green500, customer acceptance testing methodologies, and HPC performance benchmarking best practices. Experience working with HPC storage solutions such as Lustre, GPFS (IBM Storage Scale), BeeGFS, VAST, WEKA, or similar parallel file systems. Strong Linux skills across RHEL, Rocky Linux, and Ubuntu, combined with shell scripting for automation, benchmark execution, and performance analysis. Ability to identify performance bottlenecks, deliver optimisation recommendations, and create customer-facing benchmark reports, technical documentation, and performance studies. Excellent communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work directly with customers, architects, and engineering teams; experience with AI infrastructure benchmarking, LLMs, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Kubernetes, OpenShift, cloud HPC (Azure/AWS/GCP), Python automation, GPU profiling tools, and enterprise AI acceptance testing is highly desirable. items.desc: Build a Rewarding Career. Doing things differently. Research Fellow in Nonlinear Photonics £39,984 - £44,977 p.a. pro rata Full time/Fixed Term - 2 years starting on 1st January 2027 (with the potential of extension). About The Role We are seeking a Research Fellow to join an exciting European Research Council funded project focused on nonlinear nanophotonics and nonlinear metasurface-enabled spectroscopy and imaging in the Advanced Optics and Photonics (AOP) Group. The research will explore how engineered optical resonances and nonlinear light-matter interactions can enable new approaches to near-infrared detection, optical frequency conversion and computational imaging. You will undertake innovative experimental and simulation-based research, contributing to the development of new knowledge in nonlinear nanophotonics, metasurfaces and optical spectroscopy. Key activities will include electromagnetic modelling, developing optical setups, measuring linear and nonlinear optical responses, and implementing imaging and image-reconstruction techniques. The work will investigate resonantly enhanced nonlinear processes, including harmonic generation and frequency mixing, and their application to wavelength conversion and the recovery of spatial and spectral information. You will contribute to research planning, data analysis, publications, conference presentations and future funding applications. You will also support the wider research environment through collaboration with academic partners, supervision of student projects and occasional teaching of research methods and techniques. This is an excellent opportunity to develop your research profile while contributing to a cutting-edge area of photonics research. items.desc: Company Description Join iLOF to turn challenging scientific questions into implemented analyses, reproducible workflows and useful results. With a primary focus on clinical projects and contributions to preclinical work, you will take ownership of analytical deliverables, investigate unresolved problems and help move projects from exploration to completion. You will work closely with other Data Scientists and scientific colleagues, translating project needs into concrete analytical solutions and communicating what the results mean. Prepare, explore and analyse experimental and associated clinical datasets, investigating quality issues and inconsistencies. Implement and evaluate statistical and machine learning methods appropriate to the question and available data. Take ownership of unresolved analytical problems, diagnose their causes and develop practical solutions. Produce reproducible code, analyses, visualisations and documentation that colleagues can review and reuse. Apply appropriate validation procedures and communicate uncertainty, limitations and alternative interpretations. Work with colleagues from other teams and disciplines to interpret findings in their experimental and clinical context. You bring mathematical discipline, strong implementation skills and a collaborative approach. You are comfortable working in an evolving environment while keeping your work structured, reproducible and focused on the project’s needs. Qualifications Degree in Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Statistics or a related quantitative discipline, supported by relevant applied experience. Professional experience delivering Data Science or quantitative analysis projects from problem definition through implementation. Strong scientific programming skills and the ability to write clear, maintainable analytical code. Practical knowledge of statistics, machine learning, data preparation and model evaluation. Ability to investigate unfamiliar datasets, troubleshoot analytical workflows and assess whether results are credible. Experience managing your own deliverables and communicating progress, dependencies and findings. Experience in a startup or another environment requiring ownership and adaptability is particularly valuable. Experience analysing biomedical, clinical or experimental data is advantageous. The opportunity Make a visible contribution to iLOF’s scientific programmes by solving difficult analytical problems and delivering work that colleagues can use to make decisions and advance projects. Additional Information iLOF in a nutshell As personalized medicine becomes the norm, scientists, patients, and healthcare systems worldwide face massive barriers in providing the right treatment to the right patient. Recognized by CB Insights and Financial Times as one of the most promising Digital Health companies in the world, iLOF is building an AI-powered platform capable of transforming precision medicine. Our goal is to become the platform that democratizes access to personalized medicine for millions of people living with complex diseases around the globe. Thanks to our proprietary optical fingerprint library of disease biomarkers and biological profiles we can offer personalized patient screening and stratification in a faster and more affordable way, saving up to 40% of the cost and 70% of the time while enabling a more human patient experience. Supported by leading institutions like Microsoft Ventures, Mayfield, and the Oxford University, iLOF is currently focusing on validating its platform technology in one of the biggest challenges of our times: Alzheimer's, while maintaining ongoing verticals on Digestive Cancer, Stroke, and Infectious diseases. Our Team ‍ We are a mix of scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors based in London and Porto, with a passion for healthcare! Recognized by CB Insights as one of the most promising Digital Health companies in the world and by the Financial Times as a Transformational Business in Healthcare, iLOF has been regularly featured in leading outlets like Tech Crunch, Wired, and Sifted and listed as a rising star in AI-Driven Drug Discovery, …

L'offre en un coup d'oeil L'unité Institut du Développement et des Ressources en Informatique Scientifique Type de Contrat IT en contrat de projet Temps de Travail Complet Lieu de Travail 91403 ORSAY Durée du contrat 13 mois Date d'Embauche 01/12/2026 Rémuneration de 4031 € brut/mois à 4530 € brut/mois négociable selon expérience Postuler Date limite de candidature : jeudi 12 novembre 2026 23:59 Description du Poste Les Missions L’ingénieure/ingénieur prend part au programme européen MINERVA, qui vise à mettre en place un service de support à l’échelle européenne qui vise à faciliter et optimiser l’utilisation des ressources des centres de calcul HPC nationaux à destination des communautés d’Intelligence Artificielle (IA) et du Machine Learning (ML). Organisé sous forme de projets à durée limitée, la mission de cette task-force européenne distribuée consiste, en collaboration avec d’autres centres européens d'excellence, à travailler sur des actions transverses de support applicatif de haut niveau pour les communautés scientifiques développant des méthodes d’IA à l’échelle d’infrastructures de calcul nationales. Les services de MINERVA sont stratégiquement alignés sur le besoin européen de s'appuyer sur des modèles de fondation open source entièrement développés conformément aux réglementations sur l'IA éthique et responsable incluses dans la loi sur l'IA. items.desc: At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done. We’re at the forefront of the data revolution, committed to building the world’s greatest data and applications platform. Our ‘get it done’ culture allows everyone at Snowflake to have an equal opportunity to innovate on new ideas, create work with a lasting impact, and excel in a culture of collaboration. We're looking for a talented and motivated Software Engineer to join the Cortex AI Functions Platform team. AI functions are how Snowflake customers call AI directly from SQL, running models over their own tables without moving data out of the platform. Our team builds the platform that makes this work at data warehouse scale, where a single statement can expand into a large volume of inference requests that must complete predictably, within expected cost, and without compromising the query when a dependency degrades or fails. Current projects include a new architecture for multi-modal inference, quality gates that let us ship new functions and models with confidence at batch scale, and support for input data beyond plain text. Alongside these, we work continuously on throughput, cost and reliability as customer usage grows, and on making failures in the inference path easier to detect, diagnose and recover from. For this role, you don’t need to have a research background, including pre-training or fine-tuning models. items.desc: À propos de nous Établissement Public à caractère Scientifique, Culturel et Professionnel (EPSCP), l’université de Tours est la première université de la région Centre-Val de Loire. Elle propose une offre de formation large, pluridisciplinaire, et interdisciplinaire et une recherche d’excellence reconnue. C’est aussi un établissement inscrit dans un environnement régional dynamique, connu pour la qualité de vie qu’il offre à ses habitants. Dans ce cadre, l’université de Tours se présente comme une université citoyenne, aux valeurs humanistes, socialement engagée, éthiquement responsable. L’université accueille 30 000 étudiantes et étudiants, et emploie aujourd'hui plus de 1200 personnels et plus de 1400 enseignants chercheurs. Pour accompagner son développement, l'université de Tours recrute chaque année de nouveaux talents. Ce poste, comme tous les postes de notre université, est ouvert aux candidats et candidates en situation de handicap. Mission Contexte Le projet de recherche européen PRIMA réexamine la façon dont la culture a été produite et diffusée en Europe moderne, entre 1575 et 1800. Hypothèse centrale : l'imprimé n'a pas été la technologie dominante de publication, le manuscrit est resté un support de publication massif pour les littérature, science et musique, notamment en Italie. Le projet cherche à établir qui produisait ces manuscrits, pour qui, en quelle quantité, selon quelles pratiques d'écriture, et les cas d'hybridation entre manuscrit et imprimé. Il combine méthodes qualitatives, approches quantitatives, traitements computationnels pour les fouille, production, recherche de données. Ses résultats incluent la constitution d'un centre d'études du manuscrit moderne et des publications en accès ouvert. L'ingénieur·e rejoindra le volet computationnel du projet, travaillera en interaction étroite avec les historien·ne·s, paléographes, littéraires. Pas de connaissance en paléographie exigée (formation interne). Goût du dialogue interdisciplinaire indispensable. Missions Segmentation, prétraitement des images : Reprendre, évaluer, améliorer l'outil de segmentation existant, analyse du papier. Concevoir les prétraitements adaptés aux documents anciens. Automatiser la chaîne pour la rendre exploitable sur des corpus de grande taille. Caractérisation des formes de lettres : Définir, implémenter des descripteurs. Évaluer comparativement ces représentations sur les corpus du projet. Classification, modélisation : Moissonnages des images et métadonnées des filigranes, mettre en œuvre des approches pour identifier et regrouper les allographes d'une même lettre et le motif du filigrane. Modéliser la dépendance de la graphie au contexte : position dans le mot, lettres voisines, ligatures. Comparer approches classiques et connexionnistes . Datation, localisation : Construire les distributions de référence à partir des documents datés et localisés fournis par l'équipe. Concevoir et valider les mesures de comparaison entre distributions, avec quantification de l'incertitude. Produire des résultats interprétables et discutables par les historien·ne·s du projet. Ingénierie, diffusion : Développer un code documenté, testé, versionné, reproductible. Constituer et documenter les jeux de données annotés dans une perspective de science ouverte. Participer à la rédaction des publications, présenter les travaux. Contribuer à l'encadrement technique de stagiaires/doctorant·e·s sur les aspects computationnels. Profil Savoir Requis : Domaine / Attendus : Traitement du signal et des images. / Filtrage, morphologie mathématique, segmentation, extraction et description de contours, analyse de formes, mise en correspondance Apprentissage automatique. / Classification supervisée et non supervisée, clustering, réduction de dimension, sélection de modèles, protocoles d'évaluation et validation croisée Modèles probabilistes. / Modèles graphiques et réseaux bayésiens, modèles de mélange, modèles séquentiels Apprentissage profond. / CNN pour la vision, architectures à attention et transformers , apprentissage auto-supervisé et par transfert, apprentissage métrique et few-shot Développement. / Python et son écosystème scientifique, Git, environnements reproductibles, calcul sur GPU Génie logiciel. / Code structuré, testé, documenté ; conception maintenable, évolutive Langues. / Français ou anglais courant ; lire, rédiger en anglais scientifique Le corpus est déséquilibré et faiblement annoté : maîtrise des méthodes adaptées aux données rares et bruitées appréciée Appréciés : Expérience en humanités numériques, travail avec des chercheur·se·s en sciences humaines ; Reconnaissance d'écriture manuscrite, familiarité avec des outils comme Transkribus, eScriptorium, Kraken ; Traitement automatique des langues : modèles de langue, modèles n-grammes, plongements lexicaux, correction et normalisation de textes bruités, langues anciennes ; Connaissance des standards de description et d'échange du patrimoine écrit ; Curiosité pour les …

To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are. That's why we built iwoca. It owns the full offer terms strategy for customers referred through the broker network – both first-time customers and repeat. The team sets pricing, loan amounts, durations, and broker commissions, and owns the UX that presents them to brokers and customers. The team is small and interdisciplinary, combining commercial strategy, engineering, and data science. The work translates business questions into quantitative problems, and findings into actionable decisions. Active projects include: Model-based pricing – creating a sophisticated model to offer bespoke pricing to each customer A no-fee test – examining how our product performs when we remove all drawdown fees, and how that influence customer repayment behaviour Testing longer-duration flexi-loan products with particular customer segments. Reintroductions - exploring the right offer terms to give returning customers The team is small and cross-functional – commercial strategy, engineering, design, and data science – and works across the full application stack, from the Broker API to the Introducer Portal brokers use. The role You'll model expected customer take-up rates, design experiments, and translate findings into pricing and product decisions for the acquisition channel that drives the most customer lifetime value (CLTV). Because the Broker Terms team is a young team, you'll influence how its analytical approach develops, not just what it produces. The work has direct commercial consequences: brokers act on what the team builds and tests, and that shapes which customers iwoca wins and on what terms. Offer terms and experimentation. You'll model how customers respond to offer terms and how brokers make decisions under uncertainty. You'll design experiments where causal inference is central: you'll need to know where standard A/B testing breaks down and what to reach for instead. Commercial translation. You'll work with commercial and strategy colleagues and see your analysis applied directly in day-to-day decisions. That includes meeting brokers in person – gaining context that shapes how you frame and interpret results – and coordinating with adjacent teams responsible for underwriting decisions, repeat lending, and offer construction. CLTV and customer journey. You'll think across the full broker-referred customer journey – from first funding to repeat – identifying what drives CLTV and what changes to offer terms or UX improve it. You own both the strategy and the mechanism, so your findings feed directly into what the team builds and tests. AI and ways of working. You'll use AI to accelerate and automate your analytical work – not occasionally, but as a default. You should have a view on where it genuinely helps and where a different approach is better. The Requirements Essential: Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field such as mathematics, physics, or statistics. You're comfortable with Bayesian reasoning, and have applied hierarchical models or formal decision-making under uncertainty in real work. Causal inference and experimentation. You've separated signal from noise in observational and experimental data. You know where A/B testing breaks down and what to reach for instead. You have experience with careful experimental design to facilitate clean, trustworthy results. Analytical ownership. You take loosely defined problems from start to finish – framing the question, choosing the method, and landing the answer with the people who act on it. Data tooling. You're proficient with data manipulation and modelling tools, and with scientific computing libraries (pandas, numpy, sklearn, PyMC). AI leverage. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.
 The Position
 At Roche, we advance science so that we all have more time with the people we love. A healthier future. For a world where everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for the generations to come. For this, we believe the next breakthrough in medicine will be powered by the intersection of computational engineering and biology. We are building the infrastructure that transforms AI from an experimental concept into a reliable, high-impact utility for our researchers.

Roche’s Research and Early Development organizations at Genentech (gRED) and Pharma (pRED) have demonstrated how these technologies accelerate R&D, leveraging data and novel computational models to drive impact. The new Computational Sciences Center of Excellence (CoE) is a strategic, unified group whose goal is to harness this transformative power of data and AI to assist scientists to deliver more innovative and transformative medicines for patients worldwide.

The AI Enablement Engineering group sits at the heart of this mission. We aren't just training models; we are building scalable systems, data pipelines, and intelligent applications that enable our scientists to work smarter, not harder. From optimizing model performance to designing end-to-end agentic workflows, our goal is to put powerful AI tools directly into the hands of those driving drug discovery to power data-driven science and accelerate decision making. 
 We are a cross-functional, impact-driven team that values cognitive diversity and technical excellence. Here, you’ll partner with biologists, computational scientists, data experts, and researchers to architect a future where AI/ML is an essential component of every scientific discovery. If you’re an engineer who thrives on solving complex problems, spans the stack with curiosity, and wants to build tools that truly change lives, we want to hear from you.

 Contribute independently to defined projects by writing maintainable code and applying software engineering best practices (testing, CI/CD, documentation) alongside AI tooling and quantitative metrics to evaluate and scale ML systems. 
 Contribute to architectural decisions, code reviews, and the evolution of our development processes. 
 Be willing to span the stack and contribute where needed, even outside of your core area of expertise.

items.desc:
WHY FACULTY? 


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here https://faculty.ai/impact.



We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.



Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.



AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.




ABOUT THE TEAM 



Bringing medicine to patients is complex, expensive and high-risk. Faculty’s Life Science’s team is concentrated on building AI solutions which optimise the research and commercialisation of life-changing therapies.

We partner with major pharma firms, academic research centres and MedTech start-ups to design and deliver solutions which address critical healthcare challenges, and help to democratise health for all.




ABOUT THE ROLE



Join us as a Machine Learning Engineer to deliver bespoke, impactful AI solutions for our diverse clients.

You will be instrumental in bringing machine learning out of the lab and into the real world, contributing to scalable software architecture and defining best practices. Working with clients, and cross-functional teams, you'll ensure technical feasibility and timely delivery of high-quality, production-grade ML systems. 




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:



 - Building and deploying production-grade ML software, tools, and infrastructure.

 - Creating reusable, scalable solutions that accelerate the delivery of ML systems.

 - Collaborating with engineers, data scientists, and commercial leads to solve critical client challenges.

 - Leading technical scoping and architectural decisions to ensure project feasibility and impact.

 - Defining and implementing Faculty’s standards for deploying machine learning at scale.

 - Acting as a technical advisor to customers and partners, translating complex ML concepts for stakeholders.
   
   


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR:



 - You understand the full machine learning lifecycle and have experience operationalising models built with frameworks like Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, or PyTorch.

 - You possess strong Python skills and solid experience in software engineering best practices.

 - You bring hands-on experience with cloud platforms and infrastructure (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP), including architecture and security.

 - You've worked with container and orchestration tools such at Docker & Kubernetes to build and manage applications at scale

 - You are comfortable with core ML concepts, including probability, statistics, and common learning techniques.

 - You're an excellent communicator, able to guide technical teams and confidently advise non-technical stakeholders.

 - You thrive in a fast-paced environment, and enjoy the autonomy to own scope, solve and delivery solutions




THE INTERVIEW PROCESS



 1. Talent Team Screen (30 minutes)

 2. Pair Programming Interview (90 minutes) 

 3. System Design Interview (90 minutes) 

 4. Commercial Interview (60 minutes)




OUR RECRUITMENT ETHOS




We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.



If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours. 



A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

items.desc: L'offre en un coup d'oeil L'unité Institut du Développement et des Ressources en Informatique Scientifique Type de Contrat IT en contrat de projet Temps de Travail Complet Lieu de Travail 91403 ORSAY Durée du contrat 13 mois Date d'Embauche 01/12/2026 Rémuneration de 4031 € brut/mois à 4530 € brut/mois négociable selon expérience Date limite de candidature : jeudi 12 novembre 2026 23:59 Description du Poste Les Missions L’ingénieure/ingénieur prend part au programme européen MINERVA, qui vise à mettre en place un service de support à l’échelle européenne qui vise à faciliter et optimiser l’utilisation des ressources des centres de calcul HPC nationaux à destination des communautés d’Intelligence Artificielle (IA) et du Machine Learning (ML). Organisé sous forme de projets à durée limitée, la mission de cette task-force européenne distribuée consiste, en collaboration avec d’autres centres européens d'excellence, à travailler sur des actions transverses de support applicatif de haut niveau pour les communautés scientifiques développant des méthodes d’IA à l’échelle d’infrastructures de calcul nationales. Dans le projet MINERVA, l’IDRIS est en charge du développement et de la mise à jour du portefeuille de services et de la fourniture de ces services. Les services de MINERVA sont stratégiquement alignés sur le besoin européen de s'appuyer sur des modèles de fondation open source entièrement développés conformément aux réglementations sur l'IA éthique et responsable incluses dans la loi sur l'IA. Les services se concentrent sur les grands modèles d'IA, avec un accent particulier sur les modèles de fondation open source, y compris le support de pré-entrainement (le transfert et le prétraitement des données, la tokenisation, le parallélisme de modèles et de données), l'adaptation des LMM aux applications en aval et l'adaptation de la charge aux ressources HPC. Au sein de l’équipe « Support aux utilisateurs IA » de l’IDRIS, l’ingénieure/ingénieur mène des missions d’expertise à la convergence de l’IA et du HPC en collaboration avec les autres centres européens membres du programme MINERVA Son travail consistera à accompagner les communautés d’IA et de ML à maitriser les ressources d’un supercalculateur, de répondre aux questions des utilisateurs, à installer les piles logicielles adaptées, rédiger de la documentation en ligne, participer à des formations, faire de la veille technologique. Elle/il connaît le fonctionnement du centre de calcul et est capable de conseiller les utilisateurs sur l’optimisation de leurs usages des ressources matérielles et logicielles du centre. L'Activité Assurer un support technique en distanciel ou présentiel aux projets du programme MINERVA, organiser son travail sur une durée limitée afin d’atteindre les objectifs fixés, et communiquer régulièrement sur l’avancée du projet. Identifier et répondre aux besoins des projets européens sélectionnés par le programme MINERVA Assurer un accompagnement technique et scientifique dans le domaine de l'IA, aussi bien sur les aspects méthodologiques, algorithmiques que logiciels, à destination des utilisateurs du projet MINERVA Contribuer activement à l'activité de veille technologique avancée sur les évolutions dans le domaine de l'IA (architectures de modèle, méthodes de distribution, optimisation d’entraînement, logiciels, conteneurisation, accélérateurs, optimisations matérielles, etc) Organiser, définir, construire et dispenser de nouvelles formations et workshops à destination des utilisateurs IA du projet MINERVA Proposer, planifier, organiser et mettre en œuvre le déploiement, l'exploitation, les tests de fonctionnalité, de non régression et de performance des environnements spécifiques et des piles logicielles répondant aux besoins des utilisateurs et participer à leur maintenance sur le long terme Interagir avec les autres partenaires du projet, participer aux réunions d’avancement du projet et aux réflexions sur les activités ou réalisations à mettre en production. Gérer l’avancement de l’ensemble des partenaires sur le WP dont l’IDRIS est responsable, organiser la répartition du travail en fonction des engagements, faire respecter les délais et superviser la rédaction de l’ensemble des délivrables dont l’IDRIS a la charge.
