items.desc: Homa is a global mobile game developer and publisher creating games people love. We partner with studios and internally develop games, having launched over 80 titles, reached over 2 billion downloads, and seen our game All in Hole break into the global top-50 grossing charts. These are milestones, not the finish line. With deep expertise in product and technology, we built Homa Lab, our proprietary platform that gives developers the market intelligence, data tools, and game tech, with AI built in, to find product–market fit fast and scale mass-market games into lasting experiences players enjoy for years. This is our flywheel: Homa Lab helps studios spot the right ideas early, turn them into games quickly, and reach millions of players. Every launch brings back data and insights that fuel the next hit, making each turn of the loop faster, smarter, and more likely to win. AI supercharges this process, running through everything we do, from everyday tasks to our guiding principles. What powers the loop is talent density. 220+ people from 30+ nationalities, bringing expertise from the world's best studios and companies. We uphold ambition, curiosity, humility, and focus, and deliver with speed, excellence, and candor. Since the start, we've raised $165M from Headline, Northzone, Eurazeo, Bpifrance, and the founders of King, Sorare, and Spotify, people who've built and backed the games and platforms we admire, now supporting our drive to create the next ones. At Homa, we are building the next billion-player experiences from the ground up and shaping the future of entertainment. The opportunity As an AI Unity Tools Engineer, you'll build the next generation of QA automation and development tooling for Homa's games. This is a new, high-impact initiative, and you'll own it: from the first question to the tools running in production across our portfolio. You’ll work across AI, Unity, QA automation, DevOps, and infrastructure to make testing and build pipelines more reliable, scalable, and cost-efficient for games developed by Homa and its studios. You'll be working on AI-driven QA automation at the edge of what is technically possible, and you'll see the impact directly in the speed, reliability, and cost of how our games are made. What you'll do Build. Design and deploy AI-enabled QA automation pipelines across Homa's major Unity games. Run. Maintain and improve our TeamCity build pipelines and infrastructure so game builds stay reliable. Scale. Onboard new games and tools onto the platform without reducing service quality. Explore. Test AI-driven approaches to QA that cut manual testing effort and reduce reliance on costly legacy tooling. Drive adoption. Work with developers, QA teams, studios, and mobile teams so the tools you build are actually used. Measure. Track the impact of your work on testing time, build reliability, and cost, and turn it into clear recommendations. Requirements Ownership. You drive outcomes. When a build breaks or a test fails, you fix it instead of explaining why it broke. Proactive. You don't wait for instructions or perfect conditions. You spot what needs doing and do it. Pragmatism and simplicity. You look for the simplest solution that works, use whatever tools are available, and ship. You turn ambitious ideas into practical, achievable solutions. Sharp thinking. You learn fast, reason from facts, and structure your ideas clearly. You can explain a complex technical solution to developers, QA teams, and studios in a few sentences. AI-driven. AI is already part of how you work every day. You've used it to automate, speed up, or rethink at least one thing you're proud of. Hungry and motivated. You're ambitious, high-energy, and grounded. You see this role as a chance to build something new and grow faster than anywhere else, and you're ready to work for it. Bonus: you've built something. An internal tool, a testing framework, a game, a side project. We'd love to hear about it. For this role, you'll also bring Hands-on experience with Unity and the ability to understand Unity games, game systems, and testing contexts. The ability to work across technical topics while understanding the wider product and business context. Experience working in a complex environment with meaningful product and testing volumes. Bonus points if you have: Experience building QA automation or testing frameworks. Experience with AI-driven exploratory testing. Experience in gaming or another Unity-based product environment. Who we are Humanitas
items.desc: Località: Pieve Emanuele, Milano, IT, 20072 Laboratory of Cellular and Humoral Innate Immunity Work location: Via Rita Levi Montalcini 4, Pieve Emanuele (MI) Contract type: Fellowship Why Humanitas Choosing Humanitas means joining an environment where quality of care is built every day through clinical expertise, innovation and teamwork, where everyone contributes to the patient care journey. Who we are Humanitas Research Hospital is a highly specialized research and university hospital, and the first in Italy to be certified as an Academic Hospital by the Joint Commission International. Research is driven daily by over 500 physicians, biologists, physicists, data scientists, and technologists working across hospital wards and 10,000 sqm of high-tech laboratories. Our mission is to transform discoveries into concrete cures, with a strategic focus on five key areas: cancer, immunology, neuroscience, gastrointestinal medicine, and molecular cardiology. The context The Laboratory of Cellular and Humoral Innate Immunity at IRCCS Humanitas Research Hospital is seeking a motivated Predoctoral Research Fellow to join a research project funded by the Italian Ministry of Health (Ricerca Finalizzata 2024) . Our research aims to understand how soluble innate immune effectors (including PTX3 and the complement system ) regulate inflammation, antimicrobial immunity, and bone remodelling during bacterial osteomyelitis and periprosthetic joint infection . By integrating high-content information from experimental models and human clinical samples, we seek to identify novel molecular mechanisms, biomarkers, and therapeutic targets. The position offers an opportunity to gain research experience and potentially progress to the PhD program in Molecular, Experimental and Computational Medicine (MECM) at Humanitas University , starting in November 2027, subject to successful admission The successful candidate will actively contribute to the experimental activities of the project, including: performing cell and molecular biology , microbiology , and biochemistry experiments; working with cellular models of bacterial infection and host-pathogen interactions; investigating pathways involving PTX3, complement, and other soluble innate immune effectors; generating, analyzing, and interpreting experimental data in collaboration with senior researchers; contributing to scientific publications and conference presentations. The candidate will also have the opportunity to participate in in vivo studies using mouse models of bacterial osteomyelitis . The person we are looking for We are looking for enthusiastic and curious graduates with a strong interest in experimental biomedical research. Applicants should have: basic laboratory experience in cell and molecular biology, microbiology, and/or biochemistry; familiarity with mammalian cell culture and standard molecular and biochemical techniques; a genuine interest in basic and translational biomedical research; motivation, scientific curiosity, and willingness to learn new experimental approaches; good communication skills and command of English. Experience with experimental animal models, particularly mice, will be considered an advantage. An MSc in Biotechnology, Biology, Chemistry and Pharmaceutical Technologies, or a related discipline is desirable but not essential. Motivation, commitment, and enthusiasm for experimental research will be the primary selection criteria. The position will be based in the Laboratory of Cellular and Humoral Innate Immunity under the scientific supervision of Prof. Antonio Inforzato (https://www.humanitas-research.com/researchers/antonio-inforzato/) . The successful candidate will work alongside senior postdoctoral researchers and experienced research technicians , receiving close scientific mentoring and hands-on training. The candidate will join a multidisciplinary research environment bringing together expertise in innate immunity, microbiology, osteoimmunology, proteomics, computational biology, and clinical research What we offer a fully funded 1-year position, starting in January 2027, with a gross salary from 20.000 to 23.000 euro the possibility of progressing to a 3-year PhD program in Molecular, Experimental and Computational Medicine (MECM) at Humanitas University, starting in November 2027, subject to successful admission; close scientific supervision, hands-on training, and strong technical support; access to state-of-the-art experimental facilities; a collaborative and international research environment; opportunities for scientific publications, international conferences, and professional development. This offer is open to candidates in compliance with Legislative Decrees 198/2006, 215/2003 and 216/2003.

items.desc: Applied Research Engineer £50,000 GBP pa 15-MONTH FIXED TERM Counterfeiting in critical supply chains is a growing threat across high-consequence industries. Backed by recent deeptech seed funding, our initiative, Project INSIGNIA, aims to make the physical counterfeiting of critical components impossible. We do this by embedding micro-scale cryptographic signatures directly into the internal structure of 3D-printed metal parts. We are a small, focused team looking for our next colleague: an Applied Research Engineer to serve as the practical engine of Project INSIGNIA. You will work directly with the founders, taking digital models and established project milestones and turning them into working physical reality. This means taking full ownership of laboratory execution, from designing experimental architectures to validating physical cryptographic states. As an Applied Research Engineer on Project INSIGNIA, you will: Devise and build the experimental plans required to write and read physical cryptography in metal alloys. Work hands-on with materials characterisation, including metallographic sample preparation, optical microscopy, and coordinating external X-ray computed tomography (XCT) scans. Test and iterate on sensor setups for non-destructive evaluation (NDE), exploring techniques such as acoustic resonance, eddy current, or bespoke electrical interrogation rigs. Coordinate trials with national user facilities and academic partners to validate our cryptographic states. Own laboratory execution, maintaining rigorous standards of data integrity and laboratory safety while moving quickly. You will thrive in this role if you: Possess a solid core craft with a degree or hands-on background in Metallurgy, Materials Science, Physics, or Electrical Engineering. Default to high agency and autonomy, thriving in an R&D environment where the path forward is not always pre-charted. When an experimental setup fails, you diagnose the fault, redesign the experiment, and try again. Value pragmatism over pure theory, preferring robust, reproducible physical data over endless modelling. Have practical familiarity with non-destructive testing sensors, microstructural characterisation, metal additive manufacturing, or Python for experimental data capture (all valuable, though not all required). Working at Instruct3D Small team, high agency: No bureaucracy or management layers. You own your work from concept to physical test. Pragmatic flexibility: Core working hours built around getting hard technical work done in the lab, balanced with genuine respect for personal and family commitments outside work. Craft over hype: We care about physics, sound metallurgy, and building things that reliably work in the physical world. Compensation & Benefits We believe in transparent compensation, solid security, and treating team members properly. Salary: £50,000 per annum. Contract: 15-month fixed-term role for Project INSIGNIA, with the intention to transition into a permanent position subject to future funding and project milestones. Pension: 5% employer pension contribution on all earnings. Financial wellbeing: An annual one-to-one review meeting with an independent financial adviser, plus year-round access for any pension or planning queries. Healthcare: Comprehensive private medical insurance including full cancer cover, full outpatient cover, mental health & therapies. Annual leave: 28 days annual leave, plus UK bank holidays. Start date: Onboarding by January 2027 at the latest, accommodating standard industry notice periods. Right to work: You must currently hold the right to work in the UK. Due to the strict timelines of this grant, we are unable to offer visa sponsorship. Why Sheffield? Our lab and office space sits in Sheffield city centre. Sheffield consistently ranks among the most affordable and liveable technical hubs in the UK, offering an exceptional quality of life without the punishing living costs of London, Oxford, or Cambridge. Commutes are typically measured in minutes rather than hours, the local housing market remains genuinely accessible, and the Peak District National Park is just 20 minutes from the lab bench. It is an ideal base to build both a career and a life outside work. What to expect next: Stage 1 (30 minutes): An informal video chat with the founders to discuss background, project scope, and mutual fit. Stage 2 (60 to 90 minutes): A technical deep dive where you walk us through a previous technical challenge or experimental rig, discussing first-principles physics, trade-offs, and failure modes. Stage 3 (In-person): A visit to our Sheffield lab to meet the team, inspect the hardware, and ensure the environment suits you. Not the right role for you, but interested in what we do? We keep our core team lean, but we are always keen to hear from skilled engineers and scientists. Send a brief note and CV to join@instruct3d.io. Pay: £50,000.00 per year Benefits: Casual dress Company pension On-site …

items.desc: Ref Number B02-11421 Professional Expertise Research and Research Support Department School of Life & Medical Sciences (B02) Location London Working Pattern Full time Salary See advert text Contract Type Fixed-term Working Type Hybrid Available for Secondment No Closing Date 04-Nov-2026 About us The UCL Division of Surgery and Interventional Science is a collaborative and cross-disciplinary environment where clinicians, engineers, allied health professionals and researchers are constantly striving for innovative approaches to treatment. This includes developing highly effective methods which go beyond the boundaries of conventional wisdom and treating each patient as an individual. As a world leader in medical and biomedical research we can see at first-hand the directions in which medicine and science are moving and where patient and industry needs are growing. This knowledge ensures that we are producing and teaching some of the most innovative master’s courses for clinicians and scientists across the world. Additionally, our cutting-edge research expertise ensures that the latest techniques are taught using the most advanced equipment. Finally, we offer innovative master’s courses led by world leading experts, providing a truly research-based learning experience delivered by some of the greatest minds in science and medicine today. The Division reaching across three London campuses (Bloomsbury, Royal Free and Stanmore) brings together three major research departments: Targeted Intervention, Surgical Biotechnology and Orthopaedics and Musculoskeletal Science. Within these departments are world class research centres, specialising in many different surgical and interventional specialties. The Division also offers teaching and training in a wide range of subjects with intercalated BSc options for UCL medical students, direct MBBS teaching, undergraduate and postgraduate taught and research programmes for both clinicians and non-clinicians. The Division holds a silver award for the Athena Swan Charter which recognizes advancement of gender equality and aims for representation, progression, and success for all. Further information on the Division can be found at https://www.ucl.ac.uk/surgery/ About the role You will be employed on a Versus Arthritis Translational Award led by Professor John Counsell, developing in vivo CAR-T cell therapy for lupus and inflammatory arthritis using novel UCL lentiviral vector technologies, including targeted envelopes, and proprietary expression backbones. You will lead the in vivo preclinical work package, in which T cell-targeted vectors are administered intravenously to PBMC-humanised NSG mice to generate CD19 CAR-T cells directly within the animal. You will compare targeting envelopes and vector backbones for CAR-T generation efficiency, persistence, biodistribution and CD19+ target cell elimination. The post is funded from 1 November 2026 to 31 October 2027 at Grade 7, spine point 32. You will work closely with the Research Fellow leading vector development and ex vivo human cell validation, and with clinical collaborators in UCLH Rheumatology. Other The advert will close on 4th November at 23:59 GMT, however we may close applications early if we receive a high volume of applications. Early application submission is recommended. Interview Date(s) TBC If you have any queries about the role, please contact Professor John Counsell on j.counsell@ucl.ac.uk If you need reasonable adjustments or a more accessible format to apply for this job online or have any queries about the application process, please contact the HR Team on l.oppong@ucl.ac.uk The UCL Ways of Working supports colleagues to be successful and happy at UCL through sharing expectations around how we work – please visit www.ucl.ac.uk/ways-of-working to find out more. items.desc: About Us We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity. Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next. The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve. Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost. Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor. In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence. We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you. About The Role Callosum believes that orders of magnitude improvements in AI systems will come through application-aware orchestration across heterogeneous models and hardware. Our team is developing the science that makes that possible: a principled, evidence-based method for building agentic systems automatically at unprecedented scale. Today, designing these systems is a craft. Decisions about memory management, task decomposition, tool use and inter-agent coordination are made on intuition and convention. The results work until they don't, and it is rarely clear in advance which failure comes next. The team tackles these problems on two fronts. We build the tools to analyse and evaluate agentic systems rigorously enough to say where and why they go wrong, and we use what we learn to design better ones. We are not simply building a better harness; the best harness will change with every new model, task and generation of silicon. We are building the layer beneath it, so that design decisions follow from evidence rather than taste. The mandate is broad, and most of the questions inside it are still unanswered. You will have wide latitude to choose problems, and your results will shape what the company builds in the future. What You'll Build Design and run experiments that isolate why agentic systems fail - across behaviour, traces and activations - and turn those findings into interventions that measurably move intelligence, cost and reliability Attack one or more of our core research themes: context and memory management; agent steering, task decomposition and specialisation; continual learning during deployment; and inter-agent communication Build agent analysis and evaluation infrastructure - observability, behaviour analysis, evaluation harnesses, auditing - as durable instruments the whole company works from, not one-off scripts Publish. Evaluation results, methods and discoveries, as both company assets and public evidence Work across team boundaries in both directions: take a vertical domain-specific application problem and design systems which run at unpreceding scale at lowest cost and latency; or invent novel model and agent architecture which exploit emerging unconventional silicons beyond GPU What You'll Bring Evidence that you can run research of your own: you take an open question, design the experiments that settle it, and produce results other people can build on. items.desc: Data Scientist (LLMs & Conversational AI) About the role We are building production conversational AI systems powered by large language models, speech AI, and real-time AI workflows. We’re hiring two Data Scientists to join our LLM team, helping design, improve, and evaluate the systems that power our Conversational AI products in production. The focus is on defining, interrogating and solving complex modelling and evaluation problems, and building the data and experimentation foundations that will generate systematic advances in conversational AI. You’ll work closely with researchers, engineers, and evaluation teams across areas such as LLM behaviour and reasoning, prompt optimisation, conversational quality, and model evaluation. We’re particularly interested in people from strong quantitative backgrounds including Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, Computer Science, or related fields, who enjoy piecing together difficult problems, thinking rigorously, and working in environments driven by research and experimentation. What you’ll do Design and use datasets, experiments and evaluation methods to gain detailed and intimate knowledge of our conversational AI solutions. Identify opportunities to improve quality, reliability, and performance through research and experimentation Statistically investigate how changes to prompts, pipelines, models, or system logic impact real-world outcomes Think creatively about edge cases that might expose flaws in a system, and devise and test different ideas about how to handle those cases without harming global performance Develop tests and metrics that capture the many nuances of user requirements, rather than uncritically relying on industry-standard proxies that might obscure underlying issues Advance the building blocks behind LLM-powered systems, including classification, ranking, retrieval, scoring, and conversational workflows Collaborate with engineering and evaluation teams to turn product problems into measurable AI problems Stay up to date with the latest research and critically apply new ideas to production AI systems, separating out strong, flexible approaches from fragile hype What we’re looking for Degree, MSc, or PhD in Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, Computer Science, or a similarly quantitative field Strong Python skills with experience using tools such as pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn Experience working with data science, experimentation, statistical analysis, or machine learning systems Curiosity around the finer details of LLMs, NLP, or conversational AI Ability to think critically about model behaviour and system performance rather than simply training models Sceptical mindset: you are uncomfortable with taking any assumption as given, and you examine new ideas with an open but critical mind Comfortable working in fast-moving, collaborative environments with ambiguous problems Why join us Work on real-world conversational AI systems used in production Solve difficult applied AI problems in a highly collaborative environment Join a research-driven team working across LLMs, speech AI, and evaluation Influence how AI systems are measured, improved, and deployed at scale

Clear communication skills and the ability to explain scientific findings and work effectively with colleagues across engineering disciplines. Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary engineering teams. Working alongside specialists across Vehicle Science and the wider engineering organisation, you'll apply your expertise to real performance challenges where accuracy, innovation and speed matter. items.desc: THE ROLE The FAIR Programme at The Alan Turing Institute is an academic-industry collaboration developing an actionable framework for the trustworthy and reliable adoption of AI at scale within the financial services industry. Its research focuses on three key challenges: AI assurance, AI-powered financial crime detection, and trustworthy agentic workflows. We are looking for a talented Research Associate to join our FAIR Programme. The post holder will lead a focused short-term research project of their own design, advancing research across one or more of FAIR’s key challenge areas. Working alongside leading researchers, partner universities and industry, you will develop, implement and evaluate innovative methods, models or tools that address real-world challenges in responsible and trustworthy AI for financial services. ABOUT YOU The successful candidate will hold or be working toward a PhD in Mathematics, Computer Science or a closely related discipline, alongside a strong background in areas such as reinforcement learning, bandit methods, anomaly detection, privacy, robustness, uncertainty quantification or quantitative finance. You will bring experience developing research software using tools such as Python, Java, TensorFlow or PyTorch, and an understanding of the technical challenges involved in operationalising AI, including generative AI, within financial services. Excellent written and communication skills will be vital for this candidate as they will need to communicate complex technical ideas clearly and collaborate effectively with academic and industry partner. HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT Scope, pilot and deliver high-quality research activity under the direction of the Principal Investigator and Co Investigators. Drive collaboration with academic experts and industrial research partners from across the Turing and the wider Turing community Publish and disseminate high-quality research papers and publications detailing research output and project case-studies. Work with industrial partners to design and test technical solutions to key challenges in AI governance, and operationalisation. Become part of the broader FAIR Programme team. Present, disseminate and explain technical topics to colleagues, external partners, and broader community by preparing and presenting reports, blog posts, organising and delivering presentations, and taking an active role in meetings and discussions. items.desc: Magnesium alloys offer exceptional lightweighting potential for aerospace and space applications, but their wider use in extreme environments is limited by challenges including microstructural instability, temperature fluctuations and irradiation-induced damage. At the same time, oxide inclusions formed during casting and manufacturing are conventionally regarded as detrimental to structural performance. This project seeks to turn these"liabilities into assets" by exploiting solid-state, friction-based manufacturing to create finely dispersed oxide nanoparticles in magnesium alloys, enabling the development of oxide-dispersion-strengthened (ODS) magnesium alloys with enhanced thermal stability, high-temperature performance and radiation resistance. You will work within the research group led by Dr Dikai Guan at the University of Southampton on an NSF-EPSRC research project. The project brings together the University of Southampton, Baylor University, UK National Ion Beam Centre, integrating alloy processing, friction-based manufacturing, multiscale characterisation, modelling and extreme-environment testing. The position is offered until 31/05/2028 in the first instance, with the possibility of extension for up to 1 further year. The Research Fellow will be a major contributor to the experimental research activities at the University of Southampton, including: Feedstock alloy development and characterisation Multiscale microstructure characterisation Cryogenic and thermal-cycling testing Radiation-resistance testing You will have a good track record in carrying out independent and original scientific research, and publication of research papers. You should have the ability to work and communicate efficiently with other members of the team (supervisors, students and postdocs), and collaborators outside the University. Regular reports of research progress are required, and research plans should be adjusted accordingly. Critical analysis of experimental results and problem solving skills are essential to this role. You will also be required to write research papers for publication in high impact research journals and attend/present at relevant conferences. There will be an opportunity to supervisor PhD and Master students as a secondary supervisor. You should hold a PhD (or near completion)/ relevant experience in materials science or a relevant discipline. Research experience in physical metallurgy, metallic materials and advanced microstructure characterisation is particularly relevant to this position. Experience with SEM/EDS and EBSD, together with TEM/STEM or related high-resolution characterisation techniques, is highly desirable. Experience in oxide-dispersion-strengthened materials, metal casting, friction-based processing, cryogenic testing, thermal cycling, ion irradiation, or other advanced characterisation methods would be advantageous. Equality, diversity and inclusion are central to the ethos in the School of Engineering. We give full consideration to applicants who wish to work flexibly including part-time and due consideration will be given to applicants who have taken a career break. The University has onsite childcare facilities and we foster a good work-life balance. We also offer a mentorship programme and the school runs a women-oriented network event on a bi-weekly basis. The University of Southampton is in the top 1% of world universities and the top 10 of the UK’s research-intensive universities. We are committed to sustainability and being a globally responsible university, with the principles of sustainability embedded into all aspects of our individual and collective work, in our business planning, policy-making, and professional activities. items.desc: ABOUT ZENITHON Zenithon is an applied frontier lab for extreme physics. We build foundation models that simulate plasmas, so engineers can explore far more of the design space before they build anything. THE ROLE Semiconductor plasma etch is a core part of Zenithon's business, and this role helps shape it. We're hiring a computational plasma physicist to own the physics behind our etch reactor models. You'll decide how our simulations are set up, which physics matters and where, and where the work goes next. You'll work with our ML researchers to make sure the models get it right. When engineers at the companies we work with ask whether to trust a result, you'll be the person who can answer. WHAT YOU'LL DO Own how we set up reactor-scale etch simulations: geometries, chemistry, boundary conditions and the operating ranges that matter. Set the direction of our simulation work: where fidelity matters, from sheaths to surface chemistry, and which campaigns we run next. Run simulation campaigns across wide ranges of reactor geometry, chemistry and operating conditions. Check model outputs against physics and measurements, and show clearly where the errors sit. Work with ML researchers on model inputs, outputs and tests. Talk with engineers at partner companies about their reactors, and turn what they need into what we build next. WHAT YOU'LL BRING A PhD in plasma physics, applied physics, or electrical, chemical or mechanical engineering, or a related field. Hands-on experience with HPEM, VizGlow, COMSOL or a similar reactor-scale plasma code. You've built geometries, set up chemistry and boundary conditions, and fixed runs that wouldn't converge. Strong grounding in low-temperature plasma physics: sheaths, electron energy distributions, ion energy and angle distributions, and plasma chemistry. Python and scientific computing. Clear communication with engineers who don't model. This role suits someone early in their career or a few years past their PhD. BONUS POINTS Experience at a semiconductor equipment maker or a fab. Etch chemistries, surface reactions or feature-scale profile models. PIC/MCC codes, or HPC and GPU experience. Comparing simulations with experiments. You've written or extended a solver, shipped open-source code, or worked at a startup. HOW WE WORK We're a small, in-person team in London and San Francisco that works hard, moves fast and holds a high bar. Two principles guide everything we do: intellectual ambition in what we attempt, and empirical precision in how we measure it. You'll own real problems from your first week, and your work will shape what the company becomes. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive salary and meaningful equity, set by location, plus relocation support. You can be based in San Francisco or London, on site with the team. You must be authorized to work in the US or the UK, depending on where you're based. HOW TO APPLY Send your CV and a few lines on a reactor simulation you set up: what it taught you, and where it disagreed with experiment. Zenithon is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background

items.desc: We are hiring a Scientific Manager to take ownership of the machine learning and experimental design pipelines behind our customer’s genomic target prediction work. Much of this currently lives in individual scripts maintained by individual scientists. Your job is to turn it into an automated, version-controlled and reproducible platform the whole team can rely on – and to keep it scientifically sound by working shoulder to shoulder with our customer’s wet-lab and computational biology colleagues. This is a hands-on engineering role in a scientific environment. You will spend more of your time building, automating and hardening pipelines than running individual analyses, so we are looking for someone who is as comfortable with Git, containers and workflow managers as with genomics data. A PhD in bioscience engineering, bioinformatics, computer science or machine learning engineering – or an MSc with 5+ years of equivalent experience. You can demonstrate this through peer-reviewed publications, contributions to public code repositories or relevant project work. • Strong Python, and the habit of writing code that colleagues can read, test and re-run. • Proven experience taking analysis code into production: version control with Git, code review, packaging, containerization (Docker, Singularity/Apptainer) and automated testing or CI/CD. • Hands-on experience with workflow orchestration – Nextflow, Snakemake or equivalent. • Experience running workloads on cloud infrastructure (AWS) and/or HPC clusters (e.g. SLURM). • Solid grounding in statistical modelling and machine learning applied to biological data, including model evaluation and experiment tracking. • The ability to translate between engineering and bench science, and to work with scientists who are not engineers. • You are eligible to live and work in Belgium. What will you do? • Automate and professionalize internal ML and experimental design pipelines for genomic target prediction. • Migrate existing scripts and notebooks into a production-ready, version-controlled codebase. • Reduce the manual input required for dataset preparation, settings configuration and pipeline execution. • Integrate pipelines into existing digital infrastructure, including AWS and HPC environments. • Implement version control, testing and reproducibility standards across ML workflows, and help the team adopt them. • Collaborate closely with wet-lab and computational biology colleagues to make sure pipelines meet real scientific requirements. • Run several projects in parallel, (re)assigning tasks as priorities shift, and present results concisely to stakeholders inside and outside your domain.

We are facing an exciting future with considerable growth and demanding changes, as we deliver advanced technologies and mission critical solutions for the defense and aerospace industry. Our systems provide security for people on land, at sea and in the air. Therefore, we are looking for a Data Scientist to become part of this journey and contribute to our overall purpose – securing people through advanced technology. Your role in our team As a Data Scientist in AI & Advanced Analytics, you will play a pivotal role in developing advanced AI capabilities that directly support critical defense operations. Working with complex, real-world data and mission-driven challenges, you will help shape the next generation of intelligent systems used by Denmark and our international partners. You will: Build state-of-the-art AI capabilities – Work with untamed data, train deep learning models, and evaluate them to ensure top-tier quality and generalization. A strong foundation in statistics and mathematics is essential, along with the ability to apply new deep learning techniques and architectures. Take ownership of AI and data modeling for key projects – Develop AI models for impactful projects in collaboration with a talented team, solving a wide range of real-world challenges. Ensure top-tier quality and security – Handle classified information and mission-critical systems while adhering to military-grade security standards. Collaborate and engage with end users – Work closely with stakeholders to ensure AI solutions meet operational needs, delivering real-world impact. Since early 2022, the global security landscape has changed significantly. Denmark and its NATO allies face increasingly complex challenges that require rapid, innovative technological responses. Within Terma’s AI & Advanced Analytics team, we develop and deploy AI-driven capabilities that strengthen decision-making and enhance situational awareness in this evolving environment. We are a passionate and dedicated group that takes full ownership of our AI products – from initial ideas to development, delivery, and long-term maintenance. Our work extends far beyond coding; we engage directly with customers and end users to understand operational needs and ensure that our solutions make a real difference. This means you will work closely with those who rely on our technology, gaining unique insights that go well beyond the traditional developer role. You will join a team that values innovation, diversity, and psychological safety. We support each other, challenge ideas constructively and ensure everyone has the opportunity to grow and contribute to delivering meaningful solutions. How you will make a meaningful contribution Your key responsibilities include: Developing and training cutting-edge Machine learning models using complex, real-world and simulated data Taking ownership of data pipelines, AI modeling, and algorithm development for high-impact projects Ensuring high-quality, secure, and reliable AI solutions that meet military-grade standards Evaluating model performance and driving continuous improvements in accuracy, robustness, and generalization Collaborating closely with end users to understand operational needs and translate them into effective AI solutions Working with peers across engineering, domain experts, and customers to deliver mission-critical capabilities Bring your world class expertise into play You are fluent in English both in writing and verbal at a professional level. Danish is an advantage but not a requirement. items.desc: ABOUT ZENITHON Zenithon is an applied frontier lab for extreme physics. We build foundation models that simulate plasmas, so engineers can explore far more of the design space before they build anything. THE ROLE Our models learn from simulations today, and next they will learn from real experiments. Getting experimental data from an instrument into a form a model can learn from is hard, slow work, and this role owns it. You'll take data from plasma diagnostics and from the datasets our partners bring, clean it, pull out what matters and build datasets our ML researchers can rely on. You'll decide how we do this across instruments and domains, and you'll automate as much of it as you can. WHAT YOU'LL DO Take in raw data from instruments such as optical emission spectrometers, laser diagnostics, Langmuir probes and mass spectrometers, and from partner datasets in whatever form they arrive. Clean and validate it: calibrations, baselines, artefacts, missing values, and streams recorded on different clocks. Extract the quantities that matter, with their uncertainties, working closely with our physicists and ML researchers. Build training-ready datasets in Zarr and similar formats, with clear schemas, metadata and versions. Automate the path from raw files to datasets so new data flows through without hand-holding, at terabyte scale and beyond. Help decide what gets recorded in experiments, and work with our ML engineers on how data feeds training. WHAT YOU'LL BRING A degree in physics, chemistry, astrophysics, engineering or another science. Many people in this role have a PhD, but it isn't required. Hands-on experience taking messy experimental data from an instrument to clean, analysed results, ideally data you or your lab collected. Strong Python and the scientific stack (NumPy, SciPy, pandas, xarray), with Git and automated tests. Experience with large datasets and the tools to handle them. Clear, fluent English, written and spoken, for working closely with physicists, engineers and ML researchers. You don't need years of industry experience. We care most about what you've built and how fast you learn. BONUS POINTS You've trained ML models on data you processed yourself, for example to classify images, segment scans or identify compounds in spectra. Terabyte- to petabyte-scale data from experiments such as the LHC, synchrotrons or sky surveys. Spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, laser diagnostics such as Thomson scattering, or imaging data. Zarr, HDF5, NetCDF or ROOT; Dask, Ray or Spark; workflow tools and cloud storage. Signal processing and fitting: baselines, peak fitting, deconvolution and uncertainty propagation. You've built tools others rely on, contributed to open source, or worked at a startup. HOW WE WORK We're a small team that works hard, moves fast and holds a high bar. Two principles guide everything we do: intellectual ambition in what we attempt, and empirical precision in how we measure it. You'll own real problems from your first week, and your work will shape what the company becomes. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive salary and meaningful equity. You'll work from our London office near St Paul's at least three days a week. You must have the right to work in the UK. Some projects may involve export-controlled data, which can require additional screening. HOW TO APPLY Send your CV and a few lines on the messiest dataset you've worked with: what was wrong with it, what you built, and how you knew the result was right. Zenithon is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background.

items.desc:
ABOUT THE ROLE

The Enterprise Knowledge Platform team builds the data and action layer that connects Perplexity's agents to the systems where enterprise work happens. Useful agents need more than access to APIs: they need to discover the right tools, understand an organization's data and terminology, and act reliably within its permissions. This team brings native connectors, MCP servers, and CLI-backed tools into a consistent platform, and builds the marketplace through which customers adopt integrations and partners extend the ecosystem.



This is a product and platform engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from designing connector infrastructure and semantic models to shipping the experiences customers use to discover, connect, and activate integrations. You'll build the runtime that executes tool calls, the knowledge layer that makes enterprise context reusable across connectors, and the developer and marketplace foundations that help the ecosystem grow. Working with AI Research and Enterprise teams, you'll turn fragmented systems into reliable, permission-aware capabilities that agents can use to complete real work. The impact is direct: every improvement helps customers put their existing software and knowledge to work through Perplexity.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the connector runtime that registers, hosts, and executes native connectors, hosted MCP servers, and CLI-backed tools through a consistent agent-facing interface.

 - Build the semantic and knowledge layer, including tool and entity schemas, capability metadata, relationships, organization-specific terminology, and reusable corrections, while preserving provenance and source-system permissions.

 - Design discovery, search, and recommendation systems that help agents find relevant tools and context and help users and organizations choose integrations that fit their work.

 - Build the marketplace and activation experience end to end, from browsing and recommendations to installation, configuration, admin enablement, and ongoing adoption.

 - Make connector execution reliable and observable, with structured results, retries, idempotency, pagination, rate-limit handling, and recovery from partial failures. Own reliability targets, production monitoring, and incident response.

 - Implement connector authentication, credential isolation, and permission enforcement, partnering with Trust & Governance, Security, and Backend Platform on shared policies and tenant boundaries.

 - Build the onboarding and publishing path for internal teams and external partners, including schemas, test fixtures, validation, review, and versioning.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of owning complex backend systems from design through production operation.

 - Strong system design skills, including building reliable, scalable platforms that integrate heterogeneous APIs and services with clear security and isolation boundaries.

 - Sound technical judgment in security-sensitive, distributed systems, balancing credential isolation, permission correctness, and failure behavior with performance, usability, and delivery speed.

 - A track record of leading ambiguous, cross-team initiatives from architecture through adoption, setting technical direction for shared platforms, and raising engineering quality through mentorship.

items.desc: Your role ECMWF is opening an exciting new position for Computing and Software Support Specialist (A2) in the User Services Section in the Forecast Department of ECMWF. In this role you will support users working with our machine learning models and data. The Computing and Software Support Team providestechnical advice and support to all users of ECMWF software and computing, including Member and Co-operating States, ECMWF users and public users. As part of a team of ten staff you will provide day-to-day 2nd line user support and work on continuous improvements of our services, processes and documentation. With a growing user community and constant evolution in technologies we are looking for a dedicated individual with a genuine interest in helping others make the most of ECMWF’s software, data and platforms. The recent rise in machine learning for numerical weather prediction has brought new ways of working with software, data and computing, which in turn comes with a need for outstanding support processes. We are looking for a highly organised individual with a keen interest inlatest technological developments and a capacity tomanage competing priorities and a variety of tasks. In this role you will have a direct impact on our user community bysolving technical issues and shaping our client services and technologies.Hence excellent communication and collaboration skills are equally important in this role. About User Services Section The User Services Section has 26 staff providing support and advice to all users of ECMWF computing, data and software services including Member States, Co-operating States, Commercial entities, ECMWF and public users. The section comprises a Computing and Software Support team, a User Solutions Team and Data Support team and is based in Bonn, Germany, and Reading, UK. About ECMWF's Machine Learning activities ECMWF is operating and developing world-leading, machine learning-based probabilistic weather forecasting systems, which complement our existing physics-based system. A range of novel ML approaches are being investigated for improved quality and efficiency of forecasts as part of ECMWF’s contribution to the Destination Earth initiative. A team of scientists and engineers in ECMWF are working collaboratively across the Centre and in our Member and Cooperating States to undertake this challenge, including through the Machine Learning Pilot Project (MLPP). Together with our Member States; we are co-developing Anemoi, an end-to-end framework for training and operationalising data-driven weather forecasting models. The Computing and Software Support Specialist will focus on support for users and developers working in this domain. to users of ECMWF machine learning models and their output data, helping users access and make use of ML models, products and datasets Provide specialised expertise and user support in the use of Fincons Group built its reputation on foreseeing and interpreting new business models and the rapid evolution of IT systems by building a complete range of services: from research and consulting to design and development, from system integration of leading vendor software solutions right up to application management, supporting clients step by step along their digital transformation journey. Fincons is a multinational with over 2,600 people and several offices worldwide (in Italy, Switzerland, Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Belgium and the USA), but above all a Family Company where the founders play a strategic role with commitment and passion, grounding the company in the same principles of a united and caring family. items.desc: Job description Division of Heat and Power Technology at the Department of Energy Technology is seeking a Research Engineer to conduct research within the Vinnova-funded projects “Impact of INlet DIstortion on the AEROdynamic and AEROelastic characteristics of an axial compressor stage (INDIAERO)” and “AI Supported Adaptive Manufacturing (AISAM)”. The projects address two important aspects affecting the aerodynamic and aeromechanical performance of fan and compressor blades in aero-engines: blade erosion and inlet flow distortion. Leading-edge erosion can increase aerodynamic losses and consequently fuel consumption. At the same time, aero-engines are frequently exposed to non-uniform inlet flow conditions due to intake geometry and varying flight conditions. These distortions can affect both aerodynamic performance and aeroelastic stability, potentially leading to phenomena such as flutter and high-cycle fatigue. Reliable methods for assessing these effects are still under development and constitute an active area of international research. High-quality experimental data are essential for the development and validation of such methods. The work will include the development and design of experimental test setups, detailed aerodynamic measurements, and the analysis and comparison of experimental and numerical results. The position involves close collaboration with the industrial partners participating in the projects. In addition to research activities, the position may include teaching and other education-related activities corresponding to up to 10% of the working time.. BAP-2026-637) Laatst aangepast: 21/10/26 The M-Group at KU Leuven Bruges Campus is an interdisciplinary research team focusing on intelligent and dependable mechatronic systems, combining research expertise from the departments of Computer Science, Electrical Engineering and Mechanical Engineering. One of the key research tracks focusses on the application of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in real-world industrial settings on the one hand. The objective of the proposed PhD position is to investigate how novel techniques for time series representation learning on sensor data origination from complex and dynamic industrial processes can be leveraged for process characterization across multiple time series data mining tasks, such as anomaly detection, anomaly diagnosis and root cause analysis. The successful candidate will be offered to opportunity to pursue a PhD in Computer Science at KU Leuven, and will also be embedded within the Declarative Languages and Artificial Intelligence (DTAI) lab (https://dtai.cs.kuleuven.be), which pursues excellence in an explicit and synergistic combination of fundamental and applied research on machine learning and artificial intelligence. Doctoral training is provided in the framework of the Leuven Arenberg Doctoral School (https://set.kuleuven.be/phd). The PhD will be supervised by Prof. Mathias Verbeke and Mr. Louis Carpentier. Project Context Industry 4.0 has equipped industrial processes with large numbers of sensors, enabling continuous monitoring of machine and process behaviour. The resulting data allow the process to be modelled, which in turn yields analytical insights for optimising the process or for detecting and preventing faults. However, industrial processes are becoming increasingly complex, with many interacting components, varying operating conditions, and hundreds of monitored variables, which makes modelling the process as a whole increasingly difficult. Existing approaches rely mostly on deep neural networks to learn representations of the data, which are then leveraged in downstream tasks. While effective in terms of predictive performance, these models provide little understanding of the process itself, which is crucial in real-world applications. Post-hoc explanations do not solve this issue, as they only approximate the model's reasoning and are not guaranteed to faithfully reflect its behaviour. Furthermore, deep neural networks typically require large datasets to learn complex behaviours, which are rarely available in real industrial applications. Project The central research challenge of this PhD position is to automatically learn explainable representations from high-dimensional industrial time series data, and to leverage these representations across multiple time series data mining tasks. Within this PhD research, you will leverage motifs, i.e., representative subsequences, which act as the building blocks of the explainable time series representations and thereby offer a holistic view of the industrial process. To this end, you will design new algorithms for mining motifs in multivariate time series and for learning relationships among the discovered motifs. These algorithms will focus on three aspects. First, they will balance scalability and representativeness, i.e., the computational cost of building the motif-based representation against the level of detail and accuracy with which the motifs describe the process. Second, they will incorporate weak supervision, so that domain experts can steer the algorithms, and hence the motif-based representation, without needing to provide exhaustive labels. Finally, they will be simple to use, requiring minimal configuration with few hyperparameters whose meaning is intuitive to domain experts. The resulting representations will be evaluated in downstream tasks such as anomaly detection, anomaly diagnosis, and root cause analysis. The PhD position is part of an industrial research project with the aim of acquiring foundational knowledge about complex industrial systems and generating analytical insights that can be used to improve the production process. This PhD is embedded in the methodological core of the project, and is responsible for developing the representation learning methods on which the downstream analyses are built. The methods developed throughout the PhD will be validated on real-world industrial use cases leveraging operational data provided by the industrial partner in the project. Profile Profile We are seeking a highly motivated, enthusiastic, and communicative researcher, with a proactive and creative attitude who is eager to explore innovative solutions. items.desc: On the 1 August 2026, the University of Greenwich and the University of Kent formed a pioneering new multi-university group called London and South-East (LASE) University Group. Should you join us, you will be employed by LASE but will work as part of the University of Greenwich academic division, contributing to its distinct strengths, community and identity while also being part of a wider group that brings together the scale, resilience and shared ambition of both universities. Through LASE we aim to deliver outstanding education, impactful research, and meaningful regional and global impact. The Natural Resources Institute is a specialist research, knowledge exchange and postgraduate training unit based at the University of Greenwich’s Medway Campus. We aspire to be a global leader in collaborative research, knowledge exchange and learning to co-create a just, healthy, and sustainable future for all. We do this through transforming lives through research, innovation, and learning. The NRI has an international footprint and is home to over 80 international scientists and social scientists. We have made award-winning discoveries collaborating with partners across sectors and disciplines to co-create environmental resilience, sustainable agriculture, health, and food security. NRI works towards a just world free from disease, hunger, poverty, and violence. We are an inclusive, collaborative, and flexible research and learning institute. The Institute has a strong history of innovative research to address global challenges related to agriculture and food security. The unique diversity of disciplines across NRI’s three departments provides opportunities for transdisciplinary and systems research relevant to tackling the complexity of contemporary and emerging global agriculture, biodiversity, food security, food system and one-health challenges. An opportunity has arisen for a research entomologist to join the Agriculture, Health and Environment department. The successful applicant will carry out behavioural bioassays and electrophysiological assays on arthropods as part of our work on beneficial insects and sustainable control of pests and diseases of crops, livestock, and people. The post-holder’s responsibilities will include carrying out bioassays with terrestrial arthropods to measure responses to chemical and other stimuli. This will include electrophysiological assays (electroantennography, single sensillum recording) and behavioural bioassays in olfactometers and wind tunnels. The post-holder will have the opportunity to use apparatus for automated 2D- and 3D- tracking of insect behaviour. They will also be expected to work with the technical team to maintain colonies of arthropods in our insectaries and to conduct field work in the UK and for short periods abroad. The post-holder will be expected to contribute to the preparation of research outputs including published papers, and applications for future funding to continue research. There will be opportunities for the post-holder to undertake teaching at postgraduate and undergraduate level. Candidates must have a good theoretical and practical background in behavioural entomology or arthropod chemical ecology as demonstrated through a relevant PhD. Specific training in use of bioassay equipment will be provided. items.desc:
Vos missions au quotidien 
Vous êtes passionné par l’ingénierie logicielle ? Vous aimerez intervenir sur des projets stratégiques dans une équipe projet constituée de développeurs ? Rejoignez-nous !
Nous recherchons un stagiaire en Intelligence Artificielle pour rejoindre notre équipe travaillant sur l’application STAR, dédiée à la trésorerie. Le stagiaire aura l’opportunité de travailler sur des projets innovants, d’appliquer des techniques d’IA et de machine learning, et de contribuer à l’optimisation des processus de gestion de la trésorerie.
 Concrètement, vous serez amené à : 
 Participer à la conception et au développement de modèles d’IA et de machine learning pour l’application STAR
 Analyser des données complexes liées à la trésorerie pour en extraire des insights pertinents
 Collaborer avec les équipes techniques et métiers pour comprendre les besoins spécifiques à la gestion de la trésorerie
 Contribuer à la mise en place de solutions IA visant à améliorer l’efficacité et la précision des opérations de trésorerie
 Rédiger des rapports et présenter les résultats des analyses
 Utiliser les outils de Continuous Delivery mis à disposition des projets IT
Durée du stage : 6 mois.
 Et si c’était vous ? 
 Vous préparez un Bac+5 en Université ou Ecole d’ingénieur
 Vous avez des connaissances en machine learning, deep learning et traitement de données
 Vous maîtrisez les outils de programmation (Python, R, etc.) et les bibliothèques d’IA (TensorFlow, PyTorch, etc.)
 Vous avez la capacité à travailler en équipe et à communiquer efficacement
 Vous etes curieux, autonome et avez le sens de l’initiative
 Vous êtes force de proposition et effectuez de la veille technologique
 You’re fluent in english ? Vous êtes le candidat idéal !
 Plus qu’un poste, un tremplin 
Rejoignez-nous pour faire grandir vos ambitions ! Dès votre arrivée, vous serez intégré dans nos équipes et apprendrez chaque jour aux côtés de nos experts qui vous accompagneront dans vos missions. Progressivement, vous gagnerez en autonomie sur vos projets pour faire de cette expérience un vrai accélérateur de carrière. Vous découvrirez également toute la diversité de nos métiers, dans un secteur qui évolue et innove en permanence.
A la fin de vos études, diverses opportunités pourront s’offrir à vous, en France et à l’international.
 Pourquoi nous choisir ? 
Attentif à votre qualité de vie et conditions de travail , vous bénéficiez d’avantages :
 Télétravail possible selon le rythme de votre service
 Prise en charge de 60% de votre titre de transport
 Billetterie à prix réduits de notre Comité d’Entreprise (concerts, cinéma, sport…).
 Offre variée de restaurants d’entreprise et de cafétérias à tarifs compétitifs ainsi que des titres restaurants dématérialisés quand vous êtes en télétravail
Créer, oser, innover, entreprendre font partie de notre ADN. Si vous aussi vous souhaitez être dans l’action, évoluer dans un environnement stimulant et bienveillant, vous sentir utile au quotidien et développer ou renforcer votre expertise, nous sommes faits pour nous rencontrer !
Vous hésitez encore ?
Sachez que nos collaborateurs peuvent s’engager quelques jours par an pour des actions de solidarité sur leur temps de travail : parrainer des personnes en difficulté dans leur orientation ou leur insertion professionnelle, participer à l’éducation financière de jeunes en apprentissage ou encore partager leurs compétences avec une association. Les formats d’engagement sont multiples.
 Diversité et inclusion 
Nous sommes un employeur garantissant l’égalité des chances et nous sommes fiers de faire de la diversité une force pour notre entreprise. Le groupe s’engage à reconnaître et à promouvoir tous les talents , quels que soient leurs croyances, âge, handicap, parentalité, origine ethnique, nationalité, identité de genre, orientation sexuelle, appartenance à une organisation politique, religieuse, syndicale ou à une minorité, ou toute autre caractéristique qui pourrait faire l’objet d’une discrimination.
 Transparence et responsabilité 
Le groupe Société Générale a à coeur que les personnes qui nous rejoignent agissent avec éthique et responsabilité pour une culture de performance durable. Les informations mentionnées dans votre candidature peuvent potentiellement être vérifiées dans le respect du cadre légal, à tout moment pendant le processus de recrutement.

Sobre el equipo Te incorporarás a nuestro equipo de IA, en las líneas de robótica cognitiva y visión artificial. Buscamos un perfil sénior capaz de llevar sistemas robóticos con IA desde el concepto hasta su validación en entornos reales. Combinarás el diseño de arquitecturas y la integración de modelos de IA con el trabajo directo sobre plataformas, sensores y equipos experimentales, y acompañarás el crecimiento técnico de los perfiles junior del equipo. Tu rol • Diseñarás e implementarás arquitecturas de software para sistemas robóticos (humanoides, cuadrúpedos y manipuladores), integrando percepción, planificación y control. • Liderarás la puesta en marcha, validación y caracterización de plataformas robóticas y sistemas de visión artificial (cámaras 2D/3D, iluminación, calibración, sincronización de sensores). • Integrarás modelos de IA (visión, aprendizaje por refuerzo, aprendizaje por imitación, modelos visión-lenguaje-acción y modelos fundacionales) en robots reales, abordando la transferencia de simulación a realidad. • Definirás protocolos experimentales y métricas de validación, y garantizarás la reproducibilidad y documentación de los resultados. • Diagnosticarás y resolverás incidencias complejas de integración hardware-software durante la puesta en marcha y la operación. • Desarrollarás casos de uso en entornos industriales y proyectos de I+D+i (europeos y con clientes), aportando criterio técnico para evaluar viabilidad, riesgos y madurez tecnológica. • Contribuirás a la redacción técnica de propuestas. • Mentorizarás a ingenieros/as junior y de nuestro Programa de Jóvenes Talentos CIRCE Academy, revisarás su trabajo y les transferirás buenas prácticas de laboratorio y de desarrollo. items.desc: An exciting opportunity is available for a postdoctoral Research Associate to join a recently funded Leverhulme Trust project investigating air entrainment and bubble formation by plunging jets in complex fluids. The project is motivated by a recently observed and unexpected fluid-mechanical phenomenon involving plunging jets in non-Newtonian fluids. It aims to understand the physical mechanisms governing the interaction between the jet, the free surface and the entrained air, and how these are influenced by the rheological properties of the fluid. The research will combine numerical simulations with complementary experimental and theoretical investigations to develop a fundamental understanding of these flows. This project sits at the intersection of fluid mechanics, complex fluids and interfacial phenomena. It offers the chance to contribute to ambitious, curiosity-driven research aimed at understanding a phenomenon that has not previously been described in the scientific literature. The successful candidate will play a leading role in the project’s numerical programme, developing and deploying new algorithms, and carrying out simulations of jets, bubbles and air entrainment in complex fluids. The work will involve developing new algorithms for high-fidelity adaptive multiphase fluid simulations, deploying these in in-house and open-source code bases, conducting a campaign of numerical experiments, and contributing to publications and conference presentations. The post holder will work closely with other academic investigators and project partners, including researchers undertaking complementary experimental/theoretical studies. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a background in numerical method development for fluid mechanics who is excited by fundamental research and wants to help shape an emerging area of study from an early stage. Applicants should have, or be close to completing, a PhD (or equivalent) in fluid mechanics, physics, engineering, or a closely related discipline. Experience in developing, deploying and analysing new numerical methods and algorithms is essential. Experience in areas such as multiphase flows, rheology, non-Newtonian fluids, or mesh-free numerical methods would be an advantage, but we welcome applicants with a strong numerical background and enthusiasm to develop new skills. items.desc: The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research. We are ambitious and have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee. Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to collectively, and individually, make a real difference. The role The Institute for Communication Systems (ICS) home of the 5G and 6G Innovation Centre (5GIC/6GIC) is looking to recruit Research Fellow in Analog Computing for Advanced Communication Systems . The successful candidate will be part of the Wireless Systems Lab group and will have the opportunity to work very close with our industrial partners as well as with academic partners all over the world. The post holder will undertake research into ultra-low-power analog and mixed-signal computing architectures for future communication systems, with particular emphasis on receiver processing and architectures that reduce or remove reliance on conventional high-resolution analog-to-digital conversion. The research will investigate how signal-processing operations traditionally implemented digitally can be reformulated and realised using analog, mixed-signal and in-memory computing technologies. Particular emphasis will be placed on the co-design of algorithms and hardware, circuit- and system-level modelling, and evaluation of the resulting architectures in terms of communication performance, power consumption, latency, precision and implementation complexity. The post holder will be expected to be able to set, define and work towards achieving targets, disseminate results and document work done. About You ICS is the largest academic research institute in Europe specialising in all aspects of ICT (Information and Communication Technologies). It is home to over 200 researchers with expertise in all communication and broadcasting systems and has developed the best in class large scale testbeds for research and innovation and enjoys the state-of-the-art lab and computing facilities. Established in 2012, 5GIC is the world’s first dedicated centre in researching end-to-end aspects of 5G and works closely with national and international leading academic institutes and key industrial partners. In November 2020, 6GIC was officially launched with parallel research undertaken in both 5G+ and 6G for 2030+. The Post Holder Must Have Expertise In The Following Strong knowledge and research experience in analogue circuit design, particularly for low-power signal processing, computing or communication applications. Experience in circuit-level modelling and simulation, including the ability to evaluate power/energy consumption and relevant circuit non-idealities. Experience or strong knowledge of algorithm–hardware co-design, including the mapping of mathematical or signal-processing operations onto practical hardware subject to noise, precision, dynamic-range, variability and implementation constraints. Strong analytical, modelling and programming skills, including experience with MATLAB and/or Python, and the ability to communicate research findings effectively in written and oral form. It would be desirable but not essential for the post holder to also have: Experience with in-memory computing architectures, including memristive/ReRAM or other emerging-device technologies. Knowledge of signal processing and communication systems, particularly channel estimation, detection, decoding, optimisation or linear algebra. A track record of high-quality peer-reviewed publications in analog/mixed-signal circuits, in-memory/neuromorphic computing, signal processing, communications or related areas. For Informal Enquiries Please Contact k.nikitopoulos@surrey.ac.uk How To Apply To apply, please submit your application with a CV and Cover Letter online via the University of Surrey jobs portal.

Afrontar proyectos complejos con escasos precedentes, utilizando tecnologías punteras y apoyado por un equipo de profesionales expertos, del que formarás parte. Salario competitivo, con incentivos variables en función de nuestros resultados. Posibilidad de retribución variable mediante seguro médico. Flexibilidad horaria: puedes escoger entre diferentes horquillas de entrada y salida. Jornada intensiva todos los viernes a lo largo del año y en verano todos los días. ¿Te interesa? Inscríbete a nuestra oferta y síguenos en nuestras redes sociales para enterarte de todas las novedades y procesos que publicamos. En ITECAM reconocemos el valor de contar con una plantilla diversa en materia de género, edad, origen étnico, discapacidad, orientación sexual, religión y cualquier otra característica. Es por esto, que animamos a todas las personas a participar en nuestros procesos de selección, especialmente aquellas que se sientan infrarrepresentadas en base a su identidad, asegurando que serán evaluadas con criterios de igualdad, diversidad, equidad e inclusividad.
