items.desc: About The Company The Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen (GWDG) serves as the university computing center for the Georg-August-Universität Göttingen and functions as a key IT and computing competence center for the Max Planck Society. With over four decades of experience, GWDG specializes in providing high-performance computing infrastructure, including some of the most powerful supercomputers in the world, such as the HLRN-IV system "Emmy." As a member of the National High-Performance Computing (NHR) network, GWDG plays a vital role in supporting scientific research through advanced computational resources and services. The organization collaborates closely with national and international research institutions, including the German Aerospace Center (DLR), the German Climate Computing Center (DKRZ), and the Institute for Advanced Simulation Jülich (IAS-JSC). GWDG is committed to fostering innovation in scientific computing, data science, and AI, serving a diverse range of scientific disciplines from earth system science to engineering and life sciences. About The Role We are seeking a highly skilled Generative AI Developer (m/f/d) to join our interdisciplinary team within the "Computing" working group. The role offers an exciting opportunity to work at the forefront of artificial intelligence, focusing on the development, integration, and deployment of generative AI solutions tailored for sensitive and critical infrastructure. The position involves collaborating closely with customers from SMEs and startups, many of whom operate in sectors with stringent data protection requirements. You will contribute to the development of prototypes, workflows, and proof-of-concept solutions that advance GWDG's AI service portfolio and support innovative research and industry applications. The role is based within the subproject "KISSKI-EvoKS," part of the AI Service Center for Sensitive and Critical Infrastructure, and offers a dynamic environment to apply your expertise in AI, machine learning, and scientific computing. Qualifications Candidates should possess a successfully completed master’s degree in computer science or a closely related field. Strong programming skills in high-level languages, particularly Python, are essential. Proficiency in Linux environments, including Bash scripting, version control with Git, and working with containers, is required. A solid understanding of software engineering principles, including security and testing, is necessary. Experience with DevOps tools such as GitLab, CI/CD pipelines, and automated testing frameworks like pytest is highly desirable. Knowledge of databases such as SQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, and experience with web development technologies including HTTP, FastAPI, HTML, and JavaScript are important. Familiarity with generative AI models—such as large language models, diffusion models—and frameworks like Pytorch or TensorFlow is also expected. Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, along with fluency in German (C1) and English (C1), are required. Willingness to travel for business purposes is also necessary. Responsibilities The role encompasses a broad spectrum of responsibilities, which include but are not limited to designing tailored AI solutions to meet customer use cases by leveraging existing AI infrastructure. You will support companies and research institutions in developing AI services, ensuring solutions are robust, scalable, and secure. Creating detailed blueprints, whitepapers, and technical documentation for internal and external stakeholders is part of the role, facilitating knowledge sharing and smooth handovers. Representing GWDG at workshops, conferences, and industry events to showcase innovative AI solutions is encouraged. You will be involved in integrating novel AI models into the GWDG AI service portfolio and the SAIA Platform (Scalable Artificial Intelligence Accelerator), ensuring cutting-edge technology adoption. Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams to develop prototypes and workflows that can evolve into production-grade solutions will be a key focus, fostering innovation and continuous improvement. Benefits GWDG offers flexible working hours and opportunities for remote work, promoting a healthy work-life balance. The organization provides a modern and diverse work environment situated close to academic and research institutions, fostering collaboration and innovation. The position includes engaging work within a large, internationally recognized IT competence center, offering exposure to a broad spectrum of scientific and technological challenges. Employees benefit from ongoing professional development opportunities, including training, workshops, and participation in conferences. The organization also provides social benefits associated with the public sector, such as comprehensive health insurance, pension schemes, and generous leave policies. items.desc: About the company: KIEFER is building Greece's integrated AI ecosystem. From renewable energy infrastructure and AI systems to robotics and enterprise applications, we connect the technologies that power Europe's intelligent future. Founded in 2014, KIEFER has delivered 600MW+ of energy projects and is now developing sovereign AI infrastructure, enterprise AI products and physical AI systems for Greece and Southeast Europe. About The Role We are looking for an ML Engineer to improve how our language models work for Polish users. You will measure quality on real product tasks, build Polish-language data and evaluations, and improve models where the results show gaps. Your work will help us understand which Polish-language use cases are ready for launch. The methods you build should also be useful as we expand to other languages. What You Will Do Define priority Polish-language use cases and quality targets with Product and go-to-market teams. Measure current model quality in Polish and investigate errors in language use, terminology, and user tasks. Build Polish-language datasets and evaluations, using native-speaker review where needed. Use evaluation results and market feedback to identify remaining gaps and recommend next steps. What You Will Need 3+ years of hands-on ML or NLP engineering experience, including work on a non-English or multilingual system in production. Strong Python skills and experience with PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, or a similar ML framework. Experience building evaluations that reflect real user tasks and combine automatic metrics with human review. Experience preparing and checking language datasets and building reliable data pipelines. Hands-on experience fine-tuning, post-training, or adapting NLP or LLM models and measuring the results. Strong software engineering and production ML skills, including model versioning, regression testing, and monitoring. Nice to have Professional working proficiency or native-level fluency in Polish. Experience improving an AI or NLP product for a new language or market. Research or open-source work in multilingual NLP or model evaluation. What Is There For You Compensation: Competitive package aligned with talent benchmarks. Impact: Hands-on work shaping AI capabilities for Kiefer Tech’s products and real-world applications. AI-native environment: Real challenges across model development, evaluation, and production AI systems. Culture: Engineering-first, high autonomy, low bureaucracy, and space to shape meaningful AI products.

items.desc: About The Company At Zonneplan, we are committed to shaping a sustainable future by eliminating reliance on fossil fuels and promoting renewable energy sources. Our mission, known as plan Zero, aims to create a Netherlands without fossil energy by leveraging innovative solutions in energy trading, battery optimization, and AI-driven forecasting. We believe in making a tangible difference through technological advancements and dedicated teamwork. Our organization fosters a collaborative environment where expertise, innovation, and impact are at the forefront, enabling us to contribute significantly to a cleaner, greener energy landscape. About The Role As a Data Scientist within our Trading & Optimization team, you will operate at the intersection of energy and artificial intelligence. Your work will have a direct and measurable impact on the energy grid, enabling smarter energy trading and management. You will develop integrated models that combine probabilistic forecasting, optimization, and control systems, ensuring real-time decision-making and operational efficiency. The role requires close collaboration with data scientists, engineers, and traders in a flat organizational structure that encourages initiative and ownership. Your models will be deployed live, and you will be responsible for maintaining, optimizing, and troubleshooting them proactively. The position offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to plan Zero by enhancing the efficiency and sustainability of energy consumption and distribution through advanced AI tools and innovative modeling techniques. Qualifications Minimum of 3 years of experience as a data scientist with a strong foundation in statistics and machine learning. Proven experience in forecasting or time series analysis. Proficiency in Python at a production level, including deploying and monitoring models in live environments. Experience with or interest in AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or similar. Ability to translate models into measurable business impact and financial outcomes. Ownership mentality with the capacity to manage models from development to operational deployment. Curiosity and proactive approach to following developments in AI and machine learning, translating innovations into practical experiments. Fluent in Dutch at a professional level, with excellent communication skills. Responsibilities Develop, deploy, and maintain probabilistic forecasting models for energy trading and grid management. Integrate forecasting, optimization, and control models to support real-time decision-making processes. Work closely with engineers and traders to ensure models are operationally effective and aligned with business goals. Monitor model performance, troubleshoot issues, and implement improvements proactively. Leverage AI tools such as Claude Code to accelerate development and enhance model capabilities. Contribute to the continuous improvement of forecasting accuracy and operational efficiency. Translate complex data insights into actionable recommendations for stakeholders. Participate in team discussions and initiatives to innovate and optimize energy trading strategies. Benefits Competitive salary ranging from €4,000 to €6,000 gross per month, based on experience and seniority. 25 vacation days with options to purchase additional days. Reiskostenvergoeding (travel allowance). Claude Code Max 20x subscription as a secondary benefit, usable for work and personal projects. Personalized keuzebudget for sports, groceries, or other personal needs. Investment in your professional growth through the Zonneplan Academy, with opportunities for career advancement to senior roles. Access to modern tools and a collaborative, no-nonsense work environment. Engagement in meaningful projects that contribute directly to sustainability and energy transition. Equal Opportunity At Zonneplan, we are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace. We believe that a variety of perspectives and backgrounds enhances our innovation and effectiveness. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of race, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, or other protected characteristics. Our hiring practices are designed to ensure equal opportunity and to promote a respectful, supportive environment for everyone.

items.desc: The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university. We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special. Overview The University of Sheffield ATLAS group has an exciting opportunity for a Research Fellow in Particle Physics to join our effort in the construction of silicon strip detector modules for the ATLAS Phase-II tracker upgrade, the commissioning of the new detector and the detector development for future experiments alongside conducting physics measurements at the High Energy Frontier within the Sheffield ATLAS group remit (Higgs, Standard Model). You will supervise the work of a technician as well as graduate students in the project. We are looking for an enthusiastic candidate that is keen to develop and contribute to a sustainable research programme within the group and take over related responsibilities and leadership. There is the expectation to be involved in funding applications which could lead to the opportunity to (co-)supervise research associates / post-doctoral researchers. As such you will need a PhD in particle physics or a related field with relevant experience in software (e.g. C++, python, Root, Athena, GEANT4) and a track record of successful work within particle physics collaborations. You should have a track-record of contributing and leading publications regarding your research. You will be based in Sheffield, with frequent travel to CERN and other laboratories required. The Sheffield ATLAS group consists of five academics and has played a key role in the successful construction, commissioning and operation of the ATLAS SCT detector. Our particular strengths lie in searches for SUSY particles, measurements of SM diboson processes sensitive to new physics and of the Higgs boson and related performance studies. Main Duties And Responsibilities Strong Involvement in the day-to-day silicon module production and organisation. This includes: Performing reception and metrology tests on raw components for silicon detector modules and on the finished module Wire-bonding silicon detector modules Performing standardised tests on completed silicon detector modules using a data acquisition system Taking on leadership responsibilities in ITk module production and subsequent installation on the ATLAS-UK or ATLAS-wide level Leading the group’s participation in the R&D programme for the next generation of detectors (DRD3 and DRD8) International leadership in early ITk detector commissioning and alignment using cosmic-ray muons and the first Run-4 collision data using a Kalman filter techniques Leading contributions to physics analysis within ATLAS, for example H → μμ, diboson or di-Higgs measurements. Determine research objectives and initiate and implement a programme of research. This may include managing time, materials, finance and equipment. Disseminate research findings / results through the production of papers for high quality journals and presentations Identify and generate appropriate sources of funding and prepare research proposals for funding bodies Apply for, manage or co-manage external research funding over a period of grant(s). Prepare at least one grant application with Research Associate staffing and one without over the period of the post. Utilise research grants, report research budget management across relevant projects Provide support to senior colleagues for research proposals and funding applications Involvement in professional activities such as refereeing papers, editing journals, refereeing research grants, external examining, organising conferences, committee membership and involvement with professional bodies on accreditation. Supervise or co-supervise undergraduate / postgraduate project students and/or PhD students. Manage Research Assistant(s) and/or Research Associate(s) if requested. Delegate and monitor the work of research students. Deal with reactive requests relating to supervising research staff and students. Participate in consortium meetings and seminars Plan several months in advance to meet deadlines for journal publications and to prepare presentations and papers for collaboration meetings and conferences. As a member of staff you will be encouraged to make ethical decisions in your role, embedding the University sustainability strategy into your working activities wherever possible. items.desc: Vi tror på ett samhälle format av framgångsrika företag där entreprenörskap och samhällsnytta går hand i hand. Att vara en del av Fortnox är att vara en del av en ständig förändring - en förändring där du själv bestämmer hur långt du vill nå. Vårt största fokus är att ge dig rätt förutsättningar att få leva din passion tillsammans med oss. Var du kommer ifrån är inte relevant - det är vart du är på väg som är intressant för oss. Precis som vi igår inte kunde drömma om det Fortnox som finns idag, så kan du vara med och forma vilka vi är imorgon. Om tjänsten I vårt produktområde Inköp utvecklar vi några av Fortnox centrala SaaS-produkter, vilka utgör kärnan i vårt erbjudande. Här skapar vi smarta, skalbara och användarvänliga lösningar som dagligen används av hundratusentals företag i Sverige. Bland våra kunder finns en stor variation, från enskilda företagare till redovisningsbyråer. Vårt ansvar sträcker sig över produkter som bokföring, hantering av leverantörsfakturor, transaktioner, tolkning av både fakturor och kvitton och mycket mer – allt det som utgör grunden i kundernas vardag. Vi blickar mot en framtid där allt förväntas förändras, en stor del av denna förändring möjliggörs av en hög automatiseringsgrad. På Fortnox jobbar vi nu på att ta fram nästa generation av våra tolkar för allt ifrån kvitton, leverantörsfakturor och inkommande dokument. Med digitala “agenter” i olika former som stöttepelare möjliggör denna teknik att vi kan erbjuda våra kunder en upplevelse där de behöver lägga minimal tid på att hantera olika former av inkommande underlag och istället lägga sin tid på att driva sitt företag. Arbetet är redan i full gång och vårt mål är glasklart. Du kommer att bli en central del i ett av våra autonoma team med helhetsansvar för sina produkter – från idé till produktion. Vi jobbar agilt och produktnära, med stort fokus på teknik, innovation och kundnytta. Du har relevant erfarenhet inom Python, ML-ramverk som Pytorch eller TensorFlow samt SQL / RDBMs och meriterande erfarenhet från Huggingface, Kubernetes, mlflow, dvc eller motsvarande verktyg. Vidare tror vi att du bemästrar hela processen för en modell, från insamling av data till träning och optimering samt utvärdering. Du känner till de senaste teknikerna och verktygen för att skapa och implementera modeller och du är driven för att fortsätta att lära dig nya saker inom området. För denna roll värdesätter vi djup teknisk kunskap. En del av rekryteringsprocessen involverar därför tekniska intervjuer kretsande kring machine learning, systemarkitektur, och programmeringstester i python. items.desc: On this page you find: About the Science Traineeship: Context What Does the Science Traineeship Look Like? What Do We Offer? What Do We Ask? Science Trainee Testimony About Rewire Recruitment Process: Timeline The opportunity of the Science Traineeship Our Science Traineeship is meant for ambitious and high-potential master’s students who want to do things differently. In collaboration with the University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG), you are offered the opportunity to write your master thesis in the medical field. The goal is to employ the power of data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to better understand complex diseases, like various forms of cancer, and to advance medical science. Simultaneously, you get to work on transformative AI projects at Rewire. After graduation, you may have the opportunity to turn your research into a scientific publication, transforming your thesis work into tangible societal impact. The Science Traineeship is part of the collaboration between the UMCG and Rewire . Since the start, over than six years ago, we have already worked on more than 10 different research streams with many enthusiastic colleagues involved from both Rewire and the UMCG. Will you be the next to join this unique project? What does the Science Traineeship look like? The Science Traineeship is a full-time program for 12 months, dependent on the requirements for your Master thesis. During this period, you work on your thesis research for 3 days a week. On the other 2 days, you get the opportunity to work on one of Rewire’s AI Business projects in a regular project team. In the first half of the traineeship (depending on your study’s timelines), your research focuses on completing your thesis and achieving successful graduation. After graduation, you have the opportunity to further develop your work together with your UMCG supervisor, with the aim of bringing it to the next level. This potentially involves preparing it for scientific publication. This offers the possibility to translate your thesis into tangible societal impact, although publication cannot be guaranteed within the traineeship period. The research will focus on applying state-of-the-art AI techniques in a medical setting. With this research you will make a vital contribution to the clinical field. You will work together with a group of leading academics in their field. As Science Trainee, you are part of the Applied Quantitative AI team within Rewire. Being part of this team, you join all team meetings, outings and experience what working as a Data Scientist at Rewire entails. At Rewire, you’ll be part of a dynamic working environment, both literally and figuratively. For your research, you can work from the Rewire office alongside many like-minded and ambitious colleagues. During your business project, you may travel to the client’s office or collaborate with your team from one of our offices. We offer flexibility in where you work, always in alignment with your project team, while encouraging time in the office or in Groningen at the UMCG to foster connection, collaboration, and strong guidance. On Fridays, most Rewire colleagues come together at the Amsterdam office to catch up, hold team meetings, and kick off the weekend with Friday afternoon drinks. What do we offer? A unique opportunity to graduate, while employing your analytical skills to make a societal contribution. Flexibility in the duration of the program, depending on the number of ECTS and requirements for your Master thesis. Intensive personal guidance from a Rewire coach and supervisor, and UMCG biological experts and researchers. The opportunity to contribute to AI solutions or scalable skill-building within companies, while doing impactful academic research. Chance to explore working at Rewire as a Trainee both in our internal as well as client-facing teams. An above-average thesis salary, 25 holiday days and possibility for a performance-based bonus. A laptop and all other necessities for your work. Regular team building events and weekly Friday afternoon drinks. REQUIREMENTS What do we ask? Currently pursuing a Master's degree in Econometrics, Mathematics, Artificial Intelligence, or another quantitative field. A medical background is not required. Top-class academic performance, honour program and other extracurricular activities are highly valued. Strong focus on personal development, eager to learn and collaborate in a multidisciplinary team. Highly ambitious and impact-driven. Curious, pragmatic and persuasive. Excellent command of analytical programming language (like Python, R) and fluent in English. Experience with bioinformatics software is not expected. Full-time availability for a program for 12 months (depending on the requirements for your Master thesis), aiming to start in January ’27. Ready to kick-start your career, while having a lot of fun! About Rewire Rewire is an AI company with offices in Amsterdam and Heidelberg. From these offices, we drive AI …

With 500+ engineers and over 25 years of experience in mission-critical environments, we help global organizations turn ambitious ideas into working solutions. Across Europe, MENA, and North America, we combine deep engineering expertise with AI and data to support leading companies in aerospace & defense, automotive, telecom & media, IT, and financial services. Are you looking for your next data challenge where you go beyond data wrangling and into making an actual impact through big data insights? Are you constantly eager to grow and develop in a dynamic and supportive environment? Do you want to work in an outstanding data and AI team? Look no further and apply to join the AI team at Wiser. We are seeking a highly skilled and innovative AI Engineer to join our team. This role is pivotal in designing and implementing cutting-edge AI solutions for our clients, ensuring they maximize the value of AI-driven technologies. The AI Engineer will engage with customers to understand business challenges, design AI-powered solutions, and provide technical leadership throughout the implementation lifecycle. This position requires a balance of technical expertise, strategic thinking, and exceptional client engagement skills. WHAT YOU WILL DO: Design and implement cutting-edge AI-driven solutions leveraging the full spectrum of approaches from traditional ML learning to using LLMs. Work closely with data scientists, ML engineers, and software developers to ensure the successful deployment of AI models and applications. Stay updated on emerging AI technologies and industry best practices to provide innovative and forward-thinking recommendations to clients. Provide technical guidance on AI model lifecycle management, including training, tuning, monitoring, and optimization. Ensure AI solutions are scalable, secure, and compliant with industry regulations and best practices. Act as a trusted advisor to clients, helping them navigate AI adoption challenges and maximizing the impact of AI in their operations. Develop technical documentation, including solution architectures, whitepapers, and best practice guides. Technical Skills & Qualifications Extensive experience in AI/ML, deep learning, and cloud-based AI services (AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud). Proficiency in AI/ML frameworks such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, Scikit-learn, Langchain, and Hugging Face. Strong programming skills in Python or similar. Excellent proficiency with traditional SQL and big data technologies such as Apache Spark, Hadoop, and distributed computing frameworks. Ability to analyze large datasets and derive business insights using BI tools like Tableau, Power BI, or similar. Experience with MLOps practices, including model deployment, monitoring, and CI/CD for AI workflows. Hands-on experience with APIs, microservices, and AI-driven automation solutions. Excellent communication and presentation skills, capable of articulating complex AI concepts to non-technical stakeholders. Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to design tailored AI solutions for diverse business challenges. items.desc: About FoodLabs FoodLabs is Europe's leading early-stage VC and venture studio, backing founders who are shaping the future of the food, health, and climate value chains. We build companies from zero, putting capital, our own team, and hands-on operating time behind a founding team before there's a product or even a name. The studio's work spans wherever a market and the data or infrastructure underneath it are broken enough to justify building the fix from scratch. About The General Data Corporation General Data is the infrastructure for licensing proprietary data: The platform runs the whole deal from request to delivery, with privacy checks, rights evidence and contracts built in. The vision is to become the system of record between AI and the world’s private data, the data that has never been published but that the next generation of AI depends on. On one side are enterprises, AI labs and robotics teams that need real-world data, and on the other are companies whose operations generate it. General Data is the data infrastructure for the modern economy, connecting every party so that data can be licensed safely, transparently and at scale. Why this is a unique opportunity AI has absorbed the public internet, and its next gains will come from private, real-world data, yet today these deals still run on email, WhatsApp and brokers, with no visibility into what was checked, who holds the rights, or whether personal data was removed. Labs are already paying for this data, and regulation like GDPR and the EU Data Act makes a trusted, verifiable layer a necessity. General Data is VC-backed and looking for its technical co-founder. Together with Founder & CEO Louai Allani , you will own the product and architecture, shape the company’s direction as an equal partner and build the team from the ground up. About the role Supplier intake: Build connectors for where companies actually keep their data: Databases, document stores, ticketing systems, machine logs, and sensor and video archives. Transaction layer: Own the pipeline, rights evidence, contracts, permissions, audit trail and delivery API. ML and data quality: Build anonymisation across text, tables, images and video, plus re-identification checks, deduplication, quality scoring and tooling that turns raw records into training-ready data. Delivery and compute: Decide whether data is processed in our cloud or inside the supplier’s environment. Build secure delivery, recurring updates and our GPU infrastructure. Technical direction: Own the architecture and roadmap. Work directly with labs, suppliers and researchers to understand what the system needs to become. What you need to succeed Data infrastructure at scale: You have built pipelines for large unstructured datasets, such as video, images, sensor logs or documents, at terabyte scale or more. Physical-world data: You have worked with documents, logs, video or sensor streams, ideally in robotics, industrial or autonomous systems and know what embodied AI teams need from data and where it breaks. Sensitive data: You know how to handle personal and confidential data safely. Experience with regulated data is a plus. Technical leadership: You make architectural decisions, explain them clearly and raise the engineering bar as the team grows. Hands-on Builder: You have taken a product, platform or open-source project from 0 to 1 that others relied on, and you still write code and own the critical paths. Founder mindset: You care about the outcome, not the title. You form strong views, test them quickly and are comfortable owning technical, product and operational problems. Location: Paris preferred. English required; French is a plus. Please note: As a co-founder, you take a real stake in what we build. Its European tech hub delivers data and analytics projects, mostly in finance and other regulated industries. A data project for a Nordic banking customer is starting, and the delivery team is adding a data scientist from day one. Role / Mission A business problem comes in, you turn it into a machine learning solution, build it in Python on large datasets in Teradata Vantage, and hand it over ready for production. Typical use cases on banking projects like this one: fraud and anomaly detection in transactions, credit risk scoring, churn prediction and customer segmentation. Turn business problems into data science use cases and agree the approach with the business Build and test ML models, from first experiment to a production-ready version Deploy them, using feature stores to develop and serve models Use generative AI (LLMs, transformers) where the use case calls for it Present results to executives, business owners and engineers Remote, with 1–2 days a week in Prague in the initial phase for onboarding. You join a team of specialists working in an agile way and report to the Head of Delivery. Working language is English. items.desc: Le Service de la Relation Usager (SRU) compte 120 agents agentes et comprend : a. Le centre de contacts qui regroupe le centre d’appels de la Ville et l’équipe messages des Parisien-ne-s qui traite les sollicitations numériques de Paris.fr et des sites des mairies d’arrondissements b. Le pôle Outils numériques transverses et data de la Relation Usager (outils et données utilisés par toute la Ville) c. Le pôle Études d. Le pôle Accompagnement et Qualité e. Le pôle Proximités : accès, accueil et accompagnement des usagers dans les services publics parisiens f. Les mission transverses : le Multicanal et l’Intelligence artificielle Au sein du pôle Outils, l’équipe Data est chargée de la gestion de plusieurs tableaux de bord de la qualité de la relation usager. Ces outils de pilotage par la donnée permettent de cibler les irritants dans les relations entre les services de la Ville et les parisiens. L’objectif de ces tableaux de bord est de recueillir et synthétiser des indicateurs utiles au suivi de la qualité des relations avec nos usagers. Ces indicateurs sont par exemple : l’audience d’un service numérique ou des pages du site Paris.fr, le volume et les motifs des sollicitations reçues en ligne ou par téléphone, le nombre de prestations demandées, les délais moyens pour les délivrer, la satisfaction des usagers à propos de ce service, etc… Le service est à la fois opérateur de service avec le centre de contacts et expert métier au service des directions. Quelles sont vos missions ? De la technique et de la personnalité : passionné(e) de chiffres et de statistiques, vous aimez autant la Data que faire parler vos interlocuteurs interlocutrices dans les directions pour comprendre leurs besoins. Vous avez à cœur de comprendre les problématiques du service public et de la relation usager et vous êtes force de propositions. En étroite collaboration avec la DSIN, vous êtes chargé chargée de concevoir une architecture de données optimale afin de mettre en relation plus de 50 sources de données jusqu’alors silotées (services numériques de la Ville). En amont vous avez pour mission de recueillir les besoins métiers ; animer un réseau de fournisseurs de données au sein des directions ; et accompagner l’élargissement de la base de données actuelle. En aval, vous travaillez à la visualisation des données afin de les diffuser aux directions impliquées et aux organes de pilotage de la relation usager. Ce travail vise à ancrer le rôle des tableaux de bord comme outil d’aide à la décision. Vous accompagnez la montée en compétences analytique de nos directions métier sur le pilotage et la gestion de leur relation usager en leur fournissant des reporting adaptés. La pédagogie et l’aisance à communiquer avec des personnes néophytes sont des compétences importantes pour ce poste. Vous êtes amené amenée à répondre à leurs demandes d’évolution de leurs tableaux de bord (en particulier ceux de DansMaRue, Solen, Kiamo ou Rendez-vous). Vous êtes utilisateur utilisatrice de vos propres réalisations et devez réaliser des analyses poussées à destination des organes de décisions, mairies d’arrondissement et directions de la Ville pour les aider à mieux comprendre l’usager parisien et ses besoins. Vous êtes également un acteur majeur une actrice majeure pour introduire l’intelligence artificielle au sein de la Ville : analyse du langage naturel, transcriptions d’audios, segmentation… Qu’attend-on de vous ? items.desc: STRUCMEDICA : le stéthoscope du béton, au service d’une ingénierie augmentée. Nous aidons les gestionnaires d’ouvrages, ingénieurs et acteurs du diagnostic à mieux décider pour la maintenance et la rénovation. Mesures non destructives, science des matériaux et analyse assistée par IA servent à cartographier des indicateurs de durabilité, cibler les recommandations et prioriser les interventions. Notre ambition : réduire les carottages évitables, limiter les perturbations d’exploitation et accélérer la décision. Des applications liées au CO₂ uptake peuvent contribuer aux études de durabilité et d’ACV/LCA des matériaux cimentaires. Ce projet primé s’appuie sur des partenaires, contributeurs et conseillers complémentaires. Nous renforçons un comité consultatif resserré pour soutenir une croissance crédible et durable. Description du poste Associer votre expérience produit, votre expertise en IA physique et votre réseau à notre ambition : créer de la valeur et faire grandir STRUCMEDICA. En rejoignant notre comité consultatif comme Conseiller IA physique et produit, vous devenez un partenaire de réflexion actif. Nous croisons votre expertise avec notre connaissance du projet. Cette collaboration repose sur Merit, Excellence and Impact : reconnaître les réalisations et la contribution de chacun, travailler avec rigueur et transformer nos échanges en avancées utiles. Votre réputation professionnelle et les relations de confiance que vous avez construites prennent toute leur valeur lorsqu’elles éclairent un choix ou ouvrent une perspective pertinente. Ce que nous voulons faire avancer ensemble : Un produit utile aux professionnels : croiser nos connaissances pour challenger les usages, les priorités et la valeur apportée aux décisions de maintenance et de rénovation. Des choix technologiques argumentés : bénéficier de votre expérience pour éclairer la fiabilité, l’explicabilité et les limites des approches associant physique, données et IA. Des perspectives de réalisation et d’adoption : mettre en relation les besoins métier, les critères de qualité et les décisions qui permettent de développer un produit pertinent. L’accès aux bonnes expertises : mobiliser, avec consentement, des relations qualifiées avec des spécialistes, partenaires techniques et profils expérimentés. Nous prévoyons a minima 2 heures toutes les 8 semaines. Des échanges complémentaires pourront être convenus ensemble, selon les besoins et vos disponibilités. Fully self-funded, profitable and still expanding, we’re a strong and supportive team with a stable foundation. Why adstrong 100% remote: work from anywhere in the EU, with flexible hours and no weekend or night work. No process chaos: documentation and procedures are well-structured and digital. No politics: we encourage proactive decisions and make ours within 24 hours. Stable and growing: a fully self-funded, fast-growing company with no external investors. Small, skilled team: a hands-on tech team of around 6 people. Great working culture: supportive colleagues who help each other and share knowledge openly. AI-first: coding agents are how we build, and your judgement is what matters. Attractive compensation: plus all the equipment you need. Missing anything? Get a goal, not a ticket: work directly with colleagues on the business side to gather requirements, align on the solution and build it into working software. Make sound architecture and data-model decisions , keeping our systems fast and reliable as we scale. Take ownership of existing applications and build new solutions for our affiliate business. Design and develop event-driven backend systems that handle large volumes of product and campaign data, mostly in Rust and partly in Python. Own your topics end to end and keep the team and stakeholders in the loop along the way. What you bring Experience contributing to a strong engineering culture , e.g. through code reviews, knowledge sharing, or improving team tools and ways of working. Daily hands-on work with coding agents: you plan with AI, delegate the implementation and know how to review what comes back, including more complex workflows like one model writing code while another reviews it. Strong architectural awareness: you know which components and infrastructure to use for which problem, and how to structure what you build. Rust experience , or curiosity about it and readiness to make it your main language , as most of our backend is written in it. C or C++ experience is a strong alternative. Experience solving problems close to ours, ideally in e-commerce, affiliate marketing, Google Shopping, Google Ads or other data-heavy web platforms. Our business team will help you build the domain knowledge. Experience with event-driven systems (e.g. Kafka, AWS SQS/SNS or similar) A solid grasp of the full engineering process : requirements, design, trade-offs, testing and maintainability Mid- or senior-level experience. We care more about how you think and work than about years on paper. Our business team will help you build the domain knowledge. A Bachelor’s degree in computer science or a related field. Business-fluent English (C1). Our stack: Rust (plus some Python) on the backend, and TypeScript / Next.js on the frontend. The frontend is owned by our frontend engineers, so experience there is a plus but not required. How you work You communicate clearly and proactively. You’re comfortable talking to business colleagues, ask the right questions early, share progress without being asked and explain technical trade-offs in plain language. You value good engineering culture. We improve as a team, so honest feedback matters to us, and so do your ideas for improving our team culture, tools and the way we work in IT. You organize yourself. Give you a goal, and you’ll plan the work, set priorities and follow through, without needing a detailed ticket for every step. You’re genuinely curious. You enjoy digging into new topics, including the business side, and you keep learning as tools and AI evolve. You take ownership. You care about the outcome, not just the code, and you drive your topics forward instead of waiting for direction. If you match most of these points and want to help shape the technology behind one of Europe’s leading CSS providers, we’d love to hear from you. There’s no classic coding test in our process. Instead, we’ll talk through a realistic goal together and see how you approach it with AI. Apply now if you want stability without standing still: a place to learn, grow and stay.

items.desc: ABOUT BUILD AI for the Built World: Build helps the world's largest real estate and infrastructure institutions find, test and plan sites a magnitude faster than the market. Clients get site sourcing, due diligence, feasibility and test fits delivered in days rather than months, by a team of experts working alongside AI. It covers the projects that matter most: digital infrastructure, energy and industrial, from concept to completion. Our mission is to accelerate and amplify the world's most important built projects - inventing a better way to build through a collaboration between human experts and AI. We envision a future where the world's buildings are driven from concept to completion. Without delays, cost or complexity. Enabling people to deliver a magnitude more deals. To make decisions, build relationships and create. We're partnering with the world's biggest built world institutions, from $T alternative asset investors to prolific developers and even governments, to push the frontier of what's possible. We're backed by c-suite from Blackstone and OpenAI alongside the world's best venture capital firms. ABOUT THE ROLE The Computational Design Engineer owns how Build looks, feels and works, and ships it in production code. This is a design role and an engineering role in equal measure. You'll design the product and the 3D and site design tools behind it, then build them yourself: production React and TypeScript on the front end, and Rhino, Grasshopper and Python for the geometry underneath. Our clients make big decisions about land, power and buildings. What they see from us has to be clear enough to act on and good enough to defend in an investment committee. You'll design and build the product they use every day, the tools that lay out a site in minutes and the deliverables that land on their desk. There's no handoff. You sketch it, model it, build it, ship it and watch how clients use it. You'll be the design lead on a small team that ships fast, working directly with James SE and alongside our engineers and domain experts. WHAT YOU WILL OWN Spatial and 3D design tools: the parametric logic, site layouts, 3D views and CAD outputs behind the test fits clients use to decide what a site can hold Product design end to end: user flows, interfaces and the details inside them, from first concept to shipped feature The front end: building what you design in React and TypeScript, reviewed and shipped to the same standard as our engineers The design system: one set of components, type, motion and rules that keeps every surface consistent and lets the whole team ship good work without you in the room Making complex work clear: turning maps, site data and multi-step workflows into screens and reports a client can read in a minute and trust Everything around the product: flagship demos, the website and the deliverables clients actually receive Time with clients: seeing how decisions get made and approved on real projects, and feeding that straight back into what we build EXAMPLE PROJECTS Taking a site layout tool from a working prototype to something a client runs on their own, from the rules that place each block to the screen they adjust it on Building a single design package and moving the product onto it Redesigning the map so every type of site data reads at a glance Turning a complex workflow into an interface a client can follow and defend internally Redesigning the decks and drawings we deliver so they read like they came from the best firm in the market WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR A designer who engineers. You've trained in architecture, product or computational design, and somewhere along the way you started writing production code yourself. You see systems, not one-off screens, and you'd rather make a tool that produces a hundred good answers than draw one by hand. You have real taste and you're unreasonable about quality, but you ship. YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF You work in 3D and geometry: Rhino and Grasshopper, Python or C#, Three.js or similar, and you've built tools, not just used them You've shipped production front end (React, TypeScript, Next.js) as well as designing it You have a few years at a leading architecture, design or engineering practice, or at a product company building design or spatial tools, or your own practice with this at its core You've made complex tools simple enough for people who aren't technical to use Your portfolio shows both the thinking and the working thing that shipped You hold your own with engineers and want to be held to an engineering standard You care about AI, software and how the physical world gets built THIS PROBABLY ISN'T YOU IF You can design but not build, or build but have no taste You need tightly scoped specs before you can start You see polish as optional or the small details as someone else's job BONUS POINTS …

Within this department, the Soil and Plant Care Unit contributes to the development of solutions designed to improve soil quality and increase plant resistance to biotic threats, including pathogens and pests. To strengthen our expertise in this field, we are looking for a : Research engineer in Plant Science / Plant Biotic Stress, in Saint-Malo, France. About the position: Reporting to the Project Manager biotic stress, you will contribute to projects aimed at better understanding the relationships between plants and biotic threats, as well as the mechanisms involved in improving plant tolerance to biotic stress. You will be expected to demonstrate strong knowledge in plant– pathogen and/or plant–pest interactions, in microbiology and/or entomology, as well as in plant physiology. Key responsibilities : Identification, development, and implementation of methods to screen, evaluate, and investigate the efficacy of new developed products. Investigate the mechanisms involved in plant tolerance to biotic stress, as well as those underlying the virulence and/or fitness of pathogens and pests. Plan and conduct experiments, analyze the data, synthesize and interpret the results. Contribute to the project deliverables, including reports, summaries, and other scientific documents. items.desc: About Us Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces. Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. About The Role As Signal Processing Engineer within RF Processing & Analytics, you own the algorithms that turn raw electromagnetic intercepts into an actionable picture of the RF environment — detecting, characterizing, and identifying the emitters around our platforms in contested environments. You work across the signals captured by our Radar, Radio, and Electronic Warfare modules, building the classification and analytics layer that turns isolated detections into a real-time electronic order of battle for operators and downstream autonomy. Responsibilities Signal Detection & Characterization: Build algorithms to detect, deinterleave, and extract parameters (PRI, pulse width, frequency, modulation) from intercepted RF emissions. Emitter Classification & Identification: Develop classification pipelines — combining feature-based methods and machine learning — to identify emitter types and match them against threat libraries. Electronic Order of Battle: Design the analytics that turn individual detections into a coherent, real-time picture of emitters, tracks, and threat posture. AI-Assisted Analytics: Apply machine learning to modulation recognition, anomaly detection, and emitter fingerprinting where it improves classification confidence in dense, contested spectrum. Cross-Module Data Fusion: Work with signals captured by Radar, Radio, and Electronic Warfare to build a unified processing pipeline rather than siloed, single-sensor analysis. Real-Time Pipeline Engineering: Take algorithms from offline prototyping (MATLAB/Python) to real-time or near-real-time implementation, alongside software and embedded/FPGA engineers. Field Validation: Validate detection and classification performance against simulated and real-world RF datasets, in lab and field-test conditions. Candidate Requirements Master's or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Signal Processing, Applied Mathematics, or a related field. 3-6 years of experience in RF/radar signal processing, ideally with exposure to ELINT, ESM, or SIGINT applications. Strong fundamentals in DSP: spectral analysis, filtering, multi-rate processing, statistical/adaptive signal processing. Proficiency in Python and/or MATLAB for algorithm prototyping; working knowledge of C/C++ for production-oriented implementation. Comfortable applying machine learning to signal classification problems. Clear communicator, able to work across RF hardware, software, and data science disciplines. Fluency in English required; French is a plus. We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

items.desc: Är du en student som är ivrig att tillämpa dina teoretiska kunskaper och nya perspektiv på verkliga utmaningar? På Saab tror vi att innovationer växer på nya idéer, och ditt examensarbete kan vara gnistan som tänder vårt nästa tekniska genombrott. Din roll Vi ser det enorma värdet som studenter tillför vårt företag. Din akademiska precision, i kombination med din entusiasm för avancerad teknik, gör att du kan närma dig problem med en unik och insiktsfull lins. På Saab får du möjlighet att samarbeta med erfarna ingenjörer och specialister, få ovärderlig praktisk erfarenhet och samtidigt bidra till vår tillväxt och utveckling. Bakgrund Verifiering av digitala styrsystem i moderna flygplan bygger till stor del på omfattande simuleringar där flygegenskaper och systembeteenden utvärderas under olika förhållanden. För stridsflygplan ställs dessutom höga krav på att styrsystemet ska vara "care-free", vilket innebär att piloten ska kunna genomföra relevanta manövrar utan att riskera att hamna i ett farligt tillstånd. För att verifiera dessa egenskaper används idag ett stort antal fördefinierade manövrar som syftar till att utmana styrsystemet under olika förhållanden. Trots detta kan det fortfarande finnas kombinationer av manövrar, flygtillstånd och lastkonfigurationer som leder till mer kritiska utfall. Utmaningen blir särskilt relevant för framtida stridsflygsystem där nya koncept och användningsfall kan innebära helt andra dimensionerande manövrar än idag. Verifieringsutmaningen kan därför formuleras som ett sökproblem där målet är att identifiera dessa worst-case-fall. I dagsläget är verifierings- och klareringsprocessen både tidskrävande och resursintensiv, eftersom ett mycket stort antal scenarier behöver analyseras och utvärderas. Att identifiera kritiska testfall på ett mer automatiserat sätt är därför en viktig utmaning inom flygindustrin. En sådan förmåga har potential att både effektivisera verifieringsarbetet och öka testtäckningen för framtida flygsystem. Inom flygteknisk forskning har arbetet mot en automatiserad klarering främst innefattat metoder såsom Monte Carlo-simuleringar och metaheuristiska optimeringsalgoritmer. Dessa metoder optimerar dock vanligtvis mot en enskild lösning och har sämre prestanda när problemet omfattas av ett stort antal komplexa bivillkor. Reinforcement Learning (RL) har däremot visat stor potential som metod för att effektivt utforska omfattande parameterrymder och identifiera worst-case-scenarier samtidigt som givna bivillkor beaktas. Beskrivning av examensarbetet Examensarbetet syftar till att undersöka hur RL-baserade metoder kan användas för att identifiera worst-case manövrar givet en mängd olika flygtillstånd, lastkonfigurationer och andra variabler. Målet är att utveckla och utvärdera ett ramverk som kan bidra till en mer effektiv och systematisk klareringsprocess. Arbetet ger möjlighet att kombinera artificiell intelligens, optimering och simulering för att lösa ett verkligt problem inom utvecklingen av framtida flygsystem. En viktig del av arbetet kommer även att vara att analysera och visualisera den stora mängden utforskade testfallsparametrar. Detta är tänkt att användas som ett beslutsstödsunderlag som gör det möjligt att identifiera trender, avvikelser och potentiella problemområden. Arbetet kan innefatta: Litteraturstudie på tidigare forskning inom området. Formulering av lämpliga ”reward functions” utifrån systemets krav och begränsningar. Design och implementering av RL-ramverkets arkitektur och flöde. Presentation av data och worst-case fall. Jämförelse mot nuvarande metodik. Examensarbetet genomförs inom sektionen Verifiering och Validering för styrsystem på Saab Aeronautics, som arbetar med verifiering av styrsystem för både nuvarande och framtida stridsflyg. Studenten kommer att arbeta i nära samarbete med ingenjörer med specialistkompetens inom bland annat styrsystem, simulering och verifiering, och får stöd av erfarna handledare under arbetets gång. Projektet adresserar ett verkligt verksamhetsbehov och har potential att effektivisera den tidskrävande verifieringsprocessen, vilket kan bidra till snabbare utveckling av framtida stridsflygsystem. Din profil Arbetet är lämpligt för 1–2 studenter med intresse för maskininlärning, optimering och programmering. Intresse för flyg är också meriterande. Du/ni är i slutet av er civilingenjörsutbildning inom teknisk fysik, datateknik eller motsvarande utbildning och ska påbörja ert examensarbete om 30 hp. Du ska ha god analytisk förmåga och fallenhet för att tänka utanför boxen. Utbildning/erfarenhet inom följande är meriterande för detta examensarbete: Maskininlärning, specifikt Reinforcement Learning. Goda kunskaper inom exempelvis Python, Git och Matlab. Vi ger dig det stöd och den vägledning du behöver för att omsätta dina teoretiska kunskaper i praktiska lösningar. Bli en drivande kraft bakom Saabs tekniska framsteg! items.desc: WHAT YOU WILL BE WORKING ON​ Gameloft Barcelona is seeking a Data Scientist to join Gameloft Global Data team. As a Data Scientist, you will be able to deep dive into our massive streams of player data in-game, prototype and deploy machine learning models to increase game revenue. You will help move projects from exploratory analysis to deployed models across live titles, including life-simulation and racing games. What it means on a daily basis​ Analyse large-scale player data with Python and SQL, transforming it into clear, actionable insights. Perform feature engineering on large-scale data from the data warehouse, managing your code with Git. Prototype and improve machine learning models and prediction pipelines, using experimental design, causal inference, and A/B testing to raise performance baselines. Present findings and recommendations to non-technical stakeholders across the game teams. What success will look like​ In your first months, you will ramp up on our data infrastructure and deliver your first exploratory analyses.By the middle of your onboarding, you will be responsible for features or models end-to-end, framing problems clearly and presenting them to non-technical stakeholders. By the end of your onboarding, you will be conducting experiments and delivering improvements on your own, with your insights adopted across the game teams. Who you will be working with As a Data Scientist in our Global Data Science and Analytics team, you will be reporting to our Lead Data Scientist and collaborate very closely with other Data teams (Data Analyst, Data Engineering) and with our local Game teams. Our teams operate across multiple studios worldwide, including Paris, Barcelona, Montreal, Sofia, Bucharest, and others, offering opportunities to collaborate with colleagues from diverse backgrounds and perspectives. Your recruitment journey​ First interview: An initial discussion to explore how the role aligns with your background and to address your main questions.​ Test: You will be given a case study to complete.​ Second interview: A technical interview focused on presenting your test and discussing your approach, reasoning, and methodologies in more depth.​ Final interview: A conversation to discuss your experience, vision, and how you approach data topics at a broader level.​ ​Where this role can take you​ This role can be a stepping stone toward a more senior position, with the possibility of leading increasingly large and complex projects, so that your work shapes game performance and business results more widely over time. WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED​ Proficient in Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, Matplotlib, seaborn) and in SQL for large-scale data analysis. Skilled in machine learning workflows, including experimental design, causal inference, and A/B testing. Experienced with Git and comfortable working with large-scale data in a data warehouse environment. Master's degree in a quantitative field (computer science, applied mathematics, data science, or related). WHO YOU ARE​ Able to communicate and present to non-technical stakeholders in English, translating analytical work into clear, actionable recommendations. WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU​ Permanent contract, full-time employment with comprehensive Social Benefits. 25 vacation days per year + Birthday day off. Private medical health insurance. Flexible compensation with Ticket Restaurant Card. Free language courses. Work-from-home hybrid model. Merit based salary progression system and a competitive initial salary package. Life at Gameloft Our Barcelona studio offers real career development opportunities and a positive working environment in a centrally located office. We value supportive working conditions and a balanced work-life approach, and our teams work together with a collaborative mindset. Ready to level up your career? Apply now with your CV in English.

Full-time, Remote, AI / Document Intelligence Engineer Company Overview Sparengine is an AI-powered aviation technical records reconstruction and audit platform. We process raw maintenance documentation (logbooks, work orders, AD compliance records, CAMP exports) through a multi-pass pipeline that produces structured asset snapshots, component history reports, and pre-purchase inspection deliverables. We operate an international hybrid model with European direction and a high-performance technical team. We prioritize rigor and clarity in a domain where being confidently wrong is the worst possible failure. The Role: Scope & Execution This is the engineering core of the product. You will build and harden the multi-pass pipeline that turns thousands of unstructured pages into a verifiable knowledge graph. Build the pipeline: page-level vision extraction, document typing and segmentation, entity and event extraction, and graph construction Own the knowledge graph: the system's truth memory, where every claim is attached to evidence with confidence and provenance Make the model cautious: enforce the distinction between a task listed on a card and a task actually signed off, so the system behaves like a careful analyst rather than a confident guesser Improve retrieval: fuzzy part number and serial number matching, proximity search, and cross-document linking across large dossiers Technical Requirements Python and solid LLM orchestration experience Structured data: comfortable with JSON and JSONL at scale, streamable and queryable Retrieval: practical understanding of fuzzy matching and context-aware relevance A natural instinct for clean code and for catching silent failures before they reach a deliverable Professional Qualifications Proven execution: you have built and shipped real data or AI pipelines beyond tutorials Technical maturity: you simplify complex requirements and keep the system reliable Bonus: prior exposure to OCR pipelines, vision models, or graph data structures Evidence of work: a portfolio or GitHub showing end-to-end systems you have built Practical Details Location: Remote Type: Full-time Compensation: Based on profile Why Sparengine You will work at the point where messy reality meets structured truth. The product only works if the engineering is honest about what it does not know, so the work rewards people who care about precision, provenance, and shipping systems that experts can trust. You will see your code directly change how high-value aviation assets are bought, sold, and audited. About Sparengine Every aircraft has a hidden story. We make it legible. Sparengine is aircraft intelligence. Decades of scattered records, scans, inspection photos and systems become one connected view of an aircraft: its condition, its history, what the evidence supports and what is missing. Lessors, MROs and traders use it to decide what an aircraft is really worth. A small team in Toulouse and remote. Real problems, real customers, and ownership from day one. items.desc: Job reference: SAE-032577 Salary: £37,694 to £42,254 per annum depending on relevant experience Faculty/Organisational Unit: Science and Engineering Location: Oxford Road Employment type: Fixed Term Division/Team: Department of Civil Engineering and Management Hours Per Week: 35 Closing date (DD/MM/YYYY): 08/11/2026 Contract Duration: 24 months School/Directorate: School of Engineering We are seeking to appoint a talented and enthusiastic Postdoctoral Research Associate (PDRA) to play a key role in delivering an exciting investment project (IrrEO) that will develop satellite-based irrigation mapping tools for governments and development actors in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Earth Observation (EO) technologies are enabling agricultural mapping at increasingly large scales and fine resolutions. This brings exciting opportunities to understand complex farming systems, particularly in data-sparse smallholder farming regions. However, recent research has revealed the social risks of EO-based land monitoring. Examples include imperfect representations leading to poorly informed decision-making or biased investments, and marginalised people being made visible through EO in ways which may expose them to harm. There is an urgent need for improved social risk analysis and development of good practice guidance for EO-based agricultural mapping. As part of the IrrEO project, the PDRA will lead on developing guidance for the socially responsible development and use of EO-based agricultural mapping tools in small-scale farming systems in Sub-Saharan Africa. They will catalogue existing scholarship and frameworks on the ethical and equitable use of EO in agricultural mapping. They will also carry out document-based and qualitative interview research to identify potential risks of EO-based agricultural mapping in different socio-political and agricultural contexts, focusing particularly on risks to farmers and farming communities. Based on these two workstreams and consultation with the IrrEO partners, they will devise and share strategies for socially response EO-based agricultural monitoring. The PDRA will be an integral member of the IrrEO project team, working closely with Principal Investigator Prof. Tim Foster (Department of Civil Engineering and Management) and Co-Investigators Dr. Rose Pritchard (Global Development Institute). They will also work closely with a wider team of investigators and postdoctoral researchers at the University of Manchester involved in the IrrEO project and other aligned research on socially-just use of Earth Observation including the Just Earth Observation for Conservation project (JEOC – https://www.justearthobservation.org/) which is co-led by Pritchard and Foster. The role will involve close collaboration with academic and non-academic partners in the project’s case study countries (Kenya, Nigeria, and Ethiopia) and active engagement with UK and international partners including the World Bank and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. The IrrEO project is funded by a four-year (2025-2029) investment from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. Due to the nature of the funding, this post is available for a fixed term of up to 24 months with an end date of 31 August 2029. We are looking for a candidate to start in early 2027, with some flexibility over the exact start date. Enquiries About The Role, Shortlisting And Interviews Name: Prof Tim Foster, Professor of Land and Water Informatics and Director of Manchester Environmental Research Institute (MERI) Email General enquiries and administrative support

items.card: About The Role Callosum believes that orders of magnitude improvements in AI systems will come through application-aware orchestration across heterogeneous hardware. As workloads become increasingly disaggregated, the performance of the system is determined not only by where computation happens, but by how efficiently state and data can move between the hardware best suited to each part of the workload.
items.desc: About Us We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity. Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next. The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve. Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost. Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor. In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence. We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you. About The Role Callosum believes that orders of magnitude improvements in AI systems will come through application-aware orchestration across heterogeneous hardware. As workloads become increasingly disaggregated, the performance of the system is determined not only by where computation happens, but by how efficiently state and data can move between the hardware best suited to each part of the workload. Communication latency sets the boundary on how far that disaggregation can go. This role owns that boundary. You will develop the communication systems that allow heterogeneous accelerators to operate as parts of one system, working across protocols, memory movement, networking hardware, and the software layers above them. That means understanding where overhead actually comes from, removing assumptions inherited from more general-purpose workloads, and finding new ways to move data directly and efficiently across vendor boundaries. The remit is intentionally broad: from RDMA paths and programmable NICs to cache transfer formats and emerging interconnect technologies, you will own the technical strategy for making communication less of a constraint on the systems we can build. What You'll Build Characterise and simplify communication paths between accelerators, tracing latency and unnecessary overhead across networking, runtime, memory, and device layers Develop faster data movement across heterogeneous hardware, exploring RDMA, programmable NICs, DPUs, switches, and software approaches to cross-device memory management Build flexible mechanisms for transferring model state across accelerator types and execution strategies, including KV cache connectors across different forms of parallelism Evaluate existing and emerging scale-up and scale-out fabrics, informing cluster architecture, infrastructure integration, and how heterogeneous accelerator communication should evolve What Sets You Apart Deep understanding of networking and communication systems, with the ability to reason across protocols, hardware, memory systems, and software layers Experience with high-performance data movement such as RDMA, Ethernet fabrics, accelerator interconnects, programmable networking, or similar latency-sensitive systems Strong systems performance instincts, with the ability to trace bottlenecks across abstraction layers and distinguish fundamental constraints from accidental ones A demonstrable tendency to question existing abstractions, generalise across unfamiliar technologies, and simplify systems around the requirements of the workload What We Offer Competitive Salary, determined by skills and experience Equity & Ownership Private …

items.desc: Steeds meer ontwikkelaars gebruiken Large Language Models (LLM’s) tijdens het programmeren. In deze opdracht onderzoek je hoe meerdere lokale open source LLM’s objectief met elkaar kunnen worden vergeleken, zodat ontwikkelaars voor elke stageopdracht het meest geschikte model kunnen kiezen. Ontwikkelaars gebruiken steeds vaker LLM’s om code te schrijven, fouten te analyseren of technische vragen te beantwoorden. Vaak gebeurt dit via cloudoplossingen, maar dat is niet altijd wenselijk. Broncode, klantinformatie of interne documentatie mag niet zomaar naar externe diensten gestuurd worden. Open source LLM’s die lokaal draaien, bieden hiervoor een alternatief. Toch is het moeilijk om te bepalen welk model het beste resultaat geeft voor een specifieke opdracht. Elk model heeft andere sterktes, bijvoorbeeld op het gebied van codegeneratie, uitleg of redeneervermogen. Er is daarom behoefte aan een lokaal systeem dat één opdracht aan meerdere open source LLM’s kan voorleggen, de antwoorden vergelijkt en het beste resultaat helpt kiezen. De opdracht Onderzoek hoe een lokaal systeem ontwikkelaars kan ondersteunen bij het vergelijken van meerdere open source LLM-agents. Bouw een Proof of Concept waarin een ontwikkelaar één opdracht invoert, waarna het systeem deze opdracht lokaal doorstuurt naar verschillende modellen. Vergelijk de antwoorden op criteria zoals correctheid, volledigheid, snelheid, uitlegbaarheid en bruikbaarheid. Onderzoek ook de beperkingen van lokale modellen, zoals hardwarevereisten, responstijd en modelgrootte. Het resultaat is een werkende Proof of Concept met een onderbouwde vergelijking van meerdere open source LLM’s. Over Info Support Info Support is specialist in maatwerksoftware, data/AI solutions, beheer en trainingen en actief in de sectoren Finance, Industry, Agriculture, Food & Retail, Mobility & Public en Healthcare. Wij bieden solide en innovatieve oplossingen voor complexe en bedrijfkritische softwarevraagstukken. Onze hoofdkantoren zijn gevestigd in Mechelen (BE) en Veenendaal (NL). Op dit moment zijn er circa 500 medewerkers bij Info Support in dienst. De werkwijze van Info Support kenmerkt zich door een aantal kernwaarden: soliditeit, integriteit, vakmanschap en passie. Deze kernwaarden zijn verweven in ons werk en de manier waarop we met elkaar omgaan. Om te zorgen dat alle medewerkers altijd op de hoogte kunnen zijn van de nieuwste ontwikkelingen beschikt Info Support over een inhouse IT Academy waar graag wordt voldaan aan de honger naar meer of andere kennis en vaardigheden. Om deze opdracht te kunnen doen is B2-taalvaardigheid in het Nederlands vereist.

items.desc: Automated code review tools like GitHub Copilot are on the rise, but how do their reviews compare to those written by human developers? This thesis explores the quality, depth, and relevance of AI-generated reviews to understand whether these tools truly support or replace peer review. Expect to dive into real-world code review data, assess review performance and uncover when AI adds value, or falls short, in development workflows. Code reviews are a key practice in modern software engineering, improving code quality, maintainability and knowledge sharing within development teams. Traditionally, these reviews are conducted manually by peers. However, with the rise of AI tools like GitHub Copilot, developers can now request automated pull request reviews. While these AI-generated reviews promise greater efficiency, there is little empirical evidence on how their quality compares to that of human reviewers. The Assignment In this thesis, you will investigate the quality of AI-generated code reviews. Your focus will be on identifying differences in quality, depth and relevance compared to reviews written by humans. By analyzing these aspects, you will assess whether and how AI can support or complement human reviewers. Your findings will highlight current limitations and provide insights into how development teams can best utilize AI-based review tools in practice. items.desc: Met de opkomst van AI in codeontwikkeling verbeteren tools zoals GitHub en Copilot de productiviteit al aanzienlijk. Dit roept de vraag op: kunnen we nog verder gaan wanneer het gaat om het bouwen van cruciale datasystemen? Het ontwikkelen van ETL-pipelines kost veel tijd, kent veel herhalende patronen en vormt de basis voor kwalitatieve data in systemen die onze nationale digitale infrastructuur ondersteunen. Dit biedt kansen voor innovatie. Onderzoek hoe generative AI specificaties uit feature files kan omzetten in werkende code en ontwikkel een prototype dat laat zien hoe een LLM automatisch ETL-pipelines genereert op basis van standaardcomponenten, een stap richting efficiëntere, robuustere en toekomstbestendige IT-oplossingen met directe maatschappelijke waarde. Deze afstudeeropdracht maakt deel uit van het project ‘Critical IT Protocol NL’. Met dit project geven we Nederland een digitale boost door het bouwen van IT-oplossingen voor kritieke maatschappelijke uitdagingen. Van betaalverkeer en overheidsdiensten tot cybersecurity en crisisdetectie: samen versterken we de digitale infrastructuur van Nederland met impact die telt. We zien steeds meer de mogelijkheid om AI in te zetten om code te schrijven. In het geval van Github Copilot bijvoorbeeld verbetert het de productiviteit al tot 50%. Dat is een indrukwekkend getal. Maar zou je nog verder kunnen gaan? We merken bij onze klanten dat er veel tijd gaat zitten in het maken van ETL pipelines. Veel van de pipelines lijken op elkaar. We verzamelen data in een staging locatie, transformeren de data zodat we diverse kwaliteitsproblemen oplossen en zetten de data daarna om naar een dimensioneel formaat of naar een feature set voor machine learning. Zou dit niet heel handig geautomatiseerd kunnen worden door het vertalen van een specificatie in een feature file om te zetten naar werkende code door middel van generative AI?
