 · Garantizar el correcto suministro de materiales a las líneas de producción.
 · Gestionar el desempeño de los operadores logísticos mediante KPIs, SLAs y planes de mejora.
 · Coordinar la resolución de incidencias críticas y promover la implantación de medidas correctivas y preventivas.
 · Representar al sector en proyectos estratégicos de fábrica y lanzamientos industriales.
 · Impulsar iniciativas de eficiencia, optimización de costes y mejora continua.
 · Gestionar proyectos centrales, junto con otras plantas del Grupo y áreas corporativas.

 · Experiencia en gestión logística, gestión de procesos productivos o entornos industriales.
 · Capacidad de liderazgo y coordinación de equipos multidisciplinares.
 · Alta orientación a resultados y resolución de problemas.
 · Nivel alto de inglés. Alemán valorable.

 · Liderar una operación logística de gran relevancia para la planta.

items.title: Research Scientist/Engineer, Semiconductor Process Integration and 3D Technologies
items.card: Your responsibilities as Research Scientist / Research Engineer: Development and characterization of processes for monolithic and heterogeneous integration for post-CMOS integration Solving complex fabrication challenges Communicating and solving the problems in tight collaboration with others at VTT Who we are looking for: Experience in semiconductor process integration and 3D technologies You have a MSc or PhD in
items.desc: Are you interested in semiconductor fabrication and 3D integration and looking for a new job opportunity in the field? Would you like to develop innovative technology with superb colleagues who are top experts in their field? Do you want to build an excellent science career and work at the interface of academy and industry? VTT is one of the leading applied research organisations in Europe. What unites us are curiosity, a passion for learning and a purpose: to solve the biggest challenges of our time and turn them into sustainable growth and well-being. Our cross-disciplinary community of over 2300 brilliant minds is focused on creating impact through science-based innovation. Get to know us further by exploring VTT's tech & infra . We are now looking for Research Scientist or Research Engineer for 3D integration with a strong background in semiconductor device fabrication or process integration. You identify and solve problems independently and creatively, while working closely and flexibly with a team of experts. You focus on the design and fabrication aspects of developing processes for 3D integration of CMOS and semiconductor devices. You understand the big picture and participate in the concept development. Our team develops advanced semiconductor components focused on more than Moore applications such as CMOS integrated 2D sensors, in-memory analog computing, and post-CMOS 3D integration. The developments are made in close collaboration with our academic partners along the lines agreed with our industrial partners. Your responsibilities as Research Scientist / Research Engineer: Development and characterization of processes for monolithic and heterogeneous integration for post-CMOS integration Solving complex fabrication challenges Communicating and solving the problems in tight collaboration with others at VTT Who we are looking for: Experience in semiconductor process integration and 3D technologies You have a MSc or PhD in physics, electronics, or closely similar field. You have experience in cleanroom fabrication Excellent communications skills in English are required. As a person, we hope that you are: You have strong communication and collaboration skills. You are able to efficiently interact with your colleagues and with people from different fields. An enthusiastic outside-the-box thinker. You enjoy challenges and learning new things and have a strong passion for science and research and development A further benefit is knowledge about the interactions between research and business With VTT, you’ll enjoy: / What we offer you: Visionary work in technology. We offer positions at the cutting-edge of technology and engineering from next generation microelectronics and quantum technology to automation and robotics, energy systems and more. Our research agenda is dedicated to creating sustainable growth by solving systemic and technological challenges, so your work will go towards creating real, positive impact. Read more about our strategy – the path of exponential hope. Fascinating projects, excellent research environment. Our researchers get to work on a combination of cutting-edge academic research and applied customer projects, both locally and internationally. At VTT, you’ll have state-of-the-art research facilities at your disposal, such as Micronova, the Finnish research infrastructure for micro-, nano- and quantum technologies. Great career opportunities, superb colleagues. At VTT, excellence in research is a strategic priority. We offer long-term positions and stable career paths in top-level research. People tend to stay with us over 10 years since there are always new roles and responsibilities to grow into. Collaborating in a cross-disciplinary community with superb colleagues is a source of learning, inspiration, and fun. Read more about our organisational culture as the builder of the world's most meaningful place to work. Support for your well-being. Our people are our main asset, so we take good care of them. We aim to nurture great team spirit and leadership and offer versatile well-being services to enable a good work–life balance. On top of 6 weeks of paid holidays, we offer exercise and culture benefits, hobby clubs, and voluntary well-being services such as meditation programmes and trainings on cognitive ergonomics. Apply now and join our community of brilliant minds! Please send your CV with your salary request via our recruitment system as soon as possible but at the latest by 15 November 2026 Interested and want to hear more? For further information, please contact Research Team Leader Olli-Pekka Kilpi by email (olli-pekka.kilpi@vtt.fi). We look forward to hearing from you! items.desc: #StormYourCareer Rejoins STORM GROUP et construis ta carrière avec nous ! Détecte les menaces invisibles et révolutionne l?analyse comportementale du SOCAu sein du Security Operations Center (SOC) d?un grand compte, nous recherchons un(e) Data Scientist Cybersécurité / SOC. Ton rôle consistera à renforcer les capacités de détection des cybermenaces par l?exploitation avancée des données de sécurité, en concevant des modèles prédictifs et d?analyse comportementale pour isoler les signaux faibles et optimiser la réponse aux incidents. Ton futur environnementTu évolueras au c?ur du Security Operations Center d?une infrastructure d?envergure. En interface directe avec les analystes SOC, les ingénieurs SIEM et les spécialistes de la Threat Intelligence, tu interviendras sur des flux massifs de journaux d?événements. C?est le cadre idéal pour appliquer le Machine Learning et la Data Science à la lutte contre les cyberattaques, tout en industrialisant des modèles au sein d?architectures de données distribuées. Tes missions clésModélisation & Détection Avancée des Menaces (Mode DATA & IA) : Concevoir, développer et entraîner des modèles de détection d?anomalies sur des volumétries massives de journaux de sécurité (logs réseau, système, identité et applicatifs). Développer et déployer des algorithmes d?analyse comportementale des utilisateurs et des entités (UEBA) pour identifier les compromissions de comptes et les mouvements latéraux. Mettre en ?uvre des modèles de scoring et de priorisation dynamique des alertes afin de réduire le bruit et le taux de faux positifs pour les analystes. Réaliser l?ingénierie des caractéristiques (feature engineering) sur des jeux de données complexes et fortement déséquilibrés. Évaluer rigoureusement les performances des modèles à l?aide de métriques adaptées à la détection d?intrusions (précision, rappel, ROC-AUC, taux de faux positifs). Industrialisation & Collaboration SOC (Mode RUN & MLOps) : Assurer l?industrialisation, le déploiement et le monitoring continu des modèles en production (MLflow, Docker, Kubernetes). Collaborer au quotidien avec les analystes SOC et les équipes d?investigation pour qualifier les détections et réinjecter les retours terrain dans l?entraînement des algorithmes. Mener une veille active sur les nouvelles techniques d?attaque répertoriées dans le cadre de référence MITRE ATT&CK. Ton profilFormation : Diplôme d?Ingénieur ou Bac+5 en Data Science, statistiques, informatique décisionnelle ou cybersécurité. Expérience : Tu justifies d?une expérience de 3 à 5 ans en Data Science et Machine Learning, idéalement appliquée aux cas d?usage de la cybersécurité ou de la détection de fraude. Expertise Data Science & IA Impérative : Maîtrise des algorithmes de détection d?anomalies (Isolation Forest, autoencodeurs, One-Class SVM) et de l?apprentissage sur données déséquilibrées. Pratique confirmée de l?écosystème Python Data Science (Python, scikit-learn, PyTorch, pandas, numpy). Culture Cybersécurité & Données Massives : Bonne compréhension du fonctionnement d?un SOC, des typologies de menaces et de la matrice MITRE ATT&CK. Connaissance des architectures distribuées et des outils volumétriques (SQL, Spark, Kafka). Familiarité avec les solutions SIEM (Splunk, Elastic, Microsoft Sentinel) et le suivi de cycle de vie ML (MLflow). Langues : Anglais professionnel opérationnel. Tes atoutsEsprit d?Analyse et Goût pour l?Investigation : Curiosité intellectuelle pour traquer les anomalies statistiques au sein de flux de données brutes. Rigueur Méthodologique : Précision scientifique indispensable dans la validation des métriques de détection et la gestion des faux positifs. Sens du Travail d?Équipe : Aisance relationnelle pour vulgariser les choix algorithmiques auprès des analystes sécurité opérationnels. Nos avantagesRemboursement des titres de transport à hauteur de 75%. Tickets restaurant pris en charge par STORM GROUP à hauteur de 50% (10,5? / jour). Accès Gymlib / Wellpass (sport et bien-être). Contrat Santé / Prévoyance mis en place auprès de la compagnie Alan. Formation continue : Accès à Udemy Business. Prime de cooptation, prime d?intéressement et de participation. Deux à trois jours de télétravail par semaine. 5 raisons de nous rejoindreParcours sur mesure : Co-construis une trajectoire professionnelle unique, adaptée à tes ambitions. Missions Stratégiques : Interviens sur des projets d?envergure, en parfaite cohérence avec ton expertise. Suivi Dédié : Bénéficie d?un pilotage annuel structuré pour garantir ta progression continue. Excellence Continue : Développe tes compétences au quotidien au sein d?un écosystème exigeant. Performance Durable : Évolue dans un cadre où l?exigence métier respecte ton équilibre de vie.

items.card: vos missions seront les suivantes : Identifier, cadrer et mener des projets de recherche appliquée en IA et data science. Concevoir, développer et évaluer des agents IA experts et des architectures agentiques capables de mobiliser des connaissances scientifiques, de raisonner sur des problématiques métier et d’utiliser des outils, des modèles et des sources de données pour assister les workflows de recherche :
items.desc: Pourquoi a-t-on besoin de vous ? Au sein de la R&D de Saint-Gobain, l’équipe de Data Science développe et déploie des approches d’intelligence artificielle au service des activités scientifiques et industrielles du Groupe. L’équipe combine des compétences en analyse de données, statistiques, machine learning, IA générative, systèmes agentiques et graphes de connaissances pour accélérer la compréhension des phénomènes, la capitalisation des connaissances, la conception des matériaux et des procédés, ainsi que la transformation des pratiques de R&D. Dans ce cadre, vos missions seront les suivantes : Identifier, cadrer et mener des projets de recherche appliquée en IA et data science. Concevoir, développer et évaluer des agents IA experts et des architectures agentiques capables de mobiliser des connaissances scientifiques, de raisonner sur des problématiques métier et d’utiliser des outils, des modèles et des sources de données pour assister les workflows de recherche : recherche bibliographique, génération d’hypothèses, expérimentation, simulation, aide à la décision et production de livrables. Développer des méthodes d’analyse de données et de machine learning adaptées aux données scientifiques et industrielles : statistiques, apprentissage supervisé et non supervisé, modèles probabilistes, optimisation, séries temporelles, traitement d’images ou de signaux. Développer des prototypes robustes et sécurisés avec les équipes scientifiques et IT, en intégrant les usages afin de favoriser leur adoption et la transformation IA de la R&D. Assurer une veille scientifique et technologique, valoriser les résultats et développer des collaborations avec les équipes du Groupe et des partenaires académiques. Des déplacements ponctuels de courte durée sont à prévoir en France et à l’étranger (visites d’usines, conférences, formations…). *** Within Saint-Gobain’s R&D division, the Data Science team develops and deploys artificial intelligence approaches to support the Group’s scientific and industrial activities. The team combines expertise in data analysis, statistics, machine learning, generative AI, agentic systems, and knowledge graphs to accelerate the understanding of phenomena, knowledge capitalization, the design of materials and processes, and the transformation of R&D practices. In this role, your responsibilities will include : Identifying, scoping, and leading applied research projects in AI and data science. Designing, developing, and evaluating expert AI agents and agentic architectures capable of leveraging scientific knowledge, reasoning through business challenges, and utilizing tools, models, and data sources to support research workflows—such as literature reviews, hypothesis generation, experimentation, simulation, decision support, and the production of deliverables. Developing data analysis and machine learning methods tailored to scientific and industrial data, including statistics, supervised and unsupervised learning, probabilistic models, optimization, time-series analysis, and image or signal processing. Developing robust, secure prototypes in collaboration with scientific and IT teams, incorporating user needs to foster adoption and drive the AI transformation of R&D. Monitoring scientific and technological trends, showcasing results, and developing collaborations with Group teams and academic partners. Occasional short-term travel within France and abroad is to be expected (e.g., for plant visits, conferences, or training). Ce poste est-il fait pour vous ? Doctorat dans une discipline scientifique avec une forte composante en machine learning / IA, ou doctorat en ML/IA appliqué à des données et problématiques scientifiques ou industrielles. Les candidatures présentant un autre parcours, avec une expérience significative en recherche appliquée, seront également étudiées. Vous avez une bonne compréhension des modèles de langage et de leurs usages. Une première expérience du développement d’agents IA, de systèmes multi-agents ou de l’évaluation de LLM est appréciée, sans être indispensable. Vous maîtrisez Python et les bonnes pratiques de développement ; une familiarité avec le cloud Azure est un plus. Vous êtes à l’aise pour contribuer à plusieurs projets, travailler avec autonomie, proposer des orientations et communiquer clairement avec des interlocutrices et interlocuteurs scientifiques, techniques ou non spécialistes. L’entraide, l’écoute et la coopération font partie de votre manière de travailler. Atouts supplémentaires : une connaissance ou un intérêt pour les graphes de connaissances, le product management et l’expérience utilisateur. Vous maîtrisez le français et l’anglais, à l’écrit comme à l’oral. Nous savons qu’une candidature ne correspond pas toujours à 100 % des critères. Si ce poste vous intéresse et que vous pensez pouvoir y apporter votre contribution, nous vous encourageons à postuler. *** PhD in a scientific discipline with a strong machine learning/AI component, or a PhD in …

items.desc: Type de contrat : CDD Niveau de diplôme exigé : Bac + 5 ou équivalent Fonction : Ingénieur scientifique contractuel A propos du centre ou de la direction fonctionnelle Le centre Inria de Lyon est le 9ème centre de recherche Inria. Créé en janvier 2022, il regroupe environ 410 personnes au sein de 20 équipes de recherche et des services supports à la recherche. Ses équipes sont localisées à Villeurbanne, à Lyon Gerland, Lyon Bron ainsi qu’à Saint-Etienne. Le centre de Lyon est présent dans les domaines du logiciel, du calcul distribué et haute performance, des systèmes embarqués, du calcul quantique et de respect de la vie privée dans le monde numérique, mais aussi de la santé et de la biologie numériques. Contexte et atouts du poste Dans le cadre d’un partenariat : collaboration entre le programme Inria Startup Studio (centre Inria de Lyon) et le projet de startup Camly AI. L’objectif est de développer et évaluer des modèles vision-langage et un prototype de surveillance fonctionnant sur les caméras existantes , plus particulièrement dédiés à la détection de situations à risque qui persistent dans les entrepôts logistiques (issues de secours encombrées, allées obstruées, équipements de sécurité rendus inaccessibles), sans reconnaissance faciale ni suivi des personnes . Déplacements : des déplacements ponctuels sont prévus vers les sites pilotes de la région lyonnaise et pour présenter les travaux en conférence. Les frais de déplacement seront pris en charge dans la limite du barème en vigueur. Mission confiée Missions : Avec l’aide du fondateur de Camly AI (Oussama MESSAI, docteur en vision par ordinateur), la personne recrutée sera amenée à construire un protocole d’évaluation des modèles vision-langage (VLM) sur des tâches de surveillance de sécurité, et à constituer des jeux de données publics et réels d’entrepôts conformes au RGPD. Collaboration : La personne recrutée sera en lien avec le fondateur de Camly AI, qui définit la feuille de route produit et les besoins des clients, pour transformer les résultats de recherche en améliorations concrètes du produit. Elle travaillera aussi avec les sites pilotes, qui fournissent les conditions réelles d’usage, pour valider le système sur de vraies images de vidéosurveillance. L’équipe d’Inria Startup Studio accompagne le projet, et la CPPI d’Inria est consultée pour la propriété intellectuelle. Responsabilités : La personne recrutée a la charge du banc d’évaluation des VLM (tâches de référence, métriques, comparaison des modèles), du fine-tuning des modèles open-weight et de la qualité des jeux de données. Elle prendra des initiatives pour proposer de nouvelles méthodes, publier les résultats dans des conférences et revues de vision par ordinateur, et contribuer aux déclarations d’invention. Pilotage/Management : La personne recrutée aura la responsabilité de la campagne d’annotation des images issues des sites pilotes : rédaction des consignes, organisation de l’annotation, contrôle qualité et documentation. Le cas échéant, elle encadrera aussi des stagiaires. Principales activités Principales activités (5 maximum) : Concevoir un banc d’évaluation reproductible pour comparer plusieurs familles de modèles vision-langage, commerciaux et open-weight, sur des images réelles de vidéosurveillance. Recenser, sélectionner et ré-annoter des jeux de données publics de vidéosurveillance, puis constituer un jeu de données réel d’entrepôts conforme au RGPD. Fine-tuner des modèles open-weight (adaptation efficace en paramètres) et les tester, modifier et ré-évaluer jusqu’à valider leur fiabilité pour un déploiement souverain. Rédiger des articles scientifiques et diffuser les résultats (benchmarks, jeux de données, méthodes) dans les conférences et revues de vision par ordinateur, après validation de la propriété intellectuelle. Activités complémentaires (3 maximum) : Rédiger des rapports techniques internes et contribuer aux déclarations d’invention. Présenter l’avancée des travaux à l’équipe, aux partenaires et aux sites pilotes, et participer ponctuellement aux visites sur site. Compétences Compétences techniques et niveau requis : Doctorat en vision par ordinateur, en apprentissage automatique ou dans un domaine proche. Expérience démontrée sur les modèles multimodaux ou vision-langage : évaluation, prompting, fine-tuning (par exemple Qwen-VL, InternVL, LLaVA, PaliGemma). items.desc: Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe! Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy. We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide. It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone. AI is a key investment area for Kraken Technologies. You’ll join Autonomous Agents , the team building AI-powered customer service for the energy industry. We connect conversational AI to Kraken’s customer platform so agents can do more than answer questions: they can use account information and approved tools to resolve real customer needs, like understanding a bill or submitting a meter reading, and hand over to a person, with full context, when it matters. We’re launching autonomous agents with our utilities clients and the demand is growing quickly. The team is moving from initial trials to long-term production use, and we’re scaling from client-specific builds to a reusable product that can serve many clients. We’re growing the team to make that happen. Where you'll fit in: You’ll join a cross-functional team of around 10 engineers, alongside product and machine learning specialists, working closely with Kraken platform teams. The work spans two connected areas, and you’ll contribute to both: Build: the reusable core of the product. This covers client-agnostic agent journeys and tooling, MCP interfaces into Kraken, email, messaging and voice capabilities, and the observability, feature toggles and guardrails that let us roll out safely. Implementation: taking that core to individual clients. You’ll work with client teams to understand their customer journeys, configure and extend what we’ve built, and feed what you learn back into the shared product. This is a hands-on engineering role. You’ll work alongside senior engineers and leads who will support your growth, while owning meaningful pieces of work from the first few months. What you'll own: Connect the dots: Investigate customer support queries, get to grips with regulatory and business processes, and turn them into clear technical plans. Bring agents to life: Build integrations between Kraken, Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces and our AI agent setup, using Python on the Kraken side and TypeScript on the agent side. Build once, reuse everywhere: Spot patterns across customer journeys and client needs, and turn them into reusable, client-agnostic components rather than one-off fixes. Make it safe and reliable: Build authentication, permissions, validation and human handoff into the design, and help us test and monitor behaviour that is less predictable than traditional software. Roll out with confidence: Ship features behind toggles, tested and documented, so they can be introduced gradually across clients and teams. Work with clients and teammates: Take part in client conversations, explain technical details clearly, document decisions and keep your commitments on track. Operate what you build: Contribute to dashboards, monitoring and runbooks so the services you ship are observable and supportable in production. What you bring to the party: Solid software engineering: You have shipped and supported production software, and you’re comfortable with testing, code review and working in a team codebase. Python and TypeScript: You write clean, maintainable code in both and are happy moving between tools and environments. Problem-first thinking: You take time to understand the problem before jumping to the first solution. Curiosity about AI: You’re interested in LLMs, autonomous agents and MCP, and in how to give agents the right context and tools. Hands-on experience is great, but you don’t need to have all the answers. Customer and client awareness: You’re comfortable talking to non-engineers, asking good questions and translating messy real-world processes into software. Reliable delivery: You’re organised, write clear documentation and follow through on what you take on. Learning agility: You welcome feedback, ask questions when things are ambiguous and enjoy learning alongside others in a field that changes fast. What success looks like: Delivery: You ship well-scoped features and integrations that make it into production and are used by real clients. Reusability: Your work strengthens the shared product, so the next client is easier to onboard than the last. Trust: Agents you help build behave safely, resolve customer needs correctly and hand over to people when they should. Growth: You take on increasing ownership and become a go-to person for part of the platform. ️ Bonus points: AI engineering: Building with LLMs, agent …

items.desc: Invest in Values. Produce in Freedom. Boost Europe. Europe's plants run on gas, power, heat and steam – and all of them are being rebuilt at the same time. The hard part isn't ambition, it's arithmetic: which asset to buy, when to run it, what to hedge. Europe's largest companies (~2% of total energy demand) answer these questions with our Energy OS: a digital twin of the site, an optimizer that plans it, and agents that operate it. The optimizer is yours. Twenty-year investment decisions, quarter-hourly dispatch, real tariffs, real market rules. You report directly to the CTO – and nobody stands between your model and the plant it runs on. Tasks Optimization Models End-to-End: Own capacity expansion planning over multi-year horizons, dispatch at quarter-hour resolution, and MIP production scheduling with sequence-dependent setup times. Model Physics & Contracts: Storage, thermal networks, transmission, flexibility, self-consumption, minimum part loads, start-up costs – formulate what reality actually demands. Make It Solve: Tighten big-Ms, scale models cleanly, decide where decomposition earns its complexity – and where it doesn't. Smart Data Reduction: Time series clustering, extreme periods, segmentation and aggregation – without accuracy quietly disappearing. Regulation into Constraints: Model grid fees, levies, tariffs, balancing power and intraday trading per country, and understand what they do to the objective function. Prove It's Right: Test cases on real customer systems, fixtures that catch regressions, and infeasibility output an engineer can actually diagnose. Interface & Production: Define inputs and outputs with the Product Engineers; own the runs on Kubernetes – solve time, memory and cost are your numbers. Explain to the Customer: When a customer questions a schedule, you're the one who can say why the model chose it. Requirements Education & Background: Degree in mathematics, operations research, computer science, physics, energy systems engineering, business mathematics or a comparable STEM qualification. Optimization: Deep familiarity with LP and MILP and the craft around it – formulation strength, relaxations, warm starts, solver behavior. Practice over Papers: You've taken a model from formulation to production that others depended on. Code & Solvers: Strong Julia – or strong Python/C++ and a real appetite to learn Julia (JuMP) fast. Hands-on with Gurobi or HiGHS, including reading logs and knowing when to reformulate instead of tuning. Data Sense & Engineering: Comfortable with long time series, unit and sign conventions; tests, version control, code review and CI are second nature. AI-Native: Claude Code, agents and subagents are part of your daily loop – a requirement, not a plus. High Ownership, Low Ceremony: You take on the unclear. Energy domain knowledge helps but isn't required. Nice to have: Stochastic or robust optimization, Benders or column generation, unit commitment, energy market modeling. Benefits Share in the Success: Competitive base salary plus equity – we set your level during the process, not based on your CV. Top-Tier Venture Capital Network: Direct access to the Point 9 and Earlybird networks – including formats for sparring, mentoring and further education. Unforgettable Team Offsites (Workation): Once a year, the whole team goes on a workation. Including exclusive exchanges with our Visionary Voices (e.g. Robert Habeck, Kitty Mayo, James Vincent). Corporate Health: Full flexibility for your fitness and health with Urban Sports Club. Out to the Plant: Seeing the boiler you modeled changes how you build the product. Our stack: Julia with JuMP on Gurobi and HiGHS, forecasting in Python, the product in TypeScript (Vue, Node, PostgreSQL), Google Cloud with Kubernetes for optimization jobs, GitLab CI, agents on LangGraph. Small team, no layers between you and the decision. A model change that lands on Tuesday is in front of the customer on Thursday. In-person onboarding, then hybrid from Munich, Düsseldorf or Münster. Not a research position without deployment – and not a place where solve time is someone else's problem.

Responsibilities but not limited to; Design and ship production Copilot agents, owning them from prototype through production Build retrieval that holds up in production: Graph RAG combining knowledge-graph traversal over accounts, contacts, products, and prior engagements with vector search, Design agent memory: episodic and semantic memory organized as memory nodes, with recall, summarization, and decay policies tuned per use case, Own organizational context management Build and productionize ML model training pipelines Build batch and online inference for those models Own answer quality as an engineering discipline Compose multi-agent workflows using A2A, and integrate tools and data through MCP servers (CRM, client and product reference data, document stores, calendar and email, Databricks, Snowflake, Kubernetes, Confluence, Bitbucket, Splunk). Close the loop with production feedback Produce the model documentation, test evidence and controls Deploy and operate solutions on public cloud (AWS) with strong SDLC, security, resiliency, and observability practices. Partner with sales, coverage, product and business partners to turn use cases into shipped, supported agents. Essential Skills and Experience > 4 years experience building Copilot or AI agent solutions preferably from a Financial Services background > 4 years experience building and deploying machine learning models in production environments. Experience working with AWS cloud platforms. Expertise in ML Ops practices , CI/CD, model monitoring and lifecycle management. Experience with Generative AI, LLMs and R etrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures. Strong Python development skills and experience with Databricks . Experience developing batch and real-time inference pipelines. Knowledge of vector search, retrieval optimisation and AI evaluation frameworks. Experience of Graph RAG and MCP integrations. Familiarity with Kubernetes, Snowflake and enterprise data integrations . Strong understanding of security, observability and AI governance principles. Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills Deliverables: Responsibilities but not limited to: Design, build and own production-grade copilot agents that provide secure, context-aware and persistent support across the client relationship. Deliver production ML and retrieval capabilities that turn enterprise data into timely, explainable recommendations for sellers. Establish the evaluation, governance and operational controls required for trusted AI at enterprise scale. items.desc: About CommonAI CommonAI CIC is a non-profit organisation built around collaborative engineering and is backed by a mix of UK Government and private funding in order to design, build and deploy innovative AI systems. Our Scaling Inference Lab (SIL) is developing simulation grounded in real measurements to help the UK invest in promising AI infrastructure. We connect proposed hardware designs to realistic workloads, helping investors and engineers understand their potential, their limitations and the next experiment worth doing. The Opportunity Build the workloads and benchmarks that reveal how AI infrastructure performs on useful applications. You will develop reproducible LLM serving workloads, connecting application behaviour and requirements to physical measurements and SIL's simulation platform. The initial focus includes long-context inference and agentic workloads. You will investigate how request patterns, context lengths, caching, repeated model calls and interactions with tools shape the demands placed on a system. Your benchmarks will make performance comparisons meaningful by specifying the work being done and the quality and service requirements it must meet. Working with measurement and simulation engineers and our partners, you will help preserve the workload behaviour that matters when moving between real systems and models. Your work will help engineers and investors understand which infrastructure choices suit particular applications, and how conclusions change when the workload changes. What you will do Build and maintain reproducible LLM serving workloads, serving configurations and benchmark tools, including long-context and agentic workloads, using suitable existing software. Characterise relevant behaviour such as request arrivals, prompt and output lengths, caching, batching, tool interactions and dependencies between requests. Define performance measures alongside application-quality and service requirements, so comparisons reflect useful work under stated conditions. Work with measurement engineers to reproduce workloads on physical systems, and with simulator engineers to develop workload representations that preserve the behaviour and dependencies that matter. Investigate how changes in workloads and serving configurations affect conclusions, and keep the benchmark suite relevant as inference technology and workloads evolve. Document datasets, model and software versions, configurations, provenance and permitted use so other engineers can reproduce and extend the work. An example early project would be to build a reproducible agentic workload and work with measurement colleagues to compare its performance across two systems, under agreed application-quality and service requirements. Requirements Experience building or evaluating ML systems, inference services, performance benchmarks or comparable workload-driven systems. Strong practical software skills for constructing reliable benchmark tools, analysing results and debugging interactions between applications and infrastructure. Understanding of LLM inference and an interest in how serving choices affect performance and output quality. Care in designing reproducible comparisons and interpreting results against stated application requirements. Practical experience using AI coding agents, with the judgement to validate generated code, data transformations and evaluations. Experience with vLLM, SGLang or similar serving software, long-context workloads, agentic applications, trace analysis or quality evaluation would be valuable. Depth in a subset is sufficient. The initial remit is LLM serving; other forms of inference are possible later extensions. Why join us Help build UK AI capability and improve how investment and compute serve the public good. Build a network spanning UK hardware SMEs, major technology companies, venture and public investors, and leading universities. Shape a growing team with startup pace and close academic links. Use frontier models and coding agents with a substantial tooling budget. Benefits A collaborative and supportive work environment The opportunity to have a high impact in a growing organisation Competitive salary package, including pension and benefits Professional development opportunities Networking opportunities with influential figures from across the tech sector and academia A vibrant office environment located a few minutes’ walk away from Cambridge train station Working with us Hybrid, with Cambridge attendance agreed individually around collaboration and the work; applicants across the UK are welcome. We are open to permanent employment, part-time arrangements and consultancy. We would like you to start as soon as practical and can be flexible for the right person. We particularly welcome experienced engineers and can also consider earlier-career candidates with strong evidence of ability. Relevant postgraduate study is useful, but qualifications are secondary to experience and the quality …

items.desc: Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe! Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy. We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide. It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone. AI is a key investment area for Kraken Technologies. You’ll join Autonomous Agents , the team building AI-powered customer service for the energy industry. We connect conversational AI to Kraken’s customer platform so agents can do more than answer questions: they can use account information and approved tools to resolve real customer needs, like understanding a bill or submitting a meter reading, and hand over to a person, with full context, when it matters. We’re launching autonomous agents with our utilities clients and the demand is growing quickly. The team is moving from initial trials to long-term production use, and we’re scaling from client-specific builds to a reusable product that can serve many clients. We’re growing the team to make that happen. Where you'll fit in: You’ll join a cross-functional team of around 10 engineers, alongside product and machine learning specialists, working closely with Kraken platform teams. The work spans two connected areas, and you’ll contribute to both: Build: the reusable core of the product. This covers client-agnostic agent journeys and tooling, MCP interfaces into Kraken, email, messaging and voice capabilities, and the observability, feature toggles and guardrails that let us roll out safely. Implementation: taking that core to individual clients. You’ll work with client teams to understand their customer journeys, configure and extend what we’ve built, and feed what you learn back into the shared product. This is a hands-on engineering role. You’ll work alongside senior engineers and leads who will support your growth, while owning meaningful pieces of work from the first few months. What you'll own: Connect the dots: Investigate customer support queries, get to grips with regulatory and business processes, and turn them into clear technical plans. Bring agents to life: Build integrations between Kraken, Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces and our AI agent setup, using Python on the Kraken side and TypeScript on the agent side. Build once, reuse everywhere: Spot patterns across customer journeys and client needs, and turn them into reusable, client-agnostic components rather than one-off fixes. Make it safe and reliable: Build authentication, permissions, validation and human handoff into the design, and help us test and monitor behaviour that is less predictable than traditional software. Roll out with confidence: Ship features behind toggles, tested and documented, so they can be introduced gradually across clients and teams. Work with clients and teammates: Take part in client conversations, explain technical details clearly, document decisions and keep your commitments on track. Operate what you build: Contribute to dashboards, monitoring and runbooks so the services you ship are observable and supportable in production. What you bring to the party: Solid software engineering: You have shipped and supported production software, and you’re comfortable with testing, code review and working in a team codebase. Python and TypeScript: You write clean, maintainable code in both and are happy moving between tools and environments. Problem-first thinking: You take time to understand the problem before jumping to the first solution. Curiosity about AI: You’re interested in LLMs, autonomous agents and MCP, and in how to give agents the right context and tools. Hands-on experience is great, but you don’t need to have all the answers. Customer and client awareness: You’re comfortable talking to non-engineers, asking good questions and translating messy real-world processes into software. Reliable delivery: You’re organised, write clear documentation and follow through on what you take on. Learning agility: You welcome feedback, ask questions when things are ambiguous and enjoy learning alongside others in a field that changes fast. What success looks like: Delivery: You ship well-scoped features and integrations that make it into production and are used by real clients. Reusability: Your work strengthens the shared product, so the next client is easier to onboard than the last. Trust: Agents you help build behave safely, resolve customer needs correctly and hand over to people when they should. Growth: You take on increasing ownership and become a go-to person for part of the platform. ️ Bonus points: AI engineering: Building with LLMs, agent …

IMT Mines Albi is a school of the French Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industry, and is part of Institut Mines-Télécom, a French federal institute of technological universities of science and management. As an associate member of the EPE University of Toulouse, it is authorized by the Commission des titres d'ingénieur (CTI) to award engineering degrees. Positioned at the forefront of industrial and academic issues both in France and internationally, IMT Mines Albi drives scientific and economic progress by integrating its four missions into an innovative virtuous circle: training committed engineers cutting-edge research and innovation local and national economic development dissemination of scientific and technical culture Description Location: RAPSODEE Research Centre, IMT Mines Albi, France Level: Master 2 or equivalent Period: Feb 2027 – Aug 2027 Duration: 6 months The transition towards increased use of biomass in a bioreffinery approach is a major issue in the current energetic and environmental context. In this sense, the valorization of biowaste through a bioreffinery approach considering all mass and energy streams is the logical approach for industrial processes to become greener. In the sector of paper and cardboard recycling, there is a potential of production of high-added value molecules from the compounds present in the recycling process effluents. Namely, during recycling, part of the additives present in cardboard is lost, in particular starch, which is found in the process water, favorizing the growth of microorganisms and fermentation reactions and contributing to the effluent’s chemical oxygen demand. Starch is initially used in cardboad either as dry-strength agent to improve burst and bending properties of packaging papers, or as adhesive in the converting process. When dealing with recycling carboard, starch could be extracted by physico-chemical treatment during carboard pulping and chemical, enzymatic and catalytic thermo-chemical processes, which could be efficient to convert the extracted starch into added value molecules. In the framework of the PAPERS & CARDBOARDS - PAC3R project (PEPR recyclage), the work carried out on the present internship is dedicated to the valorization of soluble starch from residual cardboard recycling process effluents into valuable platform molecules by the catalytic conversion. In fact, during the recycling of carboard and paper wastes, a fraction rich in starch can be obtained. If the quality of starch, separated from physico-chemical processes, is not good enough to be recycled as additive in the production of cardboard, it will be submitted to the valorization into high added-value chemicals such as sugars (glucose, fructose etc.), furfurals, humins, levulinic acid etc., via catalytic transformations using water as green solvent, and highly-performing catalysts developed by RAPSODEE partner. For that, original multifunctional solid catalysts will be developed such as hydroxyapatite-based catalysts, natural clay-based catalysts, carbon-based catalysts etc., using non-critical metals (e.g. Fe, Ni, Co) under the form of well-divided species (nanoparticles, nanocluster, or isolated single atoms) as catalytically active phases. One-step transformation process will be targeted in order to optimize cost and minimize environment impact. Profil Master 2 or equivalent. Student in the final year of engineering studies with a specialty in energy, chemistry, materials or processes. Aptitude for work in the laboratory or on a pilot scale and chemical analysis and desire to discover applied research. Comfortable with reading and writing in French and English. items.title: Mesure de l'acceptabilité des technologies au sein des territoires de santé
items.card: Mesure de l'acceptabilité des technologies au sein des territoires de santé Réf ABG-140678 Sujet de Thèse 22/10/2026 Autre financement public Laboratoire Génie de Production - Université de Technologie Tarbes Occitanie Pyrénées Lieu de travail Tarbes - Occitanie - France Intitulé du sujet Mesure de l'acceptabilité des technologies au sein des territoires de santé Champs scientifiques Sciences de l’ingénieur
items.desc: Mesure de l'acceptabilité des technologies au sein des territoires de santé Réf ABG-140678 Sujet de Thèse 22/10/2026 Autre financement public Laboratoire Génie de Production - Université de Technologie Tarbes Occitanie Pyrénées Lieu de travail Tarbes - Occitanie - France Intitulé du sujet Mesure de l'acceptabilité des technologies au sein des territoires de santé Champs scientifiques Sciences de l’ingénieur Psychologie, neurosciences Mots clés territoire de santé; hôpital du futur; technologies; acceptabilité; mesure de performance; analyse multicritère; évaluation multiéchelle Description du sujet Description du sujet Le projet de thèse vise à mieux comprendre les risques associés à l’introduction des technologies innovantes et à mesurer leur impact dans un environnement sanitaire. Dans ce contexte, l’ingénieur aura en charge la mission de concevoir et tester un modèle permettant l’identification des déterminants (territoires, acteurs, activités et technologies) à l’œuvre dans la perception des risques dans le secteur hospitalier et leurs impacts à différents niveaux de l’organisation. Le travail à accomplir consistera à réaliser une modélisation multiéchelle des territoires de santé et des processus temporels de soin, en portant une attention particulière aux activités, aux acteurs et aux technologies impliqués. Cette modélisation s’appuiera sur les connaissances des spécialistes disciplinaires du Living Lab de l’Hospitalité, qui sera sollicité pour valider les scénarios représentatifs et les processus sous-jacents. Une cartographie des technologies sera établie et mise en regard de leur positionnement sur les processus de soin. Cette cartographie sera validée au sein du Living Lab pour garantir sa pertinence auprès de tous les acteurs identifiés. A partir de là une méthodologie de quantification d’un indicateur d’acceptabilité établi par agrégation des critères objectifs et subjectifs, aux niveaux individuels et collectifs et sur les différentes strates et échelles du territoire de santé permettra de sous peser les facteurs en faveur ou défaveur de l’intégration de la technologie. Le Living Lab participera dans le cadre de ce Work Package à l’établissement des principes de construction des seuils d’acceptabilité, de pondération des facteurs et de choix de méthodes d’agrégation en vue d’arbitrer sur l’intérêt technique mais aussi l’impact économique, écologique et sociale de l’introduction d’une technologie. Prise de fonction : 01/12/2026 Nature du financement Autre financement public Précisions sur le financement Projet ANR PRC ACACIA Présentation établissement et labo d'accueil Laboratoire Génie de Production - Université de Technologie Tarbes Occitanie Pyrénées L’ Université de Technologie Tarbes Occitanie Pyrénées (UTTOP) est un établissement public d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche spécialisé dans les sciences et technologies de l’ingénieur. Située à Tarbes, au cœur du sud-ouest européen et à proximité immédiate de l’Espagne, l’université développe des activités de recherche reconnues dans les domaines des systèmes complexes, du génie industriel, de l’intelligence artificielle, de la science des données, de l’énergie, de la mécanique et de la gestion des risques. L’UTTOP entretient des relations étroites avec les acteurs industriels, institutionnels et territoriaux et participe à de nombreux projets nationaux et européens. Son positionnement transfrontalier constitue un atout particulier pour le développement de collaborations scientifiques à l’échelle des Pyrénées et de l’espace européen. Le doctorant sera accueilli au sein du Laboratoire Génie de Production (LGP), unité de recherche de l’UTTOP. Le laboratoire développe des recherches en génie industriel et en ingénierie des systèmes complexes, avec des compétences reconnues dans les domaines de l’aide à la décision, de l’optimisation, de la fiabilité, de la transformation numérique, de l’intelligence artificielle, de la science des données et de la gestion des risques. Le LGP rassemble enseignants-chercheurs, doctorants et partenaires académiques ou industriels autour d’une approche systémique des problématiques d’ingénierie. Ses travaux portent aussi bien sur les systèmes industriels que sur les systèmes territoriaux, environnementaux ou socio-techniques. La thèse sera réalisée au sein du département scientifique « Systèmes » , dont les activités concernent notamment la modélisation, l’évaluation et l’aide à la décision pour les systèmes complexes. Les recherches menées mobilisent des approches avancées telles que les réseaux bayésiens, les jumeaux numériques, l’intelligence artificielle explicable, les méthodes probabilistes et l’analyse de données massives. Cette thèse s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet européen Interreg POCTEFA RISKRAPID consacré au développement de systèmes de prévision, d’alerte et de prévention des risques naturels à déclenchement rapide dans les petits bassins versants de montagne. items.desc: Work Your Magic with us! Ready to explore, break barriers, and discover more? We know you’ve got big plans – so do we! Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Together, we dream big and are passionate about caring for our rich mix of people, customers, patients, and planet. That's why we are always looking for curious minds that see themselves imagining the unimaginable with us. United As One for Patients, our purpose in Healthcare is to help create, improve and prolong lives. We develop medicines, intelligent devices and innovative technologies in therapeutic areas such as Oncology, Neurology and Fertility. Our teams work together across 6 continents with passion and relentless curiosity in order to help patients at every stage of life. Joining our Healthcare team is becoming part of a diverse, inclusive and flexible working culture, presenting great opportunities for personal development and career advancement across the globe. Innovation Cup 2027 – Great minds come together The Innovation Cup in its seventeenth year, brings together a promising new generation of academic talents from life sciences, material sciences, data sciences and business administration with the company’s senior management, researchers and accomplished retirees. This meeting of the minds is a creative and innovative platform aimed at advancing science and technology. What’s in it for me? If you are a post-graduate student with an interest in the pharmaceutical, chemical and digital industry, the Innovation Cup is your chance to gain in-depth knowledge about pharmaceutical and chemical research and development, to network with top students from around the world and to build a business case together with experienced professionals. Explore job opportunities at our company and visit the innovation summer camp near Frankfurt, Germany, August 14th to 20th, 2027 and take your chance to win the Innovation Cup along with EUR 25,000 with your team (EUR 10,000 for the runner-up team and EUR 5,000 for third place). All travel, accommodation and food expenses will be paid by the company. Team Oncology will work on novel, patient-data-driven cancer targets and best-in-class or next-generation therapies - especially ways to overcome resistance to targeted agents (EGFR, HER2, cMET, KRAS), ADCs and PD-(L)1 checkpoint therapy, and exploring innovative modalities incl. armed antibodies with novel payload mechanisms of action, T cell engagers and small molecule approaches. Who can apply: We invite advanced students in life sciences, chemistry, physics, computer sciences and business administration from all over the world to apply for participation in the Innovation Cup. 42 students will be selected: Sciences: Postgraduate students in the life, material and data sciences, on their way towards a PhD in biology, chemistry, medicine, physics, biotech, bioinformatics, biochemistry, pharmacy, informatics, computer science, data science, engineering or related fields. Also Post Docs can apply! Business: Advanced MBA students or recent MBA graduates with an interest in the pharmaceutical business and a life science background. The cup is not open to healthcare professionals. How it works: During a one week Summer Camp, 42 selected postgraduate students will attend in-depth presentations about the pharmaceutical and chemical industry given by our management, scientists and external experts. Participants will work in small teams to generate an innovative idea that addresses a scientific challenge and develop the idea into a business plan. Teams will receive coaching and guidance from experienced veterans of our company, the Summer Camp moderator and our Innovation Management. You will learn the essentials about R&D within the pharmaceutical and chemical industry and understand how products are successfully discovered, developed and brought to market. You will learn to evaluate your ideas from a technical and business perspective and build a convincing business plan. The teams will present their business plans to a grand jury. The jury will be composed of our top management plus external consultants. The jury will select the best business plan and present the winning team with the Innovation Cup award and cash prize of EUR 25,000 plus EUR 10,000 for the runner-up team and EUR 5,000 for the third place. At the first day of the Innovation Cup a conference with alumni from previous events will be organized with ample networking opportunities. How do I apply? Please submit your application (motivational letter, CV) through the webpage below and then select the specific team of your choice to apply for. Please include the following details in your CV): Top Publications: Listing of up to 3 of your most impactful publications. Current Institution: Indication of your current university or research institution. Awards & Innovation Prizes: Brief …

items.desc: Remote from EMEA or LATAM Remote from India ________________________ HelloI am Willian , Trading and Analytics Lead at Kayzen, and I am now looking for a Growth Analyst to join our team About Kayzen Kayzen is a mobile demand-side platform (DSP) dedicated to democratizing programmatic advertising. We enable leading apps, agencies, media buyers, and brands to run programmatic customer acquisition, retargeting, and brand performance campaigns through our self-serve and managed service options. Built on the three core pillars of performance, transparency, and control, Kayzen powers the world's best mobile marketing teams with bespoke solutions that fuel business growth and deliver a competitive advantage. With an unprecedented scale of 300B+ daily ad requests from 1.6B+ unique users worldwide, we serve up to 1B+ ads per day in 180 countries. Kayzen is accessible through our APIs and user interface. The Team The Trading team is responsible for creating growth through the management and optimization of mobile performance advertising campaigns for clients utilizing the managed service offering. The goal of the team is to deliver on the client's objectives through established or new trading best practices and communicate account status regularly and effectively with their CSM counterparts. Why this role This is a hands-on trading role where you'll manage mobile programmatic campaigns across verticals like gaming, fintech, and betting, optimizing toward CPA/ROAS targets while learning to scale efficiently. You'll work closely with senior growth analysts and cross-functional partners, gaining exposure to advanced analytics, LLM-powered workflows, and trading strategies that go well beyond what most desks offer at this level. If you're analytical, curious about automation, and want to accelerate your programmatic career, this is the role for you. What you'll do Trading excellence Manage day-to-day campaign optimization across a set of advertisers; monitor and hit KPI targets (CPA, ROAS, retention) with guidance from senior growth analysts. Execute supply-side and audience optimization tactics including publisher management, bid adjustments, and dayparting across ad formats (banner, video, native, CTV). Run A/B tests on bids, budgets, creatives, and geos as part of broader testing roadmaps; document results and contribute learnings to the Trading Playbook. Monitor pacing and budget allocation daily, flagging risks and under-delivery proactively. Build a working understanding of mobile attribution (postback flows, attribution windows, MMP integrations) and how attribution models affect how we measure and optimize campaign performance. Analytics & automation Use SQL to pull and analyze campaign data from internal databases; build comfort with joins, CTEs, and window functions over time. Learn to leverage LLMs (GPT/Claude) for recurring analyses, data briefs, and performance diagnostics, this is a core part of how our team works. Support the creation and maintenance of dashboards and reporting tools used by the trading team. Develop your analytical instincts: learn to ask the right questions, understand what's driving performance, and use available tools (SQL, AI, BI tools) to find answers. Cross-functional impact Work with CSMs to understand client goals and communicate campaign status clearly. Support QBR preparation and client-facing deliverables alongside senior growth analysts. Collaborate with Product Support to troubleshoot delivery issues and with Supply on inventory quality questions. Since I am based in Argentina and other key product and customer success team members are located mostly across EMEA and India, we are open to a remote setup of this position. For optimal overlap with customers' time zones and internal teams your main working location should preferably be close to the CET time zone. Requirements Minimum 1–3 years of programmatic ad buying, ad operations, or adjacent adtech experience is a must Familiarity with MMPs (AppsFlyer, Adjust, Singular) and attribution concepts; hands-on experience preferred. Analytical mindset; SQL ability or a demonstrated willingness to learn quickly. Curiosity about AI and automation — you don't need to be an expert, but you should be excited to use LLMs as part of your daily workflow. Nice-to-have: Any exposure to Python, CTV/OTT, or mobile in-app DSP platforms. Solution-oriented with a bias toward action. Clear communicator who's comfortable asking questions and collaborating across teams. What do we offer? Competitive compensation with a performance-based component Exceptional career growth and learning possibilities — you'll be mentored by experienced growth analysts and exposed to advanced workflows (LLMs, ClickHouse, audience strategy) earlier than at most organizations A unique opportunity to be part of an experienced team of industry experts and entrepreneurs who bring massive change to the Adtech market A high degree of responsibility and independence Direct, …

items.desc: Bring your geology expertise to a European geothermal research proposal. Inspiralia is looking for a scientist with a PhD in geology who enjoys making complex research clear, convincing and accessible. In this short-term freelance role, you will help an eight-partner consortium turn its scientific ideas into a Horizon Europe proposal exploring geothermal resources in deep sedimentary and basement reservoirs. If you enjoy connecting ideas, asking the right scientific questions and shaping a strong research narrative, this is an opportunity to put those skills into practice beyond academic publishing. You do not need previous funding-proposal experience: we value your scientific judgement and the quality of your writing. What you will work on Your main focus will be the scientific excellence section: setting out the research objectives, explaining the methodology and making a compelling case for the project's novelty. You will also draft and integrate the full proposal, expected to be around 45 pages, with substantial input and review from the consortium. Inspiralia will provide particular support on impact and implementation. Turn partners' scientific contributions into clear, persuasive proposal text. Build a coherent account of the research rationale, innovation and methodology. Identify gaps and work with experts to strengthen the scientific narrative. Align the proposal with the call's scope and evaluation criteria. Integrate feedback and keep the final document consistent. What you will bring A PhD in geology and the judgement to critically assess and synthesise complex research. Excellent written English, supported by an example of clear, persuasive scientific writing. Strong organisation and the ability to work independently while collaborating closely with a team. Availability for a concentrated period of writing and revision through to 1 December 2026. Experience in geothermal research, deep sedimentary or basement reservoirs, or related subsurface research would be an advantage. Formal postdoctoral employment and previous proposal-writing experience are not required. Why join this project? You will collaborate with an international research consortium, contribute your expertise to a geothermal research proposal and gain practical experience in Horizon Europe proposal development. With input and feedback from Inspiralia’s team, you will see how scientific excellence connects with impact, commercial potential and project delivery. Inspiralia is an international innovation funding consultancy helping organisations turn research and technology into fundable projects. The assignment Location: Remote Contract: Short-term freelance engagement Duration: Approximately four weeks, ending 1 December 2026 The project has a firm submission deadline. You will work to agreed milestones and respond promptly to feedback, with regular support from our team. How to apply Send your CV, a brief statement of your relevant expertise and availability, and a short example of your scientific writing to melanie.cohen@inspiralia.com or through this link by 30 October 2026 . **If your writing sample is co-authored or aided by AI, please indicate your own contribution.

items.desc: We are seeking a Medical Statistician/Statistical Programmer to join the Cancer Epidemiology Unit (CEU), within the Nuffield Department of Population Health at the University of Oxford. You will work closely with statisticians, epidemiologists and other colleagues on large prospective cohort studies investigating lifestyle, dietary, hormonal, molecular and genetic factors in relation to cancer and other common non-communicable diseases. The post focuses on linking and managing large epidemiological datasets, preparing data for analysis, and carrying out statistical analyses. You will work particularly with the EPIC study and EPIC-Oxford, which links cohort data with NHS records of cancer registrations, deaths and hospital admissions. You will also support EPIC-Oxford 2, a new study building on the cohort. Your work will include managing research databases; incorporating electronic health records, questionnaire data and laboratory results; deriving disease outcomes from coded health data; and preparing datasets for cohort and nested case-control studies. You will analyse data, mainly using survival and logistic regression, and prepare tables, figures and reports for research projects and publications. There may also be opportunities to work with biomarker and omics data. You will hold a graduate degree, or have equivalent experience, in medical statistics, statistics, health data science or another quantitative subject, with training in statistical analysis and epidemiological study design. You will have experience working with routinely collected electronic health records and preparing epidemiological data for analysis, including survival analysis and logistic regression. You will also be proficient in Stata and/or R, and have experience using SQL and a relational database system to manage large datasets. Excellent attention to detail, clear and well-documented coding, and the ability to work independently and collaboratively are essential, as are strong communication and organisational skills. An understanding of epidemiological concepts and study designs, experience working with NHS-linked data under information governance requirements, or experience with biobank, sample-tracking, biomarker, dietary or omics data would be an advantage. Experience contributing to peer-reviewed publications and designing databases would also be beneficial. The post is full-time (although part-time is considered) and fixed term for 2 years. The closing date for applications is noon on 16 November 2026. You will be required to upload a CV and a cover letter as part of your online application. The cover letter should clearly describe how you meet each of the selection criteria listed in the job description.

items.desc: About CommonAI CommonAI CIC is a non-profit organisation built around collaborative engineering and is backed by a mix of UK Government and private funding in order to design, build and deploy innovative AI systems. Our Scaling Inference Lab (SIL) is developing simulation grounded in real measurements to help the UK invest in promising AI infrastructure. We connect proposed hardware designs to realistic workloads, helping investors and engineers understand their potential, their limitations and the next experiment worth doing. The Opportunity Build the workloads and benchmarks that reveal how AI infrastructure performs on useful applications. You will develop reproducible LLM serving workloads, connecting application behaviour and requirements to physical measurements and SIL's simulation platform. The initial focus includes long-context inference and agentic workloads. You will investigate how request patterns, context lengths, caching, repeated model calls and interactions with tools shape the demands placed on a system. Your benchmarks will make performance comparisons meaningful by specifying the work being done and the quality and service requirements it must meet. Working with measurement and simulation engineers and our partners, you will help preserve the workload behaviour that matters when moving between real systems and models. Your work will help engineers and investors understand which infrastructure choices suit particular applications, and how conclusions change when the workload changes. What You Will Do Build and maintain reproducible LLM serving workloads, serving configurations and benchmark tools, including long-context and agentic workloads, using suitable existing software Characterise relevant behaviour such as request arrivals, prompt and output lengths, caching, batching, tool interactions and dependencies between requests Define performance measures alongside application-quality and service requirements, so comparisons reflect useful work under stated conditions Work with measurement engineers to reproduce workloads on physical systems, and with simulator engineers to develop workload representations that preserve the behaviour and dependencies that matter Investigate how changes in workloads and serving configurations affect conclusions, and keep the benchmark suite relevant as inference technology and workloads evolve Document datasets, model and software versions, configurations, provenance and permitted use so other engineers can reproduce and extend the work An example early project would be to build a reproducible agentic workload and work with measurement colleagues to compare its performance across two systems, under agreed application-quality and service requirements. Requirements Experience building or evaluating ML systems, inference services, performance benchmarks or comparable workload-driven systems Strong practical software skills for constructing reliable benchmark tools, analysing results and debugging interactions between applications and infrastructure Understanding of LLM inference and an interest in how serving choices affect performance and output quality Care in designing reproducible comparisons and interpreting results against stated application requirements Practical experience using AI coding agents, with the judgement to validate generated code, data transformations and evaluations Experience with vLLM, SGLang or similar serving software, long-context workloads, agentic applications, trace analysis or quality evaluation would be valuable. Depth in a subset is sufficient. The initial remit is LLM serving; other forms of inference are possible later extensions. Why join us Help build UK AI capability and improve how investment and compute serve the public good Build a network spanning UK hardware SMEs, major technology companies, venture and public investors, and leading universities Shape a growing team with startup pace and close academic links Use frontier models and coding agents with a substantial tooling budget Benefits A collaborative and supportive work environment The opportunity to have a high impact in a growing organisation Competitive salary package, including pension and benefits Professional development opportunities Networking opportunities with influential figures from across the tech sector and academia A vibrant office environment located a few minutes' walk away from Cambridge train station Working with us Hybrid, with Cambridge attendance agreed individually around collaboration and the work; applicants across the UK are welcome. We are open to permanent employment, part-time arrangements and consultancy. We would like you to start as soon as practical and can be flexible for the right person. Relevant postgraduate study is useful, but qualifications are secondary to experience and the quality of your work. …

items.desc: Bij RH Marine realiseren wij de systeemintegratie van elektrische- en automatiseringssystemen aan boord van marineschepen, onderzeeboten en superjachten. Een complex, maar fascinerend werkgebied vol innovaties. Ieder schip is maatwerk voor de klant en na de doop blijven wij verantwoordelijk voor het onderhoud en upgrades. Het blijft dus de hele life cycle ‘ons kindje’. Binnen RH Marine gebruiken wij AI om slimmer en efficiënter te werken. We zien volop mogelijkheden om AI nog breder in te zetten en verder te integreren in onze dagelijkse processen. Daarom zoeken we een AI Specialist die ons helpt deze ontwikkeling verder vorm te geven. Je ontwikkelt slimme AI-toepassingen, copilots en automatiseringen en helpt collega's om AI effectief in hun werk te gebruiken. Een veelzijdige functie waarin je technische kennis, innovatie en samenwerking combineert. Functie Als AI Specialist werk je nauw samen met verschillende afdelingen binnen RH Marine om kansen voor AI te ontdekken en ideeën om te zetten in concrete oplossingen. Je onderzoekt wat er technisch mogelijk is, ontwikkelt prototypes en proof-of-concepts en begeleidt de implementatie van nieuwe toepassingen. Daarbij zorg je dat oplossingen niet alleen technisch goed werken, maar ook aansluiten bij de behoeften van gebruikers en daadwerkelijk iets toevoegen aan de dagelijkse praktijk. Je concrete taken: Ontwikkelen van AI-toepassingen, copilots en slimme automatiseringen; Ontwerpen en realiseren van prototypes en proof-of-concepts; Integreren van AI-oplossingen in bestaande systemen en werkprocessen; Signaleren van kansen om bedrijfsprocessen met AI te verbeteren; Begeleiden van collega's bij het toepassen van AI en organiseren van workshops en kennissessies; Opbouwen van een intern AI-kennisnetwerk en delen van best practices; Samenwerken met onze Information Security Officer aan richtlijnen voor veilig en verantwoord AI-gebruik; Volgen van nieuwe AI-ontwikkelingen en vertalen daarvan naar praktische toepassingen binnen RH Marine. Functie-eisen We zoeken iemand met een technische achtergrond die enthousiast wordt van de mogelijkheden van AI en vooral graag zelf aan de slag gaat. Je hoeft nog geen jarenlange ervaring als AI-specialist te hebben, maar je hebt wel voldoende technische basis om ideeën om te zetten naar werkende oplossingen. Je vindt het leuk om zelfstandig nieuwe mogelijkheden te onderzoeken, maar zoekt ook actief de samenwerking met collega's. Je kunt technische oplossingen ontwikkelen én anderen enthousiast maken om ermee te werken. Verder vragen wij: Een afgeronde hbo-opleiding in bijvoorbeeld Informatica, Software Engineering of een vergelijkbare technische richting; Bij voorkeur minimaal 2 jaar relevante werkervaring in softwareontwikkeling, automatisering of AI; Ervaring met generatieve AI-tools zoals ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot of Claude; Kennis van prompt engineering en affiniteit met het ontwikkelen van AI-toepassingen; Bij voorkeur programmeerervaring, bijvoorbeeld met Python, en kennis van API's en systeemintegraties; Bereidheid een Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag (VOG) en/of Verklaring van Geen Bezwaar (VGB) aan te vragen; Uitstekende beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal. Aanbod Een geweldig bedrijf om voor te werken met een rijke historie en een mooie toekomst, met veel aandacht voor innovatie. De collegialiteit is groot; een goede sfeer en samenwerking is onmisbaar om ons complexe werk succesvol uit te voeren. Geen project is hetzelfde en ieder project is bijzonder. Het eindresultaat is altijd een prachtig varend schip waarop alles werkt. Werk waar we trots op zijn! Een veelzijdige functie waarin je de vrijheid krijgt om nieuwe ideeën uit te werken en een belangrijke bijdrage levert aan de verdere ontwikkeling van AI binnen onze organisatie. De arbeidsvoorwaarden zijn als volgt: Een salaris tussen de € 4.290,- en € 6.274,- bruto per maand, afhankelijk van kennis en ervaring; 8% vakantiegeld; Een variabele winstdeling; 25 vakantiedagen en 13 ADV dagen; Een laptop en smartphone van de zaak; Flexibele werktijden en hybride werken; Een goede pensioenregeling via PMT. Solliciteren Direct reageren kan via de button. Ben je geïnteresseerd, maar heb je toch een vraag? Neem dan contact op met Natasja Dokter via 06 -11010122 of natasja.dokter@rhmarine.com. Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld. Aan cv's die ongevraagd worden aangeleverd door uitzend- en detacheringsbureaus kunnen geen rechten worden ontleend.
