items.desc: Are you our new Data Scientist – Panels & Survey Methodology? AudienceProject is looking for a Data Scientist – Panels & Survey Methodology for our Copenhagen office to support our continued growth. — Are you a quantitative researcher who enjoys working with data about people? And are you interested in how panels and surveys can make audience measurement more reliable? Then, we have an opportunity for a career in a fast-growing scale-up with 100+ employees that collaborates directly with companies such as Heineken, L’Oréal, LVMH, Omnicom Media, Publicis Media, WPP Media, Amazon, Google, Netflix, RTL and Warner Bros. Discovery. AudienceProject is a leader in independent cross-media measurement, enabling advertisers, media owners and the industry to trust, prove, and improve advertising outcomes through a scalable SaaS platform. Our platform provides advertisers with a unified view of campaign performance, enabling confident omnichannel investment decisions, and provides media owners with comparable, third-party validation to demonstrate the value of their inventory. After more than 15 years of leading cross-media measurement, we are now looking for a motivated Data Scientist – Panels & Survey Methodology to join our Data Science Research team. Joining AudienceProject will give you a front-row seat in the rapidly evolving advertising industry and an opportunity to work within a respected business, delivering insights about audiences across the world's largest media channels to top-tier clients. What you will do You will join our Data Science Research pod, led by Jacob Daniel Kirstejn Hansen, and help turn panel and survey data into reliable audience measurement. Our panelists are recruited through several panel partners. They contribute passive measurement data through integrations and take part in surveys that help calibrate our models. You will work with 10 other data scientists and engineers, bringing together a range of academic and professional backgrounds. Your focus will be quantitative analysis, panel quality and statistical methodology. You will use Python to investigate data and develop reproducible analyses, working closely with researchers and engineers to improve the inputs and methods behind our measurement. We actively explore and apply AI in our internal work, production systems and products, combining experimentation with sound analytical judgement. You will help evaluate promising approaches with data scientists and developers and turn useful ideas into practical improvements. Your key responsibilities will include: Analyse panel composition and coverage across partners, identifying differences, gaps and potential sources of bias. Assess the completeness, consistency and plausibility of passive measurement data, and investigate unexpected changes. Design and analyse surveys that describe panelists and their behaviour and provide data for model calibration. Contribute to the development and evaluation of weighting, calibration, and statistical modelling approaches, testing how methodological choices affect audience estimates. Identify survey-response quality issues and assess the trade-off between stricter quality rules and retaining a representative sample. Clean, combine, and analyse panel and survey datasets in Python, with clear documentation of assumptions, methods and limitations. Work with panel-partner colleagues, data scientists, and engineers to turn findings into practical data-quality improvements and evaluate their effect. Who you are You combine strong quantitative skills with curiosity about how people are represented in data. You enjoy tracing an unexpected result back to its source, questioning assumptions and explaining what the evidence supports. Your background may be in statistics, quantitative social science, economics, psychology, data science or another relevant field. You bring: Strong skills in quantitative analysis and applied statistics, including regression, sampling, uncertainty and model validation. Hands-on Python skills to clean, explore and analyse real-world data independently and make your work reproducible. An understanding of panels and surveys, including representativeness, selection bias, non-response and measurement error. A careful approach to data quality and the ability to judge how data issues affect an analysis or model. The ability to explain methods and findings clearly to both technical and non-technical colleagues. A relevant quantitative education or equivalent applied research experience. Useful additional experience includes weighting, calibration or passive behavioural data. We value thoughtful analysis, openness to different perspectives and colleagues who share what they learn. You ask questions, test assumptions and explain your conclusions clearly. What we offer You will join a curious, collaborative and energetic environment where data scientists and developers share ideas and learn from one another. Different perspectives help us …

items.desc: The Role Work directly with the founding team to define and build the technical foundation behind our AI Workers. These systems operate inside live logistics workflows across email, telephony, and enterprise software, where reliability matters and edge cases are the product. You will own the hard parts underneath the features: agent architecture, context and state, evaluations, observability, execution reliability, data flows, and the platform other engineers build on. This is a hands-on role. You will write production code every day, but your job is bigger than shipping a backlog. You will decide which abstractions survive, where we need rigor, what we build next, and how the engineering team operates as we grow. This is not a research-only role, and it is not an architecture role where you stop coding. You build, ship, measure, fix, and keep raising the bar. What You'll Do Own the architecture and evolution of the core AI Worker platform across backend services, agent workflows, integrations, data, and infrastructure. Build reliable, long-running AI workflows that make decisions and take action across inboxes, phone calls, TMS, ERP, EDI, SFTP, APIs, and event queues. Develop the systems that make agents dependable in production: evaluations, tracing, feedback loops, guardrails, retries, fallbacks, and human escalation. Work through the difficult parts of applied AI: ambiguous inputs, changing context, tool use, state management, latency, cost, and failure recovery. Turn patterns from customer deployments into reusable product capabilities instead of one-off fixes. Make deliberate technical tradeoffs between speed and durability. Ship the simple version first, then know when the system needs to be rebuilt properly. Shape product and technical direction with the founders. Challenge assumptions, propose better approaches, and own decisions through production. Help set the engineering standard for the company, from system design and code quality to how we use AI tools to build faster. Help hire and develop the engineering team as we grow. Who You Are You take ownership of unclear, important problems. You do not wait for a ticket, a complete spec, or someone else to define the path. You have strong technical judgment. You can simplify a system without being careless, and add structure without slowing everyone down. You think like a product builder, not only an engineer. You care whether the system solves the real operational problem, not whether the implementation looks clever. You move fast and iterate constantly, but you do not hide behind prototypes when customers depend on the system. You build with AI, not just around it. AI-native development is how you think and work. You are low ego and direct. You can disagree clearly, change your mind quickly, and make the best argument win. You are comfortable being close to customers, production incidents, and the messy details of logistics operations. You want to be in the room. Munich office, in person. This is not a remote role or a 9-to-5. What You Bring Strong software engineering fundamentals: Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, SQL, REST APIs, data modeling, and system design. Experience owning production systems across architecture, implementation, deployment, and operations. Hands-on experience with LLM systems in production: agent workflows, tool use, prompt engineering, structured outputs, context management, evaluations, and observability. Strong understanding of distributed and asynchronous systems, including queues, retries, idempotency, concurrency, background jobs, and failure handling. Experience with Docker, CI/CD, cloud infrastructure, monitoring, and production incident debugging. A track record of shipping products or systems that real users depend on. Bonus: experience with enterprise integrations, voice systems, email automation, logistics, supply chain, or freight. Process We move fast. Expect a decision within one week. Application. Send your CV and the one thing we care about most: an AI coding session. A transcript or log from Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or whatever tool you build with. It can be .md, .txt, several sessions, or a hosted link. We want to see how you actually work. Online interview. One conversation covering technical depth, product judgment, ownership, and team fit. No multi-round gauntlet. Technical session (60 min). Build a small service from scratch with an AI assistant that we provide. We watch how you work, then you walk us through your decisions. Founder session. A direct conversation about how you think, what you want to build, and the level of ownership you want to take. Decision. Feedback and a potential start within one week.

items.desc: We’re looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer to turn AI and machine learning opportunities into production solutions. Solita is helping organizations move from experimenting with AI and machine learning to using them as a meaningful part of their business and operations. Our customers' opportunities span traditional machine learning, optimization, computer vision, generative AI and intelligent agents. Turning these opportunities into solutions that work reliably in production requires much more than choosing the right technology. In this role, you’ll work closely with our customers’ business and technology experts to understand their challenges, identify where AI or machine learning can create meaningful value, and determine what should actually be built. You then take promising use cases from exploration and prototyping into production, where they become part of real business processes and everyday work. AI coding agents are naturally used in your daily work. You’ll give them clear specifications, provide the right context, and ensure the quality and reliability of what is produced. While AI helps accelerate development, you remain responsible for delivering solutions that work in production and create real business value. Responsibilities Collaborate with customer domain experts to identify high-value AI/ML opportunities, define measurable success criteria, and validate where AI can create meaningful business impact. Turn ambiguous business challenges into concrete solution approaches, rapidly testing ideas and taking the most promising use cases from exploration into production. Design, build, and integrate production-grade AI/ML solutions using approaches such as machine learning, optimization, computer vision, LLMs, or intelligent agents, depending on the problem. items.desc: Accurate software sizing using Function Point Analysis or Easy Functional Sizing remains a manual, expert-driven process. This thesis explores how Large Language Models can automate this task by translating common project artefacts into traceable size estimates. You’ll investigate which artefacts are essential, assess LLM accuracy versus expert judgment, and design an end-to-end framework that links early project bids to delivery metrics. Today, accurate Function Point Analysis (FPA) or Easy Functional Sizing (EFS) counts rely on experts interpreting heterogeneous artefacts (user stories, APIs, diagrams, code) and aligning their understanding. It is unclear which minimal set and quality of artefacts are required for reliable counting, and how consistently a Large Language Model (LLM) can translate those artefacts into FPA/EFS elements. Additionally, there is no standard workflow connecting early bidding to realised throughput in Function Points. This thesis addresses these gaps. The Assignment Investigate how to automate and operationalise FPA/EFS within Info Support’s Way of Working using AI. Deliver a Proof of Concept (PoC) that ingests typical project artefacts and produces traceable FPA/EFS counts, along with a framework to integrate this process from bid to delivery metrics. Evaluate accuracy, consistency and lead time against a human baseline on multiple cases. Documentation readiness for FPA/EFS – Analyse which artefacts (and quality criteria) must be present pre‑bid and per delivery phase for accurate counting (e.g., backlog items, acceptance criteria, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, entity models, sequence diagrams, code). Produce a readiness checklist and examples. LLM‑based translation to FPA/EFS – Design and implement a pipeline that maps artefacts to FPA/EFS elements (EI, EO, EQ, ILF, EIF) and/or an EFS estimate with explanations and traceability (why each element was counted). Compare prompting vs. structured extraction, few‑shot exemplars, and rule‑assisted post‑processing. Integration framework in the Way of Working – Define how this fits Info Support’s standard process: from bid (initial sizing and pricing), through project start (baseline), to tracking (FP delivered per sprint/context) and retro (variance analysis). Provide reference integrations (e.g., Azure DevOps/Jira for backlog; OpenAPI; dashboards). Example Research questions What is the minimal viable artefact set (and quality level) needed for accurate and reproducible FPA/EFS counts? How accurate and consistent are LLM-assisted counts compared to expert counts across domains and artefact types? How can we operationalise FP metrics in our Way of Working to improve bidding and delivery predictability? About Info Support Info Support specializes in custom software, data/AI solutions, management, and training and is active in the Finance, Industry, Agriculture, Food & Retail, Mobility & Public, and Healthcare sectors. We provide solid and innovative solutions for complex and critical software issues. Our headquarters are located in Veenendaal (NL) and Mechelen (BE). Alan exists to end the wait. Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way. So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience. We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture . We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR. Prevention as the new norm. We move fast, with a lot of ownership, and are proud to tackle big problems! Our process is very simple: those who make product decisions are the same ones who build them. Want to know more? Read this article if you want to discover how life as an Engineer at Alan and this article on our Engineering career path. 🛠️ The Stack Python/Flask, React, React Native, PostgreSQL in a monorepo. It is a platform with a product on top. The product is the first and most demanding user of reusable components for agent orchestration, isolated execution, skills, connectors, permissions, audit, and evaluations. Our 2026 focus is to make it the AI companion every Alaner can rely on: faster and more durable sessions, safe access to company tools and data, HDS-compatible infrastructure for sensitive workloads, stronger evaluations, and results people can inspect before acting on them. 👀 Focus for 2026: In 2026, we're moving from "AI tools you monitor" to "AI agents you trust." That means scaling Hopper — Alan's own background coding agent — alongside the infrastructure that makes it reliable: managed agent pools, sandboxed environments, autonomous testing, and CI auto-fix. Engineers will routinely offload tasks to agents. Non-engineers will open pull requests after having easily tested their changes. Agents will validate their own work before it ships. ⭐ Is it you we’re looking for? items.desc:
We are seeking an experienced Front-End Developer to join the Literature Services team at the European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI), based at the Wellcome Genome Campus near Cambridge, UK. 
 About the Team 
 The Literature Services team develops and operates Europe PMC , a major open research infrastructure providing access to biomedical and life sciences literature. Europe PMC contains over 47 million publications, including more than 12 million full-text articles, and connects the scientific literature with research data, grants, citations, persistent identifiers and text-mined biological information. The service supports millions of users and large-scale programmatic access to the scientific literature. 
 What you will do 
 You will have a key role in developing the user-facing Europe PMC service, creating fast, accessible and intuitive interfaces that enable researchers to search, navigate and understand a large and increasingly interconnected scientific literature corpus. 
 Working closely with UX and product colleagues, back-end developers, data scientists and other members of the Literature Services team, you will translate user needs and designs into robust, reusable and maintainable front-end applications and components. 
 You will contribute to the ongoing evolution of Europe PMC's web architecture, helping us improve performance, accessibility, maintainability. 
 Your key responsibilities will include: 
 Designing, developing and maintaining responsive, accessible and high-quality web interfaces for Europe PMC. 
 Building reusable front-end components and contribute to a consistent design system across the service. 
 Translating UX designs, prototypes and user requirements into production-quality interfaces. 
 Developing interfaces for complex, data-rich functionality including literature search, filtering, article pages and research workflows. 
 Integrating front-end applications with APIs and other web services using structured data such as JSON. 
 Optimising front-end performance, including page loading, rendering and efficient delivery of web assets. 
 Developing automated tests and contributing to continuous integration and deployment practices. 
 Ensuring interfaces meet appropriate accessibility, usability and web standards. 
 Working collaboratively with software developers, UX/product specialists, data scientists and scientific colleagues as part of cross functional teams 
 Participating in code review, technical design and architectural discussions. 
 Contributing to Agile development processes and the continuous improvement of Europe PMC. 
 You will have: 
 Strong knowledge of HTML, CSS and JavaScript and modern web development standards. 
 Experience developing responsive, cross-browser web applications using a modern front-end framework such as React, Vue or equivalent. 
 Experience building reusable components and maintainable front-end architectures. 
 Experience integrating web applications with REST APIs and working with structured data such as JSON. 
 A good understanding of web performance and experience diagnosing and improving front-end performance. 
 Experience with automated testing and modern front-end testing frameworks. 
 Experience using source control, particularly Git, and collaborative software development practices. 
 Good understanding of web accessibility, usability and responsive design. 
 An understanding of interaction and visual design, with the ability to work effectively with UX specialists and translate designs into high-quality interfaces. 
 Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work effectively with complex requirements and large, data-driven applications. 
 Fluency with AI-assisted coding and development tools as part of standard working practice 
 Excellent communication and collaboration skills 
 It would be advantageous to have additional experience in: 
 Developing high-traffic or large-scale public web services. 
 Design systems and component libraries. 
 Front-end performance monitoring and optimisation. 
 Search and discovery interfaces or other complex data-intensive applications. 
 Agile development methodologies such as Scrum or Kanban. 
 Bioinformatics, scientific information services, scholarly publishing or open research infrastructure. 
 Working Pattern: This role offers a hybrid working arrangement, with 1-2 days per week on site, including one designated team day to support collaboration and connection. 
 Contract length: Grant-funded, 3-year fixed-term Staff Member contract. 
 Salary: Grade 5 - Monthly salary from £3,452.05 after tax, plus generous benefits and financial allowances based on individual circumstances. Excluding 12.99% personal pension and insurance contributions.

About the job 
 Help make Graphcore hardware feel native inside the ML frameworks engineers use every day.
 As a Software Engineer in our PyTorch team, you will help build the software that connects Graphcore accelerators with state-of-the-art machine learning frameworks. You will design, implement, optimise and support features across PyTorch, Triton and related technologies.
 Your work will help ML engineers and researchers get more from Graphcore hardware, without changing how they want to build. That means better compatibility, stronger performance and cleaner developer experiences.
 You will contribute to upstream PyTorch, support our hybrid Python and C++ extension, and help integrate compiler backend capabilities with torch.compile. You will learn fast, solve real engineering problems and build expertise in a large open-source ecosystem.
 The team and culture 
 You will join the PyTorch team within Frameworks, working in a SCRUM team that ships features, reviews code, writes documentation and supports users. Work happens through clear ownership, practical decisions and close communication across software, AI/ML, research and hardware teams.
 The team values maintainable code, thoughtful design and curiosity about unfamiliar systems. Engineers are trusted to investigate, speak up and improve the codebase as they learn.
 This is a team for people who like open-source communities, complex technical problems and visible impact. You will move quickly, but with care for users and long-term quality.
 What we're looking for 
 · Strong core software engineering skills and a collaborative team mindset
· Experience developing Python libraries
· Experience building performant C++ applications in a commercial setting
· Understanding of linear algebra, floating-point arithmetic or numerical analysis
· Confident using Git and reviewing code in a commercial team setting
· Willingness to explore large, unfamiliar open-source codebases independently and with others
 Benefits 
 · Flexible working: Balance your work and personal life with greater flexibility
· Generous leave: Take time to rest, recharge and enjoy life outside of work
· Retirement planning support: Up to 5% matched pension
· Phantom equity: Share in Graphcore’s success
· Workplace experience: Enjoy thoughtfully designed office spaces for collaboration, with free food and an on-site barista to support your day
· Peace of mind protection: Income protection and life assurance to provide financial security for you and your loved ones
· Flexible benefits: Tailor your benefits package with a choice of additional options, including private medical insurance and dental cover
· Optional benefits: Dental cover, health cash plan, private medical insurance, cycle to work scheme, give as you earn
 We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.
We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you.
 Join the team at Graphcore 
 Graphcore is one of the world’s leading innovators in Artificial Intelligence compute. It is developing hardware, software and systems infrastructure that will unlock the next generation of AI breakthroughs and power the widespread adoption of AI solutions across every industry.
 As part of the SoftBank Group, Graphcore is a member of an elite family of companies responsible for some of the world’s most transformative technologies. Together, they share a bold vision: to enable Artificial Super Intelligence and ensure its benefits are accessible to everyone.
 Graphcore’s teams are drawn from diverse backgrounds and bring a broad range of skills and perspectives. A melting pot of AI research specialists, silicon designers, software engineers and systems architects, Graphcore brings together deep expertise to solve complex problems and deliver meaningful progress in AI compute.
 If you want to help shape how PyTorch runs on Graphcore hardware, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now to be part of the journey.

ESRIN, Frascati, Italy 
 Description 
 Earth Observation Security Applications Engineer in the Industrial Competitiveness Section, Green Solutions Division, Science Applications and Climate Department, Directorate of Earth Observation Programmes.
 Duties 
 You will be responsible for building up the increased use of civilian EO capabilities, in line with the ESA Convention, in all security and resilience domains in the framework of the ERS programme. This will include law enforcement (environmental crime, crimes against humanity, proliferation, organised crime and terrorism), intelligence analysis, actions addressing fragility, conflict and violence, hybrid threats and civil/military cooperation in Earth observation.

 engaging key stakeholders from the law enforcement/security community, identifying opportunities for strategic collaboration at international and national level;
 building awareness and acceptance of civilian EO capabilities among law enforcement/security-sector stakeholders to foster longer-term adoption, consolidating their information requirements;
 identifying and addressing structural impediments to the uptake of civilian EO-based products and services in the law enforcement/security domain;
 defining and implementing innovative projects to foster the use of civilian EO, in particular private sector systems, in this domain;
 defining and implementing innovative projects to combine EO data with non-EO datasets, new architectures (e.g. edge processing) and advanced processing methods (including AI) to address emerging needs from security stakeholders;
 assessing EO science and applications developments (data analytics, artificial intelligence, etc.) regarding the exploitation potential for the law enforcement/security domain;
 cooperating with other ESA teams involved in industrial innovation to address evolving priorities in this domain;
 liaising with the other divisions and departments involved with the ERS-EO Element 1 activities and the ERS-EO Element 2 Clusters where appropriate;
 contributing to ESA communication efforts promoting EO results, mission achievements and EO benefits for society;
 supervising and supporting the work of Young Graduate Trainees, National Trainees and Research Fellows.
 Technical competencies 
 Experience in the application of satellite/airborne EO with stakeholders from the security domain in Europe and worldwide
 Knowledge of European and Global law enforcement/security environments
 Experience in setting up and implementing projects involving exploitation of Earth observation data
 Behavioural competencies 
 Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking
For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

 A master's degree in engineering, Earth science, computer science, applied physics or data science is required for this post together with, in principle, six years of relevant professional experience.

 Specialist experience of working in the one of the following areas would be an advantage: law enforcement, fragile states, civil-military cooperation

 The Exploration and Science PA&S Section provides PA&S management and coordination for the missions and activities of the Directorate of Human and Robotic Exploration and the Directorate of Science.
 Upon joining the Exploration and Science PA&S Section, you will assume the role of PA&S Engineer for the LISA Project and become part of the related Project Core Team.  Duties 
 Your tasks and responsibilities will include supporting the Project PA&S Managers in:
 establishing and maintaining the PA&S requirements baseline in compliance with ESA policies;
 ensuring the implementation of the PA&S requirements by industry and other suppliers (e.g. CFI providers), supporting milestone reviews and participating in the process of verifying compliance with requirements;
 monitoring the implementation of approved plans and specifications from industry and other suppliers (e.g. CFI providers), ensuring that adequate resources are deployed for the implementation of the PA&S programme;
 coordinating the technical aspects of relevant service support and acting as the primary point of contact between service functions and project teams;
 planning, coordinating and monitoring the support provided by the assigned PA&S workforce;
 participating in the boards for the disposition of deviations from the requirements baseline (CCB), and changes to the agreed design;

You will build the foundational data infrastructure that powers cutting-edge AI applications leveraging LLMs, retrieval systems, workflows, and emerging agentic architectures.
 You will design and maintain scalable data pipelines, manage secure data environments, and prepare data for AI-driven systems while collaborating with cross-functional teams and clients. You’ll tackle real-world challenges by contributing to the development of next-generation AI systems and grow as a technologist by working alongside diverse experts across industries.
 You will design and build the scalable, reproducible data components essential for machine learning, agentic, and autonomous AI systems. You’ll assess data landscapes, apply data quality fundamentals, and prepare data for AI solutions. Additionally, you’ll learn to translate simple hypotheses into engineered features, manage secure data environments, and contribute to R&D initiatives focused on innovating and scaling next-generation AI capabilities.
 Your work will help solve some of the most complex and high-impact challenges facing clients across industries. Collaborating across QuantumBlack, AI by McKinsey and QuantumBlack Labs teams, you’ll help develop innovative AI capabilities and scalable enterprise solutions. You’ll help build robust data foundations for scalable, production-ready AI systems. Your contributions will directly support the firm’s ability to accelerate AI adoption, solve complex business problems at scale, and enable clients to achieve meaningful, lasting impact.
 You’ll be based in one of our BeNeLux offices as part of our global Data Engineering community. Working in cross-functional Agile teams, you’ll collaborate closely with Data Scientists, Machine Learning Engineers, and industry experts to deliver AI solutions. By partnering with clients from data owners to C-level executives you’ll help solve complex problems that drive tangible business value and begin to build your skills as a client-facing technologist.
 Your work offers a unique opportunity to grow at the forefront of AI, data engineering, and emerging agentic technologies. You’ll develop expertise at the intersection of technology and business by tackling diverse challenges in the evolving AI landscape. Working alongside multidisciplinary teams, you’ll gain a holistic understanding of how data engineering enables advanced AI while collaborating with several leading AI and data experts in the industry.

 Familiarity with commonly used data platforms (Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery, PSQL, etc.), cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) and engineering tools (Pandas, Spark, dbt, LangChain, etc.)
 Exposure to modern software development practices, including version control (Git) and foundational concepts in DevOps and MLOps/LLMOps and CI/CD principles
 Exceptional time management in a complex and largely autonomous work environment
 Willingness to learn quickly and adapt to different project situations and tech stacks
 Experience using coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, etc.) is a plus
 Strong communication skills, both verbal and written, in English

Powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform WPP Open, WPP unites cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, creativity, production, enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel. Working alongside our AI Lead, you'll bring creative thinking and hands-on experimentation to customer experiences and enterprise challenges. You'll help shape the ideas, make them tangible, and develop the strongest ones with clients and colleagues. We're looking for someone who is curious about technology, cares about the quality of what they make, and enjoys discovering possibilities through the work. What will your day look like? Your time will be spent researching, experimenting, designing, building with AI, presenting, and debating ideas. We work in a nimble, collaborative way, moving between customer journeys, Figma, vibe coding, and client conversations. Some projects will begin with a clear brief; others with a question. Think across journeys, services, channels, physical and digital touchpoints, and the people and systems behind them. Help shape the brief and identify where AI could make a meaningful contribution. Creative development: Use Figma and vibe-coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex, or equivalents to bring ideas to life as interactive experiences, tools, and AI-powered products. Developing ideas into useful solutions: Help promising concepts progress through pilots and into reusable experiences, products, or services. Work with product and engineering colleagues to refine how they should work, document key decisions, and support their development into solutions clients can use and adopt. Research and practice development: Stay curious about emerging AI capabilities, creative applications, and ways of working. Run focused experiments, share discoveries, and help the Agentic AI Lab develop reusable approaches. Contribute ideas that other teams can build on and adapt as the technology evolves. Who are you going to work with? You will join our AI Consulting team, bringing together consulting, customer experience, product thinking, and the ability to apply emerging technologies creatively. We share early ideas, learn by making, and bring different perspectives to the work. You will work alongside our AI Lead and senior colleagues as you develop your own approach. AI Consulting is part of the wider AI Capability, alongside dedicated engineering and product teams. Together, our team explores opportunities, develops new concepts, and turns promising ideas into enterprise solutions. You will also collaborate with strategists, designers, consultants, and specialists across the wider business. What do you bring to the table? We welcome junior and mid-level applicants, including recent graduates with a strong portfolio. We do not expect a particular academic or professional background: our team is multifaceted – your path might be product design, service design, creative technology, computer science, or something entirely different. We care about what you have …

items.desc: Description du poste Domaine Mathématiques, information scientifique, logiciel Contrat Stage Intitulé de l'offre Intership Agentic Multimodal AI for Understanding and Reasoning over Complex Technical Documents-H/F Sujet de stage The internship aims to develop multimodal agentic AI for understanding and reasoning over complex technical documents containing text, tables, figures, diagrams, and equations distributed across multiple pages. The work will focus on evaluating recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs), designing an agentic architecture capable of decomposing complex queries, planning multi-step reasoning, and dynamically selecting relevant pages, tools, and models, and combining information across multiple modalities. A dedicated benchmark may also be developed, and the proposed approach will be evaluated against direct VLM and multimodal RAG baselines. Durée du contrat (en mois) 6 mois Description de l'offre As an intern at the CEA, you will have the opportunity to work within a world-renowned research environment. Our teams consist of passionate and dedicated experts, providing an ideal setting for learning and collaboration. You will have access to state-of-the-art equipment and top-tier research resources to carry out your assignments. The work conducted may potentially lead to a scientific publication. Context : Complex technical documents combine heterogeneous information such as text, tables, diagrams, figures and equations, often distributed across multiple pages. They include technical manuals, maintenance procedures, user guides, datasheets, product specifications, engineering documents, and technical or scientific reports. Understanding such documents raises several challenges: retrieving relevant information across long documents, jointly interpreting heterogeneous modalities, linking information distributed over multiple pages, and performing multi-step reasoning. This internship aims to develop multimodal agentic AI capable of planning and orchestrating specialized models and tools for complex document understanding and reasoning. What do we expect from you? To address these challenges, the internship will investigate the following research directions: Review existing benchmarks and, if necessary, develop a benchmark covering a fine-grained taxonomy of technical documents and multimodal reasoning tasks. Evaluate recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for technical document understanding. Design an agentic architecture able to decompose complex queries and plan multi-step reasoning. Dynamically retrieve relevant pages and select appropriate tools or models. Combine and reason over information from text, tables, figures, diagrams and equations across multiple pages. Evaluate the proposed approach against direct VLM and multimodal RAG baselines. # Cea-List Profil du candidat Students in their 4th or 5th year of studies (M1, M2 or gap year) Strong interest for Multimodal Generative AI Knowledge of LLMs, Vision-Language Models (VLMs), Transformers, RAG and agentic systems Computer vision skills Machine learning skills (deep learning, perception models, generative AI…) Python proficiency in a deep learning framework (especially TensorFlow or PyTorch) Localisation du poste Site Saclay Localisation du poste France, Ile-de-France, Essonne (91) Ville Saclay Critères candidat Langues Français (Courant) Anglais (Courant) Diplôme préparé Bac+5 - Diplôme École d'ingénieurs Formation recommandée Apprentissage automatique et IA Possibilité de poursuite en thèse Oui Informations générales Entité de rattachement Le CEA est un acteur majeur de la recherche, au service des citoyens, de l'économie et de l'Etat. Il apporte des solutions concrètes à leurs besoins dans quatre domaines principaux : transition énergétique, transition numérique, technologies pour la médecine du futur, défense et sécurité sur un socle de recherche fondamentale. Le CEA s'engage depuis plus de 75 ans au service de la souveraineté scientifique, technologique et industrielle de la France et de l'Europe pour un présent et un avenir mieux maîtrisés et plus sûrs. Implanté au cœur des territoires équipés de très grandes infrastructures de recherche, le CEA dispose d'un large éventail de partenaires académiques et industriels en France, en Europe et à l'international. Les 20 000 collaboratrices et collaborateurs du CEA partagent trois valeurs fondamentales : La conscience des responsabilités La coopération La curiosité Référence 2026-41999 Description de l'unité Based in Saclay (Essonne), the LIST is one of the two institutes of CEA Tech, the Technological Research Division of the CEA. items.desc: Description We are seeking an AI Data & Integration Engineer to connect Plessey’s data and systems to AI. The company operates an advanced compound semiconductor fab and develops complex MicroLED display and optical interconnect technologies. This role will give AI agents secure, efficient and reliable access to data from across the business, including manufacturing, engineering, quality and business systems, so they can deliver real outcomes. The successful candidate will combine strong data and software engineering skills with a deep understanding of how AI agents use tools and data. They will build the connections, shape the data so agents use it well, and prove through testing that agents can complete real work with it. Success in this role will be demonstrated by AI agents that answer questions and complete tasks accurately and efficiently using Plessey’s data. This will include clear evidence of faster access to information, less time spent gathering and analysing data, and measurable productivity gains across fab operations, engineering and business functions. The role reports to the Lead AI Solutions Engineer and works closely with IT, data owners and teams across the business. As AI agents take on longer-running and more complex work, this role will make sure Plessey’s data is ready for them: secure, well structured and efficient to use. Key Responsibilities Map Plessey’s data sources with their owners: structure, quality, sensitivity and who should see what. Build pipelines that turn raw fab data into agent-ready data: tool logs, recipes, statistical process control, metrology, test and inspection data. Build and own the connectors that give AI agents access to company data and systems, using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). These include the Manufacturing Execution System (MES) data warehouse, Microsoft 365, engineering file shares, tool and process data, and business systems. Design connections that agents can use effectively and efficiently: easy to find and understand, economical with tokens and cost, and ready for longer-running, multi-step and event-driven work. Prove every connection works by testing it with real agents on real Plessey tasks, measuring accuracy and cost, and monitoring it in production without degrading source systems. Secure every connection so people only reach data they’re already entitled to. Protect personal, commercially sensitive and IP data, guard against AI-specific risks such as prompt injection, and keep full audit trails. Work with production, engineering, quality and business teams, IT, data owners and vendors to turn real needs into documented connections that deliver measurable gains. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Fully committed to AI: uses AI tools every day, keeps pace with the latest models and agent capabilities, and believes in a future where AI is part of everything we do. Strong software engineering in Python, with production experience of APIs, services and data pipelines. Strong experience working with databases and large, complex datasets. Good understanding of how LLM agents use tools, and what makes a tool easy or hard for an agent to use. Experience testing or evaluating LLM systems for accuracy, reliability and cost. Practical knowledge of token efficiency in LLM systems. Experience with AWS (or a comparable cloud), containers and infrastructure as code. Understanding of identity and access control: OAuth 2.0, single sign-on, least privilege. A disciplined approach to security, privacy and safe access to production systems. Ability to work with engineers, operators and managers to understand what they need from their data. Advantage Experience building Model Context Protocol servers or tools for AI agents. Experience with Amazon Bedrock or Anthropic’s Claude models and agent tooling. Experience with semiconductor, photonics or advanced manufacturing data, Manufacturing Execution Systems, statistical process control, yield or equipment data. Experience with big data platforms and tools, such as data lakes, data warehouses and distributed processing. Experience with event-driven systems and observability tools. Experience in a secure, IP-sensitive environment, including Data Protection Impact Assessments and information security reviews. items.title: Bioinformatician / Computational Scientist (m/f/d) – Cancer Neuroscience
items.card: Aufgaben You will work closely with experimental scientists, clinician scientists, pathologists and international collaborators and will take responsibility for the computational analysis of complex translational datasets. Key areas include: single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, high-plex spatial imaging and transcriptomic platforms, bulk RNA sequencing, multimodal datasets, tumor microenvironment
items.desc: Chirurgie Voll- und Teilzeit befristet Stellen-Nr.: 26_10_019 Ismaninger Straße (TUM Klinikum Rechts der Isar) We are looking for an ambitious Bioinformatician / Computational Scientist to become a central part of our research program in Cancer Neuroscience and Translational Oncology . Our laboratory studies how neural, immune, stromal and malignant cell populations interact within tumors and how these interactions influence tumor evolution, invasion, metastasis and therapeutic resistance. A major focus of our work is the systematic characterization of the neural ecosystem of cancer using single-cell, spatial and multimodal datasets and the development of computational approaches capable of uncovering previously unrecognized cellular states and intercellular communication programs. The group is supported by highly competitive funding including the European Research Council (ERC), Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG), Deutsche Krebshilfe and Else Kröner-Fresenius-Stiftung and operates within a strong international cancer neuroscience network. Our ambition is to establish computational cancer neuroscience as a defining component of the emerging field and to generate datasets and concepts with international visibility. Aufgaben You will work closely with experimental scientists, clinician scientists, pathologists and international collaborators and will take responsibility for the computational analysis of complex translational datasets. Key areas include: single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, high-plex spatial imaging and transcriptomic platforms, bulk RNA sequencing, multimodal datasets, tumor microenvironment analysis, cell-state and trajectory analysis, ligand–receptor and cell–cell communication analyses, neural–tumor–immune interaction networks, integration of experimental and clinical datasets Depending on your interests and expertise, projects may also involve: development of novel computational approaches for identifying neural-associated tumor states, spatial neighborhood and tissue architecture analyses, integration of transcriptomic, genomic and epigenomic datasets, comparative analyses across cancer entities, machine-learning-based patient or phenotype stratification, analysis of large public cancer datasets, generation of publication-quality computational frameworks and visualizations A particular scientific opportunity will be the development of computational strategies to identify and characterize neural-like, neuroplastic and neuron-interacting cancer cell states and their spatial relationship with nerves, immune cells and stromal populations. Profil We are looking for a candidate with a background in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Systems Biology, Biostatistics, Data Science or Computational Genomics strong expertise in several of the following areas: R and/or Python, single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, RNA-seq analysis, statistical analysis of high-dimensional biological data, data visualization, reproducible computational workflows, integration of heterogeneous biological datasets Experience in cancer biology, neuroscience, immunology or spatial biology is particularly welcome but is not mandatory if there is a strong interest in learning the underlying biology. We value candidates who do not see bioinformatics merely as a service function, but who want to formulate biological hypotheses, develop computational concepts and actively shape scientific projects . Benefits You will become a core member of a highly interdisciplinary research group combining: Cancer Biology, Neuroscience, Immunology, Spatial Biology, Computational Science An extension beyond the initial funding period is explicitly envisaged, depending on scientific performance, project development and future funding. access to unique and deeply characterized human and experimental datasets and close interaction with experimental scientists and clinician scientists highly competitive ERC-, DFG-, Deutsche Krebshilfe- and foundation-funded projects opportunities for first- and co-authorship on high-impact publications as well assubstantial freedom to develop computational projects and methodological approaches participation in an international network at the forefront of Cancer Neuroscience the possibility to establish an independent computational profile within this rapidly developing field EGYM well pass, corporate benefits and discounts (e.g. Käfer), cafeteria, sports and cultural offers, company bike Working in the heart of Munich at Max-Weber-Platz with very good accessibility by public transport such as the subway, S-Bahn or tram Company pension plan through the Federal and State Pension Institute (VBL) Kontakt Sarah Mößmer Klinik und Poliklinik für Chirurgie 089 4140 2044 Weitere Informationen If the candidates’ suitability for the position in question is equal, severely disabled applicants shall be given preference. items.desc: Who we are At Frontiers, we are on a mission to make science open. Most research today sits behind paywalls, meaning only people at well-funded universities or those who can pay get to read it. Open access flips that: every article we publish is peer-reviewed and made available online to anyone, anywhere at no cost. As one of the world’s largest and most influential open-access publishers, we’ve seen Frontiers research cited 16 million times, and viewed and downloaded more than 5.3 billion times, proof of what science without barriers can do. About the role Do you have an academic or professional background in biology, microbiology, biotechnology, environmental science, agriculture, food science or a related discipline? Looking for an alternative career path where you can stay connected to research while developing commercial, business development and relationship-management skills? As a Publishing Development Specialist at Frontiers, you will combine subject-area understanding with proactive outreach, consultative conversations and data-informed journal development. You will work with researchers, editors and academic communities worldwide to identify opportunities, build strong relationships and generate high-quality submissions for Frontiers journals. What you'll do Reach out directly to researchers and editors to spark new collaborations, launch dedicated article collections, recruit into the Editorial Board, commission manuscripts, and liaise with Chief Editors at a journal section level. Manage a dynamic sales pipeline, taking opportunities from first contact through to successful publication. Use AI tools daily to research prospects, personalize outreach, and manage your pipeline more efficiently. Cultivate trust and build long-term professional relationships with editors and authors. Represent our journals at scientific conferences, webinars, and online events to increase their market footprint. Requirements About You You bring experience in sales, outreach, or business development with a proven track record of hitting targets. You enjoy fast-paced environments, handle multiple projects with ease, and know how to prioritize your day. You have a strong grasp of AI-based tools in a business operations context. Experience using AI in sales or outreach workflows is a plus. You are a natural communicator who is persuasive, personable, and loves building professional relationships and your English is fluent, both spoken and written, as you will be communicating with global researchers and international teams every day. You have an entrepreneurial mindset, always looking for opportunities and taking the initiative to make things happen. This opportunity may be particularly relevant if your background includes microbiology, cellular and infection microbiology, bioengineering, biotechnology, agronomy, soil science, environmental science, environmental chemistry, water research, food science, food technology or related life-science fields. Para ello, buscamos una persona especialista en teledetección, con una buena base científica y
items.desc: DESCRIPCIóN ¿Disfrutas investigando, desarrollando y poniendo a prueba nuevas metodologías de teledetección? De los datos al modelo y del modelo a su validación: combina tu base científica con la programación y el análisis geoespacial en proyectos de I+D aplicados a agricultura, recursos hídricos y medio ambiente. Para ello, buscamos una persona especialista en teledetección, con una buena base científica y experiencia en programación y análisis geoespacial. ¿QUÉ HARÁS Y EN QUÉ PROYECTOS PARTICIPARÁS? Te incorporarás al desarrollo de soluciones de teledetección y observación de la Tierra, participando en el diseño, implementación y validación de metodologías que transformen datos satelitales, meteorológicos y otras fuentes geoespaciales en productos, indicadores y modelos. EN TU DÍA A DÍA… Desarrollarás flujos de adquisición, preparación y procesamiento de datos, integrando distintas fuentes y trabajando con grandes volúmenes de información geoespacial. Analizarás imágenes satelitales y series temporales, aplicando técnicas de análisis espectral y multiespectral. Desarrollarás y validarás modelos físicos, estadísticos y de Machine Learning para tareas de estimación, clasificación, segmentación, detección de objetos, cambios y anomalías. Evaluarás los resultados de las metodologías y los modelos, mediante métricas estadísticas y procedimientos de validación adecuados para cada aplicación. Participarás en proyectos de I+D, contribuyendo a generar soluciones robustas, reproducibles y escalables. Tus desarrollos podrán aplicarse a ámbitos como agricultura y vegetación, recursos hídricos, medio ambiente, atmósfera y clima, territorio e infraestructuras, riesgos naturales y gestión de emergencias. ¿QUÉ CONOCIMIENTOS Y EXPERIENCIA NECESITAS? Teledetección: tienes una buena base científica y una comprensión global de la disciplina, incluidos sus fundamentos físicos, los principios de adquisición y procesamiento de datos, las características de los sensores y la interpretación de la información obtenida mediante observación de la Tierra. Sensores satelitales: cuentas con experiencia con Sentinel-2 y Landsat . También se valorarán tus conocimientos de Sentinel-1 (SAR), Sentinel-3 y otros sensores . Programación Python: manejas Python a nivel intermedio y tienes experiencia con NumPy, Pandas, PySTAC, Xarray, Rasterio, GeoPandas y GDAL . Procesamiento geoespacial: sabes realizar reproyecciones, remuestreos, máscaras y mosaicos, y trabajar con sistemas de coordenadas y datos ráster y vectoriales. Análisis espectral: tienes conocimientos de cálculo de índices de vegetación, análisis multiespectral y tratamiento de series temporales. Fuentes de datos y repositorios abiertos: conoces las principales plataformas, repositorios y datasets de acceso libre de observación de la Tierra y sabes localizar, consultar, seleccionar y obtener datos adecuados para diferentes aplicaciones. Machine Learning: tienes conocimientos de regresión, clasificación, Random Forest, XGBoost y validación de modelos mediante métricas estadísticas. Herramientas de desarrollo: cuentas con experiencia con QGIS, Git y entornos de desarrollo Python . Acceso a datos satelitales: estás familiarizado/a con catálogos STAC y el procesamiento de grandes volúmenes de datos. ¿QUÉ OTROS CONOCIMIENTOS VALORAMOS? Programación orientada a objetos, manejo de clases y métodos. Deep Learning aplicado a imágenes satelitales (PyTorch). Procesamiento de datos térmicos, SAR y LiDAR. Técnicas de superresolución o downscaling de imágenes ópticas o térmicas. Procesamiento escalable con Dask, Zarr y herramientas cloud. Modelos de transferencia radiativa (PROSPECT, SAIL) y estimación de parámetros biofísicos. Formación: teledetección o tecnologías geoespaciales, Física, Ingeniería Geomática, Geografía, Ingeniería Agronómica, Informática o titulaciones afines ¿QUÉ TE OFRECEMOS HOY? Flexibilidad horaria y teletrabajo para facilitar la organización de tu día a día. Jornada intensiva en verano para disponer de más tiempo para ti. Retribución flexible para adaptar parte de tu salario a tus necesidades. Participación en proyectos tecnológicos de alto impacto, nacionales e internacionales. Entorno innovador vinculado a GIS, Inteligencia Artificial y Observación de la Tierra. Formación continua y desarrollo profesional. Colaboración con un equipo multidisciplinar altamente especializado. Autonomía para liderar proyectos y aportar nuevas ideas.

items.desc: Who we are At Frontiers, we are on a mission to make science open. Most research today sits behind paywalls, meaning only people at well-funded universities or those who can pay get to read it. Open access flips that: every article we publish is peer-reviewed and made available online to anyone, anywhere at no cost. As one of the world’s largest and most influential open-access publishers, we’ve seen Frontiers research cited 16 million times, and viewed and downloaded more than 5.3 billion times, proof of what science without barriers can do. About the role Do you have an academic or professional background in biology, microbiology, biotechnology, environmental science, agriculture, food science or a related discipline? Looking for an alternative career path where you can stay connected to research while developing commercial, business development and relationship-management skills? As a Publishing Development Specialist at Frontiers, you will combine subject-area understanding with proactive outreach, consultative conversations and data-informed journal development. You will work with researchers, editors and academic communities worldwide to identify opportunities, build strong relationships and generate high-quality submissions for Frontiers journals. What you'll do Reach out directly to researchers and editors to spark new collaborations, launch dedicated article collections, recruit into the Editorial Board, commission manuscripts, and liaise with Chief Editors at a journal section level. Manage a dynamic sales pipeline, taking opportunities from first contact through to successful publication. Use AI tools daily to research prospects, personalize outreach, and manage your pipeline more efficiently. Cultivate trust and build long-term professional relationships with editors and authors. Represent our journals at scientific conferences, webinars, and online events to increase their market footprint. Requirements About You You bring experience in sales, outreach, or business development with a proven track record of hitting targets. You enjoy fast-paced environments, handle multiple projects with ease, and know how to prioritize your day. You have a strong grasp of AI-based tools in a business operations context. Experience using AI in sales or outreach workflows is a plus. You are a natural communicator who is persuasive, personable, and loves building professional relationships and your English is fluent, both spoken and written, as you will be communicating with global researchers and international teams every day. You have an entrepreneurial mindset, always looking for opportunities and taking the initiative to make things happen. This opportunity may be particularly relevant if your background includes microbiology, cellular and infection microbiology, bioengineering, biotechnology, agronomy, soil science, environmental science, environmental chemistry, water research, food science, food technology or related life-science fields. items.desc: We are seeking an exceptional Consultant Clinical Scientist to provide scientific, strategic and managerial leadership within the Proton Beam Therapy Physics service at UCLH. This is a rare opportunity to lead a key specialist area of a national proton therapy service, driving innovation, research and service development while ensuring the highest standards of patient safety and clinical excellence. Working within a highly experienced multidisciplinary team, you will play a key role in developing advanced proton therapy techniques, leading complex projects and influencing the future direction of radiotherapy physics locally, nationally and internationally. You will lead a key area of the Proton Beam Therapy Physics service, with responsibility for clinical service delivery, scientific leadership, treatment planning or dosimetry & quality assurance activities, and the implementation of new technologies and techniques. Acting as a Medical Physics Expert, you will provide highly specialised advice on complex clinical and technical issues, oversee commissioning and quality assurance programmes, and ensure compliance with all relevant legislation and professional standards. You will manage and develop staff, lead service improvement and research initiatives, contribute to strategic planning, and work closely with clinicians, radiographers, physicists, engineers, academic and industrial partners to deliver world-class proton therapy services. University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (UCLH) is one of the most complex NHS trusts in the UK, serving a large and diverse population. We provide academically led acute and specialist services, to people from the local area, from throughout the United Kingdom and overseas. Our vision is to deliver top-quality patient care, excellent education, and world-class research. We provide first-class acute and specialist services across eight sites: University College Hospital (incorporating the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing) National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitals University College Hospital Grafton Way Building Royal London Hospital for Integrated Medicine University College Hospital Macmillan Cancer Centre The Hospital for Tropical Diseases University College Hospital at Westmoreland Street We are dedicated to the diagnosis and treatment of many complex illnesses. UCLH specialises in women’s health and the treatment of cancer, infection, neurological, gastrointestinal and oral disease. It has world class support services including critical care, imaging, nuclear medicine and pathology. We are committed to sustainability and have pledged to become a carbon net zero health service, embedding sustainable practice throughout UCLH. We have set an ambitious target of net zero for our direct emissions by 2031 and indirect emissions by 2040. As one of the best-known retailers of tech, we’re proud of the service our customers receive – and it’s all down to our team of caring and committed colleagues. Join us and you’ll work in a great team where you can be yourself and bring your personality. Working as one team, we learn and grow together, celebrating the big and small moments that make every day amazing. As a Site Reliability Engineer you will apply software engineering practices to operations, owning the end-to-end availability, performance and resilience of our customer-facing and core trading services. You will work as part of a centralised SRE squad, embedding with product engineering teams to design reliability in from the start: defining service level objectives, automating away operational toil, and continuously improving how we build, deploy, observe and operate software at scale. A core focus of this role is the design and build of our central AIOps platform: a shared capability that ingests telemetry, events and change data from across the estate and applies machine learning and AI-assisted automation to detect anomalies earlier, correlate and suppress alert noise, predict capacity and performance issues before they impact customers, and drive automated diagnosis and remediation of common failure modes. You will help shift Currys from reactive incident response towards predictive, self-healing operations. This is an operations role first and foremost. However you will write production-quality code, treat infrastructure and operational tooling as software, and bring rigour to incident response, root cause analysis and the systematic elimination of repeat failures. Role overview: Reliability Engineering: Define, implement and report on SLIs, SLOs and error budgets with product squads, and use them to drive engineering prioritisation and release decisions. AIOps platform: Design, build and operate Currys’ central AIOps platform, covering telemetry ingestion and event correlation, ML-based anomaly detection and predictive alerting, intelligent alert routing and noise reduction, and automated runbook execution and remediation, integrated with our ITSM, incident and on-call tooling. Observability: Build and evolve a modern observability stack (metrics, logs, traces and events) using open standards such as OpenTelemetry, ensuring services are instrumented, debuggable and measurable by default. Automation: Eliminate operational toil through software: infrastructure as code, self-service tooling, CI/CD pipeline improvements and automated reliability testing, including chaos and resilience experiments. Incident Response: Act as an escalation point for major incidents, lead blameless post-incident reviews, and drive root cause analysis through to permanent fixes, increasingly augmented by AI-assisted diagnosis from the AIOps platform. Design for reliability: Review and challenge architecture and designs (HLD/LLD) to embed reliability, scalability, security and operability principles; set direction on strategic tooling and reduce duplication and technical debt. Peak Readiness: Lead capacity planning and performance engineering for peak trading events (e.g. Black Friday), using predictive modelling from platform telemetry. Experience in retail, e-commerce, consumer goods or finance is valued. Essential: Strong software engineering skills: proficiency in at least one modern language (e.g. Python, Go, PHP or Java), with experience writing, reviewing and operating production code. Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (Azure preferred; AWS/GCP valued), containers and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes) and Linux/Windows environments. Deep observability and monitoring experience (e.g. OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, New Relic, Azure Monitor, PagerDuty), including designing SLIs/SLOs and alerting strategies. Experience with AIOps capabilities such as anomaly detection, event correlation, predictive alerting or automated remediation, either building them or applying platforms. Solid incident management experience in complex, fast-paced IT environments, including post-incident review and root cause analysis. Desirable: Applied ML/data engineering for operations: …

items.desc: The University of Oxford is a stimulating work environment, which enjoys an international reputation as a world-class centre of excellence. Our research plays a key role in tackling many global challenges, from reducing our carbon emissions to developing vaccines during a pandemic. The Department of Psychiatry is based on the Warneford Hospital site in Oxford – a friendly, welcoming place of work with an international reputation for excellence. The Department has a substantial research programme, with major funding from Medical Research Council (MRC), Wellcome Trust and National Institute for Health Research (NIHR) and provides highly rated medical training in psychiatry. The Head of Department is Professor Belinda Lennox. Reporting to the Dr Chloe Yap, the post holder is a member of the Immuno-Metabolism & Severe Mental Illness research group with responsibility for the provision of research support for a project investigating the role of accelerated biological aging in psychosis. What We Offer As an employer, we genuinely care about our employees’ wellbeing and this is reflected in the range of benefits that we offer including: An excellent contributory pension scheme 38 days annual leave A comprehensive range of childcare services Family leave schemes Cycle loan scheme Discounted bus travel and Season Ticket travel loans Membership to a variety of social and sports clubs This role also offers the opportunity for hybrid working About the Role The post is a part-time, 7.5 hours per week (20.13%FTE), funded to 31 January 2028, and based in the Department of Psychiatry at the Warneford Hospital. You will analyse large multi-modal datasets relevant to psychosis, including proteomic, metabolomic, neuroimaging and genomic data, and generate and apply biological ageing clocks across a range of omics modalities. You will select, adapt and develop appropriate analytical methodologies, as well as review and synthesise literature on biological ageing and undertake systematic literature reviews. You will contribute to research publications and conference presentations and support wider project planning and day-to-day project administration. You will have experience using command line tools for reproducible data analysis, alongside skills in statistics, machine learning, data cleaning and analysis pipelines. You will also have experience working with large multi-modal datasets relevant to psychiatry and sufficient specialist knowledge of biological ageing to work within established research programmes. You will be able to communicate research findings clearly, including writing for publication, presenting data at conferences and representing the research group at meetings. items.desc: Who we are At Frontiers, we are on a mission to make science open. Most research today sits behind paywalls, meaning only people at well-funded universities or those who can pay get to read it. Open access flips that: every article we publish is peer-reviewed and made available online to anyone, anywhere at no cost. As one of the world’s largest and most influential open-access publishers, we’ve seen Frontiers research cited 16 million times, and viewed and downloaded more than 5.3 billion times, proof of what science without barriers can do. About the role Do you have an academic or professional background in biology, microbiology, biotechnology, environmental science, agriculture, food science or a related discipline? Looking for an alternative career path where you can stay connected to research while developing commercial, business development and relationship-management skills? As a Publishing Development Specialist at Frontiers, you will combine subject-area understanding with proactive outreach, consultative conversations and data-informed journal development. You will work with researchers, editors and academic communities worldwide to identify opportunities, build strong relationships and generate high-quality submissions for Frontiers journals. What you'll do Reach out directly to researchers and editors to spark new collaborations, launch dedicated article collections, recruit into the Editorial Board, commission manuscripts, and liaise with Chief Editors at a journal section level. Manage a dynamic sales pipeline, taking opportunities from first contact through to successful publication. Use AI tools daily to research prospects, personalize outreach, and manage your pipeline more efficiently. Cultivate trust and build long-term professional relationships with editors and authors. Represent our journals at scientific conferences, webinars, and online events to increase their market footprint. Requirements About You You bring experience in sales, outreach, or business development with a proven track record of hitting targets. You enjoy fast-paced environments, handle multiple projects with ease, and know how to prioritize your day. You have a strong grasp of AI-based tools in a business operations context. Experience using AI in sales or outreach workflows is a plus. You are a natural communicator who is persuasive, personable, and loves building professional relationships and your English is fluent, both spoken and written, as you will be communicating with global researchers and international teams every day. You have an entrepreneurial mindset, always looking for opportunities and taking the initiative to make things happen. This opportunity may be particularly relevant if your background includes microbiology, cellular and infection microbiology, bioengineering, biotechnology, agronomy, soil science, environmental science, environmental chemistry, water research, food science, food technology or related life-science fields. items.desc: Department: Data & AI Location: UK - London Description Insurance isn’t the first industry most data scientists think of when they imagine cutting-edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) work, but the incredibly rich data and nature of the business make it a great place to put cutting-edge AI to use. CFC's Data & AI team is building production agentic and ML systems that automate and inform complex underwriting decisions that drive real business outcomes - not demos, not proof-of-concepts sitting on a shelf. The team includes ML engineers and software engineers shipping production services, and this role sits alongside them as an analytical counterpart: running experiments, stress-testing assumptions, and generating the evidence that shapes what gets built and how it improves over time. We are looking for a mid-level Data Scientist to join the team that owns business-critical, live solutions utilising Large Language Models (LLMs), such as an email ingestion/extraction solution and underwriting agents. This is not a pure research or offline-modelling role - when research is carried out and potential opportunities identified it is expected that you will work closely with ML engineers and software engineers to build this into a live system, where quality, reliability, and evaluation rigor directly affects the business. We expect that a successful candidate will be able to own the data science side of a production LLM system end-to-end: partnering with stakeholders to build early prototypes, designing evaluation frameworks, measuring agent quality, and turning ambiguous "is this good?" questions into repeatable, defensible metrics - while working closely with engineers to understand what it takes to take that work from prototype to live system. About the role Explore complex, high dimensional, real-world datasets to uncover insights that meaningfully improve underwriting decisions and system performance at scale. Partner directly with underwriting and business stakeholders to scope problems, assess feasibility, and build early prototypes (e.g. PoC agents, rapid evaluation of an LLM approach) before committing engineering investment. Stay involved from prototype through to production, working with ML/software engineers to harden, scale, and maintain what you've built as a key contributor to the codebase. Design and run evaluation frameworks for LLM-powered agent behaviour, including offline (golden datasets, regression suites) and online (production monitoring, A/B testing) evaluation. Build and maintain analytical pipelines — prompt design, calibration against human labels, bias/consistency checks, LLM-as-a-judge, and ongoing validation that the judge stays trustworthy as the underlying models change. Partner with ML engineers to design system nodes/components, translating data science findings into concrete engineering requirements. Define quality metrics for agent outputs (accuracy, hallucination rate, task completion, groundedness, latency/cost trade-offs) and track them over time. Work with software engineers on productionising evaluation and monitoring code: CI/CD integration, release gating, and operational readiness (alerting, dashboards, on-call awareness). Actively explore cutting-edge developments in AI and machine learning — with the space and support to experiment, prototype, and bring new techniques into production where they add value. Investigate how agentic systems behave in production — identifying edge cases, failure modes, and opportunities to make systems more robust and reliable. Prototype and iterate on features for AI/ML pipelines, taking ideas from early exploration through to measurable impact in production services. Document experiments, findings, and methodologies clearly so that insights are reproducible and decisions are traceable. About you We're looking for a curious and technically strong Data Scientist who is passionate about applying AI and machine learning to complex, real-world business challenges. You'll be equally comfortable analysing data, designing experiments, engaging with stakeholders and collaborating with engineers to deliver production solutions. You'll have: Experience working in Data Science, Applied Machine Learning, NLP or LLM-focused roles. Strong Python and SQL skills, with experience working in production codebases and collaborative engineering environments. Hands-on experience evaluating, deploying and monitoring machine learning or LLM-powered applications. A solid understanding of experimentation, model evaluation, A/B testing and performance measurement. Experience working with modern AI frameworks, agent architectures or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) solutions. Knowledge of cloud-based AI platforms, ideally within Azure. An understanding of how AI and ML systems are operationalised, monitored and maintained in production. Strong communication skills and the ability to translate complex technical concepts into practical business outcomes. Confidence …
