items.desc: Transport is at the core of modern society. Imagine using your expertise to shape sustainable transport and infrastructure solutions for the future. If you seek to make a difference on a global scale, working with next-gen technologies and the sharpest collaborative teams, then we could be a perfect match. This is the Volvo Group Graduate Program A new era of manufacturing and R&D is here. Are you passionate about technology, eager to solve real business challenges, ready to drive innovation, and join our transformation journey? Then this Graduate program is for you! As part of the Graduate Program at Volvo Group, you will tackle real challenges from day one and contribute to the development of next-generation production solutions. The 15-month Graduate Program combines 50% time in your home department with 50% dedicated program activities, giving you broad exposure across Volvo Group. Through local and international rotations, short-term assignments, and targeted training in areas such as operations, engineering, and purchasing, you will build a strong understanding of our business, brands and strategy. The Volvo Trucks Technology & Industrial (TTI) division and the Defence Vehicle Development department are leading this initiative. We encompass the value chain from customer requirements to engineering to a complete product through coordinating cross functional resources. We also plan to ensure that the Volvo Group is at the forefront of utilizing new technology for the armed forces. This role contributes to establishing this tech area in the Volvo Group while building sustainable competence and knowledge. How you’ll contribute As Product Architect for Remote and Autonomous Vehicle development in the Defense segment, you will combine data-driven strategic thinking with hands-on project execution, turning business needs into scalable digital and operational improvements. Key responsibilities: Business Needs Translation: Clarify and understand customer needs, define the roadmap, and translate requirements into technical solutions. Drive business intelligence, including AI-supported development, and build awareness of this tech area across Volvo Defence, Renault Defence, Mack Defense, TTI Defence Vehicle Development (Gothenburg and Lyon), and other relevant departments. Project Planning and Execution: Develop and manage project plans and timelines, and support in securing funding for the initiatives needed. Stakeholder Management and Documentation: Communicate project progress, challenges, and results to stakeholders and senior management, while maintaining comprehensive project documentation, including requirements, design, and implementation details. You thrive in dynamic environments, embrace new challenges and ambiguity, and take ownership of your own development and growth. With strong analytical skills, you take initiative and drive tasks forward with determination while bringing fresh perspectives and innovative ideas to the team. You enjoy building relationships and leveraging a global network to create impact while working collaboratively across teams and functions. In addition, you contribute to a culture of continuous learning by actively sharing knowledge, exchanging insights, and supporting the development of others. You're comfortable gathering insights from multiple sources, such as engineering reports, field tests, customer test drives, and performance data. You can identify what matters, draw practical conclusions, and translate them into recommendations that support the roadmap while balancing input from colleagues. You are also interested in vehicle regulations, legal aspects and AI-driven work in these technical areas as these will be presented by authorities in parallel with the development work that we conduct. items.desc: Job Description At H&M Creative Studios, we develop and deliver H&M’s customer-facing brand and content experiences globally. Bringing together strategists, creatives, designers, creators, producers and specialists, we are responsible for H&M’s global campaigns, editorial storytelling, creator marketing, organic social channels, e-commerce content, brand design and physical brand experiences. Together, we shape how millions of customers discover, experience and engage with H&M every day. WHAT YOU'LL DO As Organic Social Specialist, you’ll bring deep platform expertise and a strong understanding of social culture to develop H&M’s presence across your assigned social channels. You’ll turn audience insights, platform behaviours and performance learnings into clear priorities, helping us create content that feels relevant to both the platform and the communities we want to reach. You’ll combine strategic thinking with hands-on channel development, continuously exploring how new behaviours, formats and platform features can strengthen our organic social presence. Implement channel strategies, roadmaps and development plans for assigned social platforms, identifying opportunities to strengthen relevance, engagement and growth. Lead content planning and channel prioritisation based on audience behaviours, business needs and platform opportunities. Translate audience insights, performance findings and channel needs into clear, actionable briefs for creative and content teams. Identify and test emerging formats, features, creator behaviours and cultural opportunities, building a structured approach to experimentation and applying learnings to future activity. Monitor channel and content performance, translating insights into practical recommendations that continuously improve our approach. WHO YOU'LL WORK WITH You’ll work closely with creative, content and wider marketing teams, bringing platform expertise into both planning and execution. As a trusted specialist for your assigned platforms, you’ll help teams understand what audiences expect, how channels are evolving and what that means for the content we create. Who you are We are looking for people with… 3-5 years strong experience working with organic social media, with proven responsibility for developing and growing social channels. Deep knowledge of social platforms, including how platform mechanics, audience behaviours and content formats influence performance. Experience developing channel plans, content priorities and briefs based on audience insights and business needs. Confidence working with performance data and turning insights into clear recommendations and actions. A strong understanding of social culture, emerging behaviours, creators, trends and evolving platform features. And people who are… Culturally curious and genuinely engaged in social media and the conversations shaping it. Creative in their thinking, with strong judgement around what makes content relevant and impactful. Analytical and comfortable balancing instinct with performance insights. Curious and experimental, with the confidence to test ideas, learn and adapt. Collaborative communicators who can translate platform expertise into clear recommendations for creative, content and marketing partners. Interested in fashion and how brands can participate meaningfully in social communities. WHO WE ARE H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices and sustainable solutions. Job Description A global retail organisation is looking for a Frontend Engineer to develop digital solutions that support retail operations, store planning and the design of physical customer environments. The organisation delivers a range of digital capabilities, including web platforms, digital design systems, store planning and optimisation tools, digital retail experiences, learning platforms and knowledge management solutions. The successful candidate will work closely with product, business and UX teams to understand user needs, identify optimal solutions and deliver scalable digital experiences. The role requires a strong understanding of modern web architecture, system integrations and component-driven development. The candidate is expected to build upon the existing architecture rather than replace it, ensuring a clean, maintainable solution that supports the organisation's evolving technical landscape. UX-driven development. DevOps experience. AI-assisted, specification-driven development. State management. Web accessibility. Component-driven UI development and design systems. Headless CMS solutions and dynamic page rendering. AI-assisted solutions and integrations. Event-driven architectures and observability tooling. Retail planning, commercial planning or experience from large-scale retail environments. items.desc: Om jobbet Vi är Göteborg! Nu behöver vi dig som vill vara med och utveckla och förvalta Göteborgs Stads ServiceNow-plattform. Hos oss finns personer med lång erfarenhet som gärna delar med sig av sin kunskap. Du får arbeta med varierande uppgifter – ena dagen kan det handla om felsökning och rättning av en bugg, nästa om att utveckla en ny funktion och därefter om att förbättra en befintlig lösning. Din huvudsakliga arbetsuppgift är utveckling, konfigurering och implementation av funktioner i ServiceNow. Du kommer också att arbeta med att analysera behov och krav och omsätta dessa till tekniska lösningar i dialog med kollegor och verksamhet. Exempel på arbetsuppgifter: Utveckla, konfigurera, testa och underhålla lösningar i ServiceNow. Utveckla och anpassa funktionalitet med bland annat JavaScript och ServiceNows verktyg för utveckling och automatisering. Felsöka, rätta fel samt testa och kvalitetssäkra förändringar. Hos oss finns möjlighet att arbeta på distans upp till två dagar i veckan, utifrån verksamhetens förutsättningar. För tjänsten krävs att du har praktisk erfarenhet av systemutveckling i ServiceNow-plattformen. Du har erfarenhet av att utveckla, konfigurera och anpassa funktionalitet i ServiceNow samt av JavaScript-programmering. Du är van vid att självständigt arbeta med utvecklingsuppgifter och att ta fram tekniska lösningar utifrån verksamhetens behov och krav. Du ska som lägst ha genomgått utbildningen ServiceNow Administration Fundamentals. Följande ser vi som meriterande: Ytterligare utbildningar inom ServiceNow, exempelvis Scripting in ServiceNow Fundamentals. Erfarenhet av ServiceNow ITSM och/eller service catalog. Praktisk erfarenhet av utveckling och konfigurering i ServiceNow, exempelvis genom client scripts, business rules, flow designer eller motsvarande funktionalitet i ServiceNow. Erfarenhet av arbete med CMDB (Configuration Management Database) och hantering av konfigurationsdata. Erfarenhet av arbete med update sets samt hantering av leveranser mellan olika ServiceNow-miljöer. Kunskap kring ITIL, minst version 3. Erfarenhet av utvecklingsarbete i en större organisation (10 000+ anställda). Utöver din tekniska kompetens lägger vi stor vikt vid dina personliga egenskaper. Vi söker dig som är analytisk, flexibel, samarbetsinriktad och noggrann. Vi ser också positivt på att du är nyfiken, delar med dig av din kunskap och vill fortsätta utveckla din kompetens inom ServiceNow. För att klara jobbet hos oss behöver du behärska svenska och engelska i tal och skrift. Varmt välkommen med din ansökan! Om oss Intraservice levererar tjänster och digital infrastruktur som hjälper medarbetare och chefer i Göteborgs Stad att arbeta smart och effektivt. På så vis gör vi det enklare att arbeta i staden och skapar förutsättningar för en god service till göteborgarna. Vi har en central roll i stadens digitalisering och automatisering och våra kunder är Göteborgs alla förvaltningar och bolag. Vi är drygt 700 medarbetare som arbetar i centrala Göteborg. Hoppas du vill bli en av oss! items.desc: Om oss På Techrytera AB börjar rekryteringen med dig. Vi är ett bemannings- och rekryteringsföretag med spetskompetens och ett tydligt fokus inom IT och Engineering. Korta feedbackloopar och tät dialog med Kunden och dess verksamhet bidrar till att Leverantören är delaktig i hela utvecklingsprocessen. För att lyckas långsiktigt handlar en viktig del av utvecklingsarbetet om att bygga för kvalitet och automatisering, där stort fokus ligger på agilt arbetssätt. I uppdraget ingår att Leverantören ska dokumentera för Kundens räkning och kompetensöverföra till relevant personal hos Kunden. Övriga arbetsuppgifter Testdriven och beteendedriven utveckling (TDD/BDD). Arbete med asynkrona API:er och Apache Kafka. Arbete med WSO2 (API Manager), Micro-services (API). Arbete med processhantering i Camunda. Arbetssätt Agilt, iterativt och värdeskapande med SAFe som agilt ramverk och inspiration. Agilt team med stort eget ansvar. Skicka in din ansökan eller hör av dig till oss så berättar vi mer. Vi ser fram emot att hitta nästa steg i din karriär tillsammans med dig.

items.desc: Acne Studios is a progressive luxury house and through collaboration and curiosity, we set high aspirations and strive for excellence. We value everyone’s contribution and embrace feedback to develop ourselves and others. We aim to minimise our environmental impact across all our operations and to address societal challenges in the way we conduct our business. As Analytics Engineer at our Stockholm Head Office, you will transform clean, validated data into well-documented, trusted datasets that teams across Acne Studios rely on. Your work enables self-service analytics through Power BI and other consumption layers, so that business users can find and use data without ad-hoc engineering support. You succeed when datasets are accurate and trusted, and when metrics are consistent across the company. To get there, you build strong relationships with stakeholders, communicate clearly, deliver reliably and share your knowledge with the team. CULTURE OF COLLABORATION We firmly believe that when you feel supported, included, and trusted, it enables you to enjoy your work and thrive in it. You will be a part of a team of colleagues with diverse roles and backgrounds, each with their unique skills and experiences. WHAT YOU WILL DO As Analytics Engineer your main contribution will be to build the data foundation that turns raw, validated data into business-ready models used across the company. You will report to Manager Data Insights. You will play a vital role in making data accessible, reliable and consistent for everyone at Acne Studios by: Designing and maintaining dimensional models (facts, dimensions, lookups) in the gold layer, following star schema principles Building and operating reusable data transformation pipelines using PySpark and SQL on Databricks Structuring and exposing data for consumption by Power BI and external systems such as Centric and Dema Contributing to building a centralized semantic layer in Databricks Implementing and maintaining core business metrics, logic and KPIs Ensuring data quality through automated testing and validation Documenting datasets and making them easy to find and use Partnering with stakeholders to translate business needs into requirements and data models Supporting analysts working in Power BI and Databricks Dashboards with clear and structured guidance Communicating proactively with business users about what data is available, what it means and how to use it Contributing to improvements in transformation patterns, testing frameworks, tools and ways of working WHO YOU ARE You have high aspirations and focus on details that create substantial impact. You enjoy working as a team and you embrace feedback to develop yourself and others. You are curious and thrive in a dynamic environment. Cooperation, respect, and clear communication are important, along with your ambition to learn and grow. If these qualities speak to you, we would love to have you on our team. Specific personal qualities for this role: Clear communicator with both technical and business audiences Service-minded and responsive Structured and detail-oriented, with high standards for accuracy and documentation Proactive in identifying improvements Curious and motivated to keep learning Team player who shares knowledge through code reviews, demos and presentations Specific experience and knowledge for this role: Strong dimensional modelling skills (star schema, SCD2 etc.) Advanced PySpark and SQL (window functions, complex joins, incremental processing) Experience working with Spark Solid Python skills (data validation, scripting, testing) Experience with the Databricks platform: Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, notebooks, jobs, workflows Experience with orchestration tools (Databricks Workflows, Data Factory or similar) Familiarity with Power BI (semantic models, relationships, DAX basics) Familiarity with AI-assisted Lakehouse tools (code assistants, Genie spaces, AI/BI dashboards, model serving endpoints) Familiarity with CI/CD for data assets (Databricks Asset Bundles, Git integration) Familiarity with data quality frameworks (Great Expectations or custom assertion patterns) Fluent in English What matters most to us is not whether you master all the listed knowledge and skills. We are dedicated to recognising the potential in each individual. We embrace diversity of people as well as ideas and viewpoints and encourage everyone's individual expression of their own identity.

The OE team ensures the application of these processes through comprehensive (i) operational policies & procedures, (ii) system solutions & data flows (iii) change management & reporting, (iv) support provision to internal & external actors and (v) execution of defined process responsibilities. Within the OE team, the Business Process Optimization team is accountable for the development of the business process design, system solutions & data flows; change management; alignment with operational policies & procedures; and successful mainstreaming to integrate changes into business operations, support and process execution & monitoring for core GLC processes (throughout this document understood to include policies and procedures, system solutions and data flows). The team thus contributes to the delivery of the primary business of the Global Fund. The Officer, Business Process Optimization & Operations is responsible to contribute to: Strong project management to support timely and quality delivery. Quality diagnostics to identify opportunities for business process redesign. Business process design and documentation to define business needs. Systems design and user acceptance testing to ensure quality system solutions. Change management and mainstreaming to facilitate integration of changes into regular business operations. Business process management to ensure timely and quality completion of deliverables (on demand). The Officer collaborates with a wide range of stakeholders within the Global Fund and uses strong interpersonal, communication and diplomacy skills to integrate the perspectives of different stakeholders while ensuring that the processes, policies/procedures, systems solutions, data flows and associated change management remain coherent, user-friendly, and streamlined. They are expected to systematically identify and operationalize opportunities for automation and Artificial Intelligence within their scope of work. Key Responsibilities The Officer, Business Process Optimization & Operations is responsible for the below areas of work, as assigned: Project Management Substantively contribute to well-defined project plans, including key project deliverables, owners and deadlines, considering resource and time constraints. Track progress and flag potential delays and dependencies early. Document key decisions and open points and follow up for timely resolution. Identify, monitor, and support early mitigation of risks to de-risk project delivery. Prepare and support GLC Governance meetings, materials & documentation. Develop and revise process maps, RACIs, forms & other process materials and ensure alignment with operational policies and procedures, significantly inputting into required updates in collaboration with the OE Policy team. Document requirements at an appropriate level of detail and with end-to-end process thinking in Business Requirements Documents (BRDs) and other supporting assets, consulting functional teams and end users to ensure suitability of requirements and with an end-to-end view of the GLC for alignment & identification of up/downstream impacts. Contribute to the development of business process metrics and reporting requirements to strengthen organizational oversight, in collaboration with other teams, including the OE Business Support and Operations team. Define and lead projects to remedy data quality issues and ensure consistent definition of data elements and UI for clarity. items.desc: The Royal Marsden has a vital role in championing change and improvement in cancer care through research and innovation, education and leading-edge practice. We are incredibly proud of our international reputation for pushing the boundaries and for our ground breaking work ensuring our patients receive the very best and latest in cancer treatment and care. As part of the department expansion, an opportunity has arisen for a Genetic Technologist Analyst to join the Clinical Genomics department. The Clinical Genomics laboratory at the Royal Marsden is part of the North Thames Genomic Laboratory Hub (NT GLH), one of seven national Genomic Laboratory Hubs offering Cancer Genomic testing in England. The department is located in the Centre for Molecular Pathology in Sutton. The Centre for Molecular Pathology is a state-of-the-art facility bringing together translational science and molecular diagnostics. It is one of the few specialised laboratories in molecular diagnostics of cancer in Europe. The department provides a reference Molecular Diagnostics and Cytogenetics Service for solid tumours and haematological malignancies, as well as participating in clinical trials and collaborating with the industry (https://www.royalmarsden.nhs.uk/royal-marsden-partnership-create-state-art-house-liquid-biopsy-testing-facility) to provide cutting-edge genomic technologies to support personalised cancer treatment. The post holder will undertake technical, analytical and administrative duties required to support the scientific teams in the provision of an effective and high quality molecular diagnostics service to patients. This will require detailed theoretical and practical knowledge. They will be responsible for carrying out analytical molecular diagnostics investigations. There will be occasions when the post holder takes sole responsibility for their work. The range of tests available will be in continuous development and the post-holder will be responsible for the validation and verification of new techniques and tests, including the provision of NGS and ddPCR for molecular diagnostics in haematological and solid tumours. They will collaborate and plan complex activities with other members of the team to achieve an effective and reliable service. The post holder will be expected to assist in training of new staff members and visitors as well as to contribute to IT development and data management relating to the technical aspects of the molecular service In addition the post holder will be required to support activities such as quality, including compliance with laboratory accreditation standards, equipment maintenance and participate in the departments training programme. The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust is a world-leading cancer centre. Our role is to offer our patients the best cancer care available anywhere in the world, and to continue to make a global contribution to finding better ways of diagnosing and treating cancer. We employ over 4,500 staff in a diverse range of careers including nursing, medical, science, radiography, pharmacy, occupational therapy, finance and administrative services. We have two hospitals – one in Chelsea, London, and one in Sutton, Surrey – as well as a Medical Daycare Unit in Kingston Hospital. At The Royal Marsden, we deal with cancer every day, so we understand how valuable life is. When people entrust their lives to us, they have the right to demand the very best. That's why the pursuit of excellence lies at the heart of everything we do. At the heart of the hospital is our dedicated team. We offer a stimulating and dynamic working environment, a wide range of staff benefits, learning and development opportunities and clear career pathways. There are opportunities to work flexibly across a range of areas and specialities and we welcome flexible working requests from point of hire to support employees work life balance. We are looking for employees who aspire to excellence, share our values and can play a crucial role in our on-going achievements. For further information please refer to the job description and personal specification 1.1 To be responsible for own work and that of junior members of staff under the direction of senior scientific staff/clinical scientist. This will include all aspects of the clinical scientific & technical work, staff, equipment and quality system. 1.2 To ensure the timely and efficient provision of core and technologically complex analytical/diagnostic services, including but not limited to PCR, RQ-PCR, sequencing, NGS and ddPCR. To take day to day responsibility for the quality of technical and analytical work produced. To ensure that clinical requests are met according to agreed policies on availability of tests and priorities in accordance with user guide. items.desc: About Aura Biosciences Aura Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing bel-sar, a potentially transformative, first-in-class therapy for patients living with ocular cancers. Bel-sar represents an entirely novel approach to treating ocular cancers via its dual mechanisms of action of acute tumor necrosis and secondary anti-tumor immune activation. The Phase 3 registration study of Bel-sar in early choroidal melanoma, the largest patient segment of uveal melanoma, is fully enrolled, and earlier stage studies in metastases to the choroid and cancers of the ocular surface are ongoing. Aura's mission is to improve outcomes for patients living with ocular cancers by delivering a therapy that not only arrests tumor growth but also preserves vision and quality of life. For more information, visit aurabiosciences.com. Follow us on X, @AuraBiosciences, and visit us on LinkedIn. The Clinical Scientist will be a key scientific member of cross-functional study teams, contributing to the design, execution, analysis, interpretation, and communication of Aura's clinical programs. Working closely with the Vice President Clinical Development and colleagues across Medical, Clinical Operations, Biostatistics, Safety, Data Management, Regulatory, and other functions, this individual will help translate clinical strategy into high-quality studies and actionable scientific evidence. Author and/or contribute to protocols and amendments, clinical study reports, investigator brochures, regulatory briefing documents, health authority responses, and other key clinical documents. Evaluate emerging clinical data, scientific literature, and competitive programs to inform study and development strategy. Ensure clinical data and scientific rationale are presented clearly, accurately, and consistently across clinical and regulatory deliverables. Scientific Communication Develop clear presentations of clinical data for study teams, internal governance, and external scientific audiences. Contribute to abstracts, posters, presentations, manuscripts, and other scientific communications. items.desc: ARC Regulatory combines specialist IVD/CDx clinical research expertise with laboratory services and software solutions to support Sponsors across the clinical trial lifecycle and accelerate global precision medicine studies. Through its Dx CRO and Sponsor Delegation services, ARC supports the planning, delivery and oversight of global CDx clinical trials, acting as an extension of the Sponsor team and providing clear ownership and accountability across delegated activities. ARC Laboratories, based in Belfast, Northern Ireland, provides in-house assay and clinical trial sample testing capabilities across IHC, qPCR, ELISA and NGS-based testing. The laboratory is UKAS ISO 15189 and CAP accredited, providing high-quality biomarker testing for precision medicine clinical trials. ARC’s Health Institution status, under the IVDR Article 5(5), provides a practical route for early-phase clinical trial sample testing in the EU and UK, helping reduce regulatory burden and enable faster sample testing for eligible studies. ARC also combines its regulatory expertise with technology through ARC360® powered by AURA AI. ARC360® is a regulatory intelligence and submission collaboration platform scoped specifically for CDx clinical trials, bringing national regulatory requirements, submission workflows, document generation and project reporting into one place. AURA AI capabilities combine the speed of AI with human expertise to support structured, traceable and auditable regulatory outputs. By connecting clinical research, laboratory and technology expertise, ARC helps Sponsors reduce complexity, manage risk and maintain control across their global precision medicine clinical trials. Reporting to the Laboratory Manager, the IVD Technician will perform routine laboratory activities, prepare materials, maintain equipment and manage consumables and laboratory records. Working closely with Laboratory Scientists and project teams, the postholder will help maintain an organised, safe and audit-ready laboratory environment, supporting the successful delivery of internal and client projects. Maintain accurate and traceable laboratory documentation, including equipment logs, calibration records, reagent preparation records and laboratory notebooks. Support the preparation and maintenance of COSHH assessments, risk assessments and health and safety documentation. Work in accordance with laboratory quality systems, SOPs and applicable standards. Assist with internal audits, external inspections and quality reviews by providing accurate records and supporting documentation. Collaborate with scientists, quality personnel and operational teams to support laboratory activities and project delivery. An understanding of good laboratory practices and laboratory documentation requirements. Strong attention to detail, with the ability to maintain accurate, complete and traceable records. items.desc: Job Description Biology - Industrial Placement 12 Months Milton Park, Oxford Vertex is a global biotechnology company that aims to discover, develop and commercialize innovative new medicines so people with serious diseases can lead better lives. Founded in 1989 in Cambridge, MA, Vertex today has research and development sites and commercial offices around the world in the United States, Canada, Europe and Australia. We are recruiting for an Industrial placement student in the Biology Department, at our research facility in Oxfordshire, as part of our wider intern intake for the year. Main Duties & Objectives The research site is a dynamic, fast-paced environment, where you will be embedded within research teams working on any one of several diseases. You will be working in a close-knit, multidisciplinary team of scientists, located in our research laboratories, where you can expect to gain a broad understanding of the drug discovery process from target validation through to small molecule discovery and optimisation. As part of your time here you can expect to learn about disease biology, the pharmaceutical discovery and development process and gain valuable laboratory skills. During your Industrial Placement you will get the opportunity to learn about our industry from a hands-on perspective. You will be working closely with and learning from some of the brightest people in the industry. Students can expect to be challenged by their work, connect with other students, and feel valued by the Vertex community. Every day, we provide essential water and wastewater services to millions of people, and we are committed to delivering reliable, affordable and sustainable services while supporting our communities and protecting the environment. By focusing on the outcomes that matter most to our customers, we are also working towards our ambition to be the National Leader in sustainable water and wastewater services. Working within the Strategic Planning team, the role uses asset, operational and business data to forecast future performance, model investment scenarios, inform PR29 planning and provide evidence-based recommendations to decision makers. You will investigate and develop asset performance relationships using statistical analysis, technical knowledge and industry insight. You will identify critical data needs, data quality issues and gaps, and influence the business to address them sustainably. You will develop, maintain and enhance asset performance, deterioration and forecasting models and apply optimisation techniques to identify the most efficient intervention and investment solutions. You will produce forecasts of asset condition and performance and recommend interventions to support service plans. About you If you have experience of solving problems using data mining techniques and statistical modelling to develop practical solutions, we would love to hear from you! You will have excellent interpersonal and engagement skills and the ability to build positive relationships with stakeholders at varying levels, communicating clearly and with confidence. You will be skilled in data analysis, modelling, machine learning and programming, with a good working knowledge of a statistical programming language. We will be hosting an Open Evening session to learn more about PR29 roles at our Northumbria House office in Pity Me, Durham on Tuesday 10th November 2026. Cloud development experience (AWS, GCP or Azure). Working knowledge of Medallion Architecture. Demonstrated capability in implementing and supporting pipelines in demanding environments. Certifications in Data Engineering, Cloud, Data Modelling or Data Architecture. Experience with development lifecycle processes for data pipelines. STEM degree (Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Physics) or equivalent practical experience. items.desc: Description White Swan Data is a small but rapidly growing team of mathematicians, data scientists and software engineers who are constantly striving to refine world class probability models while also researching and deploying new ones. Our work bridges three domains, each challenging in its own right - iGaming, quantitative research and software development. As a Football Trader, you will monitor and manage betting markets, analyse live football data, and make decisions to optimize trading outcomes. This role combines a strong mathematical aptitude with a deep understanding of football dynamics. Prior trading experience is not required but will be considered a plus. You will be expected to work over the weekend during football season and at least 2 evening shifts (finish past 10:30 pm). This role will reward individuals who are curious, hungry for learning and value attention to detail. Key Responsibilities Monitor football betting markets, track odds movements, and identify trading opportunities. Analyse live and historical football data to inform trading strategies. Adjust prices in response to market trends and real-time events (e.g., goals, injuries, substitutions). Collaborate with analysts to refine trading models and improve market predictions. Maintain focus and accuracy in high-pressure, fast-paced environments, particularly during live matches. Stay informed about football leagues, teams, players, and trends to gain a competitive edge. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Essential: Strong mathematical background (degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Engineering, or a related field preferred). Comprehensive knowledge of football, including leagues, teams, and strategies. Strong analytical skills and attention to detail. Ability to make quick decisions under pressure. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and/or basic data analysis tools. Desirable: Experience with statistical programming languages (e.g., Python, R). Knowledge of betting markets or prior experience in a trading environment. Understanding of predictive modeling and probability theory. Passion for football analytics and/or sports betting. Benefits Salary depending on experience. Annual discretionary performance bonus. Comprehensive training in trading strategies, market dynamics, and tools. Opportunities for career growth in a dynamic and exciting industry. A collaborative work environment surrounded by football enthusiasts and data experts. Flexible working hours, particularly during the football calendar. 25 days holiday per annum, plus UK bank holidays. Private health & dental insurance. Optical cover through Aviva. Pension plan. Gympass membership to over 1900 gyms and wellness businesses. Breakfast bought in everyday and lunch bought in twice a week Free coffee & snacks at the office. Regular team events & socials. About White Swan Data Technology is at the heart of our business and has produced consistent and significant results. We are a small but rapidly growing team of mathematicians, data scientists and software engineers constantly striving to refine our world class statistical models while also researching and deploying new ones. Our work bridges three domains, each challenging in its own right - iGaming, quantitative research and software development. This convergence demands a rare blend of skills and creativity to identify and capitalise on inefficiencies across the iGaming landscape. The opportunities are vast, but we are only as good as the people we bring on board. As a startup, we offer a dynamic and entrepreneurial environment where you’ll work on impactful projects and have the autonomy to explore new ideas. In-person collaboration and innovation are at the heart of what we do, and we are always looking for individuals who can contribute their unique perspectives and talents to help us stay ahead in a constantly evolving industry. At White Swan Data, we recognise that building a diverse and inclusive workforce within a highly technical field presents both opportunities and challenges. We recognise the value that a variety of perspectives can bring to innovation, problem-solving, and business success. A team composed of individuals from different backgrounds, experiences, and ways of thinking fosters creativity, enhances decision-making, and ultimately strengthens our ability to tackle complex challenges.

Are you our next Quality Engineer? We're looking for an experienced Quality Engineer who combines strong technical testing skills with the confidence to take ownership of projects and work directly with clients. You'll join our team of software testing specialists, working across a variety of technologies, industries and delivery environments. You could be embedded within a client's development team, leading testing on a project or helping a client improve their approach to quality. We're looking for someone who can get to grips with complex systems, investigate technical issues and make informed decisions about what needs testing and how. Design and execute functional, exploratory, integration, API and regression testing. Investigate complex technical issues using APIs, databases, browser developer tools, application logs and other diagnostic resources. Understand how systems and services interact, identifying risks across integrations, data flows and end-to-end processes. Develop appropriate test approaches, adapting testing techniques to suit different projects and delivery environments. Communicate testing progress, findings and risks clearly, helping clients make informed decisions. Identify opportunities to improve testing processes, coverage and efficiency. Apply test automation where it adds value, working with existing frameworks or contributing to automated testing activities. The ability to write SQL queries to investigate issues, validate data and understand how applications interact with databases. Experience using browser developer tools, application logs and other diagnostic resources to investigate defects. A good technical understanding of software architecture, system integrations and data flows. Experience working directly with developers, product owners and other stakeholders in Agile delivery environments. The confidence to work independently, make decisions and provide direction to other testers when required. Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain technical issues, challenge assumptions and discuss risks directly with clients. A practical, analytical approach to problem-solving and a willingness to learn new technologies. It would also be great if you have: Experience with test automation tools or frameworks such as Playwright, Cypress or Selenium. Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines, Git or cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure or Google Cloud. Experience testing complex integrations, data migrations or enterprise systems. Experience improving testing practices or introducing new tools and approaches. ISTQB certification or other relevant technical qualifications. Working with colleagues across IT and software development, you'll help ensure our infrastructure remains available, well-maintained, and aligned with operational requirements. This role suits an infrastructure professional who enjoys troubleshooting complex issues, automating routine tasks, and finding practical ways to improve system performance. What You'll Be Responsible For Configure, maintain, and monitor cloud infrastructure across platforms such as Microsoft Azure or Amazon Web Services (AWS). Manage virtual machines, storage, networking, access permissions, and other infrastructure resources. Monitor system availability, performance, and capacity, investigating issues and implementing corrective actions. Diagnose infrastructure incidents, identify root causes, and work towards lasting solutions. Maintain operating systems, apply security patches, and coordinate infrastructure upgrades. Experience administering Windows Server or Linux environments. Knowledge of identity and access management, security controls, and infrastructure maintenance. Experience monitoring system performance and investigating technical incidents. Familiarity with scripting or automation using Python, PowerShell, or Bash. items.desc: Great manufacturing businesses don’t simply create exceptional products – they build the processes, systems, and technical foundations that turn innovative designs into high-quality, reliable solutions. By combining engineering expertise, attention to detail, and a commitment to continuous improvement, they ensure products can be manufactured safely, efficiently, and consistently to meet customer expectations. As our BioPRO Manufacturing Engineer, you’ll play an important role in translating engineering designs and product requirements into accurate production documentation and manufacturing-ready CAD data. Working closely with the Senior Engineer and wider Engineering and Manufacturing teams, you’ll develop detailed drawings, Bills of Materials, manufacturing layouts, cutting patterns, and work instructions that bring designs to life on the production floor. With a strong focus on accuracy, practical problem-solving, document control, and manufacturability, you’ll help ensure our BioPRO products can be manufactured efficiently, repeatedly, and to the high standards our customers expect. In this role you will: Create and maintain accurate production drawings, 2D and 3D CAD models, and manufacturing documentation from approved engineering designs and specifications. Develop complete manufacturing packages for foam products and assemblies, including Bills of Materials, manufacturing layouts, cutting patterns, and assembly drawings. Produce clear, practical work instructions that translate engineering requirements into safe, efficient, and repeatable manufacturing processes. Support prototype builds and new product introduction, working with the Senior Engineer and wider teams to resolve production queries and manufacturing challenges. Implement approved engineering changes promptly, maintaining accurate drawings, Bills of Materials, work instructions, and controlled revisions. Identify and deliver continuous-improvement opportunities to enhance manufacturability, production efficiency, product quality, and process consistency. Maintain high standards of document control, revision management, and configuration control, ensuring manufacturing teams have access to accurate, up-to-date information. You’re someone who takes pride in getting the details right. You understand that successful manufacturing starts with clear engineering documentation, accurate drawings, and practical solutions that work on the production floor. You’re methodical, organised, and proactive, with the technical capability to turn engineering requirements into manufacturing-ready outputs. You enjoy solving problems, working collaboratively across teams, and finding better ways to do things, ensuring quality and consistency are built into every stage of the process. You will: Have practical CAD experience and the ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and product requirements accurately. Demonstrate strong technical drawing and CAD-modelling skills, with exceptional attention to detail and a commitment to producing high-quality documentation. Have experience creating production drawings, manufacturing documentation, and clear work instructions within an engineering or manufacturing environment. Take a methodical approach to manufacturing process development, document control, revision management, and configuration control. Be proficient in Microsoft Office, with experience using Fusion 360, CATIA, or comparable 2D and 3D CAD systems being desirable. items.desc: An exciting opportunity has arisen for an enthusiastic and motivated Activity Coordinator to join the multidisciplinary team at Butler Green Enhanced Intermediate Care Unit. The post holder will play a key role in supporting the delivery of a holistic rehabilitation model by developing, coordinating and facilitating a varied programme of meaningful therapeutic, cognitive, social and recreational activities for patients. Working alongside nursing, therapy and wider multidisciplinary colleagues, the Activity Coordinator will support patients to maintain independence, improve wellbeing, enhance social engagement and maximise their rehabilitation potential during their stay. The post holder will assess individual interests, abilities and needs to ensure activities are person-centred, inclusive and aligned with rehabilitation goals. They will promote patient participation, record engagement and outcomes, and contribute to improving the overall patient experience within the unit. The role will also support the development of relationships with community organisations, volunteers, charities and external partners to enhance opportunities available to patients and support community integration where appropriate. Unfortunately, this role does not meet the criteria required to qualify for sponsorship. With support from the Ward Leadership Team/Multidisciplinary team, contribute to providing a range of social interaction and well-being activities, e.g., activity groups, and on an individual basis, with minimal supervision. In collaboration with the client group and Ward Manager, maintain and develop the activities timetable for the ward and for each client on an individual recovery focussed basis. Work alongside colleagues e.g., Occupational Health, Physiotherapy and Nursing staff to deliver a range of activities that are recovery focussed and suit the individual needs of each client. Contribute to the regular updating of individual activity timetables for clients which offer a range of activities on an individual and group basis dependent on the client’s needs. This can be subject to regular change. Document all engagement with clients in their case notes to ensure the clinical team is kept up to date with client’s participation in activities. Verbally hand over this information to the Therapeutic and nursing team on a shift-by-shift basis as appropriate. The post holder will support learners in the workplace by providing an opportunity for shadowing with the activity co-ordinator to observe activities being planned and delivered. Ensure the provision of timely fundamental patient care by working alongside the ward team to support patients with activities of daily living. The Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust (NCA) provides hospital and integrated health and social care services to over one million people living across Greater Manchester. Our 20,000 colleagues care for people in hospital and in the community, working across Bury, Rochdale, Oldham and Salford, to save and improve lives. As a large NHS trust we are committed to enhancing the health of our local population by delivering consistently high standards of care and working closely with local authorities and key partners. We believe in our power and potential to make a difference and we’re always looking for people who demonstrate our three core values - care, appreciate and inspire – to join our team. In return, we can offer you a job role with purpose and flexibility. The size and scale of the NCA means we can provide more challenge and opportunities so your career can always be moving in the right direction. By joining us you can also access a competitive benefits package, including, a fantastic annual leave allowance, flexible working opportunities and protected hours for health and wellbeing activities, helping you to achieve more personal downtime and a better work-life balance. Learn more about us in our Candidate Information Pack (opens in existing window) To read more information about the advertised role, and the main job duties/responsibilities please open the Job Description and Person Specification located under the supporting documents heading. You can also read more information about working at the Northern Care Alliance within the attached Candidate Information Pack or by visiting our careers website: www.careers.northerncarealliance.nhs.uk

items.desc: We are seeking a part time Specialty Doctor in CAMHS Eating Disorder Service based at St George's Hospital in Stafford, working alongside the Consultant Child & Adolescent Psychiatrists and other members of the multi-disciplinary team. This is an exciting opportunity to join a newly mobilising specialist eating disorders day hospital service The CYP Eating Disorders Day Hospital Service is currently mobilising. This specialist provision delivers intensive, evidence-based care to children & young people experiencing moderate to severe eating disorders. This innovative service aims to bridge the gap between inpatient and community care, offering a safe and structured alternative to Tier 4 admission & facilitating earlier discharge from hospital settings. Operating through a MDT working collaboratively to provide holistic, person-centred care, each professional brings their expertise to support physical health monitoring, nutritional rehabilitation, psychosocial interventions & occupational engagement, all tailored to the unique needs of each young person & their family. In-reach and Outreach support to prevent unnecessary hospital admissions & reduce relapse. Intensive day hospital interventions focused on recovery, risk management, & re-engagement with daily life. Meal support and psychoeducation for young people & their families, promoting sustainable recovery at home. Multidisciplinary care planning and supervision , ensuring continuity & quality of care across settings. Training and consultation to professionals and carers, enhancing system-wide understanding and support for eating disorders. Come and work with us at our award-winning NHS Trust, leading the way for trying new and better ways of working to help improve life for our local communities. We have around 9,000 staff who provide physical and mental healthcare, support for people with learning disabilities, and adult social care across Staffordshire, Stoke-on-Trent, Shropshire, and Telford & Wrekin. We also run regional and national services, including help for new parents (perinatal care), eating disorders, forensic services, sexual health, and support for people in prison with mental health, drug, or alcohol problems. We offer great career development for both clinical and non-clinical roles, with ongoing training and support to help you learn and grow. We are ‘United in our Uniqueness’ and committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels welcome and can be themselves, no matter their background or identity. We want our staff to feel supported and valued, and we aim to build a team that reflects the communities we serve. Together, we can make sure every voice is heard, and every difference is respected. This mobilisation represents a significant step forward in the West Midlands CAMHS Provider Collaboratives commitment to transforming eating disorder care for children and young people and aligns with nationally driven new care models for children and young people.

items.title: Clinical Fellow in Haematology
items.card: The King’s Haematology service satisfies all the level 4 BCSH criteria including bed numbers, isolation facilities, equipment, hospital infra-structure, laboratory services, radiotherapy, medical and nursing staffing, pharmacy facilities and support services. The department has dedicated Haemato-oncology consultants, in addition to medical and nurse transplant co-ordinators, specialist junior medical and nursing
items.desc: The King’s Haematology service satisfies all the level 4 BCSH criteria including bed numbers, isolation facilities, equipment, hospital infra-structure, laboratory services, radiotherapy, medical and nursing staffing, pharmacy facilities and support services. The department has dedicated Haemato-oncology consultants, in addition to medical and nurse transplant co-ordinators, specialist junior medical and nursing staff. The multidisciplinary team extends to all clinical specialties that are represented in the established weekly regional MDT meetings. The Department, which is the largest in South East of the UK, has an extensive referral base within the SE London, Kent, Sussex and Surrey area with more than 75% of regional referrals coming to Kings. This hub and spoke network is a model for the sharing of patient care between centre and unit. Applications are invited to work in the Department of Haematological Medicine at King’s College Hospital, for an initial period of 6 months. This is an exciting opportunity to join a centre of excellence specialising in haemato-oncology, bone marrow transplantation, haemoglobinopathy, coagulation and transfusion medicine. Our integrated haemato-oncology and transplant service has 4 dedicated wards treating all forms of haematological malignancy as well as marrow failure disorders. It carries out all forms of autologous and allogeneic transplantation and has an active cell and gene therapy program. The Department looks after approximately 1200 adults and children with Sickle Cell disease. King’s is an NHS Exemplar Centre for prevention and management of venous thromboembolism (VTE), and has a large multi-disciplinary Anticoagulation and Clinical Thrombosis Team. The Haematology medical team comprises 30 Consultant Haematologists, 1 Clinical Lecturer, 14 Specialist Registrars, 5 Senior Clinical Fellows and 11 SHOs. King’s College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is one of the UK’s largest and busiest teaching Trusts with a turnover of c£2.1billion, 1.5 million patient contacts a year and around 14,000 staff based across 5 main sites in South East London. The Trust provides a full range of local hospital services across its different sites, and specialist services from King’s College Hospital (KCH) sites at Denmark Hill in Camberwell and at the Princess Royal University Hospital (PRUH) site in Bromley. King’s is committed to delivering Sustainable Healthcare for All via our Green Plan. In line with national Greener NHS ambitions, we have set net zero carbon targets of 2040 for our NHS Carbon Footprint and 2045 for our NHS Carbon Footprint Plus . In June 2026, we launched our new strategy for 2026-31. Our vision is to transform healthcare, and we have agreed six strategic ambitions to help us improve care for patients, and the working lives of our staff. Our six strategic ambitions are delivering high-quality patient care ; creating a great place to work ; leading pioneering research, innovation and education ; building strong and successful partnerships ; providing timely and efficient care ; and ensuring long-term financial sustainability . This post is for a full time clinical fellow (ST3+) within the Department of Haematological Medicine at King’s College Hospital Foundation Trust. This post will join the haematology specialist trainees rota. This will provide broad experience in haemato-oncology, laboratory and general haematology, haemoglobinopathy, paediatric haematology and thrombosis. This position will be an ideal opportunity to develop supervised experience in haematology, and for more experience candidates to explore an area of interest. Appointees will be expected to undertake both undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, and research is encouraged. The appointee must have (or be eligible for) GMC registration. A medical degree or diploma and MRCP (or equivalent) from a recognised UK or overseas University or Institution is required. The appointment will be initially for a period of 6 months with the potential for renewal. Any candidate who is unable for personal reasons to work full-time will be eligible to be considered for this post; if such a person is appointed, modification of the job will be discussed on a personal basis with the Trust.

items.desc: We are recruiting to our new Intensive & Assertive Team , launching across Norfolk to provide intensive, flexible and recovery-focused support for people living with severe and enduring mental illness. This is a unique opportunity to join a service from the outset and help shape its future. As a Care Coordinator, you will work with people who often find it difficult to engage with traditional mental health services, delivering assertive outreach, intensive community support and recovery-focused interventions. You will help improve engagement, reduce hospital admissions and support individuals to live more fulfilling lives within their communities. Posts Available and Locality Working We currently have 8.5 Care Coordinator vacancies across Norfolk and Suffolk. This is an excellent opportunity for a doctor looking to strengthen their clinical experience, develop their surgical skills and build a portfolio for future career progression. Previous NHS experience is essential. The department has an established track record of supporting Trust Grade Registrars to successfully progress through national Urology ST3 selection. We also welcome more senior candidates, with experience of supporting doctors pursuing the FRCS (Urol) examination and CESR pathway. The successful candidate will contribute to the delivery of high-quality elective and emergency urological services, gaining experience across outpatient clinics, diagnostic services and core urological procedures. The department offers exposure to a broad range of specialist procedures and techniques, including percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL), robotic prostatectomy, brachytherapy, laparoscopic nephrectomy, UroLift, holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP), and flexible ureterorenoscopy with laser treatment. There are also opportunities to participate in clinical research, quality improvement initiatives and clinical audit, alongside involvement in departmental and undergraduate medical education. The department actively encourages registrars to contribute to teaching and the continued development of the service. The department has strengthened its emergency urology provision through the development of a dedicated 1 in 7 non-resident middle-grade on-call rota, supported by a Urology SHO-equivalent doctor during working hours. This provides an opportunity to develop experience in the assessment and management of emergency urological presentations within a supportive clinical team. items.desc: Job overview Nursing Associates (NA) and assistant practitioners (AP) work as part of the wider health and social care team and have direct contact with patients, services users or clients providing high quality and compassionate care. They will work within both the surgical admissions and pre operative assessment environments developing the additional skills and knowledge required. In the pre operative assessment clinic the NA or the AP will undertake pre-operative assessment on suitable patients that are waiting for elective surgery. The pre-assessment covers the physical, social, emotional and spiritual needs of the patient. They will be supported by the registered pre assessment nurse and expected to work within their determined scope of practice. They also support band 3 healthcare assistants in the testing clinic. When working in the surgical admissions area, the NA or the AP will support the patient on the day of their surgical journey, working with the surgeon and anaesthetist, ensuring they are safe and ready for theatre. They will escort the patient to the anaesthetic room where they will ensure correct monitoring is placed and to be present whilst the anaesthetic is administered by the team. They will advocate for the patient and ensure patient safety. The NA/AP will have responsibility for actively participating as part of the Multi-disciplinary team within the department, to provide a seamless service to patients with proximal supervision from a registered nurse /practitioner Act with professionalism and integrity- being a role model for those around you, ensuring that everyone has equal opportunity Find solutions to problems and be able to demonstrate a positive approach to new challenges, encouraging others to do the same Understand what people need and be adaptable and responsive to help provide a individualised service Help to create an environment where differences are valued, encouraged and supported To provide a high-quality person-centred service which complies with the relevant Legislation and standards Be honest and learn from mistakes. To provide a high quality, comprehensive IT helpdesk service to the users of the IT network at all Trust sites Royal Surrey is a compassionate and collaborative acute and community Trust. Recognising that our 5,000 colleagues are our greatest strength, we offer a comprehensive health and wellbeing programme alongside a strong commitment to developing your career. Our diverse and welcoming Royal Surrey family ensures you feel valued from your initial interview and throughout your time with us. We are clinically led and provide joined-up care by bridging hospital and community services, alongside delivering regional specialist cancer care. Our main acute hospital site is in Guildford, with community sites at Milford, Haslemere and Cranleigh, and services delivered in patients’ homes across Guildford and Waverley. We work in partnership with Ashford & St Peter’s Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust through a collaborative Group Model, supporting joined-up services, workforce flexibility and development opportunities. The Care Quality Commission (CQC) has rated us as Outstanding. We are proud of our achievements and continue to invest in our people and infrastructure. To learn more about life at Royal Surrey, please watch our short video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R96pMboIYdo Adverts may close early, so you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible. The Digital Service Desk Analyst is the first point of contact between end users and the IT organisation. The analyst is responsible for recording the details of reported IT service issues and service requests, and working to either restore service as quickly as possible or alerting / escalating them to the appropriate specialist support groups. The position requires technical troubleshooting abilities and excellent customer service skills

items.desc: Job number MED06046 Faculties Faculty of Medicine Departments National Heart & Lung Institute Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £67,351 per annum Location/campus White City Campus - On site only Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 6 Dec 2026 About the role The British Heart Foundation Centre of Research Excellence (BHF CRE) at Imperial College London invites applications to its Transitional Fellowship Programme open to exceptional postdoctoral candidates with a basic science background. This two‑year fellowship is supporting transition to competitive external funding and emerging independence that will add value to Imperial’s cardiovascular research portfolio. We also welcome applications from researchers who already hold an external career development award and wish to combine it with this transitional fellowship as a relocation package. This is a fantastic opportunity to embark on a path to leadership with the support of world-leading research centre. The BHF CRE is based across Imperial College London’s Hammersmith and White City campuses and comprises four research themes that focus on: population cardiovascular health, the factors driving heart adaptation during disease development, endothelial resilience, developing personal monitors of cardiovascular health. Further information on the research themes: https://www.imperial.ac.uk/bhf-research-excellence/. Recruitment is open to expertise in all relevant areas including discovery science and molecular mechanisms of disease. The proposed research project will be hosted by one of our BHF CRE Principal Investigators and should be developed in liaison with your sponsor. Applicants must apply online via Imperial’s jobs website and include CV, research plan, statement on career intention, and a letter of support from a BHF CRE Principal Investigator confirming agreement to act as sponsor. What you would be doing With the support of your sponsor, you will develop applications for highly competitive Career Development Awards, generate preliminary data, and gain experience in award management. You will also have extensive opportunities to network with UK‑based and international leaders, enhancing your research profile and fostering collaborations. What we are looking for PhD (or equivalent) in cardiovascular research or related discipline and extensive postdoctoral experience. A proven track record of excellent academic research An ability to raise research funding from external sources, commensurate with your career stage. A strong interest in interdisciplinary working and translational research. Interest in widening participation and outreach activities. Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey ideas and concepts clearly and effectively to a range of audiences. "A proven track record of contributing to the wider academic and institutional community". What we can offer you Support for the Career Development Award applications to external funders, such as BHF, Wellcome Trust, MRC, BBSRC, UKRI Future Leader Fellowship. This includes extensive academic and administrative support throughout the application process and interview preparation. Networking opportunities with UK-based and international leaders in the cardiovascular fields. Access to sector-leading career development and mentoring programmes offered by Imperial College London as well as opportunities for promotion and progression. Access to cutting edge facilities at Imperial College London. Opportunities to attract students from undergraduate and postgraduate programmes at Imperial College London. Opportunities to develop teaching skills. Sector-leading remuneration package (including 41 days off a year and generous pension schemes) and access to local and national discounts through Imperial Perks at Work. Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing. Further information How to apply: Please upload the following documents with your application: CV Research plan statement on career intention A letter of support from a BHF CRE Principal Investigator confirming agreement to act as sponsor. For available sponsors, please refer to the investigator lists under each research theme: https://www.imperial.ac.uk/bhf-research-excellence/. Application deadline 06.12.2026 . Interviews will be held in January. The role is full‑time and fixed‑term for up to 24 months (12 months contract will be also considered). Appointment will be offered at either the Research Associate (£50,773 - £59,484) or Research Fellow (£57,075 - £64,619) level, depending on candidate’s experience. We also offer research consumable support depending on the specific requirements of the project. If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Dr. Magdalena Zak (m.zak1@imperial.ac.uk), manager of Imperial BHF CRE. items.desc: Our Values In line with our One Coventry Values, we want to ensure that our communities are represented across our workforce. A vital part of this is ensuring we are a truly inclusive organisation that encourages diversity in all respects, including diversity of thinking. We particularly welcome applicants from minority ethnic, LGBT+, disabled and neurodiverse communities to make a real difference to our residents so that equity and respect remains at the heart of everything we do. Our Values are: Open and fair: We are fair, open, and transparent. Nurture and develop: We help and encourage everyone to be their best and do their best. Engage and empower: We talk and listen to others, working together as one. Create and innovate: We embrace new ways of working to continuously improve. Own and be accountable: We work together to deliver the best services for our residents. Value and respect: We put diversity and inclusion at the heart of all we do. We value diverse perspectives and experiences and are striving to create a workplace culture that is inclusive, is accepting of all and is free from discrimination and bias. The Revenues Service is a large team of more than 60 people working together to collect £340 million of corporate revenue to help the Council provide vital services to Coventry residents. From council tax to business rates to invoices for stalls at the Godiva Festival, the team perform a range of roles to ensure we provide excellent services to residents and internal council departments and that ultimately, we maximise the collection of public funds. The revenue we collect ensures the council can provide services from bin collections to looking after our parks and green spaces to providing the best possible chances in life for our looked after children. Our team is uniquely placed within the council as we interact with every one of Coventry’s 140,000 residential properties and 9,000 commercial properties. Every resident and customer we deal with has a unique set of circumstances - our team challenge those who can pay and don’t pay – applying a range of legal remedies to compel people to pay what they owe. But the team also listen to and support those who can’t pay and help some of our most vulnerable residents find a way out of debt. What is the job role? This is an exciting opportunity for a highly motivated individual to join our Revenues & Benefits Systems Support Team. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting and developing the systems used across the Revenues & Benefits Service, with a particular focus on Housing Benefits. Working closely with operational teams, system suppliers and stakeholders, you will help ensure our systems remain effective, accurate and resilient in supporting service delivery. You will be responsible for investigating system and process issues, analysing data and reports, testing new functionality, supporting business processes and helping to identify opportunities for continuous improvement. Main duties will include, but are not limited to: Providing specialist support for the IT systems used within the Revenues & Benefits Service. Running and monitoring critical business processes to ensure systems remain operational and service objectives are met. Investigating system and process failures, identifying root causes and taking appropriate action to resolve or escalate issues. Analysing system data, reports and outputs to identify issues, trends and opportunities for service improvement. Testing new functionality, system upgrades and legislative changes to ensure changes meet business requirements before implementation. Working with operational teams, ICT colleagues and software suppliers to diagnose, track and resolve system-related issues. Conducting audit checks on batch processing, system outputs and financial reconciliations to ensure data integrity and accuracy. This post is exempted under the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 and as such appointment to this post will be conditional upon the receipt of a satisfactory response to a check of police records via Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS). All candidates must have the Right to Work in the UK. We are currently not offering sponsorship for this role. Who are we looking for? We are looking for an individual with recent experience working within a Revenues and Benefits service and a strong understanding of Housing Benefit legislation and administration. The successful candidate will have excellent analytical and problem-solving skills and be confident using systems, reports, spreadsheets and data analysis techniques to investigate issues and support service improvement. You will be able to work independently and as part of a team, prioritising workloads effectively while maintaining a high level of accuracy and attention to detail. You should be able to communicate effectively with a wide range of audiences, explaining technical information clearly and managing stakeholder expectations …

items.desc: Power Electronics Engineer - KTP Associate Location Cambridge, England, United Kingdom Date posted October 23, 2026 Job ID 23558 Our Opening and Your Responsibilities We have an exciting opportunity for a Power Electronics Engineer to work with the University of Sheffield and METTLER TOLEDO Safeline X-ray (SLXR) on a Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) to develop next generation high voltage generators for X-ray inspection machines. In this role, you will design, implement, and test digitally controlled power electronic systems, such as power factor correctors and high voltage inverters, to enhance X-ray generator performance. You will lead the project and work closely with METTLER TOLEDO engineers to support product development and commercialization efforts. Although you will be employed by the University of Sheffield, you will be predominantly based at METTLER TOLEDO Safeline X-ray’s office in Royston, Hertfordshire and may be required to work from Sheffield occasionally. You will need to apply via the University website: Power Electronics Engineer Job Details | University of Sheffield Main Responsibilities Develop a power supply subsystem for an X-ray inspection machine. Explore and analyse existing solutions, determining areas for improvement. Develop, simulate, implement and test power electronic conversion circuits. Assist in the development of closed-loop controller for power electronics circuits. Develop suitable and safe testing methods for effective testing of various high voltage subsystems. Lead the project, monitor milestones and produce technical documents as required. Work with SLXR and the university to identify and protect intellectual property and work with commercial partners. Work within an existing agile scrum project management framework. Participate in regular project meetings with Mettler Toledo Safeline X-ray and the university. Plan your own workload to ensure the overall project milestones and objectives are met on time. Engage fully with the requirements of the knowledge transfer partnership scheme, including personal development and reporting. Work across multiple sites, including at Mettler Toledo Safeline X-ray and the University of Sheffield. Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post. What You Need to Succeed Have at least a Master's degree (PhD is desirable) or have equivalent experience in electronic, electrical or control engineering (assessed at application) Experience in designing, constructing and experimental testing of power electronic systems (assessed at application/interview) Experience with analogue/digital control for power electronics systems (assessed at application/interview) Experience of using computer-aided engineering including PCB design, schematic capture, embedded programming and circuit simulation (assessed at application/interview) Evidence of working effectively in a team and presenting findings to a wide range of audiences (assessed at application/interview) Ability to plan own workload and prioritise conflicting deadlines. (assessed at application/interview) Ability to make decisions and apply creative approaches to solving complex technical problems (assessed at application/interview) Appreciation of the commercial implications of decisions, particularly for costs (assessed at application/interview) Willingness to be based in Royston, Hertfordshire but regularly visit Sheffield (assessed at application) Have not previously worked on and completed an Innovate UK-funded KTP project (assessed at application) The University is offering: Salary: £42,000 - £55,000 depending on experience.
