Mobile Architecture & Development: Build and evolve screens and user flows in React Native using TypeScript, ensuring clean architecture, and solid performance across devices. API & Service Design: Design and build, and maintain RESTful APIs and decoupled services in .NET (C#), establishing reliable integration contracts and robust throughput. Shift-Left Culture & Quality: Own code quality across both layers. Write and maintain unit, integration, and E2E tests, ensuring software reaches production with maximum stability and confidence. Direct Collaboration with Discovery: Partner directly with our Product Designer and Product Data Analyst without relying on managers as bridges. Continuous Delivery & Vertical Slicing: Break down complex epics into small, functional slices supported by feature flags, maintaining a steady, predictable delivery pace across parallel products. Your Profile Solid Experience with React Native & TypeScript: At least 3 - 4 years designing, developing, and maintaining production-grade mobile applications for iOS and Android. Backend & API Development Expertise: Proven hands-on experience designing, building, and integrating RESTful APIs and backend services, preferably in C# / .NET. Automated Testing Across the Stack: Practical experience with unit and integration testing frameworks (Jest, xUnit/NUnit). Technical Pragmatism (KISS / YAGNI): Balanced judgment between clean, extensible architecture and delivering fast, iterative business value without over-engineering. Assertive Technical Communication: Ability to articulate technical decisions with data, defend estimations constructively, and participate comfortably in technical debates Nice-to-Have: Experience with event-driven architectures and message brokers (NATS, Kafka, or RabbitMQ). Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, or cloud deployment environments. Knowledge of Infrastructure as Code (IaC) technologies. Hands-on experience working with shared design systems and component libraries. Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, Fastlane). Understanding of observability, tracing, and metric visualization (Prometheus, Grafana). Practical familiarity with Xcode and Android Studio, a clear understanding of the native bridge / NitroModules, and native integration.

items.desc: About the role We are looking for a hands-on Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) Architect to help develop a credit analytics platform for a regulated financial-services business operating in the UK and Ireland. The platform brings together lending and servicing data to support portfolio analysis, credit-risk modelling and better business decisions. Current work covers probability of default, redemption and prepayment, expected credit loss, and interactive analytics. The next challenge is to turn this work into a reliable, maintainable platform that can support different portfolios and client needs. You will work directly with the client’s business and technology teams, alongside a credit-domain and modelling lead and other engineers. You will own the engineering architecture, contribute production code, and help the team decide what to build and how to deliver it. We need someone who can question assumptions, propose simpler alternatives and explain technical trade-offs clearly. What you will do Translate business problems into an architecture, practical delivery plan and clear acceptance criteria. Identify gaps in requirements, data and dependencies before they become delivery problems. Design the path from working models and dashboards to a production-ready ML platform. Make deliberate choices about shared components, portfolio-specific configuration, model calibration and future client onboarding. Build and improve reproducible workflows for data preparation, feature engineering, training, validation, scoring and deployment. Establish clear versioning for code, data, models and calibration logic. Work with the modelling lead on how probability of default, prepayment, lifetime risk and loss estimates are calculated, tested and exposed to applications. Keep business definitions consistent across models, tables and dashboards. Strengthen the data foundation: trace results to source, investigate data-quality issues, document assumptions and build automated checks around important transformations. Improve the reliability of the Snowflake-backed analytics application, including deployment, testing, permissions and integration with model outputs. Put appropriate MLOps practices in place, including repeatable releases, monitoring, failure handling, rollback and operational documentation. Design for privacy, access control, auditability and model governance. Work with domain experts to make validation, stability and fairness checks practical and reviewable. Lead technical discussions, review code, unblock engineers and keep the client informed about progress, risks and architectural decisions. Assess where natural-language or LLM-assisted analytics would add value, without losing focus on trustworthy data, robust models and useful products. What we are looking for A track record of designing and delivering production data or ML systems, with ownership extending beyond prototypes and architecture diagrams. Strong hands-on Python and SQL. You should be comfortable investigating a dataset, reviewing modelling code and implementing critical parts of the solution yourself. Practical MLOps experience: reproducible pipelines, model and data versioning, testing, deployment, monitoring and the operational consequences of model updates. Experience with cloud data platforms and modern warehouses. Snowflake experience is particularly relevant; you should be able to reason about data access, performance, cost and deployment constraints. An understanding of model evaluation, calibration, data leakage, changing populations and the difference between model quality and system reliability. The ability to work through incomplete documentation and inconsistent business definitions, and turn findings into maintainable code and clear documentation. Strong client-facing communication in English. You can explain trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders, constructively challenge a requirement and take responsibility for the resulting decision. Experience leading a small technical team while remaining actively involved in implementation. Useful additional experience Credit-risk, lending or servicing analytics, including PD, LGD, ECL, prepayment or portfolio stress testing. Regulated financial-services delivery and model governance. Streamlit, Azure ML, semantic data layers or analytics applications built on Snowflake. Configurable ML products serving multiple portfolios or clients. Evaluated natural-language analytics, text-to-SQL or LLM-assisted workflows. Current technical environment Snowflake, SQL, Python, Streamlit and an Azure ML environment. The team also uses AI-assisted development tools. You will help evolve the architecture based on the product’s needs rather than introduce a predetermined stack. What we would like to discuss A production ML or analytics system you personally helped build, including the architecture decisions and code you owned. How you would adapt a model and its calibration for a new portfolio while …

items.desc: Luleå Referensnummer 5512–2026 Vill du utveckla din forskning och undervisning i en miljö där samverkan med industri och samhälle är en självklarhet? Hos oss får du arbeta med engagerade kollegor, tillgång till modern forskningsinfrastruktur och goda möjligheter att attrahera extern finansiering. Du ges utrymme att göra verklig skillnad för dina studenter, din forskning och samhället i stort. Robotics & AI Group vid Luleå tekniska universitet söker en amanuens med fokus på hårdvaru- och mjukvaruutveckling för autonoma robotar. Robotics & AI-gruppen är involverad i många fältorienterade projekt, vilket kräver en mångsidig och proaktiv person som trivs i en miljö med högt tempo. Vill du kombinera dina studier med ett givande arbete inom akademin? Robotics & AI Group söker en eller flera studenter som vill arbeta som undervisningsamanuens (teacher assistant) som stöd till vår undervisande personal. Vi erbjuder Luleå tekniska universitet är en statlig myndighet och erbjuder goda anställningsvillkor. Med en anställning som amanuens får du som student möjlighet att förena studier med arbete för att komplettera dina teoretiska kunskaper med praktisk arbetslivserfarenhet. Arbetsuppgifter Arbetsuppgifterna varierar och ger inblick i den akademiska världen. Du kommer att ha löpande kontakt med kursansvariga lärare. Exempel på arbetsuppgifter: Samarbeta med forskare från RAI-teamet som bedriver grundläggande och principiell forskning inom alla aspekter av robotik Undervisningsstöd inom grundutbildning (handledning av laborationer och övningar) Rättning av rapporter, inlämningar och laborationer Kompetens och erfarenhet För att vara behörig för tjänsten måste du vara inskriven som student vid ett universitetsprogram inom tillämpad artificiell intelligent eller närliggande område och ha bakgrund inom robotik. Du behöver vara intresserad av att utveckla navigeringsalgoritmer för autonoma fordon inom ostrukturerade komplexa områden med störningar i form av miljöfaktorer. Du måste också ha erfarenhet av programmering med Python, C++ och MATLAB med fokus på datorseende. Eftersom en del av arbetsuppgifterna är att kommunicera resultaten på engelska med kollegor och forskningspartners måste du kunna uttrycka dig både muntligt och skriftligt på engelska. Du behöver också kunna ta egna initiativ och arbeta självständigt. Villkor Anställningen regleras enligt Högskoleförordningen (HF 5 kap §10). Du måste vara aktiv student under hela anställningstiden. Anställningen får motsvara högst 50 % av heltid. En anställning kan ske på högst ett år i taget, dock sammanlagt högst tre år. Timlön/ersättning För alla uppdrag får du timlön samt värdefull arbetslivserfarenhet för ditt CV. Timlön beroende på arbetsuppgiftens svårighetsgrad: Nivå 1: 156 kr/timme (motsvarar ca 25 700 kr/månad vid heltidsarbete). Nivå 2: 171 kr/timme (motsvarar ca 28 200 kr/månad vid heltidsarbete). Information Tjänsten omfattar 25 % av heltid, dvs. i genomsnitt 1,25 dagar i veckan under 6 månader, från den 01/11/2026 till den 31/05/2027 eller enligt överenskommelse. Tjänstgöringsort är Luleå Arbetsbelastningen kan komma att variera över tid och enligt överenskommelse men målsättningen är att den fördelas på ett sätt som gör det förenligt med studier vid universitetet. För ytterligare information är du välkommen att kontakta: Dr. Anton Koval, 0920-49 2381, anton.koval@ltu.se Fackliga kontaktpersoner Ansökan Vi ser helst att du söker befattningen via ansökningsknappen nedan där du bifogar personligt brev samt CV/meritförteckning och kopior av verifierade examensbevis. Var vänlig och märk din ansökan med referensnumret nedan. Både ansökan och examensbevis ska vara skrivna på svenska eller engelska. Om jobbet Som Platform Engineer till vårt team på Länsförsäkringar AB i Stockholm får du en central roll i vår växande platform engineering-funktion. Du arbetar med drift, utveckling och automation av vår containerplattform byggd på OpenShift och säkerställer en stabil och effektiv plattform för utvecklingsteam och applikationsdrift. Du blir en del av ett kompetent och positivt team som driver innovation och utveckling inom containerplattformar, där du får arbeta med moderna verktyg och har goda möjligheter att utvecklas. Du kommer ingå i ett team med med produktägare, arkitekter och andra platform engineers där du rapporterar till chefen för Public Cloud Platforms. Ni har fokus på OpenShift/Azure RedHat OpenShift, Azure och AWS. Enheten Digital & IT inom Länsförsäkringar AB levererar förstklassiga IT-lösningar och digitala tjänster till de lokala Länsförsäkringsbolagen, vilket innebär breda kontaktytor inom hela LF-federationen. Dina arbetsuppgifter kommer vara bland annat: Underhålla och vidareutveckla vår Kubernetes/OpenShift-baserade containerplattform. Arbeta med CI/CD-pipelines och GitOps för att förenkla och automatisera deployment och drift. Samarbeta med utvecklare och arkitekter för att optimera plattformens prestanda och säkerhet. Stötta med expertis i incident- och felsökningsarbete. Arbeta med onboarding och utbildning av våra DevOps-team för att säkerställa att de effektivt kan använda plattformen. Vi har riktigt bra förmåner Personalvillkor på bolån och blancolån Rabatt på sak-, person- och djurförsäkring Friskvårdsbidrag och friskvårdstimma Gym & gruppträning på kontoret Lunchförmån Fyra extra lediga dagar/år utöver semesterdagarna Kvalifikationer Följande kommer göra dig framgångsrik i denna tjänst: Erfaren hands-on Kubernetes-expert med minst 3 års erfarenhet av Kubernetes och containerorkestrering, gärna inom finanssektorn. Tidigare erfarenhet av att arbeta i gränslandet mellan infrastruktur, utveckling, säkerhet och cloud native-teknik. Kunskap om CI/CD-pipelines, GitOps och automation. Erfarenhet av att arbeta i Microsoft Azure. Grundläggande förståelse för nätverk, lagring och säkerhet i Kubernetes-miljöer. Goda kunskaper i svenska och engelska, både tal och skrift. Meriterande är även om du har: Du har kompetens på AWS plattformar. Som person är du positiv, initiativtagande och självgående, samtidigt som du är en god team-player. Du är lösningsorienterad, ansvarstagande och nyfiken, med en stark vilja att automatisera och förbättra arbetsflöden. Du trivs med att arbeta både självständigt och i team, och har god kommunikativ och samarbetsinriktad förmåga. Kontaktuppgifter: Rekryterande chef: Klaus Seidel, klaus.seidel@lansforsakringar.se Facklig representant Forena: Jessica Lööw, jessica.loow@lansforsakringar.se Facklig representant Akademikerföreningen: Lisa-Maria Carensjö, lisa-maria.carensjo@lansforsakringar.se Låter det spännande? Då vill vi veta mer om dig! Välkommen med din ansökan redan idag. Vi arbetar löpande med denna rekrytering och kan komma att tillsätta tjänsten innan sista ansökningsdag. Om företaget Länsförsäkringar AB är en inkluderande arbetsplats där mod, möjligheter och engagemang står i centrum. Vi erbjuder ett hållbart arbetsliv med flexibla villkor och satsar på att alla medarbetare ska kunna växa och trivas, oavsett bakgrund. Digital & IT är hjärtat i Länsförsäkringsgruppens digitala utveckling. Vi driver den gemensamma digitala transformationen och levererar förstklassiga IT-lösningar, datadrivna insikter och innovativa digitala tjänster som skapar värde för hela verksamheten. Vårt uppdrag är att bygga en robust och framtidssäker IT-miljö – både på plats och i molnet – som möjliggör kundnära och effektiva affärer i hela gruppen. Hos oss möts teknik, affär och innovation. Vi arbetar tvärfunktionellt ute i verksamheten i agila team där utveckling, drift och strategi går hand i hand. Vi ansvarar för allt från IT-styrning, enterprisearkitektur och leverantörshantering till applikationsutveckling, cybersäkerhet och verksamhetsberedskap. Klaus Seidel | Kontaktperson

items.desc: Lead the development and growth of our Vulnerable Children and Families activity, working with charity leaders to strengthen their organisations and maximise their impact. Venture Partners are at the core of Purposeful Ventures' work. They bring the knowledge, skills and experience needed to help shape our portfolios, identify opportunities for investment and support the organisations we work with to thrive. In this role, you will help shape the future of our Vulnerable Children and Families work, leading the review and development of our strategy and identifying where Purposeful Ventures can make the greatest difference. You will develop new opportunities and partnerships, work closely with our Philanthropy team to attract and direct funding to charity partners, and support and monitor the progress and impact of the organisations we work with. Alongside this, you will contribute to the broader work of our Venture Partners, working closely with charity leaders to strengthen their organisations, develop effective strategies and build the capabilities needed to bring about change. We are looking for a Venture Partner with a deep understanding of the challenges facing vulnerable children and families, and experience of working to address them. We welcome candidates who have developed their expertise in a range of settings, including working in a charity, delivering services, shaping government policy, working within children's social care or making funding and investment decisions related to the sector. What matters most is your ability to draw on this knowledge and experience, exercise sound judgement and work with others to bring about meaningful change for children and families. We are particularly interested in candidates who can combine their sector expertise with strong strategic and analytical skills, experience of leading projects or organisations, and the ability to build trusted relationships and work collaboratively to deliver impact. More information on our broader Children and Families portfolio Our ambition is for every child to grow up in a safe, stable and supportive environment, with the relationships and opportunities they need to thrive. Du ansvarar för att analysera, strukturera och dokumentera verksamhetsbehov samt funktionella och icke-funktionella IT-krav inom bland annat trafiknära system, fordonssystem, integrationer och IT-säkerhet. Ta fram kravspecifikationer, kravbilagor och utvärderingskriterier för IT-upphandlingar enligt LOU/LUF. Planera och leda workshops och intervjuer för kravinsamling och förankring. Arbeta med kravställning inom trafiknära system, fordonssystem, integrationer och IT-säkerhet. Samverka med verksamhet, IT och leverantörer samt säkerställa spårbarhet från krav till test och införande. items.desc: Solna Referensnummer 2026/064759 På Arbetsmiljöverket jobbar vi tillsammans för att ingen ska bli sjuk, skadas eller dö av jobbet. Därför hjälper vi arbetsgivare att uppfylla de krav som finns och informerar om hur arbetsmiljöarbetet blir en naturlig del av vardagen. Med arbetsmiljölagen som grund tar vi fram regler, inspekterar arbetsplatser och sprider kunskap om arbetsmiljöfrågor. Uppdraget är allvarligt men vår vardag präglas av arbetsglädje och vi är omtänksamma och hjälpsamma kollegor. Om sektionen IT-enheten på arbetsmiljöverket består av fyra sektioner, Digitalisering, IT-utveckling, Infrastruktur och Helpdesk. Tillsammans arbetar dessa fyra sektioner för att tillhandahålla stabila och innovativa tekniska lösningar som stödjer både daglig drift och vår långsiktiga utveckling. Vårt mål är att bygga en organisation som klarar av att växa med fler utvecklarteam och stärka vår kompetens inom utveckling och modernisering. Sektionen för IT-utveckling består idag av 12 medarbetare fördelade på tre agila team som ansvarar för utveckling och leveranser av främst våra egenutvecklade applikationer och tjänster. Ditt nya jobb Som vikarierande systemutvecklare kommer du erbjudas ett stimulerande arbete i en kunskapsintensiv organisation. Du blir en del av ett team som arbetar med systemutveckling och förvaltning av Arbetsmiljöverkets egenutvecklade system, främst .Net baserade webbapplikationer och API:er. Som systemutvecklare arbetar du från krav till release och med hela teknikstacken. Du kommer medverka till att förvaltning och utveckling av våra system drivs framåt. Rollen bidrar till myndighetens digitaliseringsresa där vi nu satsar mycket på IT för att stärka våra digitala tjänster, öka tillgänglighet av data och använda oss av AI för att förbättra och effektivisera verksamhetens flöden. Gemensamt driver vi utvecklingen där hög ambition och tydliga mål präglar vårt arbete. Din bakgrund Rollen kräver att du har: Eftergymnasial utbildning inom system-, information- eller datavetenskap, alternativt motsvarande kunskaper förvärvade genom arbetslivserfarenhet som vi bedömer som likvärdiga. Minst 2 års aktuell erfarenhet av systemutveckling inom C# och .Net. Goda kunskaper och erfarenhet av frontend-utveckling i React, CSS och HTML. Goda kunskaper och erfarenhet av databaser och SQL. Goda kunskaper och erfarenhet av REST-API:er. God förmåga att kommunicera på svenska och engelska i tal och skrift. Det är meriterande om du har: Erfarenhet av att arbeta i agila team. Erfarenhet av CI/CD och Azure DevOps. Goda kunskaper och erfarenhet av kvalitetssäkring och testning. Som person ser vi att du kommer att trivas i rollen om du fokuserar på att nå uppsatta mål och trivs med att utvecklas. Du tar egna initiativ inom ditt arbetsområde och är snabb på att respondera på kundbehov. Vidare ser vi att du kan självständigt lösa problem och har förmågan att hantera oväntade händelser på ett flexibelt sätt. Du samarbetar bra och bidrar till ett positivt arbetsklimat. Vid urvalet kommer vi att lägga stor vikt vid dina personliga egenskaper. En anställning hos oss kan innebära att befattningen placeras i säkerhetsklass. Säkerhetsprövning med eller utan registerkontroll kan därför komma att göras före beslut om anställning. För en del av våra arbetsuppgifter i säkerhetsklass krävs svenskt medborgarskap. Säkerhetsprövning genomförs enligt Säkerhetsskyddslagen (2018:585). Vad vi erbjuder dig Arbetsmiljöverket är en trygg arbetsgivare och en myndighet som hela tiden förändras med samhället vi verkar i. Vi är stolta över att få använda vår kunskap och vårt förtroende i vårt viktiga samhällsuppdrag. Tillsammans skapar vi en inkluderande kultur, som rymmer hjärta, mod och hjärna. Hos oss blir hela du en viktig del i något större. Anställningen är ett vikariat, på heltid i cirka 11 månader och är för närvarande placerad på vårt kontor i Solna. Vi tillämpar individuell lönesättning. Vi strävar efter att alla medarbetare ska ha en hållbar arbetsmiljö och en balans mellan jobb och fritid. Därför har vi flexibla arbetstider eller tillämpar förtroendearbetstid och ger möjlighet till distansarbete där verksamheten så tillåter. Så rekryterar vi Vi använder kompetensbaserad rekrytering, både för att kvalitetssäkra rekryteringen och för att motverka diskriminering. Vi ber dig därför att endast bifoga ett CV, och svara på några frågor istället för ett personligt brev när du registrerar din an. Eftersom vi arbetar kompetensbaserat använder vi oss också av arbetspsykologiska tester i den här rekryteringen. Intervjuer sker från vecka 48. För oss är det viktigt att rekryteringsprocessen är ömsesidig. Tveka inte att höra av dig om du har några frågor. Fackliga kontaktpersoner är Adam Jansson för Saco, Marianne Martin för ST samt Jenny Bengtsson för Seko. Samtliga nås via Arbetsmiljöverkets växel: 010-730 90 00. Vill du jobba tillsammans med oss för att ingen ska bli sjuk, skadas eller dö av jobbet? Välkommen med din an senast den 4 november 2026 ! …

Teamet arbetar i hela kedjan från krav, design till utveckling, förvaltning och drift. Tillsammans med teamet kommer du upprätthålla en hög leveransförmåga och kontinuerligt leverera nytta till användare och tågresenärer. Våra team består av flera roller och kompetenser som samarbetar i ett agilt arbetssätt. I teamen jobbar vi ständigt med att utveckla och förbättra vårt arbetssätt. Du blir en del av kittet mellan IT och Verksamheten och får en unik förståelse för båda delarna. Med ett nyfiket sinne och en förmåga att våga tänka utanför ramarna medverkar du dagligen till att förbättra det svenska transportsystemet." Vad kan vi erbjuda dig? items.desc: TIKK TAKK söker en systemutvecklare inom Java och Angular för ett konsultuppdrag hos en större statlig myndighet i Gävle. Du blir en del av ett agilt utvecklingsteam som utvecklar och förvaltar applikationer där fokus ligger på att skapa värde för myndigheten och för medborgarna. Teamet arbetar i högt tempo och i nära samarbete med verksamheten. Här arbetar anställda och konsulter tillsammans, och teamet värdesätter kvalitet, noggrannhet och helhetstänk. Rollen passar dig som är trygg i både backend och frontend, gillar att dela med dig av dina erfarenheter och vill fortsätta utvecklas tillsammans med andra. Om rollen Du deltar i alla delar av utvecklingsarbetet, från backend i Spring och Java till frontend i Angular och automatiserad testning. Vissa av teamets applikationer är verksamhetskritiska, vilket innebär att arbete utanför ordinarie kontorstid kan förekomma ibland. Kompetensöverföring sker löpande inom teamet. Uppdraget kan även komma att omfatta arbete i ett annat team inom myndighetens systemutveckling. Dina arbetsuppgifter omfattar att: - Utveckla och vidareutveckla backend i Spring och Java. - Utveckla och vidareutveckla frontend i Angular. - Ta fram och underhålla automatiserade tester. Arbeta agilt i nära samarbete med verksamheten och övriga i teamet. - Bidra till hög kvalitet och ett helhetstänk i teamets leveranser. - Dela med dig av dina erfarenheter och bidra till löpande kompetensöverföring i teamet. Arbetsuppgifterna kan utvecklas utifrån verksamhetens behov och din kompetens. Vi söker dig som har - Erfarenhet av backendutveckling i Spring med Java. - Erfarenhet av frontendutveckling i Angular. - Erfarenhet av automatiserad testning. - Övergripande förståelse för relationsdatabaser. Förmåga att arbeta självgående och ta ansvar för din egen kompetensutveckling, samtidigt som du bidrar till teamets. Du behöver kunna arbeta på plats i Gävle minst en dag i veckan. Övrig tid är distansarbete möjligt. Uppdraget är säkerhetsklassat. Det innebär att du behöver vara svensk medborgare och att säkerhetsprövning med registerkontroll genomförs innan uppdraget startar. Meriterande erfarenhet Det är ett plus om du har arbetat med något av följande: - Automatiserad gränssnittstestning med Selenium. - Handläggningsstöd inom fastighetsinskrivning. Som person Du är prestigelös och kan både ge och ta emot kritik på ett konstruktivt sätt. Du är strukturerad och ordningsam, tar ansvar för din egen utveckling och bidrar gärna till att hela teamet utvecklas. Du arbetar självgående men trivs i ett nära samarbete med kollegor och verksamhet. Om uppdraget Plats: Gävle, minst en dag i veckan på plats och övrig tid med möjlighet till distansarbete Omfattning: Heltid, 100 procent Antal tjänster: En Planerad start: Slutet av mars 2027 Uppdragsperiod: Till och med 31 mars 2028, med möjlighet till förlängning upp till tre år Ansökan Skicka ett uppdaterat CV och en kort motivering till varför du passar för uppdraget. Beskriv hur du uppfyller varje krav, med antal år av erfarenhet av Java och Spring respektive Angular, och ange när du kan börja. Urval sker löpande. Ansök snarast, senast den 25 oktober 2026.

items.desc: Who we are and what we do: Viedoc is a Swedish medtech company offering a clinical trials platform. It supports clinical studies in over 100 countries and is trusted by some of the largest pharmaceutical companies in the world. Our cloud-based platform holds sensitive medical data for millions of patients, so security and reliability come first. As a Platform Engineer, you’ll help shape how the platform is built and operated, at a time when we’re actively evolving it. Your team owns the infrastructure and works closely with teams across the company. If you want to work on critical infrastructure that helps bring new treatments to patients faster, we’d love to have you on the team! What you’ll do: You’ll own the database infrastructure behind our product, from availability and access to performance, and help us run it as code. We’re moving from a traditional ops setup toward modern platform engineering and SRE practices, so you’ll help design the new infrastructure, not just maintain what’s already there. We’re an enabling team that builds and runs our infrastructure in Azure, from landing zones and governance to containers, networking and security, giving our developers and data teams a secure, reliable platform to build on. We work in an agile way, often pair up to solve problems, and AI is a natural part of our daily work. What your day-to-day could look like: Manage our MySQL, PostgreSQL and Redis databases, from high availability to disaster recovery Keep the database platform secure, audit-ready and performant, together with our developers Enable our new data warehouse team with the infrastructure, access and pipelines they build on Build infrastructure as code, CI/CD pipelines and automation Contribute to Azure governance and landing zone architecture Work across the wider platform, from containers to networking and security Our current tech stack: Azure, Bicep, Azure DevOps/GitHub, PowerShell, MySQL/PostgreSQL, Azure Managed Redis, AI assistants Who you are: You’ve got a strong background as a DBA or in a similar role You have hands-on experience with Redis or another in-memory data store You have experience with scripting, ideally PowerShell You have a doer mindset, enjoy teamwork and share what you learn You’re fluent in English Bonus if you have: Experience with Azure in production environments Working knowledge of infrastructure as code, ideally Bicep Experience with CI/CD pipelines, ideally in Azure DevOps or GitHub Don’t tick every box? Apply anyway. We care more about a strong database foundation and curiosity than a perfect match. Why Viedoc: Work on infrastructure supporting clinical research globally Close relationship with Microsoft, to ensure we adapt both modern and best practices Flat organization where engineers influence the platform’s direction Hackathons and an annual education budget Central office in Uppsala (Juvelen) and a hybrid work setup Interested? Apply by November 9th. We review applications on a rolling basis, so the position may be filled before the closing date. We are currently not able to support relocation for this role.

items.desc: Systems Engineering / Storage Engineer 80%-100%, Lugano, fixed-term The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) develops and operates cutting-edge, High-Performance Computing (HPC) systems as an essential service facility for science. The centre enables world-class research through its scientific user lab, which is available to domestic and international researchers in academia, industry, and the business sector. The centre is operated by ETH Zurich and has offices in Lugano (headquarter) and Zurich. Project background With the convergence of HPC and cloud technology, supercomputing service providers like CSCS strive to improve our service portfolios that focus on large, complex, and diverse scientific and engineering applications. Effectively providing performant and capable storage systems supporting the needs of HPC platforms running on a multi-tenant infrastructure is complex and challenging engineering work. To support these efforts, CSCS is seeking a Storage Engineer (Systems Engineering) to join our team in Lugano. The position is initially offered on a two-year contract, with the possibility of extension. This position is funded by a project that will enable scientists to benefit from large scale climate and earth observation data, and will involve collaboration with partners such as the ETHZ Geolab and C2SM, as well as international partners such as ECMWF, NASA and NOAA. Job description The main goal of this position is to implement and operate HPC storage services in a multi-tenant infrastructure. As a Storage Engineer you will directly contribute to the designing, implementation, maintenance, and documentation of storage services for HPC. Your contributions will directly impact the development and enhancement of HPC systems, thereby enhancing overall system functionality and efficiency. Profile You have a sound knowledge of Linux administration skills Generic filesystem aspects and functions (data, metadata, block-size etc.) Storage redundancy technologies (RAID, D-RAID, EC etc.) Backup solutions (DMF, TSM, Veeam) and backup concepts Object Storage concepts and S3 service usage/implementation Automation tools and framework, including CI/CD processes and ecosystem (e.g., Gitlab CI, HashiCorp Vault) Experience with the following is preferred, though there will be ample opportunities to learn and gain more experience with all of these skills on the job: Experience with parallel file systems (GPFS, Lustre) Experience with Ceph Storage Clusters Experience with versioning systems and CI/CD workflows such as ArgoCD Experience with physical servers automated installation systems such as OpenCHAMI, MAAS, or Foreman Experience with developing Ansible configurations Experience developing services on top of Kubernetes You should have a bachelor’s or higher degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Workplace Workplace We offer In an organization that values autonomy, ownership and continuous learning, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to gain specialized hands-on experience through activities characterized by the challenging aspects typical of the HPC field. Our core values as guiding principles: Curiosity: You enjoy learning, exploring new ideas, and understanding problems deeply. Openness: You listen, collaborate, and are receptive to different perspectives. Courage: You tackle challenging or ambiguous problems and are willing to take initiative. Supportiveness: You help colleagues and users succeed and contribute to a positive team culture. Integrity: You act honestly, ethically, and reliably in your work. Our culture and benefits: We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive engineering team and particularly encourage applications from from groups underrepresented in tech. If you are technically strong, curious, and eager to grow, we want to hear from you. At CSCS, being family-friendly is much more than a label. We provide flexible and supportive working conditions that help employees manage both their careers and family responsibilities. For example, one of our Lugano buildings hosts a childcare facility, and we financially support up to three weeks of summer camp for primary school children. If your child is sick and you need assistance, we will even cover the cost of in-home childcare for our Lugano based employees. We are proud to be a genuinely family-friendly employer and are committed to supporting our employees when they need it most. You can look forward to an exciting working environment, cultural diversity and attractive offers and benefits. items.desc: WSL-Institut für Schnee- und Lawinenforschung SLF Das WSL-Institut für Schnee- und Lawinenforschung SLF gehört zur Eidg. Forschungsanstalt WSL und damit zum ETH-Bereich. Die WSL befasst sich mit der nachhaltigen Nutzung und dem Schutz der Umwelt sowie mit einem verantwortungsvollen Umgang mit Naturgefahren. Sie beschäftigt rund 600 Mitarbeitende, davon 180 am SLF in Davos. Die Gruppen Lawinenwarnung und Warn- und Informationssysteme, welche Teil der Forschungseinheit Lawinen und Prävention sind, suchen auf Anfang 2027 oder nach Vereinbarung einen Data Engineer 80-100% (w/m/d) Im SNF-Forschungsprojekt THIRST (Towards high-resolution, intelligent, spatio-temporal avalanche forecasting) entwickeln wir neue Methoden, um die Lawinengefahr mithilfe physikalischer Modelle, künstlicher Intelligenz und räumlich hochaufgelöster Daten künftig präziser und automatisierter vorherzusagen. Dafür suchen wir eine Person, die eine skalierbare Simulations- und Dateninfrastruktur aufbaut, um grossräumige Modellrechnungen und den effizienten Zugriff auf umfangreiche Forschungsdaten zu ermöglichen. Gleichzeitig sollen automatisierte und zuverlässige Daten- und Modellpipelines für das Testen neuer Methoden entwickelt werden, welche auch die technische Grundlage für deren spätere Überführung in den operationellen Lawinenwarndienst legen sollen. Zu Ihren Aufgaben gehören der Aufbau, Betrieb und die Weiterentwicklung einer skalierbaren Simulations- und Dateninfrastruktur für grossräumige, rechenintensive Modellierungen sowie die Entwicklung effizienter Lösungen zur Verarbeitung, Speicherung und Bereitstellung grosser räumlich-zeitlicher Datensätze. Sie entwickeln robuste und automatisierte Daten- und Modellpipelines für Forschung und operationelle Live-Tests und stellen mit Testing, Monitoring und Qualitätssicherung einen zuverlässigen und reproduzierbaren Modellbetrieb sicher. Ein weiterer Schwerpunkt liegt auf dem Aufbau und Betrieb von MLOps-Prozessen für das automatisierte Training und Re-Training, das Deployment und die Inferenz von Machine-Learning-Modellen sowie deren Verwaltung und Monitoring. Dabei arbeiten Sie eng mit Forschenden und Softwareentwickelnden zusammen, um neue wissenschaftliche Methoden so weiterzuentwickeln und technisch umzusetzen, dass sie für einen späteren operationellen Einsatz vorbereitet sind. Sie verfügen über einen Hochschulabschluss in Informatik, Computational Science, Data Engineering oder einem verwandten Fachgebiet und bringen fundierte Programmiererfahrung, insbesondere mit Python, mit. Sie sind mit Linux-basierten Entwicklungsumgebungen vertraut und haben idealerweise bereits mit Technologien wie Kubernetes gearbeitet. Erfahrung im Aufbau und Betrieb skalierbarer Daten- und Computing-Infrastrukturen, vorzugsweise im wissenschaftlichen Umfeld, ist ebenso erwünscht wie Kenntnisse moderner Software-Engineering-Praktiken, darunter Versionskontrolle, automatisiertes Testing, CI/CD und Containerisierung. Erfahrung mit paralleler Datenverarbeitung, HPC oder dem Betrieb rechenintensiver Modelle ist von Vorteil. Sie interessieren sich für die Zusammenarbeit mit Forschenden und dafür, wissenschaftliche Methoden in robuste und zuverlässige Anwendungen zu überführen. Eine selbstständige und strukturierte Arbeitsweise, Teamfähigkeit sowie gute Kommunikationsfähigkeiten runden Ihr Profil ab. Gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse werden vorausgesetzt; Interesse an Schnee und Lawinen ist von Vorteil. Die Stelle ist zunächst auf zwei Jahre befristet, mit Aussicht auf Verlängerung. Bitte richten Sie Ihre vollständige Bewerbung an Ivana Bohac, Human Resources SLF, indem Sie die verlangten Unterlagen über unser Bewerbungsportal einreichen. Bewerbungen per E-Mail sowie auf dem Postweg werden nicht berücksichtigt. Für Fragen steht Ihnen Christoph Suter, Leiter Gruppe Warn- und Informationssysteme, Tel. +41 (0)81 417 02 52, gerne zur Verfügung. An der WSL sind Vielfalt und Inklusion gelebte Werte. Wir setzen uns engagiert für die Gleichstellung der Geschlechter sowie für die Förderung eines offenen und inklusiven Arbeitsklimas ein. Flüelastrasse 11, CH-7260 Davos Dorf

Our Finance Core Platform is at the heart of this ecosystem, ensuring high performance, scalability, and absolute precision for every single booking made on our platforms. We are looking for a Software Engineer to join our Finance Core Platform team in Chiasso, building robust, high-throughput microservices that power our core financial flows. Why this role matters As a Software Engineer in the Finance Core Platform team, you will design and implement the resilient infrastructure and microservices that handle critical financial data across the entire traveler journey. Working in a hybrid setup from Chiasso, you will collaborate closely with cross-functional engineers, architects, and business stakeholders to solve complex technical and transactional challenges. If you thrive on writing clean code, applying solid architectural principles to massive-scale systems, and taking end-to-end ownership of mission-critical platforms, this is the seat for you. The setup Job Title: Software Engineer – Finance Core Platform Working model: Hybrid (from Chiasso) Team: Finance Engineering Level: Professional Location: Chiasso, Switzerland Contract: Permanent — Full-time (36 hours/week) Main Language: English What your impact will be You will proactively design, develop, and maintain high-quality software for our core financial platforms, ensuring resilience, performance, and scalability across all global transactions. items.desc: COMPANY & ROLE OVERVIEW Kodiform Therapeutics is a discovery-stage spin-out from the Institute of Cancer Research and the University of Oxford, based on the pioneering research of our Founders, Professors Terry Rabbitts and Angela Russell. We develop small-molecule inhibitors of hard-to-drug proteins, including intrinsically disordered proteins, using our intracellular domain antibody (iDAb) platform. Our technology finds new functional binding sites on these proteins and opens new routes to target them with small molecules. We are based at the Scale Space science innovation hub in White City, London. The role. We are looking for a protein scientist to join our small, multidisciplinary laboratory team on a fixed-term contract. Working hand in hand with colleagues in structural biology and pharmacology, you will clone, express, purify and quality-control the proteins at the heart of everything we do: our iDAbs and intrinsically disordered target proteins (full-length or as fragments) produced in bacterial and mammalian systems. These reagents power our platform, assays and structural studies, and ultimately our search for new medicines against proteins long considered hard to drug. You will already have some hands-on experience of protein expression and purification (preferably nanobodies and or disordered proteins), and we will support you in building it further. You are organised, keep meticulous records and enjoy being part of a close-knit team. We offer a competitive salary and pension. PURPOSE & MISSION This role will supply high-quality recombinant proteins to support Kodiform's intracellular antibody (iDAb) discovery activities. The postholder will design constructs for, express, purify and quality-control iDAbs and target proteins (full-length or domain fragments) from bacterial and mammalian expression systems. These reagents support library selection, binder characterisation, assay development and biophysical and structural studies on hard-to-drug proteins. DIMENSIONS & STAKEHOLDERS Line manager [experienced protein scientist, biophysicist and structural biologist]. Scientists team: iDAb platform, cell biology and assay development colleagues who use the proteins. External service providers and collaborators receiving protein (e.g. biophysics, mass spectrometry and structural biology CROs), through the line manager. Suppliers of reagents, gene synthesis and consumables. Laboratory Manager and Biological Safety Officer: laboratory operations, genetic modification (GM), biosafety and COSHH compliance. No direct reports and no budget responsibility. KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES Molecular biology Design and build expression constructs for iDAbs and target proteins or domain fragments (e.g. PCR, restriction, Gibson or Golden Gate assembly, site-directed mutagenesis), and verify them by sequencing. With guidance, choose construct features such as tags, fusion partners, protease sites, signal peptides, codon optimisation and domain boundaries. Expression Express iDAbs and target proteins in E. coli (cytoplasmic and periplasmic) and in transient mammalian systems (e.g. Expi293/HEK293, ExpiCHO). Run small-scale expression and solubility screens, and scale up successful conditions. Purification Purify proteins by affinity (e.g. IMAC, Protein A/G or other tag-based capture), ion-exchange and size-exclusion chromatography on automated systems (e.g. ÄKTA), including tag removal where needed. Optimise buffers and handling to keep proteins stable, including aggregation-prone and disordered targets. Quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) Carry out protein QC: SDS-PAGE, Western blot, concentration (A280), analytical SEC and intact mass (in-house or external). Use stability and aggregation methods (e.g. nanoDSF, DLS) and endotoxin testing where required. Confirm that iDAbs are functional by binding assays (e.g. ELISA, BLI or SPR). Release each batch against agreed specifications and record the results in a batch QC record or certificate of analysis. Register, aliquot, label and store protein stocks. Maintain the protein inventory and sample archive. Prepare samples and paperwork for shipment to partners. General Keep meticulous records in line with company data-integrity standards. Communicate results at team meetings and in short written reports. Propose improvements to protocols and processes, e.g. yield, purity or throughput. Be an effective member of our laboratory team and contribute to the efficient running of the lab. This includes health and safety compliance (GM contained use, Containment Level 2, COSHH) and care of shared equipment, as well as contributions to lab housekeeping and maintenance of reagent stocks. Skills Essential Hands-on recombinant protein expression in E. coli. Protein purification by affinity and size-exclusion chromatography, ideally on an automated system (e.g. ÄKTA). Standard protein QC: SDS-PAGE, Western blot, concentration measurement. Core molecular cloning: PCR, cloning, plasmid …

items.desc: We are seeking to appoint a Research Assistant in VLP Vaccine Development to work with Associate Professor Sandy Douglas’ group. items.desc: About Clear Street: Clear Street's mission is to give every sophisticated investor access to every asset, in every market, through a unified platform built for speed, transparency and scale. We give our clients the technology, tools, and service once reserved for the largest institutions, rebuilt with modern infrastructure. Our single, cloud-native, end-to-end capital markets platform powers investor growth today and is transforming how they can interact with markets tomorrow. For more information, visit https://clearstreet.io. The Role As a Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) you sit at the intersection of software reliability and operational excellence. You own the health, resilience, and recovery of our production systems—while spending equal energy innovating solutions that eliminate human toil, reduce incident blast radius, and raise the reliability bar across the entire platform. You will partner closely with engineering, operations, and business teams to understand daily pain points and translate them into lasting automated solutions. Half your time is spent in the trenches—supporting production, responding to incidents, and deeply understanding how our systems behave under real conditions. The other half is yours to build: automation, tooling, and observability platforms that make tomorrow's on-call shift meaningfully easier than today's. You will work on challenges like: Design and build comprehensive monitoring and observability platforms that surface the right signal at the right time—eliminating alert fatigue and accelerating root-cause analysis. Develop intelligent automation and self-healing capabilities that diagnose issues, trigger recovery workflows, and reduce mean time to recovery (MTTR) without manual intervention. Analyze incidents, identify systemic trends, and engineer solutions that prevent entire classes of failures from recurring. Build reusable runbooks, diagnostic tooling, and recovery playbooks that turn tribal knowledge into scalable platform capabilities. Create golden-path operational workflows—making the safest, most reliable path also the easiest one for engineering teams to follow. Partner with Platform Engineering to influence CI/CD pipelines, deployment safety, and infrastructure resilience from a production reliability perspective. Champion Infrastructure as Code, GitOps, and SRE best practices while helping teams adopt modern engineering workflows. Continuously measure production health through SLIs/SLOs/SLAs, and drive engineering priorities based on reliability data. Explore emerging technologies—including AI-assisted diagnostics and developer tooling—that transform how we operate production systems. The Team We believe resilient systems are built by engineers who understand them end to end. Our Production Engineering team is the first and last line of defense for our production platform. We treat reliability as a product, with uptime and engineer experience as our north stars. We combine the discipline of SRE with a builder's mindset: when we see a recurring problem, we build a solution—not a workaround. You will work across every engineering and operations team to understand failure modes, quantify reliability gaps, and build platform capabilities that scale with the organization. Whether it's reducing MTTR from hours to minutes, building self-service diagnostic tools, or designing proactive alerting that catches issues before customers notice, your work will have immediate, measurable impact. If you're passionate about making production systems invisible to end users—and you get energy from both firefighting and building the systems that make fires less likely—you'll thrive here. What We're Looking For We're looking for engineers who combine operational instinct with a builder's discipline. You should have: Strong hands-on Python skills—this is your primary language for automation and tooling. Experience in SRE, Production Engineering, Platform Engineering, or a related discipline with direct production ownership. Proven track record of building automation and diagnostic tooling that improved recovery times or reduced operational toil. Deep familiarity with cloud-native technologies—Kubernetes, containers, distributed systems—and how they fail in production. Experience with observability platforms such as Datadog, and a strong intuition for what "good" monitoring looks like. Exposure to Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) and GitOps-based deployment workflows (ArgoCD, GitHub Actions, or similar). Familiarity with the broader technology stack: Java, Go, Kafka, Redis, Snowflake, and Postgres. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills—you thrive on ambiguous, high-stakes production problems. A product mindset applied to operational tooling: you think about usability, adoption, and documentation when building internal solutions. Excellent communication skills and the ability to work fluidly across engineering, operations, and business stakeholders. Self-starter …

items.desc: Product Designer About Teton On a night shift, three carers can be responsible for a hundred residents, each behind a closed door. Teton tells them what’s going on in every room, so they know who to check on first. We put a sensor in the ceiling of each room: an infrared camera wired to a small computer. The computer turns what the sensor sees into facts, like who is in bed, how fast someone is breathing, or whether someone has fallen. We train one model in our office and copy it to every device, so every site improves at once. Staff get the facts through a mobile app on the floor, a desktop app for leaders and planning, and a screen on the wall. Around that sits the service: installation, onboarding, training, and a support chat any member of staff can use. Around 10,000 care staff use Teton in care homes and hospitals in the US, Denmark, the UK, and Switzerland. Many of the falls we help prevent come from staff seeing what’s going on and planning their shift around it, rather than from alarms. The Role You’ll design the apps care staff use every day, from the alarm a carer hears in the corridor to the overview a regional leader uses for every home they cover. You’ll report to Julius, who leads design, work alongside Balazs, our other product designer, and build directly with our engineers. You’ll work with the AI team that trains our models and the engineers who run them at the edge, on what the models can see and how it reaches staff. Few product design jobs sit this close to the technology. Most of our users are floor staff, and many are new or temporary. Most never go deeper into the app than reacting when something happens, so it can’t have a learning curve. A smaller group of leaders, nurses and physiotherapists dig into the data, and the same product has to serve both. What you’ll work on: Agency with oversight. Good results only come from staff actually engaging with the product. To do this you have to design a product that gives accountability and agency to staff, whilst still giving the oversight to the leadership. It's a tricky balance to create for each workflow. The same facts at every level. A night carer can finish a shift thinking it went well, then hear from a manager about a problem that was only visible on an executive’s dashboard. Everyone has to have a shared understanding of a community and how its running, at the level of detail their job needs. Health data people can read. We track sleep, breathing, movement and more for every resident, but most staff aren’t used to reading a respiration trend. The design challenge is making this information tractable and showing it in the right place at the right time. What We’re Looking For 4+ years designing software people use daily, ideally a product that had to stay coherent as it grew. Precision. You structure things well: information architecture, states, edge cases, components. You can say exactly what a design does and why. You go and see. You’ll travel to customers in Denmark, the UK and the US, sometimes for a night shift. You look forward to it, and what you see changes your designs. You learn how the technology works. Some things are hard for any sensor to tell apart, like a visitor and a member of staff. You find out where those limits are and design with them in mind. You help define the problem. When a brief is unclear, you work it out with engineers and product instead of waiting, then pick what it needs: a site visit, a prototype, or just building it. You prototype in code. What You’ll be doing Luton Borough Council is looking for a Data, Accuracy and Reconciliation Officer to help ensure the accuracy, integrity and security of data held across the Council’s People systems. items.desc: Driving The Future of Smart Fleet Logistics At Xirgo, we’re not just transforming logistics — we’re redefining what’s possible. Let’s move forward together. Our Purpose We believe smarter tools create smarter operations. As the switched-on experts in IoT fleet solutions, we transform uncertainty into confidence, complexity into clarity, and data into decisions. Our Vision We empower partners with intelligent fleet logistics to create a more connected future. From bustling cities to open highways, from railroads to runways, our innovative technologies make peace of mind the new normal. Our Mission To be the world’s most trusted partner in smart fleet logistics, delivering comprehensive IoT solutions that transform data into useful information. We enhance fleet safety, efficiency, and performance—ensuring confidence at every step. About the role Xirgo Technologies is seeking a Product & Test Engineer to support the development and validation of our current and next-generation Video Telematics products. This hands-on role is ideal for someone passionate about in-vehicle testing, video analysis, hardware validation and test automation. As a Product & Test Engineer, you will execute real-world drive tests, review and classify ADAS and DMS video events, and validate accessories such as extension cameras and custom OBD cables. You will take ownership of test vehicles, ensuring they are properly equipped and maintained to meet evolving business and testing needs, and collaborate with other engineers to build and maintain lab-based automated test setups. You will also develop Python-based test automation and test fixtures, using AI-assisted tools to accelerate development while remaining accountable for the quality of everything you deliver. Location Requirement: This role requires the successful candidate to work from the Belfast office. Hybrid working will be available where work requirement allow. Remote or fully remote arrangements are not available for this position. Right to Work: Applicants must have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom at the time of application. We are unable to offer sponsorship for this role. What you'll do Drive Testing & Field Validation Conduct in-vehicle drive tests to validate ADAS (Advanced Driver Assistance Systems) and DMS (Driver Monitoring Systems) features. Safely simulate real-world driving scenarios to trigger and verify system behaviour. Record and document test results, environmental conditions and system responses. Take ownership of test vehicles, including installation, configuration and maintenance of required hardware and accessories to support ongoing testing and business requirements. Video Review & Classification Review recorded video events from ADAS and DMS systems. Accurately classify events as True Positive, False Positive or False Negative based on defined criteria. Maintain detailed logs and support the QA team in identifying trends or anomalies in system performance. Accessary & Hardware Testing Design and execute test plans for hardware accessories such as extension cameras, custom cables, mounts and other peripherals. Validate compatibility, durability and performance of accessories under various conditions. Provide feedback to engineering teams on usability and integration issues. Test Automation & Tooling Develop, extend and maintain Python-based test automation frameworks and scripts for device and accessory validation (e.g. serial/ADB control, power and ignition cycling, OTA update regression, log capture and parsing). Integrate automated tests with lab equipment such as programmable power supplies, relay boards and CAN interfaces, and report results into JIRA/TestRail. Use AI-assisted tools (e.g. code assistants, LLMs) to accelerate script development, test case generation and log analysis. Apply human review to all AI-generated output: verify it against requirements and real device behaviour, peer-review code before merge, and take ownership of anything committed or reported. Use only approved AI tools, and follow company policy on the handling of confidential and customer data. Test Fixtures & Lab Infrastructure Design, build and maintain test fixtures and bench rigs (wiring harnesses, power/ignition simulation, camera mounts, enclosures) to enable repeatable lab testing. Document fixture designs, wiring and configuration so setups can be reproduced and audited. Maintain lab equipment and fault-find fixture issues, distinguishing rig faults from device faults. Test Execution & Reporting Follow structured test plans and procedures to ensure consistent and repeatable results. Document test outcomes, issues and observations in issue tracking systems (e.g. JIRA, TestRail). Collaborate with QA engineers to reproduce and isolate bugs or unexpected behaviour. Qualifications Essential Criteria Degree in Electronics, Computer/Software Engineering, Automotive Technology or a related technical field, or an HND with equivalent hands-on experience. …

Specsavers are looking for an Audiologist or Hearing Aid Dispenser to become the Store Partner, Director, and Business Owner. Grow your own business, look after your customers, serve your community, create an asset for your family’s future and enjoy the profits of all your hard work. This opportunity is an existing audiology business within a store that already has a customer database and clinical administration team. It requires an initial investment to purchase the shares, you will receive a guaranteed salary and collect profits as dividends. Your focus will be on continuing to service the existing customers and grow the store even further. Why Saffron Walden? Located in one of the UK’s most desirable and affluent market towns, this established hearing business benefits from an ageing population, strong demand for services, and limited local competition. The business has been built on solid foundations and now operates as a highly successful practice with significant opportunities for further growth. The main Saffron Walden location features two testing rooms, including a soundproof room, both positioned away from the shop floor to provide a comfortable clinical environment. Current clinic utilisation remains below capacity, with scope to expand from six-day coverage to a full seven-day service and increase testing availability across both rooms. The business is also supported by the Haverhill spoke location, which currently operates three days per week and presents clear opportunities to expand service provision. Planned investment includes the installation of a soundproof booth to further enhance the clinical offering. In addition, an approved white-space location is scheduled to open shortly, creating an exciting platform for future growth across the territory. A strong and established team is already in place, including: A Registered Hearing Aid Dispenser (RHAD), a trainee Hearing Aid Dispenser working towards qualification, a fully trained Wax Removal Accreditation Programme professional and experienced retail and support colleagues. This provides continuity, stability, and a strong platform for continued growth and success. This represents an excellent opportunity to take ownership of a thriving, well-established hearing business with a loyal customer base, strong operational foundations, and multiple avenues for expansion. Why Choose Specsavers? As an Audiology Partner, you'll enjoy the freedom to run your own business while benefiting from dedicated support. You'll have ongoing assistance from our expert support office teams and existing Optics and Retail partners, ensuring you have everything you need to succeed. We’re looking for a passionate, ambitious, and hard-working Audiologist or Hearing Aid Dispenser, ready to continue to lead and grow the existing Audiology business. You are the heartbeat of your growing business, you will serve your community, and you will create a lasting asset for your family. Essentially, you can look after your customers and take care of your teams, while we look after you. As a partner, you will: Build and develop your own team. Be the driver for clinical and retail excellence. Look after your customers and serve your community. Make critical, everyday decisions. As a partner, you will get: Security of a guaranteed competitive salary. Increased income from business profit as dividends. Access to cutting-edge clinical technology and outstanding opportunities for professional development to reach your ambitions. Generous benefits including medical, dental, pension, and more. Ability to blend leadership, business acumen, and clinical skills effectively. About Joint Venture Partnership We’re a family-run business, with a small-company feel but totally-global stature. Each of our businesses follows our Joint Venture Partnership model. Partners are ‘A’ shareholders in charge of the day-to-day running of the business. This means you’ll receive the profits and enjoy the capital growth, as well as a market salary and other benefits from our joint venture business entity, to give you that extra bit of security. items.desc: Frontier Economics is an economics consultancy that tackles the big questions facing governments, businesses and society. We help our clients to analyse and understand their markets and to formulate strategies based on sound economics. The methods and models we use are often complex, but our advice is always succinct, clear and honest . We advise across sectors and countries and we are one of the largest economic consultancies in Europe with more than 350 Economists based in our offices in Amsterdam, Berlin, Brussels, Cologne, Dublin, London, Madrid, Paris and Prague. Owned entirely by our staff, our business attracts the best people and the most interesting work. We go beyond the numbers to find out what's really going on. Our clients enjoy objective advice, clearly expressed. With our help, they make better decisions and get better results. About the role Our Graduate Analyst programme runs for two years and is designed for those with a Master's degree with a strong focus on Economics. The work is varied. You might analyse data, build or develop an economic model, research a market, test assumptions or sensitivities, contribute to a client presentation, or help turn detailed analysis into a clear conclusion. We do not expect you to know how to do everything from day one. You will build strong economic and technical foundations and, as you develop, take increasing ownership of your work, apply your judgement and contribute your own ideas. What you'll be doing You will use economics and analysis to help answer real-world client questions. With support from experienced colleagues, you will build your skills and gradually take on more responsibility. Your work could involve: applying economic frameworks and empirical techniques to real-world problems working with data and evidence, using Excel confidently and developing your skills in tools such as R researching unfamiliar topics and deciding what information is most relevant taking questions that may not be fully defined, working out what is really being asked and shaping a sensible approach to answering them testing assumptions, checking the quality of analysis and thinking about what the results mean contributing to reports, presentations and client meetings managing your own tasks and deadlines, and raising questions or risks at the right time working collaboratively with colleagues across projects and offices contributing to wider Frontier initiatives. As you develop, we will increasingly encourage you not just to produce analysis, but to form a view on it: to ask good questions, explain your reasoning, challenge assumptions and think about what should happen next. Technology, including Generative AI, is increasingly part of how we work. You may use it to support areas such as research, coding, analysis, drafting and quality assurance. What matters is using these tools thoughtfully and responsibly: understanding the underlying problem, checking and challenging outputs, and remaining accountable for the quality of your work. What you'll get out of it You'll gain two years of hands-on economic consulting experience across a variety of projects, supported by training, mentoring and seminars. You'll work with and learn from colleagues across Frontier, including opportunities to collaborate across our European offices. As your experience grows, you'll have the opportunity to tackle less-prescriptive problems, develop greater independence and build the judgement and ownership needed for the next stages of your career. You'll also join a collaborative and supportive environment where different perspectives are valued and where asking questions, sharing ideas and learning from feedback are an important part of how we work. What we're looking for There are a small number of essential requirements for the role. You will be predicted or will have achieved a 2:1 or above in an Economics-focused degree (or equivalent: Germany 2.0 or better, Netherlands 7.0+, France 14+, Spain 7.0+), together with a Master's degree with a strong economic focus. You will also need to be fluent in the language of the office to which you are applying, except Brussels, where English is sufficient. Beyond these requirements, we are interested in how you think, how you approach problems and how you learn. items.desc: Job Advert One definition of every metric. One version of the truth. Join Protein Works as our Analytics Engineer and build the numbers a fast-growing brand runs on. We are rolling out safe, self-serve AI analytics so teams can answer many of their own questions rather than raise a ticket. That only works if the models behind it reflect how the business wants to measure itself, and every metric means one thing. What you will be doing Own the transformation layer in Dataform end to end: the models, dependency graph, tests and documentation between raw BigQuery data and everything the business sees. Build the semantic layer that gives revenue, margin, customer and order one definition, read by every report and every AI tool. Own our Looker Studio reporting, from executive dashboards to the self-serve datasets our analysts and the wider business build on. Shape safe, self-serve AI analytics by structuring and documenting models so AI tools answer standard questions reliably, and deciding where the boundaries sit. Partner with marketing, trading, operations and finance to work out what they really need to measure, then turn it into models that answer it. Drive data quality with tests and checks that catch problems before they reach a report, and agree contracts and conventions with our Data Engineer. Ideal Candidate Proven analytics engineering experience, with production models you've built that other people depend on. Excellent SQL and hands-on Dataform or dbt (testing and documentation included), ideally on BigQuery, with an eye for cost as well as correctness. Strong data modelling: you can take a messy source system, shape something the business can use, and explain why you built it that way. Experience with a semantic layer or shared metric definitions, plus reporting in Looker Studio, Looker or a similar BI tool, all in a Git and CI/CD workflow. You turn a vague business question into a working model without waiting for a spec, and you explain your thinking clearly to non-technical teams. Over a decade later, we are a £50m business with five consecutive years of double-digit growth, a brand new £10m campus in Liverpool, and ambitions that go well beyond where we are today. We are a brand, a retailer, a manufacturer and a fulfilment operation. All in-house, all under one roof. That breadth is deliberate. It gives our people exposure and influence that most businesses simply cannot offer, and it gives us a platform to scale in a way that few companies in this space can match. items.desc: Location : London Status : 9 month fixed term contract, asap start Direct reports : Information Associate Reports to: Technology Operations Manager (EMEA & APAC) Team: Enterprise Applications Manager, Project Manager - IT Initiatives, Security Lead, AV Team, IT Technicians Job purpose The IFRS Foundation is seeking a skilled IT Automation & Systems Specialist to provide drive automation, optimisation, and administration of the user-facing components of our Microsoft Azure environment. Additionally, this role will help accelerate the migration to Windows 11 and Autopilot based laptop deployment. These initiatives are aimed at improving user experience, increasing operational efficiency, and reducing manual intervention across IT services. You will work at the intersection of support and engineering—resolving complex technical issues while proactively identifying opportunities to automate processes, streamline onboarding and implement system integration across platforms. The Team This role sits within the Technology Operations function, reporting to the Technology Operations Manager responsible for EMEA and APAC. The Technology Operations Manager: Reports into the Infrastructure & Cyber Security Director, who in turn reports to the Chief Technology Officer (CTO). The role will operate as an individual contributor with no direct reports, working closely with colleagues across infrastructure, service desk, security, and application teams. The role has a global remit, collaborating across regions to deliver consistent, scalable solutions and support a unified user experience. Principal accountabilities: Automation, Optimisation & Integration Design and implement automation solutions to reduce manual IT tasks and improve service delivery. Simplify and optimise existing Microsoft Intune configurations to reduce complexity and improve maintainability. Develop automated workflows where possible. Initial focus on: User onboarding and offboarding License assignment based on role or department Device provisioning and configuration Reduce onboarding time through process re-engineering and automation. Evaluate and implement AutoPilot if feasible. Automate data flows and triggers between HR and IT systems (e.g., joiners, movers, leavers processes). Accelerate the migration to Windows 11 Environment Alignment & Standardisation Review and rationalise existing configurations originating from parallel or historically separate environments. Identify inconsistencies across identity, device management, and access configurations, and implement a unified, standardised approach. Consolidate policies within Microsoft Intune and Azure AD to reduce duplication, conflicts, and administrative overhead. Align user lifecycle processes, licensing models, and security controls to a single operating model. Second-Line Support Provide advanced technical support for escalated end-user issues across Azure, Microsoft 365, and endpoint management platforms. Troubleshoot and resolve incidents related to identity, device management, access, and cloud services. Collaborate with first-line support to ensure smooth escalation and knowledge transfer. Azure & Endpoint Administration Administer and maintain the user-facing elements of the Azure environment, including Azure AD (Entra ID), Intune, and Microsoft 365 services. Monitor system performance, security, and compliance across managed endpoints and cloud services. Work with stakeholders to carefully transition legacy configurations with minimal disruption to end users. Reporting & Continuous Improvement Build automated reporting solutions to provide insights into system usage, performance, and service delivery. Identify trends and recommend improvements to enhance efficiency and user experience. Contribute to documentation, knowledge base articles, and standard operating procedures. Skills & Experience Essential: Strong experience with Microsoft Azure, including Azure AD (Entra ID) and Microsoft 365. Hands-on expertise with Microsoft Intune (Endpoint Manager) administration and configuration. Experience with scripting and automation (PowerShell preferred). Proven ability to troubleshoot complex technical issues in a cloud-first environment. Experience integrating systems via APIs or automation tools. Desirable: Familiarity with ITSM tools, particularly HALO or similar platforms. Knowledge of identity lifecycle management and role-based access control. Experience with reporting tools (e.g., Power BI). Personal Attributes Strong problem-solving mindset with a focus on efficiency and automation. Ability to balance reactive support with proactive improvement initiatives. Clear communicator, able to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders. Self-motivated and comfortable working in a dynamic, evolving environment. items.desc: Job Introduction We are looking for an experienced and knowledgeable Early Years Inclusion Outreach Officer to help early years providers develop high-quality, inclusive practice. This is an opportunity to use your SEND expertise to support settings across Portsmouth and help ensure that children receive the right support at the earliest opportunity. About the service Early Years Inclusion is part of Portsmouth City Council’s Early Years Service. The service works to improve outcomes for young children who have, or may be at risk of developing, special educational needs or disabilities. It supports early years settings to deliver high-quality, inclusive provision in partnership with parents, families, health professionals and other services About the Role Working as part of the Early Years Inclusion team and reporting to the Early Years Advisory Teacher Team, you will provide practical support, guidance and specialist advice to early years settings. You will help providers strengthen their SEND practice through early identification, observation and assessment, planning for children’s progress and evaluating the impact of support. You will model appropriate strategies and interventions, helping practitioners translate professional recommendations into effective everyday practice. You will work closely with early years providers, health visitors and other relevant partners to support the effective delivery of SEND outreach. You will also contribute to training delivered by the wider Early Years team and help settings develop their understanding of the Portsmouth Local Offer. The role includes recording visits, preparing actions and guidance, collecting and submitting data, and keeping up to date with relevant SEND legislation and national and local developments The ideal candidate You will hold an NVQ Level 3 qualification in childcare, health and social care, or have equivalent relevant experience. You will have recent experience of working within an early years setting and a strong understanding of the Early Years Foundation Stage, children’s learning and development, the SEND Code of Practice and the role of the Early Years SENCo. You will have experience of identifying and supporting children with a range of special educational needs and disabilities, including using observation and assessment to monitor progress. You will also understand the approaches, interventions and strategies that can be used to support individual children effectively. You will be able to offer constructive support and challenge to early years providers, helping them ensure that their provision is inclusive and effective. Strong written and verbal communication skills are essential, as you will need to summarise visits, agree actions, provide clear guidance and produce reports and other documents. You will be organised, able to manage competing priorities and confident working both independently and collaboratively. You will also need good IT skills, an understanding of safeguarding and child protection, and the ability to travel independently between settings and sites across Portsmouth Please ensure that you read the full job profile attached for the details and expectations of this role, paying particular attention the section 'Who is the person' as you will need to refer to this when completing your Personal statement. Working Arrangements: You will be required to work a minimum of 2 days in the office each week About Portsmouth City Council Portsmouth City Council is a unique organisation, committed to making a difference, and is guided by core values that set who we are as people, what we stand for, and how we act. We are committed to our values of respect, integrity, collaboration, inclusivity and being people-focussed. These values set out how we can contribute to the success of the council and our own success as individuals. Learn more about our values and behaviours. Application process We anonymise applications during application & shortlisting to ensure only relevant information is considered. We strongly encourage candidates to add all Career and Education History to their application, as CVs are not reviewed as part of the shortlisting process. As part of your application, we ask that you complete a personal statement, this statement is crucial and is where you must demonstrate how you meet the requirements of the job against each of the points described in the 'Who is the Person' points on the Job Profile using examples from your experience or transferable skills. This might be through qualifications or descriptive examples from your work / personal experience. We are a disability confident employer and Armed Forces Covenant gold standard.
